question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. unemployment rate for September 2025 be initially reported as 4.4% or higher?
subquestions.background_information: In September 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) lowered the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 4.00%-4.25% (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm). As recent monetary policy decisions have demonstrated, the Fed is closely monitoring downside risks to the labor market; the August 2025 unemployment rate rose to 4.3% alongside significantly slowed job gains, prompting the initial rate cut (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm). Because the Fed's dual mandate requires balancing inflation with maximum employment, a continuing rise in the unemployment rate to 4.4% or higher would signal a deteriorating labor market, increasing the likelihood of aggressive policy actions such as a 50+ basis points rate cut at or before the January 2026 meeting. Tracking the September 2025 unemployment rate, typically released on the first Friday of October, provides a vital early indicator of whether the labor market is stabilizing or worsening. Sources: Federal Reserve Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm | BLS Employment Situation Summary: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm | FOMC Meeting Calendars: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the seasonally adjusted U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) for September 2025 is initially reported as 4.4% or higher by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). This event must occur between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18 (inclusive). The primary resolution source will be the initial Employment Situation Summary news release for September 2025 published by the BLS (available at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm or the historical archive at https://www.bls.gov/bls/newsrels.htm). Only the headline, seasonally adjusted U-3 rate from the initial release for September 2025 will be used; any subsequent revisions or data updates will not affect the resolution. If the data release is postponed beyond the resolution window and does not occur by 2025-10-18, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: The recent 25 basis point rate cut by the Federal Reserve in September 2025 was driven heavily by an unexpectedly weak labor market, highlighted by an August unemployment rate of 4.3%. A further increase in the September unemployment rate to 4.4% or above would strongly suggest that the U.S. labor market is continuing to cool, increasing the pressure on the FOMC to act aggressively and making a larger 50+ basis points cut at the January 2026 meeting highly probable. Conversely, if unemployment stabilizes or falls, the Fed will likely maintain a slower pace of rate cuts.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate for September 2025 must be initially reported by the BLS as 4.4% or higher. The BLS Employment Situation Summary for September 2025 must be published between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18. Observable evidence would be the BLS news release at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm. Key entity: BLS. Threshold: U-3 rate ≥ 4.4%. Timing: must occur by 2025-10-18.

'US unemployment rate October 2025 BLS jobs report' (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-18) - to find report release. 3. 'BLS September jobs report released government shutdown ended' (2025-10-07 to 2025-10-18) - to find if shutdown ended and data released. 4. 'US government shutdown ended October 2025 BLS data release' (2025-10-07 to 2025-10-18) - to check shutdown resolution. 5. 'government shutdown ended resolved October 17 18 2025' - to check final days of window. 6. 'BLS employment situation September 2025 unemployment rate released' (2025-10-14 to 2025-10-18) - final check.

All sources confirm: (1) The BLS September Employment Situation report was scheduled for October 3, 2025 but was NOT released due to the government shutdown beginning October 1, 2025. (2) The BLS explicitly stated that only the September CPI (released October 24) would be published during the shutdown, with no other data releases rescheduled. (3) The shutdown was still ongoing as of October 17, 2025 (day 17), with the next vote scheduled for October 20. Sources: RISMedia (Oct 2), Investing.com UK (Oct 10), USA Today (Oct 17), KTTC (Oct 17), Livemint (Oct 17).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires the BLS to publish the initial Employment Situation Summary for September 2025 by October 18, 2025. This did NOT occur. Multiple high-quality sources explicitly confirm the report was not released: [RISMedia](https://www.rismedia.com/2025/10/02/no-news-likely-good-news-shutdown-postpones-jobs-report/) confirms the September jobs report was postponed with no release date. [USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/10/17/government-shutdown-trump-congress-day-17-live-updates/86626986007/) confirms the shutdown was still ongoing on Day 17 (October 17). [Yahoo Finance/AFP](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/shaheen-says-nothing-official-happening-180301738.html) confirms no resolution by October 17.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp exists for the BLS September 2025 Employment Situation Summary release within the resolution window (September 18 - October 18, 2025). The report was not released within this window.

evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The Workers World article (Oct 11) suggested the report was 'completed and verified' but still not released — this supports the finding that the report exists but was withheld/delayed. The BLS itself confirmed no other releases besides the CPI would occur during the shutdown. The shutdown was confirmed ongoing as late as October 17, 2025, with the next vote not until October 20 at the earliest.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria explicitly states: 'If the data release is postponed beyond the resolution window and does not occur by 2025-10-18, the question should be considered unresolvable.' The U.S. government shutdown (beginning October 1, 2025) caused the BLS to not release the September 2025 Employment Situation Summary within the required window. The BLS confirmed only the CPI would be released during the shutdown. The shutdown was still ongoing on October 17, 2025 (day 17), with no resolution before October 18. subquestions.question: Will a US congressional committee or task force hold a public hearing primarily focused on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs) or UFO declassification between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?

There is growing momentum for UAP transparency in Washington, with the Pentagon's All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) aiming to release more unclassified data (https://abcnews.go.com) and lawmakers floating proposals like the UAP Transparency Act to mandate disclosure (https://medium.com). Congress typically reconvenes in September following its August recess. A public congressional hearing focused on UAPs during this first month back would be a critical leading indicator of sustained legislative momentum. It would demonstrate coordinated pressure on the Trump administration to fulfill its promises of 'radical transparency' and actively declassify UAP files by the end of 2025.

Delayed Events: If a qualifying hearing is scheduled but postponed beyond 2025-10-01, it will not count towards resolution, and the question will resolve 'No'.

The primary resolution sources will be the official calendars of the US House of Representatives (https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Calendar/ByWeek.aspx) and the US Senate (https://www.senate.gov/committees/hearings_meetings.htm). Credible news reporting (e.g., from major outlets like AP News, Reuters, or ABC News) verifying that the hearing occurred will also be considered if official calendars are delayed or unavailable.

If Congress prioritizes this issue immediately after their August recess, it significantly increases the likelihood that the Trump administration will respond by declassifying files by the end of 2025. Conversely, a lack of legislative activity in September may suggest the topic is losing priority among lawmakers.

question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for August 2025 be reported at 4.4% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
The unemployment rate is a critical indicator of economic health and a key metric evaluated by the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) when determining recession timelines. As of earlier in 2025, the U.S. unemployment rate was recorded at 4.2%. Despite a Q1 2025 GDP contraction of 0.5%, Q2 GDP rebounded strongly to an estimated 3.3% growth. However, a significant component of recession forecasting hinges on labor market dynamics. The Sahm Rule, an empirical indicator of recessions, tracks upward momentum in the unemployment rate. A continued rise in unemployment to 4.4% or higher for August 2025 would signal substantial labor market cooling. This would indicate an increased probability of negative GDP growth in Q3 and Q4, or a broad economic decline prompting an NBER recession declaration in 2025.

Sources:
Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) Unemployment Rate: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports that the headline, seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (U-3) for August 2025 is 4.4% or higher in its initial Employment Situation news release published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive). The resolution will be based strictly on the headline one-decimal figure (e.g., 4.4%) published in the initial release (typically found in the summary text and 'Table A. Major indicators of labor market activity, seasonally adjusted'). Subsequent revisions to this figure in later months will not affect the resolution. If the August 2025 Employment Situation report is delayed and not published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30, this question will resolve as unresolvable. The official BLS Employment Situation release will be the primary source: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm.
subquestions.rationale: The NBER relies heavily on broad employment data to date recessions. Furthermore, a rising unemployment rate triggers the Sahm Rule, which correlates strongly with economic downturns. Identifying whether unemployment reaches 4.4% or higher in August acts as a leading crux for Q3 economic weakness, strongly updating forecasters' probabilities regarding a recession in 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: BLS reports seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate for August 2025 at 4.4% or higher in initial Employment Situation release published September 1–30, 2025. Observable evidence: BLS press release with headline U-3 figure ≥4.4%. Key entities: BLS, U-3 unemployment rate, August 2025, initial release. Threshold: 4.4% or higher.

The BLS reported 4.3% for August 2025 per [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/august-jobs-report-shows-us-labor-market-continues-dramatic-summer-slowdown-153001758.html), [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/09/05/august-jobs-bls-22000-jobs-slowdown/1471757080514/), [Mint](https://www.livemint.com/economy/us-unemployment-jumps-to-4-3-in-august-as-job-growth-slows-sharply-despite-trump-s-shake-up-at-bls-11757077053743.html), [Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/bls-jobs-august-22k-unemployment-43), and others. 4.3% < 4.4%, so the Yes condition is NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The BLS August 2025 Employment Situation report was released on September 5, 2025 (Friday), explicitly stated by multiple sources. This is within the September 1–30, 2025 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is the initial BLS release for August 2025 data. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists within the window. All sources confirm this was the first release.
evidence.step7_verification: All 10+ independent sources consistently report 4.3% for the August 2025 unemployment rate. No source reports 4.4% or higher. The figure is below the resolution threshold. There is no contradictory evidence. The Yes condition (≥4.4%) became definitively impossible when BLS published 4.3% on September 5, 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BLS reported the seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate for August 2025 at 4.3% in its initial Employment Situation release on September 5, 2025. As of late September 2025, Verstappen was reported to be 69 points behind the championship leader, Oscar Piastri, with only seven rounds remaining. Despite this significant deficit, Red Bull has recently found renewed form, with Verstappen winning the late-season races at Monza and Baku (https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/after-baku-brilliance-heres-why-singapore-gp-is-key-for-max-verstappens-f1-title-hopes/10656600/). To close the 69-point gap in the final stages of the season and win the 2025 Drivers' Championship, Verstappen needs to consistently outscore his rivals and secure more race victories. subquestions.question: Will the US or Chinese government officially announce a planned in-person meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information: US-China trade talks resumed in Stockholm in late July 2025, with negotiators aiming to extend a 90-day tariff truce that was originally set to expire in mid-August (https://www.marketscreener.com). According to analysts, an extension of the truce would prevent new tariffs and pave the way for an in-person meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping later in the year, potentially in late October or November (https://www.indiatoday.in). Given the massive logistical and diplomatic preparation required for a bilateral summit between the US and Chinese leaders, such an event is typically announced weeks in advance by either the White House or the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Thus, an official announcement by October 1 would serve as a strong early indicator of whether a meeting will materialize by the end of October. Sources: Market Screener - https://www.marketscreener.com | India Today - https://www.indiatoday.in
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if an official announcement confirming a scheduled in-person meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). To qualify, the announcement must be made by the White House, the US Department of State, or the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) via an official press release, a formal statement published on their website, or an on-the-record public statement by an official spokesperson or the leaders themselves. The announcement must clearly state that an in-person meeting has been agreed upon. Statements that merely express a desire to meet, indicate that a meeting is being 'explored', or rely solely on anonymous media reports will not count toward resolution. The planned date of the meeting does not need to be before October 31; the question resolves based entirely on whether the confirmation is announced within the specified window. If no such official announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question resolves No. If an official press conference or scheduled announcement event intended to confirm the meeting is explicitly postponed beyond the resolution window, the question should be considered unresolvable and canceled. Resolution Sources: White House Briefing Room: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/ | US Department of State Press Releases: https://www.state.gov/press-releases/ | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China: https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/
subquestions.rationale: An official announcement of a meeting is a necessary precursor to a highly-choreographed US-China presidential summit. If an announcement occurs before October 1, it significantly increases the likelihood that a meeting will take place by the ultimate question's October 31 deadline. Conversely, the lack of an announcement strongly implies that no meeting is imminent, heavily updating the probability of the ultimate question toward No.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: An official announcement by the White House, US Department of State, or Chinese MoFA — via official press release, formal statement on their website, or on-the-record public statement by an official spokesperson or the leaders themselves — explicitly confirming a scheduled in-person meeting between Trump and Xi, occurring between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive. The announcement must clearly state an in-person meeting has been agreed upon (not merely desired or explored).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump Xi Jinping meeting announcement official 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 1): to find official announcements. 2) 'White House China summit Trump Xi scheduled meeting' (Sep 1–Oct 1): to find White House-level confirmations. 3) 'White House official statement Trump Xi APEC meeting announcement September 2025' (Sep 19–Oct 1): to confirm White House involvement. 4) 'China Ministry of Foreign Affairs MoFA Trump Xi meeting announcement APEC 2025' (Sep 19–Oct 1): to find Chinese MoFA confirmation.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Primary candidate event: On September 19, 2025, Trump posted on Truth Social that he and Xi 'agreed to meet at the APEC Summit in South Korea' (Oct 31–Nov 1, 2025). The post explicitly confirms an agreed in-person meeting. Multiple sources cite Trump's exact words: 'I also agreed with President Xi that we would meet at the APEC Summit in South Korea.' China's MoFA/Xinhua described the call as 'pragmatic, positive, and constructive.' White House officials confirmed the call took place (one source states 'according to a White House official' the call began at 8 a.m. ET). The Diplomat notes that China's Foreign Ministry readout did NOT mention the agreed-upon visits — but the White House/Trump side explicitly confirmed the meeting. The Korean government also confirmed preparations for the Trump–Xi meeting at APEC. No events before September 19 within the window qualify (prior to that date, reports were speculative/anonymous).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Trump's Truth Social post on September 19, 2025 constitutes an on-the-record public statement by the leader himself: 'I also agreed with President Xi that we would meet at the APEC Summit in South Korea, that I would go to China in the early part of next year, and that President Xi would, likewise, come to the United States at an appropriate time.' This clearly states that an in-person meeting has been agreed upon. White House officials confirmed the call details on the record. Chinese state media (Xinhua) confirmed the call took place and described it positively, though China's MoFA readout did not explicitly confirm the APEC meeting. However, the resolution criteria requires an announcement by the White House, US State Department, OR Chinese MoFA — only ONE of these sources needs to confirm. Trump's own public on-the-record statement (and White House official confirmation of the call) satisfies the 'White House' criterion. Multiple news sources including AP, Fox News, Reuters, Yonhap corroborate this. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/trump-xi-tiktok-china-united-states-e6b6334aef2946b5b8c809be4240cad1) [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/trumps-call-with-xi-jinping-ends-with-announcement-of-a-tiktok-approval-and-plans-for-in-person-meetings-161114876.html) [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-announces-meeting-xi-jinping-south-korea-apec-summit-scheduled-next-month) [Newsmax](https://www.newsmax.com/finance/financenews/trump-xi-jinping-china/2025/09/19/id/1227070/)
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Trump's Truth Social post was made on September 19, 2025. The Yahoo Finance article specifies the call 'began at 8 a.m. ET, according to a White House official.' The Trump Truth Social post was made after the call concluded (before 11:30 a.m. ET per Breitbart). Multiple sources date this to September 19, 2025. This is within the resolution window of September 1–October 1, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Before September 19, searches reveal only speculative/anonymous media reports (e.g., Mehr News Agency on Sept 14 citing unnamed sources, Firstpost on Sept 15 about the Madrid talks). These do not meet the resolution criteria (anonymous reports explicitly excluded). The first qualifying official on-the-record public statement is Trump's September 19 Truth Social post, corroborated by White House officials quoted in news reports. No earlier qualifying event exists within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Potential contradiction: The Diplomat (Sep 19) notes that China's Foreign Ministry readout did not mention the agreed-upon visits and differed on TikTok interpretation. However, this does not negate Trump's own on-the-record statement, which is sufficient under the resolution criteria. The resolution criteria explicitly accepts 'on-the-record public statement by an official spokesperson or the leaders themselves' — Trump himself made this statement. Additionally, Chinese state media (Xinhua) confirmed the call took place and described it positively. The Korean government confirmed preparations for the Trump–Xi APEC meeting. Subsequent articles through September 30 continue to treat the Trump–Xi APEC meeting as confirmed. No evidence of cancellation or withdrawal within the resolution window. The CNN article from September 30 mentions new US export controls but still treats the APEC meeting as planned. The resolution criteria does not require the planned meeting date to be before October 31.
evidence.step8_final_decision: On September 19, 2025, within the resolution window, US President Donald Trump made an explicit on-the-record public statement confirming that he and Xi Jinping agreed to meet in person at the APEC Summit in South Korea (October 31–November 1, 2025). This was corroborated by White House officials quoted by name in news reports. The statement explicitly confirmed an agreed-upon in-person meeting — not merely a desire to meet or exploration. This satisfies all resolution criteria: (1) the announcement was made by the President himself (qualifying source), (2) it explicitly states an in-person meeting has been agreed upon, (3) it occurred within the specified window (September 1–October 1, 2025). Resolution: YES.

question: US x Venezuela military engagement by October 31?

This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will either the United States Armed Forces or the Venezuelan military fire warning shots at the other's vessels or aircraft between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tensions between the United States and Venezuela have sharply escalated following the U.S. deployment of a major naval task force to the Caribbean. The U.S. currently has over 4,500 personnel in the Southern Caribbean, supported by three destroyers, two landing-dock ships, an amphibious assault ship, a littoral combat ship, and the guided-missile cruiser USS Lake Erie. U.S. warships carry Coast Guard detachments tasked with drug interdiction operations and making arrests (https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-crosses-panama-canal-trumps-caribbean-buildup-continues). In response to the U.S. military presence, Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro has ordered the deployment of 4.5 million members of the Bolivarian Militia, while Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino announced 'significant' deployments of drones, warships, and larger vessels to patrol territorial waters (https://www.news24.com/news24/world/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-to-confront-us-destroyers-submarines). The close proximity of heavily armed forces performing overlapping patrols and interdiction missions greatly increases the risk of a confrontation. The firing of warning shots is a standard naval de-escalation or signaling tactic used before lethal force is applied, and serves as an excellent early indicator of escalating hostilities.

Sources:
Newsweek - USS Lake Erie crosses Panama Canal as Trump's Caribbean buildup continues: https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-crosses-panama-canal-trumps-caribbean-buildup-continues
News24 - Venezuela deploys warships, drones to confront US destroyers, submarines: https://www.news24.com/news24/world/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-to-confront-us-destroyers-submarines
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if there is a consensus of credible reporting or official government confirmation that either the United States Armed Forces (including the U.S. Coast Guard) or the Venezuelan military (including the FANB, Venezuelan Coast Guard, or Bolivarian Militia) fired warning shots at, or in the immediate vicinity of, a vessel or aircraft operated by the other country between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

- 'Warning shots' are defined as the intentional discharge of a weapon (e.g., deck guns, machine guns, artillery, or missiles) intended to signal a warning, demand compliance, or deter an adversary, without the intent to strike, damage, or destroy the target.
- The shots must be directed near a state-operated military, militia, or coast guard vessel/aircraft belonging to the US or Venezuela. Warning shots fired exclusively at civilian smuggling vessels, unidentified narco-submarines, or commercial shipping will not count toward a 'Yes' resolution unless a state-operated vessel is directly involved as the target.
- If a military engagement occurs involving the use of destructive force (which would trigger the ultimate question), this subquestion will still resolve 'Yes' if credible reports indicate that warning shots were fired as a precursor during an incident within the specified time window.

Resolution will be based on official press releases from the U.S. Department of Defense (https://www.defense.gov/), U.S. Southern Command (https://www.southcom.mil/), the Venezuelan Ministry of Popular Power for Defense (http://www.mindefensa.gob.ve/), or a consensus of credible mainstream media reporting (such as Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/ or Associated Press: https://apnews.com/). If no such event is reported to have occurred between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question explicitly excludes 'non-violent actions, such as warning shots' from its definition of a military engagement. Consequently, asking whether warning shots will be fired acts as a perfect subquestion: it tracks a measurable, distinct event that falls strictly short of the ultimate resolution criteria, yet acts as a severe escalation and a profound indicator that the two militaries are in direct tactical friction. Forecasters who expect an actual military engagement by late October would likely expect warning shots to occur beforehand, making this a strong crux.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Either the US Armed Forces (including Coast Guard) OR the Venezuelan military (FANB, Venezuelan Coast Guard, Bolivarian Militia) must have intentionally discharged a weapon as a warning shot directed near a state-operated vessel/aircraft of the OTHER country between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Observable evidence: official DoD/SOUTHCOM/Venezuelan MoD press release OR consensus of credible mainstream media reporting an intentional weapon discharge as a warning, aimed at a state military vessel/aircraft. Excluded: strikes on civilian narco/smuggling boats; overflights without shots fired.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US military Venezuela warning shots vessels aircraft 2025' (Sept 1 - Oct 1) — to find direct reports of warning shots; 2) 'Venezuela FANB US Navy Coast Guard incident confrontation September 2025' — to find any confrontations; 3) 'Venezuela US warning shots fired military vessels September 2025' — targeted; 4) 'Venezuelan military fire shots US warship destroyer Caribbean 2025' — to find Venezuelan-fired shots; 5) 'Venezuela US military clash exchange fire warning shots warship September October 2025' — late period; 6) 'Venezuela United States military escalation incident late September 2025' — late period; 7) 'Venezuela FANB navy shoots US destroyer warship F-35 Caribbean 2025' — specific aircraft/vessel types; 8) 'Venezuela US military direct exchange fire state vessel September October 2025 SOUTHCOM' — SOUTHCOM angle.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) US lethal strike on alleged narco speedboat Sept 2, 2025 — killing 11. REJECTED: Target was a civilian/cartel vessel, not a Venezuelan state military vessel/aircraft. Strike was lethal/destructive, not a 'warning shot.' (B) US lethal strike on alleged narco vessel Sept 15, 2025 — killing 3. REJECTED: Same reasons as (A). (C) Venezuelan F-16s buzzing USS Jason Dunham Sept 4-5, 2025. REJECTED: Multiple sources confirm 'the destroyer did not engage the aircraft' and that no shots were fired by either side — one article explicitly notes 'the event illustrates how a government can signal intent without firing a shot.' (D) Venezuelan military drills 'Caribe Soberano 200' Sept 18, 2025 — Sukhoi Su-30s, naval vessels. REJECTED: These were exercises, not shots directed at US vessels. (E) US potentially planning strikes inside Venezuela (late Sept 2025) — REJECTED: Described as being considered/mulled, no confirmed execution. No other candidate events found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that satisfies all criteria: (1) intentional discharge of a weapon; (2) directed at a state-operated military vessel/aircraft; (3) of the OTHER country (US vs Venezuela); (4) intended as a warning signal. The US strikes were lethal actions against civilian/cartel boats, not against Venezuelan state military vessels. The Venezuelan F-16 overflights of USS Jason Dunham involved no weapons discharge by either side — confirmed by Pentagon officials and multiple credible reports including Reuters via Yahoo [https://ca.news.yahoo.com/us-says-2-venezuela-military-021754808.html] and Medium analysis [https://medium.com/@DanielzNova/two-jets-one-destroyer-and-the-thin-line-between-signaling-and-war-c1da141eb284].
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event was found, so no timestamp to extract.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at any point in the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) One article is headlined 'Warning shot or start of something bigger?' but this is using 'warning shot' metaphorically/rhetorically to describe the US strike strategy as a political signal — not as an actual warning shot fired at a Venezuelan state vessel. (2) Trump threatened to shoot down Venezuelan jets, but no shooting occurred. (3) Multiple authoritative sources (Pentagon, Reuters, NYT) confirm the US destroyer did NOT engage the Venezuelan F-16s. (4) No Venezuelan source reports firing on US state vessels. (5) Late September 2025 reporting focuses on possible future strikes inside Venezuela, confirming no actual state-vs-state weapons discharge had occurred yet. The overall picture is one of high tension with close encounters but no actual weapons discharge between state forces.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question requires warning shots fired at/near a state-operated vessel/aircraft of the other country. All evidence in the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window shows: (1) US conducted lethal strikes on civilian/cartel boats — not against Venezuelan state vessels; (2) Venezuelan military aircraft buzzed US warships without any weapons discharge by either side; (3) Both sides made threats but no shots were fired between state forces. The resolution criteria are not met. Resolution: No, at end of window October 1, 2025.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla officially open its Austin, Texas Robotaxi service to the general public between September 1, 2025 and September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tesla has been operating a pilot Robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, since June 2025. Currently, this service is restricted to an invite-only group of testers and requires a safety monitor in the vehicle. In August 2025, CEO Elon Musk and Tesla indicated that the Austin Robotaxi service would be rolled out to the general public in September 2025. 

Opening the service to the general public is a critical intermediate milestone for Tesla's autonomous ride-hailing ambitions. For the ultimate question of whether Tesla will launch a fully driverless Robotaxi service by October 31, 2025, observing whether Tesla meets its near-term September rollout goal will provide strong evidence regarding the company's development timeline and operational momentum. If the service opens early in September, it suggests Tesla is executing rapidly; if it is delayed, it casts doubt on the strict October 31 timeline for an even more advanced (fully driverless) launch.

Sources:
GuruFocus - Barclays Expects Long Approval Process for Tesla's (TSLA) Robotaxi: https://www.gurufocus.com
Tesla North - Tesla Hints at Chicago Robotaxi Launch with New Job Listings: https://teslanorth.com
NewsBytes - Musk confirms Tesla robotaxi rollout for the public in September: https://www.newsbytesapp.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 (inclusive), Tesla officially announces that its Robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, has been opened to the general public, or if the service concretely becomes available to the general public in Austin within this time window. 

"General public" is defined as individuals who are not Tesla employees, contractors, or part of a specifically invited closed-beta/early-access group, meaning any ordinary user in the operational area can download the app (or use the existing Tesla app) and summon a Robotaxi ride. The presence of a safety monitor in the vehicle does not preclude a Yes resolution for this subquestion, as long as the service is openly available to the public. 

The resolution will be based on official communications from Tesla, such as its official press releases (https://ir.tesla.com/#tab-press-releases), the Tesla blog (https://www.tesla.com/blog), or statements from the official Tesla X account (https://x.com/Tesla) / Elon Musk's official X account (https://x.com/elonmusk). Corroboration from credible technology and automotive news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, The Verge, Electrek) reporting that public rides are actively being offered will also suffice for a Yes resolution. 

If no such public rollout occurs or is announced between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 at 11:59 PM ET, the question will resolve No. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Tesla has publicly targeted September 2025 for opening its Austin Robotaxi pilot to the general public. Tracking whether they achieve this in the first week of September serves as a highly informative crux. If they cannot hit this intermediate milestone early in the month, it significantly lowers the probability that they will achieve the much harder milestone of a fully driverless (no safety monitor) service by October 31.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08, Tesla must officially open its Austin Robotaxi to the general public (any ordinary user, not just invited beta testers). Observable evidence: Official Tesla announcement (press release, blog, or X post) or credible tech/auto news reporting public rides are actively available. Key entities: Tesla, Austin TX Robotaxi, general public (non-employee, non-invited). Threshold: Service available to any ordinary user who can download the app and summon a ride. Timing: September 1-8, 2025 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Tesla Robotaxi Austin Texas general public launch September 2025' (Sept 1-8 window) — to find launch announcement. 2) 'Tesla Robotaxi service open public Austin 2025' (Aug 25–Sept 8) — to find earliest occurrence. 3) 'Tesla Robotaxi app public waitlist September 3 4 2025 announcement' — to pin exact date. 4) 'Tesla Robotaxi general public Austin closed beta invite only September 2025' — to check if it remained closed beta.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: On September 4, 2025, Tesla launched a public iOS app on the Apple App Store allowing any member of the public (18+) to download and join a waitlist for Robotaxi rides in Austin. Tesla's official @robotaxi X account stated 'Robotaxi app now available to all.' Multiple users who joined were granted access within hours. Sources: Forbes (Sept 4), CNET (Sept 4), Teslarati (Sept 4), Electrek (Sept 4), Investing.com (Sept 4), San Jose Mercury News (Sept 4), PCMag (Sept 4), Tech Times (Sept 5), Business Insider (Sept 6). No candidates were rejected — all corroborate the same event on Sept 4.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The event EXACTLY satisfies resolution criteria: (1) Tesla officially announced via its @robotaxi X account that the app is 'now available to all' on September 4, 2025. (2) Any ordinary user (18+) could download the app and join a waitlist — not limited to Tesla employees or specifically invited closed-beta groups. (3) Users were being granted ride access within hours of joining the waitlist. (4) Forbes stated 'Tesla opened its Robotaxi service to the public in Austin on September 4 2025. Anyone can download the app, create an account... and join a waitlist.' [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/scottyreiss/2025/09/04/tesla-robotaxi-is-now-open-to-all-in-austin-heres-what-its-like/). CNET: 'Tesla is letting regular folks take a seat.' [CNET](https://www.cnet.com/roadshow/news/want-to-try-teslas-robotaxis-testing-is-now-open-to-all-alongside-dedicated-app/). San Jose Mercury News: 'Tesla Inc. has opened its robotaxi rideshare app to the general public.' [Mercury News](https://www.mercurynews.com/2025/09/04/tesla-says-its-robotaxi-app-now-open-to-public-riders/). Safety monitors present but resolution criteria explicitly permits this.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The event occurred on September 4, 2025. Multiple sources published on September 4, 2025 confirm the launch happened that day. One source (mySA) references September 3 as the date the app was released for iOS, but the majority of sources — including the official Tesla X announcement — point to September 4, 2025 as the public launch date. The exact sub-day timestamp cannot be pinned from search results, but September 4, 2025 is confirmed by numerous high-quality sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence found. The service prior to September 4, 2025 was limited to specifically-invited beta testers (investors, analysts, influencers, media) — not the general public. The September 4 app launch was explicitly described as the first time the service moved 'beyond early access' (Tech Times). This is confirmed to be the first public opening within the September 1-8 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Electrek noted the fleet size and in-car supervisors mean it's 'effectively a large-scale FSD demonstration ride' and was somewhat skeptical of calling it a true public launch. However, this is editorial opinion — the factual evidence is clear that any member of the public could download the app and join a waitlist, which satisfies the resolution criteria's definition of general public. Business Insider reported some users had access revoked after initial grant, suggesting imperfect rollout, but this does not negate the public opening. The resolution criteria allows for a waitlist as long as the service is 'openly available to the public.' No contradictory evidence that the launch did NOT happen or that it remained invite-only.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Tesla officially opened its Robotaxi service to the general public in Austin, Texas on September 4, 2025 — within the September 1-8, 2025 window. The official @robotaxi X account announced 'Robotaxi app now available to all.' Any ordinary user (18+) could download the iOS app and join a waitlist, with access being granted within hours. This is confirmed by multiple credible sources including Forbes, CNET, Electrek, San Jose Mercury News, Teslarati, Investing.com, and PCMag. The presence of safety monitors does not preclude Yes resolution per the explicit criteria. Resolution: YES.

question: OpenAI browser by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI publicly releases a standalone web browser that is intended for general web browsing and is available for use by the public in at least one country or region by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes," such a browser must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling free waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by OpenAI as being accessible to the general public.

Browser extensions, plugins, or integrations within third-party browsers do not count; it must be a standalone browser application.

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from OpenAI. If there is ambiguity, a consensus of credible reporting will be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI officially announce or open a closed beta/waitlist for a standalone web browser between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
OpenAI has been rapidly expanding its product ecosystem, with recent launches including the gpt-realtime speech-to-speech model and Codex IDE integrations (https://www.winbuzzer.com/2025/08/28/openai-supercharges-codex-ai-coding-agent/). The AI browser space is heating up, with competitors like Anthropic rolling out closed-beta browser extensions for Claude (https://www.zdnet.com/article/anthropics-claude-chrome-browser-extension-rolls-out-how-to-get-early-access/) and Perplexity launching its 'Comet' browser. Furthermore, Windows Central recently noted 'OpenAI's rumored project' in the context of emerging AI browsers (https://www.windowscentral.com/let-me-scam-that-for-you). For OpenAI to meet the October 31, 2025 deadline of publicly releasing a standalone web browser (general availability or open beta), it is standard industry practice to first announce the project or open a closed beta/waitlist to a limited group of users. This subquestion tracks whether OpenAI takes this preliminary step by October 1, 2025.

Sources:
Winbuzzer: https://www.winbuzzer.com/2025/08/28/openai-supercharges-codex-ai-coding-agent/
ZDNet: https://www.zdnet.com/article/anthropics-claude-chrome-browser-extension-rolls-out-how-to-get-early-access/
Windows Central: https://www.windowscentral.com/let-me-scam-that-for-you
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if OpenAI officially announces the development of a standalone web browser, OR opens a closed beta, private preview, or waitlist for a standalone web browser, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 11:59 PM ET (inclusive).

To qualify:
1. The announcement or waitlist must be published on an official OpenAI channel, such as the OpenAI News/Blog (https://openai.com/news), the official OpenAI X/Twitter account (https://x.com/OpenAI), or the X/Twitter account of CEO Sam Altman (https://x.com/sama).
2. The product must be explicitly described as a "standalone web browser" (a dedicated desktop or mobile application for general web browsing), not a browser extension, plugin, or an in-app browser within the existing ChatGPT client.
3. If OpenAI bypasses a closed testing phase and directly releases the browser to the public (open beta or general availability) during this timeframe, this question also resolves Yes.

If no such announcement or testing phase is officially initiated by OpenAI between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves No. Any events, announcements, or leaks occurring after 2025-10-01 11:59 PM ET will not count toward a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A standalone web browser is a major product release. Software companies typically announce such products, or open closed betas and waitlists, weeks or months prior to a full public or open-beta launch. If OpenAI officially announces the browser or opens a closed beta by October 1, it significantly increases the probability that a public release or open beta will occur by the October 31 deadline. Conversely, if no announcement or private beta is seen by October 1, the likelihood of a surprise public launch by October 31 drops considerably.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: OpenAI officially announces development of a standalone web browser, OR opens a closed beta/private preview/waitlist for one, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 11:59 PM ET. Must be on official OpenAI channel (openai.com/news, @OpenAI on X, or @sama on X). Product must be explicitly described as a 'standalone web browser.' Observable evidence: a blog post, X/Twitter post, or official press release from OpenAI naming a standalone web browser product and announcing its development or testing phase.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'OpenAI standalone web browser announcement 2025' (Sept 1-Oct 1) - to find any official announcement; 2. 'OpenAI browser launch beta waitlist September 2025' (Sept 1-Oct 1) - to find any beta/waitlist; 3. 'OpenAI web browser official announcement Sam Altman September October 2025' (Sept 1-Oct 1) - to find official channel announcements; 4. 'OpenAI browser Chromium Operator agent launch announcement' (Sept 1-Oct 1) - to find specific product details; 5. 'OpenAI "AI browser" OR "web browser" official blog' (Aug-Oct 2025) - extended search for official blog posts; 6. 'OpenAI "standalone browser" OR "browser app" announcement release' (Sept 1-Oct 1) - to find explicit standalone browser terms.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (A) Bleeping Computer (Aug 16, 2025) - OpenAI 'prepares Chromium-based AI browser' - REJECTED: before window, based on leaked/source info, not official announcement. (B) TechCrunch (Sept 4, 2025) and multiple sources (Sept 5, 2025) - Sam Altman mentions browser as one of several future apps Fidji Simo will oversee, in context of Jobs Platform blog post - PARTIALLY qualifying but falls short: mentioned as future project alongside jobs platform and social app, not a dedicated browser announcement; no specific standalone browser blog post cited. (C) Computerworld (Sept 18, 2025) roundup mentions OpenAI 'announced a new AI-powered browser' - REJECTED: secondary/aggregator source, no specific date/post for browser announcement, no official URL cited. (D) Opera launch article (Sept 30, 2025) - describes OpenAI as 'reportedly developing' a Chromium-based browser - REJECTED: 'reportedly' language, no official announcement. (E) Multiple sources (Sept 21-30) mention OpenAI is 'planning' a browser - all describe it as a future/rumored product, not an official launch/announcement.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires: (1) official OpenAI channel publication, (2) product explicitly described as 'standalone web browser,' (3) announcement of development OR beta/waitlist opening OR public release. The TechCrunch article ([TechCrunch Sept 4](https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/04/openai-announces-ai-powered-hiring-platform-to-take-on-linkedin/)) reports Sam Altman mentioning a browser as one of several future Fidji Simo projects - but this is a secondary mention within a Jobs Platform announcement, not a dedicated standalone browser announcement. No evidence of an official OpenAI blog post, @OpenAI tweet, or @sama tweet specifically and dedicatedly announcing a standalone web browser. The Computerworld roundup mentions an 'announced AI-powered browser' but provides no source URL or date for that specific announcement, and it's a secondary source. Multiple articles consistently use 'reportedly developing' and 'planning' language, suggesting no official dedicated announcement occurred.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp found for a qualifying official OpenAI standalone browser announcement within the window. The Sept 4-5 Jobs Platform blog mentioned a browser incidentally. No dedicated browser announcement post/tweet with timestamp was identified.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Even if the Jobs Platform blog's incidental browser mention were considered qualifying (which it does not meet the 'explicitly described as standalone web browser' criterion), the Bleeping Computer report from August 16 (pre-window) shows earlier reporting. No qualifying first occurrence found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Multiple sources from late September 2025 (Opera launch Sept 30, Perplexity Comet articles Sept 21) still describe OpenAI's browser as 'reportedly developing' or 'reportedly planning' - indicating no official announcement had been made by that point. If OpenAI had officially announced its browser in early September, these later articles would likely reference that announcement rather than using 'reportedly' language. This strongly suggests no official standalone browser announcement occurred within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence does not support a Yes resolution. While Sam Altman mentioned a browser as a future project within the Jobs Platform announcement context, and while multiple secondary sources mention OpenAI 'reportedly' developing a browser, no official OpenAI channel published a dedicated announcement explicitly describing a standalone web browser, nor was any beta/waitlist opened during the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window. Late-September articles still using 'reportedly' language confirm no official announcement occurred. The window closed with no qualifying event. Resolution: No.

question: Will Iran close the Strait of Hormuz before 2027?
description:
If Iran halts or severely restricts international maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official governmental information, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will UKMTO or US NAVCENT report that Iranian forces have seized or detained at least one commercial vessel in or near the Strait of Hormuz between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06?
subquestions.background_information:
Following US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites, Iran's parliament approved a measure to close the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway that handles approximately 20% of global daily oil consumption. The final decision rests with Iran's Supreme National Security Council. Amid these escalating tensions, former Iranian officials have threatened to restrict traffic, and there are reports of increased Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) naval activity and GPS jamming in the region. Historically, Iran has used the harassment and seizure of commercial vessels as leverage and as a retaliatory measure. An actual seizure of an international commercial vessel by the IRGC or Iranian Navy during this period would serve as a strong leading indicator that Iran is actively escalating towards a de facto or formal closure of the strait.

Sources:
What if Iran tries to close the Strait of Hormuz? - https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/what-if-iran-tries-to-close-the-strait-of-hormuz
Iran approves closure of oil corridor, Strait of Hormuz, after US strikes: Report - https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/iran-approves-closure-of-oil-corridor-strait-of-hormuz-after-us-strikes-report-2556637-2025-06-22
Strait of Hormuz Disruption Fears Surge After Former Iranian Minister Threatens Transit Restrictions - https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/strait-hormuz-disruption-fears-surge-after-former-iranian-minister-threatens-transit
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 (inclusive), the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) or the US Naval Forces Central Command (NAVCENT) / US 5th Fleet officially reports that Iranian forces (such as the IRGC Navy or the Islamic Republic of Iran Navy) have seized, detained, or forcibly diverted at least one international commercial vessel (e.g., oil tanker, container ship, or bulk carrier) in the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf, or the Gulf of Oman.

The incident must occur and be officially reported within the specified time window (2025-11-06 to 2025-12-06).

Resolution will be based on official reports, warnings, or press releases from:
- UKMTO (https://www.ukmto.org/)
- US NAVCENT / 5th Fleet (https://www.cusnc.navy.mil/)

Edge cases:
- Temporary boardings where Iranian forces depart and the vessel is permitted to continue its voyage on the same day without being diverted to Iranian territorial waters for detention do not count.
- 'Commercial vessel' excludes military vessels, state-owned warships, or small local fishing dhows; it must be an internationally recognized cargo, tanker, or merchant vessel.
- If the event is reported by credible news outlets but not confirmed by UKMTO or NAVCENT by the end of the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A vessel seizure by Iranian forces is a distinct, observable tactical event that demonstrates Iran's willingness to use physical force to disrupt maritime traffic. If Iran begins seizing vessels, major shipping and oil companies will likely halt transits, effectively leading to a closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Therefore, this serves as a highly informative, early proxy for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: Between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 (inclusive), UKMTO or US NAVCENT/5th Fleet must officially report that Iranian forces (IRGC Navy or Islamic Republic of Iran Navy) seized, detained, or forcibly diverted at least one international commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, Persian Gulf, or Gulf of Oman. The vessel must be an internationally recognized cargo, tanker, or merchant ship. Observable evidence: official UKMTO advisory/warning or NAVCENT/CENTCOM press release confirming Iranian seizure of a commercial vessel.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Iran IRGC seize detain commercial vessel Strait of Hormuz 2025' — to find any qualifying seizure events. Query 2: 'UKMTO NAVCENT Iran ship seizure Persian Gulf November December 2025' — to find official reports from required sources. Query 3: 'UKMTO official report Talara tanker seizure November 14 2025' — to confirm UKMTO reporting. Query 4: 'NAVCENT CENTCOM 5th Fleet Talara tanker Iran seizure November 2025 statement' — to confirm NAVCENT/CENTCOM official reporting.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event identified: Seizure of the Marshall Islands-flagged oil tanker M/V Talara by Iran's IRGC on November 14, 2025, in the Strait of Hormuz / Gulf of Oman area (~20 nautical miles east of Khor Fakkan, UAE). The vessel was en route from UAE to Singapore carrying high-sulphur gasoil. IRGC forces approached via small boats and later by helicopter, boarded the vessel, and diverted it to Bandar Abbas, Iran. The vessel was detained for approximately 5 days before being released on November 20, 2025. A second seizure of an Eswatini-flagged vessel occurred on November 30, 2025 in the Persian Gulf, but this was apparently a smaller vessel in Iranian territorial waters involved in fuel smuggling. No events are rejected — the Talara seizure clearly qualifies.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The M/V Talara seizure fully satisfies all criteria: (1) UKMTO confirmed 'state activity' and reported the vessel being steered into Iranian waters [AFP, Nov 14](http://doc.afp.com/843E3T4); (2) US NAVCENT/5th Fleet confirmed it was 'actively monitoring' the situation and stated 'Commercial vessels are entitled to largely unimpeded rights of navigation and commerce on the high seas' [Newsweek, Nov 15](https://www.newsweek.com/us-navy-monitoring-tanker-seizure-iran-revolutionary-guard-11054225); (3) US CENTCOM formally stated Iran's seizure was a 'blatant violation of international law' [USNI News, Nov 17](https://news.usni.org/2025/11/17/iran-strait-of-hormuz-tanker-seizure-violates-international-law-centcom-says); (4) The vessel is an internationally registered oil tanker (Marshall Islands-flagged), not a military vessel or fishing dhow; (5) The vessel was diverted to Iranian territorial waters (Bandar Abbas) and detained for 5 days — not a temporary boarding same-day; (6) The seizure occurred on November 14, 2025, within the resolution window (Nov 6 – Dec 6, 2025); (7) The IRGC (a qualifying Iranian force) conducted the seizure.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The seizure occurred on November 14, 2025. The vessel lost contact at approximately 08:22 local time (04:22 UTC) on November 14, 2025. UKMTO reported the incident on November 14, 2025. CENTCOM/NAVCENT issued formal statements between November 15-17, 2025 — all within the resolution window. Exact timestamp: 2025-11-14T04:22:00Z (vessel lost contact / seizure commenced).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is the first qualifying event in the window. Multiple sources confirm this was the first Iranian vessel seizure since April 2024 (MSC Aries). No earlier qualifying event exists within the 2025-11-06 to 2025-12-06 window — the November 13 incident mentioned in one article was a border guard seizing a small vessel carrying ~3,000 liters of diesel (likely a small local vessel/dhow, not an internationally recognized commercial vessel, and captured in Iranian territorial waters by border guards not IRGC Navy). The Talara seizure on November 14 is unambiguously the first qualifying occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) IRGC claimed the seizure was a domestic judicial/legal action, but CENTCOM explicitly stated it violated international law — this does not undermine resolution, as the question only requires official reporting of Iranian forces seizing/detaining a commercial vessel; (2) The vessel was released on November 20, 2025, but detention had already occurred for 5 days — this confirms it was NOT a same-day boarding, which is the relevant edge case; (3) The Eswatini-flagged vessel seized November 30 appears to be a smaller vessel carrying smuggled diesel in Iranian territorial waters, likely not qualifying as an 'internationally recognized cargo, tanker, or merchant vessel' and not reported by UKMTO/NAVCENT — but this is moot since the Talara already resolves the question; (4) Multiple independent, high-quality sources (AP, AFP, USNI News, Al Jazeera) corroborate both the event and the UKMTO/CENTCOM official responses.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves Yes. On November 14, 2025, Iran's IRGC seized the Marshall Islands-flagged oil tanker M/V Talara in the Strait of Hormuz/Gulf of Oman area. UKMTO confirmed 'state activity' and the vessel being diverted into Iranian waters on November 14, 2025. US Naval Forces Central Command (5th Fleet/CENTCOM) confirmed monitoring and officially declared the seizure a 'blatant violation of international law' — constituting an official report by NAVCENT. The event occurred on November 14, 2025, squarely within the November 6 – December 6, 2025 window. The vessel was detained for 5 days (not a same-day boarding). All resolution criteria are met.

question: Will Wicked: For Good be the top grossing movie of 2025?

subquestions.question: Will any film record a domestic gross of $500 million or more on the Box Office Mojo 2025 calendar grosses chart by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The ultimate question asks whether 'Wicked: For Good', scheduled for release on November 21, 2025, will be the highest-grossing domestic film of 2025. The original 'Wicked' film grossed roughly $756 million worldwide and was pushing toward the $500 million milestone at the domestic box office. For 'Wicked: For Good' to become the top-grossing film of 2025, it will have to out-earn every other movie released during the year. Knowing whether any 2025 release has already crossed the $500 million mark domestically by the beginning of October serves as a critical indicator, as it sets the concrete baseline that 'Wicked: For Good' must surpass. Tracking the top gross of the year leading into Q4 provides an observable hurdle. Sources: [1] Comicbook: Prime Video Just Added One of the Biggest Movies of 2024 (https://comicbook.com), [2] Pinkvilla: Box Office: Wicked returns to theaters for one night (https://www.pinkvilla.com), [3] Box Office Mojo 2025 Calendar Grosses (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the 'Gross' column for any film on the Box Office Mojo 2025 Calendar Grosses page (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses) shows a value of $500,000,000 or greater. The resolution will be based on data available on the page at any time during this window. If no film reaches or exceeds a gross of $500,000,000 within this timeframe, the question resolves No. If the site alters its formatting, the equivalent domestic cumulative gross metric for the calendar year 2025 will be used.
subquestions.rationale: If an existing 2025 release has already accumulated $500 million at the domestic box office by October 1, 2025, it establishes a substantial financial hurdle that 'Wicked: For Good' must overcome. Given that the first 'Wicked' film maxed out near $500 million domestically, a requirement for the sequel to significantly exceed this figure just to rank first would decrease the likelihood of the ultimate question resolving Yes.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Any film on Box Office Mojo's 2025 Calendar Grosses page must show a domestic gross ≥ $500,000,000 at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Observable evidence: explicit reporting of any 2025 film reaching $500M+ domestic gross during this window. Key threshold: $500,000,000 domestic (US/Canada) gross.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Box Office Mojo 2025 highest grossing films domestic $500 million' (Aug-Oct 2025) - to find any film hitting threshold. 2. '2025 box office record $500 million domestic gross film' (Aug-Oct 2025) - similar. 3. 'Minecraft Movie Lilo Stitch domestic box office September 2025 total gross' - to check top films' totals. 4. 'Demon Slayer Infinity Castle domestic box office 2025 $500 million' - to check September release. 5. 'box office Mojo 2025 top domestic grossing films list September October' - for comprehensive list. 6. evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate films: (1) A Minecraft Movie - ~$423.9M domestic as of Sept 17 [Businessday NG, Sept 20]. (2) Lilo & Stitch - ~$423.7M domestic as of Sept 17 [Businessday NG, Sept 20]. (3) Superman - ~$353.9M domestic. (4) Jurassic World Rebirth - ~$339.4M domestic. (5) Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle - $104.7M domestic as of its second weekend (Sept 22) [ComingSoon.net, Sept 22]. No candidate reached $500M domestic. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No film explicitly reached $500M domestic gross during the window per: [Businessday NG Sept 20](https://businessday.ng/life-arts/article/2025-hollywood-box-office-leaders-reflect-franchise-dominance/) shows top domestic = $423.9M; [TheWrap Sept 1](https://www.thewrap.com/summer-box-office-2025-flat/) notes 'Lilo & Stitch [is] the only film that crossed $400 million domestically'; [ScreenRant Aug 20](https://screenrant.com/lilo-and-stitch-box-office-not-beat-minecraft-domestic/) shows Lilo at $421.7M and Minecraft at $423.9M as of late August. Demon Slayer was only $104.7M domestic by Sept 22 [ComingSoon.net](https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/2030385-demon-slayer-infinity-castle-box-office-beat-fantastic-four-superman). No article within the window reports any domestic $500M milestone for any film.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The condition for Yes was never met — no $500M domestic threshold was crossed. evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence found — the $500M domestic threshold was never reached by any film during the Sept 1–Oct 1 window. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Multiple consistent, explicit sources from within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window confirm that no film reached $500M domestic gross on Box Office Mojo's 2025 calendar. The top domestic grossers were A Minecraft Movie and Lilo & Stitch, both plateauing at approximately $424M domestically. No film crossed the $500M domestic threshold during this period. The condition became definitively unfulfillable by the window's close given the films' declining theater runs with no new release approaching the threshold. The window closed on October 1, 2025 with no qualifying event.

question: Israel and Saudi Arabia normalize relations in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Israel and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia officially announce the establishment of diplomatic relations between Janaury 26, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israel and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will an official, publicly acknowledged in-person meeting take place between a cabinet-level or higher official from Israel and a cabinet-level or higher official from Saudi Arabia before October 2, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Saudi Arabia has officially maintained that normalization of relations with Israel is contingent on an end to the war in Gaza and the establishment of a Palestinian state. Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan has publicly stressed that without meaningful progress on a two-state solution, normalization talks cannot proceed. Concurrently, U.S. diplomatic efforts have pushed heavily for an expansion of the Abraham Accords. The UN General Assembly, held every September in New York, traditionally provides a prime venue for high-level diplomatic engagements and backchannel meetings. If Israel and Saudi Arabia are genuinely on track to officially normalize relations by the end of 2025, observable high-level diplomatic steps—such as direct meetings between foreign ministers or state leaders—are highly likely to occur in the preceding months. 

Sources:
Saudi Press Agency: https://www.spa.gov.sa/en
U.S. Department of State - Abraham Accords: https://www.state.gov/the-abraham-accords/
Reuters Middle East: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), a publicly acknowledged in-person meeting takes place between at least one cabinet-level official, head of government, or head of state representing Israel and a counterpart or cabinet-level/higher official representing Saudi Arabia.

- "Cabinet-level or higher" includes roles such as Prime Minister, Crown Prince, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Minister of Defense, etc.
- The meeting must be explicitly scheduled or acknowledged as a bilateral or trilateral (e.g., brokered by the U.S.) meeting. 
- Passing encounters, unacknowledged brief handshakes, or simply being in the same room at a multilateral summit without a dedicated sit-down meeting do not count.
- The occurrence of the meeting must be confirmed by official government sources from Israel (https://www.gov.il/en), Saudi Arabia (https://www.spa.gov.sa/en), or the United States (https://www.state.gov), or by a consensus of credible reporting from major news agencies such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/) or the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/hub/middle-east).
- If a meeting is scheduled but postponed beyond the resolution window, it does not count.
- If no qualifying meeting is confirmed to have occurred during the resolution window of 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01, the question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: For normalization to be formalized in 2025, preliminary high-level meetings are necessary to hammer out complex conditions, such as U.S. security guarantees, Palestinian concessions, and civil nuclear agreements. The September UN General Assembly window is a crucial indicator. If high-ranking officials from both nations are willing to be seen meeting publicly by October 1, it demonstrates substantial momentum toward a deal, strongly updating the ultimate question toward 'Yes'. A lack of such meetings would indicate negotiations remain stalled over red-line issues, significantly dragging down the likelihood of a 2025 normalization.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: An in-person meeting between at least one Israeli cabinet-level official (PM, FM, Defense Minister, etc.) and at least one Saudi cabinet-level official (Crown Prince, FM, Defense Minister, etc.) that is publicly acknowledged as bilateral or trilateral. Must occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Must be confirmed by official government sources or major news agencies.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Israel Saudi Arabia meeting cabinet official September 2025' - to find any bilateral meetings. Query 2: 'Israel Saudi Arabia normalization talks bilateral meeting 2025' - to find normalization-related meetings. Query 3: 'Israel Saudi Arabia foreign minister meeting bilateral September October 2025' - specifically targeting foreign minister contacts. Query 4: 'Netanyahu Saudi Arabia crown prince MBS meeting September 2025' - for head-of-government meetings. Query 5: 'Israel Saudi Arabia direct contact meeting UNGA September 2025' - for UNGA-margin meetings. Query 6: 'Netanyahu Trump Saudi Arabia normalization deal meeting September 2025' - for US-brokered trilateral meetings. Query 7: 'Israel minister Saudi Arabia normalization meeting handshake encounter 2025' - to find any lower-level encounters. Query 8: 'Netanyahu Faisal bin Farhan Saudi Arabia bilateral meeting' - specific officials.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No direct Israel-Saudi bilateral meetings were found in any search results. Candidate events examined and rejected: (1) Trump's multilateral meeting with Muslim leaders (Sept 23-24) explicitly excluded Israel ('all the big players except Israel'). (2) Saudi FM Prince Faisal's UNGA meetings included Egypt, India, France, Luxembourg, UN SG - but no Israel. (3) The France-Saudi two-state solution summit (Sept 22) was explicitly boycotted by Israel. (4) Trump-Netanyahu meeting (Sept 29-30) was bilateral US-Israel, with Saudi Arabia expressing support for the US plan indirectly. (5) Emergency Arab-Islamic Summit (Sept 15) was an anti-Israel gathering without any Israeli participation.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found matching the criteria. Multiple sources confirm: Saudi-Israeli normalization remains 'frozen' ([Middle East Monitor](https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20250903-the-stalemate-behind-the-smiles-why-saudi-israeli-normalisation-remains-a-mirage/)), relations were severely strained by Israel's Sept 9 strike on Hamas leaders in Doha ([AP News](https://apnews.com/article/israel-hamas-war-qatar-strike-uae-saudi-politics-e72213f436ce2021ff284c586de75e42)), Saudi Arabia repeatedly condemned Israel throughout the month, and Saudi FM held no meetings with Israeli counterparts at UNGA ([Arab News](https://www.arabnews.com/node/2616790/saudi-arabia)). All Israeli-Saudi contacts appear to have been through indirect channels (Saudi messages to Israel via US, Saudi warnings to Israel via media).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found; no timestamp to extract.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event was found.
evidence.step7_verification: Extensive searches across multiple angles (bilateral meetings, UNGA encounters, Trump-brokered talks, normalization discussions) all returned no evidence of a direct Israel-Saudi official meeting. Multiple sources explicitly state normalization talks are frozen and that Saudi Arabia and Israel are in a state of deep hostility during September 2025. The context of the period (Israel striking Hamas in Qatar on Sept 9, Saudi Arabia condemning Israel repeatedly, Saudi Arabia boycotting pro-Israel summits) strongly corroborates the absence of any bilateral meeting. No contradictory evidence suggesting a meeting occurred was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. During the entire resolution window of September 1-October 1, 2025, Saudi-Israeli relations were at an extreme low following Israel's strike on Hamas leaders in Doha on September 9, 2025. Saudi Arabia repeatedly condemned Israel, called for accountability, warned Israel on red lines, and actively worked to counter Israeli policies at UNGA. The Saudi FM held numerous UNGA meetings but none with Israeli officials. No bilateral, trilateral, or any acknowledged meeting between Israeli and Saudi cabinet-level officials took place during this period. The window closed on October 1, 2025 without a qualifying event.
