subquestions.question: Will an official Israeli delegation travel to Doha, Qatar, or Cairo, Egypt, for ceasefire or hostage negotiations between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 18, 2025, Hamas reportedly approved a 60-day temporary ceasefire proposal mediated by Egypt and Qatar, based on a framework previously presented by US mediators (https://egyptianstreets.com). However, as of late August, Israel had not formally responded to this acceptance. Instead, reports indicated that Israel's security cabinet was convening on August 31 to review plans for a major military offensive to seize control of Gaza City, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu deliberately keeping the ceasefire deal off the formal agenda (https://abc17news.com). Furthermore, Israeli officials stated that Israel and the US have shifted toward backing a comprehensive plan to end the war, moving away from partial or temporary deals (https://www.timesofisrael.com). Sending a high-level delegation to Cairo or Doha would signify that Israel is returning to active, mediated negotiations and strongly exploring the proposed frameworks. If Israel continues to boycott such talks to focus on the Gaza City offensive, the prospects of an overarching ceasefire agreement before 2026 will diminish significantly.

Sources:
Egyptian Streets - https://egyptianstreets.com
ABC17NEWS - https://abc17news.com
The Times of Israel - https://www.timesofisrael.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if credible media reporting (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, Axios, The Times of Israel) or official government statements confirm that an official Israeli delegation traveled to Doha, Qatar, or Cairo, Egypt, to engage in Gaza ceasefire or hostage release negotiations between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

An 'official Israeli delegation' is defined as a group of authorized government representatives, which must include high-level officials such as the Director of Mossad, the Director of Shin Bet, or formal envoys explicitly appointed by the Prime Minister's Office or the Ministry of Defense for this purpose.

The physical presence of the delegation in Doha or Cairo for the purpose of negotiations must occur at least partially between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Virtual meetings or phone calls do not count toward resolution; physical travel to either city is strictly required. If a delegation travels but the visit is exclusively unrelated to the Gaza conflict (e.g., routine bilateral economic or security discussions), it will not qualify.

If no such travel is reported to have occurred within the specified window by 2025-10-01 at 23:59 UTC, the question resolves 'No'. Resolvers will primarily consult international news wires such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) and AP News (https://apnews.com) for definitive reports.
subquestions.rationale: Direct, in-person participation by an Israeli delegation in regional talks is a necessary leading indicator of an eventual official ceasefire agreement. Given the reported reluctance of Israel's Prime Minister to prioritize negotiations over a looming Gaza City offensive, the dispatch of a delegation would show renewed commitment to a negotiated track. Conversely, the failure to send a delegation within this critical one-month window would suggest an extended phase of military escalation, substantially reducing the likelihood of a formal ceasefire agreement.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: An official Israeli delegation (including high-level officials such as the Director of Mossad, Shin Bet, or formally appointed envoys) must physically travel to Doha, Qatar, or Cairo, Egypt, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 for the purpose of Gaza ceasefire or hostage release negotiations. Virtual meetings/phone calls do not count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Israeli delegation Doha Qatar ceasefire hostage negotiations September 2025' - to find any official visits; 2) 'Israeli delegation Cairo Egypt Gaza negotiations September 2025' - to find Cairo visits; 3) 'Israeli hostage negotiation team travel Doha Qatar September October 2025' - to find specific travel; 4) 'Mossad Shin Bet director Gaza ceasefire talks Doha Cairo September 2025' - for senior official travel; 5) 'Israel ceasefire talks resumed Doha Cairo September 2025 apology Qatar' - to check if talks resumed after apology; 6) 'Steve Witkoff Israeli officials Cairo Egypt negotiations September 2025' - to check for Witkoff or Israeli officials in Cairo.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Israel's September 9 airstrike on Hamas in Doha ('Operation Summit of Fire') - REJECTED: this was a military strike, not a negotiation delegation visit; (2) Phone calls between Netanyahu and Qatari officials (Sept 29-30) - REJECTED: phone calls explicitly excluded from resolution criteria; (3) Qatari delegation in Washington (Sept 29-30) - REJECTED: this was Qatari officials visiting Washington, not Israeli delegation in Doha/Cairo; (4) September 30 Times of Israel report that Israeli hostage team was 'awaiting PM's go-ahead' and 'may be sent to Qatar in coming days' - REJECTED: this confirms no travel had occurred yet as of Sept 30; (5) Egyptian/Turkish intelligence chiefs in Doha on Sept 30 - REJECTED: these were not Israeli officials.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No confirmed evidence found of an official Israeli delegation physically traveling to Doha, Qatar or Cairo, Egypt for Gaza ceasefire or hostage release negotiations between September 1-October 1, 2025. The [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/israeli-hostage-team-said-awaiting-pms-go-ahead-for-resumed-talks-may-be-sent-to-qatar/) on September 30 explicitly states the Israeli hostage team was still awaiting Netanyahu's authorization and 'may be sent to Qatar in the coming days' - this is forward-looking and confirms no travel had occurred yet. Qatar withdrew from mediation after the September 9 strike and only accepted Israel's apology on September 29-30, with talk of resumed negotiations still pending as of October 1.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. The September 30 Times of Israel article is the closest — and it explicitly indicates travel had NOT yet occurred (team 'awaiting PM's go-ahead' and 'may be sent to Qatar in coming days').
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: N/A — No qualifying occurrence was found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: RT.com (Sept 30) stated the September 9 Doha strike targeted 'Hamas officials attending negotiations with an Israeli delegation' — however, this refers to pre-September 1 negotiations (the Hamas delegation was in Doha, not an Israeli one; Israel struck from afar via aircraft). No source confirms physical Israeli delegation travel to Doha or Cairo during the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window: (1) The September 9 Israeli airstrike on Doha was a military operation, not a diplomatic delegation visit; (2) Qatar suspended mediation from ~Sept 9 to ~Sept 29; (3) Netanyahu's apology was delivered via phone call (not physical travel); (4) As of September 30, the Israeli hostage negotiating team was still awaiting authorization and had not yet traveled to Qatar. No credible reporting confirms a physical Israeli negotiating delegation traveling to Doha or Cairo in the specified window.

question: Will the U.S. invade Venezuela by December 31, 2025?

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. military conduct a kinetic strike on the sovereign land territory of Venezuela between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06?
subquestions.background_information:
As of early October 2025, tensions between the United States and Venezuela have sharply escalated. The U.S. administration declared a 'non-international armed conflict' targeting Latin American drug cartels and conducted lethal strikes on suspected narcotrafficking boats in the Caribbean Sea. According to reports, the Pentagon has deployed significant military forces near Venezuela, including F-35 jets and the 22nd Marine Expeditionary Unit, and has even drafted plans that include seizing ports and airfields (https://www.the-sun.com/). In response, Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro declared a nationwide 'state of external emergency,' putting the armed forces on a wartime footing and repositioning air defense systems to protect infrastructure (https://www.defenseworld.net/). The U.S. strikes so far have been restricted to maritime targets (https://tass.com/). Expanding military operations from international or territorial waters to direct kinetic strikes on Venezuelan land territory would indicate a profound escalation in the conflict.

Sources:
Defense World: https://www.defenseworld.net/
The US Sun: https://www.the-sun.com/
TASS: https://tass.com/
AP News: https://apnews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Defense (https://www.defense.gov/) officially confirms, or if there is a consensus of credible independent reporting from major news agencies such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) and the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), that the United States military intentionally conducted a kinetic attack (such as an airstrike, missile strike, artillery fire, or naval bombardment) that physically impacted the sovereign land territory of Venezuela between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06 (inclusive).

The strike must hit a target on land (e.g., a port facility, airfield, military base, or land vehicle). Strikes exclusively targeting maritime vessels at sea, even if within Venezuelan territorial waters, do not qualify for a Yes resolution unless the strike also damages land-based infrastructure. Cyberattacks, electronic warfare, or intercepted projectiles that do not impact the land territory do not count. The action must be intentional and not an accidental misfire. If no such event occurs and is confirmed to have occurred during the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A kinetic strike on Venezuelan land would represent a major escalation from the ongoing maritime counter-narcotics operations. Because the ultimate question asks whether the U.S. will invade to establish control over parts of Venezuela, an invasion would almost certainly be preceded by or begin with strikes on land-based air defenses, ports, and military installations. If the U.S. shows the willingness to strike Venezuelan soil in this timeframe, the probability of a broader invasion before December 31, 2025, increases dramatically.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: U.S. DoD officially confirms, or major news agencies reach consensus, that the U.S. military intentionally conducted a kinetic attack (airstrike, missile strike, artillery, or naval bombardment) that physically impacted the sovereign land territory of Venezuela between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06 inclusive. Maritime strikes at sea do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US military strike Venezuela 2025' (Oct 7–Nov 6) — to find general strike news; 2) 'United States airstrike attack Venezuela land territory' (Oct 7–Nov 6) — to find land-specific strikes; 3) 'US military strike Venezuela land territory confirmed November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 6) — to find late-window events; 4) 'Venezuela airstrike bombing attack November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 6) — to find any attacks in final window; 5) 'Pentagon DoD confirms attack Venezuela airport port facility infrastructure' (Oct 7–Nov 6) — to find confirmed land infrastructure hits.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple confirmed strikes found: Oct 15 (boat, international waters), Oct 16 (semi-submersible, international waters), Oct 19 (boat, international waters), Oct 21 (boat, Eastern Pacific), Oct 24 (boat, international waters), Nov 2 (boat, Caribbean). ALL were against maritime vessels in international waters, NOT on Venezuelan land territory. Reports of considering land strikes (WSJ, Miami Herald, Oct 31) were prospective/planning discussions. Trump denied on Oct 31 he was 'considering strikes in Venezuela.' Senate vote on Nov 6 was about LIMITING future strikes, indicating none had yet occurred on land.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event matches the resolution criteria. All confirmed U.S. strikes during the window targeted vessels at sea in international waters. The resolution criteria explicitly exclude 'strikes exclusively targeting maritime vessels at sea, even if within Venezuelan territorial waters.' There is no report from DoD, Reuters, or AP confirming a kinetic strike physically impacting Venezuelan sovereign land territory. Reports from [The Independent](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-us-strikes-venezuela-maduro-b2856358.html) (Oct 31), [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5585967-trump-maduro-days-numbered/) (Nov 3), [Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/11/04/world/trump-weighs-options-risks-attacks-venezuela/) (Nov 5), and [BNO News](https://bnonews.com/index.php/2025/11/senate-rejects-measure-to-limit-trumps-military-actions-against-venezuela/) (Nov 6 Senate vote) all indicate land strikes were being planned/debated but not executed.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a qualifying event can be extracted because no qualifying event (kinetic strike on Venezuelan land territory) occurred within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found within the window. All U.S. strikes were against maritime targets in international waters.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: Trump denied considering land strikes on Oct 31 aboard Air Force One. The Senate vote on Nov 6 to limit Trump's authority to expand military operations to Venezuelan territory was rejected 49-51, but this vote itself confirms that strikes inside Venezuela had not yet occurred (they were trying to prevent future ones). Venezuela's Nov 5 claim of 'foiling' a CIA false-flag attack, if anything, refers to alleged covert operations, not confirmed kinetic strikes. GPS jamming near Venezuela (reported Nov 5) is explicitly excluded by resolution criteria as electronic warfare. All evidence consistently shows strikes remained at sea throughout the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No U.S. kinetic strike impacted Venezuelan sovereign land territory during the resolution window (Oct 7–Nov 6, 2025). All confirmed strikes were against maritime vessels in international waters. The window closed on Nov 6, 2025 with no qualifying land strike having occurred.

question: Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”  if, Ukraine signs any written instrument (e.g., treaty, ceasefire/armistice, framework/“roadmap,” exchange of letters, or mediated agreement text) that: (i) includes both Ukraine and the Russian Federation as parties, and (ii) either ends hostilities/establishes a ceasefire or commits both sides to a defined process toward ending the war (i.e., stated objective of peace/normalization plus principles, steps, and/or a timetable) by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

Only Ukraine’s signature is required; Russia’s signature or ratification is not.

Localized, temporary, or issue-specific arrangements—such as airstrike-limitation or deconfliction protocols, humanitarian pauses, evacuation corridors, prisoner-exchange or trade/export arrangements, border/DMZ adjustments, or ceasefires limited to a particular sector/front/municipality—will not qualify.

The document must bear a wet-ink or officially issued electronic signature of an authorized Ukrainian representative. Unsigned agreements (e.g., the 2023 Ohrid arrangement) will not qualify regardless of if they are otherwise officially enacted. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a direct call or meeting between the President of Ukraine and the President of Russia take place or be officially announced between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent diplomatic momentum has increased following a US-Russia summit in Alaska involving US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, where the war in Ukraine was a central topic. According to reports from August 2025, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated that President Putin is 'ready to meet' with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, provided that high-level issues are prepared in advance and concerns regarding Zelensky's legal legitimacy (following the expiration of his presidential term in May 2024) are addressed. Additionally, US President Trump has indicated his intention to arrange a meeting between Putin and Zelensky, potentially culminating in a trilateral summit or three-way call involving Washington. Given that the ultimate question asks whether Ukraine and Russia will sign a binding peace deal by the end of 2025, a direct discussion between the two state leaders—either held or officially scheduled during October 2025—would serve as a highly informative leading indicator. If October passes without any direct communication or concrete plans for a summit, the timeline to negotiate, draft, and sign a complex peace agreement before December 31, 2025, becomes exceptionally tight.

Sources:
Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/
WION News: https://www.wionews.com/world/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), a direct communication (either a phone call, video conference, or in-person meeting) involving both the President of Ukraine (currently Volodymyr Zelensky) and the President of Russia (currently Vladimir Putin) takes place, OR if an official announcement is made that such a meeting or call has been firmly scheduled.

- The interaction must involve both heads of state. It can be a bilateral discussion or include other leaders (such as a trilateral format with US President Donald Trump).
- If either leader is replaced as the internationally recognized head of state of their respective country before or during the resolution window, this criteria will apply to their official, recognized successor.
- For a 'scheduled' event to trigger a 'Yes' resolution, an official statement must be released by the Office of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en), the Kremlin (http://en.kremlin.ru/), or the US White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) confirming that a specific date has been agreed upon for the leaders to speak or meet. If one government announces a meeting but another officially and explicitly denies that an agreement to meet was reached, it will not count until confirmed or acknowledged by the counterparties.
- If the meeting or call takes place within the resolution window without prior announcement, it must be confirmed by official government sources or a consensus of credible reporting from major international news agencies (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com, AP: https://apnews.com, or Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com).
- Proposals, suggestions, or rumors reported by anonymous sources without official confirmation from the respective governments do not qualify.
- The event must take place or the announcement must be issued strictly within the resolution window. Events or announcements occurring before 2025-10-01 or after 2025-10-31 will not count toward a 'Yes' resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A peace deal between Ukraine and Russia by the end of 2025 would almost certainly require direct, high-level negotiations between the two nations' top leaders to resolve fundamental differences (e.g., territorial boundaries, security guarantees, sanctions). The occurrence or scheduling of a direct call or meeting in October 2025 acts as a necessary procedural milestone. If no such event is held or announced by October 31, 2025, the remaining two months of the year would likely be insufficient to bridge the substantial gaps in their negotiating positions, making the ultimate outcome highly unlikely.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) A direct communication (phone call, video conference, or in-person meeting) between Zelensky AND Putin taking place between Oct 1–31, 2025; OR (2) An official announcement from the Kremlin, Office of the President of Ukraine, or US White House confirming a specific date for such a communication. The interaction can be bilateral or trilateral (e.g., with Trump). Proposals, rumors, or unconfirmed reports do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'Zelensky Putin direct call meeting October 2025' — to find any direct interaction; (2) 'Ukraine Russia leaders phone call contact October 2025' — broader search for any leader contact; (3) 'Zelensky Putin direct meeting bilateral talk October 2025' — to find bilateral meetings; (4) 'Trump Budapest summit Zelensky Putin trilateral meeting October 2025' — to check if a trilateral meeting was confirmed; (5) 'Zelensky Putin phone call direct contact bilateral late October 2025' — to find late-October interactions; (6) 'Ukraine Russia peace summit trilateral meeting confirmed announced October 2025' — to verify confirmed announcements; (7) 'Trump Putin Zelensky trilateral summit meeting end October 2025' — to find trilateral meeting details; (8) 'Zelensky Putin phone call direct bilateral October 28-31 2025' — final window check.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Trump-Putin phone call on October 16, 2025 — does NOT qualify as Zelensky was not part of this call; (2) Trump-Zelensky meeting at White House on October 17, 2025 — does NOT qualify as Putin was not present; (3) Proposed Budapest summit (Trump + Putin, possibly Zelensky) — this was discussed but never confirmed or scheduled with a specific date; (4) Trump-Putin phone call on October 28 per one article — does NOT include Zelensky; (5) Multiple mentions of Zelensky being willing to join Budapest summit 'if invited' — but no confirmed, officially-announced meeting with specific date. All trilateral meetings remained speculative or were explicitly cancelled/postponed. No Zelensky-Putin direct interaction found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of any direct communication between Zelensky and Putin during the October 1–31, 2025 window. Multiple sources confirm: [Trump won't 'waste his time' with Putin per The Times of India, Oct 26](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/not-wasting-time-trump-says-no-meeting-with-putin-until-deal-on-ukraine-admits-hes-disappointed/articleshow/124821520.cms); [Budapest summit cancelled per USA Confirms Cancellation](https://tfiglobalnews.com/2025/10/21/usa-confirms-cancellation-of-second-trump-putin-summit-in-hungary-amid-stalled-ukraine-peace-efforts/); [No trilateral summit confirmed per Medium.com, Oct 22](https://medium.com/@rajk100/peace-talks-collapse-new-proposal-to-end-russias-war-2a7580a05951) — 'As of October 22, 2025, no formal tripartite meeting has been confirmed'; [Zelensky says 'Putin doesn't want peace' per Hindustan Times, Oct 17](https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/zelensky-says-ukraine-ready-to-negotiate-in-any-format-during-meeting-with-trump-we-want-peace-putin-doesnt-101760730802210.html). Trump explicitly noted 'bad blood' between Zelensky and Putin and planned separate meetings. All contacts were either Zelensky-Trump or Trump-Putin, never Zelensky-Putin.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found — no timestamp for a Zelensky-Putin direct communication can be established because no such communication took place.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Irrelevant as no qualifying event was found during the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checking confirms: Throughout October 2025, the diplomatic pattern was clear — Trump spoke separately with Putin (Oct 16 call, ~2.5 hours) and separately with Zelensky (Oct 17 meeting), explicitly acknowledging 'bad blood' between the two. The proposed Budapest trilateral/bilateral summit was postponed indefinitely by Oct 21-22. Putin's envoy Dmitriev met US envoy Witkoff in Florida (Oct 25-26) — neither Zelensky nor Putin were directly involved. No source (Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, Kremlin, Ukrainian presidency, White House) reported a Zelensky-Putin call or meeting in October 2025. Multiple sources note Putin has 'not shown interest in direct talks' with Zelensky. The window closed on Oct 31 with no such event occurring.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. Throughout October 2025, there was no direct communication between Zelensky and Putin — neither a phone call, video conference, nor in-person meeting. There was also no official announcement from Kremlin, Ukrainian presidency, or White House confirming a specific date for such a meeting. The planned Budapest summit (which might have been trilateral) was postponed indefinitely by October 21-22, 2025, and Trump explicitly ruled out a trilateral format citing 'bad blood.' The window closed October 31, 2025 with no qualifying event.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995, “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia, which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement, is an example of a qualifying agreement.

An official unilateral pledge by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution even if not part of an agreement with Russia.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the Ukrainian government officially announce a nationwide referendum regarding the status of its territories or peace terms with Russia between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Ukrainian lawmakers have vehemently rejected formal territorial concessions, emphasizing that such actions violate the Ukrainian Constitution. Lawmakers have explicitly stated that altering Ukraine's territorial makeup requires a nationwide referendum (https://www.yahoo.com/news/shocked-us-peace-proposal-ukrainians-000000000.html). Furthermore, officials warned that any peace agreement recognizing Russian control would risk unrest, making a referendum politically necessary to secure a mandate for such a drastic constitutional change (https://kyivindependent.com/dangerous-and-cruel-trumps-reported-crimea-proposal-sparks-horror-among-ukraines-lawmakers/). Because a referendum is a legal and political prerequisite to changing Ukraine's borders or formally conceding territory, whether the Ukrainian government initiates one is a critical indicator of their willingness to agree to a peace deal involving territorial concessions to Russia.

Yahoo News: https://www.yahoo.com/news/shocked-us-peace-proposal-ukrainians-000000000.html
Kyiv Independent: https://kyivindependent.com/dangerous-and-cruel-trumps-reported-crimea-proposal-sparks-horror-among-ukraines-lawmakers/

The announcement must be an official statement, published decree, or passed parliamentary resolution representing the government's formal stance. Unofficial comments, proposals by individual politicians, or unconfirmed rumors do not qualify.

If no such official announcement is made between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z, the question resolves to 'No'. If the announcement is delayed beyond this resolution window, the question resolves to 'No'.

Sources to be used for resolution include the official website of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en) and the official portal of the Verkhovna Rada (https://www.rada.gov.ua/en), supplemented by credible international reporting such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) and the Kyiv Independent (https://kyivindependent.com).
subquestions.rationale: For Ukraine to formally recognize Russian sovereignty over any of its UN-recognized territory, it would likely need to bypass or amend constitutional prohibitions against territorial concessions. Ukrainian officials have explicitly stated that altering the country's territorial makeup requires a nationwide referendum. Therefore, an official announcement of a referendum in September 2025 would be a highly informative early indicator that Ukraine is preparing the legal and political groundwork to formally recognize Russian sovereignty by the end of 2025. Conversely, if no referendum is announced, the likelihood of the ultimate question resolving 'Yes' decreases significantly, given the time needed to organize such a vote and change the legal framework.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) an official announcement from the President of Ukraine, Verkhovna Rada, or Cabinet of Ministers; (2) the announcement must be about scheduling or intending to hold a nationwide referendum on Ukrainian territory status, territorial concessions, or peace terms with Russia; (3) it must be a formal official statement, decree, or parliamentary resolution; (4) it must occur between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025. Unofficial comments by individual politicians or unconfirmed rumors do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Ukraine referendum territories peace Russia official announcement 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 1) — to find any official announcement. Query 2: 'Zelensky Verkhovna Rada referendum announcement September 2025' — to find parliamentary or presidential announcements. Query 3: 'Ukraine official referendum announcement September October 2025 Zelensky decree' — to find formal decrees. Query 4: 'Ukraine Verkhovna Rada referendum resolution territorial concessions peace 2025' — to check for any parliamentary resolutions. Query 5: 'Ukraine referendum territorial status scheduled official September 2025' — to find any scheduling. Query 6: 'Ukraine rejects referendum territorial concessions Zelensky position 2025' — to find contradictory evidence and Ukraine's actual stance.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Putin's statements on September 3–4, 2025, saying Ukraine 'must hold a referendum' on territories per its Constitution — these are RUSSIAN demands/statements, not Ukrainian official announcements; REJECTED. (2) Zelensky in Paris (Sep 3–4) and Copenhagen (Sep 3) explicitly REJECTING territorial concessions to Russia — this is the opposite of the required event. (3) Rada Chairman Stefanchuk stating 'any concessions on territory or sovereignty are unacceptable' (Sep 5) — explicitly against any territorial referendum. (4) Zelensky ruling out territorial concessions in an Axios interview (Sep 26) — again opposite of qualifying event. (5) No Ukrainian presidential decrees, parliamentary resolutions, or cabinet decisions about holding a referendum on territories were found in any source during the September 1–October 1, 2025 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that matches the resolution criteria. All relevant Ukrainian official statements in the period were explicitly AGAINST territorial concessions and referendums on territorial status. Putin demanded such a referendum as a Russian condition ([bne IntelliNews](https://www.intellinews.com/putin-says-ukraine-must-hold-referendum-on-territories-to-achieve-peace-399566/)), but Ukraine's position was the opposite — [Zelensky reaffirmed Ukraine will not cede territory](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/zelenskyy-reaffirms-ukraine-will-not-cede-territory-calls-for-binding-security-guarantees/3677532), [Rada chairman Stefanchuk stated territorial concessions are unacceptable](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/4033120-stefanchuk-european-parliament-president-discusses-strengthening-sanctions-against-russia.html), and [Zelensky ruled out recognizing annexed territories](https://www.rt.com/russia/625338-zelensky-ukraine-territorial-concessions/). Additionally, martial law is still in effect in Ukraine during this period, and Ukraine's Constitution bars referendums under martial law — making such an announcement legally and practically impossible.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp exists because no qualifying event occurred. The window closed at 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z with no official Ukrainian referendum announcement made.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at any point during the September 1–October 1, 2025 window. The search was comprehensive across multiple query variations.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence strongly supports the No resolution: Ukraine was under martial law throughout this period, which under the Ukrainian Constitution prohibits referendums. Zelensky, the Rada chairman, and the Foreign Ministry all consistently stated that territorial concessions are unacceptable. Zelensky confirmed he would call for elections only after a ceasefire, but even this was about elections not a referendum on territories. Ukraine's official positions were the exact opposite of what would be needed for Yes resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No official Ukrainian government announcement of a nationwide referendum on territorial status or peace terms with Russia was made during September 1–October 1, 2025. Ukraine's official stance throughout this period was firmly against territorial concessions. Martial law in Ukraine — which prohibits referendums under Ukrainian constitutional law — remained in effect throughout the window. The only referendum demands came from Russia (Putin), not from Ukraine. The window closed on October 1, 2025, with the condition definitively unmet.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Any contract representing an individual woman (e.g., Taylor Swift, Kamala Harris) must have a daily closing price of at least $0.15 on any day between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 in the Polymarket TIME Person of the Year 2025 market. subquestions.question: Will Eric Adams publicly agree to Jim Walden's ranked-choice poll pledge by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Non-Democratic or independent candidates are currently splitting the alternative vote, with Andrew Cuomo at 25%, Republican Curtis Sliwa at 12%, and incumbent Mayor Eric Adams at 7%. To consolidate the opposition against Mamdani, attorney and candidate Jim Walden introduced a pledge for the four non-Democratic candidates to participate in an October ranked-choice poll. The agreement stipulates that only the winner of this poll would continue to the general election, while the others would presumably step aside to prevent a split vote. Andrew Cuomo has already joined the pledge, but Adams and Sliwa have yet to follow suit. If Adams signs the pledge, it strongly signals his willingness to step aside and potentially back Cuomo, who currently holds a commanding lead over Adams in the polls.

Sources:
Editorial: Jim Walden To The Rescue? - The Wave: https://rockawave.com/articles/editorial-jim-walden-to-the-rescue/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if Eric Adams, or his official campaign representatives, publicly announce that he has signed, joined, or formally agreed to participate in Jim Walden's proposed ranked-choice poll pledge between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 at 11:59 PM ET.

The agreement must be confirmed via an official channel (such as an official press release or Adams' official campaign social media, e.g., https://x.com/ericadamsfornyc) or reported by a consensus of credible news organizations (e.g., The New York Post at https://nypost.com, The New York Times at https://www.nytimes.com, or Politico at https://www.politico.com).

subquestions.rationale: Jim Walden's pledge serves as an active structural mechanism for candidates to drop out and consolidate support behind the strongest non-Mamdani candidate. Because Cuomo has already signed the pledge and is heavily outpolling Adams, Adams agreeing to participate is a strong leading indicator that he is prepared to concede the race and endorse Cuomo to avoid splitting the moderate vote.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition for Yes: Eric Adams or his official campaign representatives must publicly announce that he has signed, joined, or formally agreed to participate in Jim Walden's ranked-choice poll pledge between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 at 11:59 PM ET. evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is definitively No. Adams explicitly rejected Walden's ranked-choice poll pledge before the resolution window. question: Will tariffs generate >$250b in 2025?
description:

The resolution source will be the Treasury Department.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury report $45 billion or more in customs duties for the month of August 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Through July 2025, U.S. customs duty collections reportedly reached $150 billion for the fiscal year, with a record $28 billion collected in July alone. President Trump implemented higher 'reciprocal' tariffs on U.S. trading partners effective August 1, 2025. For the U.S. government to reach the $250 billion threshold by the end of Fiscal Year 2025 (which ends September 30, 2025), it must collect roughly $100 billion over the final two months—averaging $50 billion per month. The U.S. Department of the Treasury publishes monthly tariff revenue data in the Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) (https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mts/). The August 2025 MTS, typically released in mid-September, will provide the first clear indicator of whether the August 1 tariffs are generating revenue at the pace needed to exceed $250 billion for the fiscal year.

Sources:
U.S. Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mts/
U.S. Treasury Financial Report: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/financial-report/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) for August 2025 reports that 'Customs duties' receipts for the month of August are $45 billion ($45,000 million) or greater.

The official resolution source will be the August 2025 Monthly Treasury Statement published by the U.S. Treasury (https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mts/). The specific value will be taken from 'Table 3. Summary of Receipts and Outlays of the U.S. Government' (or the corresponding 'Receipts by Source' table) under the 'Customs duties' row for the 'This Month' column.

This question resolves Yes if the qualifying event (the publication of the August 2025 MTS showing customs duties of at least $45,000 million) occurs between the start date of 2025-09-01 and the end date of 2025-09-30 (inclusive). If the published figure is less than $45,000 million, or if the U.S. Treasury Department does not publish the August 2025 MTS by 2025-09-30 at 11:59 PM ET, the question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: To hit >$250 billion in FY 2025 after reaching $150 billion by July, the U.S. needs to average $50 billion in customs duties for August and September. Since new 'reciprocal' tariffs took effect on August 1, the August MTS will be the ultimate crux for whether these new rates are high enough to bridge the remaining $100 billion gap. A strong August showing (>$45 billion) strongly predicts the FY 2025 total will surpass the $250 billion threshold.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: August 2025 MTS published between Sep 1–30, 2025, with 'Customs duties' (This Month column) ≥ $45,000 million. Observable evidence: official MTS publication from fiscal.treasury.gov or credible reporting of exact customs duties figure. Key threshold: $45 billion.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'U.S. Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement August 2025 customs duties' — to find MTS publication and customs figure; 2) 'Monthly Treasury Statement MTS August 2025 receipts published' — to confirm publication date; 3) 'Treasury MTS August 2025 customs duties exact figure billion tariff receipts' — to find exact dollar amount; 4) 'fiscal.treasury.gov MTS August 2025 table receipts customs' — to find direct source reference.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple sources (Reuters/Investing.com, Bloomberg Law, The Hill, Yahoo Finance, NewsMax, ZeroHedge, Fox News, Market Screener, InstaForex, Devdiscourse) all published on September 11, 2025, reporting from the Treasury Department's August 2025 MTS. All consistently report customs duties (net customs receipts) of approximately $29.5 billion for August 2025, with some rounding to $30 billion. One Fox News source cites $31 billion but uses a broader category ('Customs and Certain Excise Taxes'). No source reports a figure anywhere near $45 billion.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The August 2025 MTS was published September 11, 2025. Multiple sources report customs duties of ~$29.5 billion for August 2025 [Reuters/Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/us-august-deficit-falls-to-345-billion-as-tariff-revenues-rise-4235923), [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/international-trade/us-deficit-tracks-third-highest-ever-even-as-tariff-take-rises), [The Hill](https://thehill.com/business/5499132-customs-duties-hit-new-record-in-august-on-tariff-revenues/), [NewsMax](https://www.newsmax.com/finance/financenews/u-s-august-deficit/2025/09/11/id/1226092/). The $29.5 billion figure is approximately 34% below the $45 billion threshold. Criteria NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The August 2025 MTS was published on September 11, 2025. Multiple sources were published on this date citing the Treasury data. Exact time not available from news sources, but the date is clearly September 11, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier publication of the August 2025 MTS exists. The MTS was first published September 11, 2025, within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources consistently report ~$29.5 billion in customs duties for August 2025, which is well below $45 billion. The highest figure cited is $31 billion from Fox News, which uses a broader category. No source contradicts this. The figure represents a record high for monthly customs duties, yet remains far below the $45 billion threshold required for Yes resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The August 2025 MTS was published September 11, 2025 (within the Sep 1–30 window), reporting customs duties of approximately $29.5 billion — far below the $45 billion threshold. The condition for Yes is definitively not met. The question resolves No, with the definitive No moment occurring on September 11, 2025 when the MTS was published showing the actual figure.

subquestions.question: Will the French government led by Prime Minister François Bayrou fall via a successful vote of no confidence between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
France is currently navigating a severe political crisis. Prime Minister François Bayrou, who heads a minority government, is facing a critical confidence vote scheduled for September 8, 2025. The vote centers around Bayrou's highly controversial proposal for €44 billion in spending cuts and tax increases, which includes scrapping two public holidays and freezing spending increases (https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/). 

Opposition parties across the spectrum, from the far-right National Rally to the far-left France Unbowed, have expressed intent to vote against the plans and topple the government. Far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon has explicitly demanded that President Emmanuel Macron resign if Bayrou loses the confidence vote (https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/). 

If the government falls, Macron would be forced to appoint his seventh Prime Minister since 2017, dissolve the parliament again, or resign. Although Macron has publicly vowed to serve out his mandate until its conclusion in 2027 (https://www.yahoo.com/news/), the successful passage of a no-confidence motion is a critical trigger event that would massively escalate pressure on his presidency.

question: Will Hamas agree to disarm by December 31?

Announcements of partial disarmament (e.g., surrendering a class of weapons or agreeing to disarm in stages or a certain region) will qualify as long as it is part of an acknowledged disarmament process.

subquestions.question: Will Hamas and Fatah officially announce an agreement to form a unified government or joint committee to govern the Gaza Strip between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-25?
subquestions.background_information:
A US-backed 20-point peace plan, currently in its first phase, mandates a ceasefire and hostage releases in Gaza. The upcoming 'Phase Two' requires the dismantling of Hamas's military infrastructure and the demilitarization of the territory under international monitoring (https://www.nzherald.co.nz/). However, Hamas has consistently rejected unilateral disarmament or handing over weapons to a foreign-led 'Board of Peace' or International Stabilisation Force (https://www.gatestoneinstitute.org/). On November 26, 2025, Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem reiterated that the group will not disarm unless the issue is resolved through an 'internal Palestinian dialogue' and national consensus, tying the fate of its weapons to a broader political agreement with other Palestinian factions (https://www.israelnationalnews.com/). Hamas is currently engaging in consultations with Fatah and regional mediators to reach such an understanding before moving to Phase Two. A formal governance agreement between Hamas and Fatah is widely viewed as a necessary precursor to any potential announcement of disarmament, as Hamas insists any security forces must be integrated into a unified Palestinian state structure.

Sources:
NZ Herald - https://www.nzherald.co.nz/
Gatestone Institute - https://www.gatestoneinstitute.org/
Arutz Sheva Israel News - https://www.israelnationalnews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-25 (inclusive), official representatives of both Hamas and Fatah (or the Palestinian Authority), or an official government statement from a mediating country (such as Egypt, Qatar, or Turkey), publicly announce that Hamas and Fatah have reached a formal agreement to form a unified government, administration, or joint committee to govern the Gaza Strip.

The announcement must confirm that an agreement has been finalized. Statements indicating that talks are merely progressing, that a draft is being reviewed, or that an agreement is strictly contingent on future unspecified conditions will not qualify. The agreement must cover the governance of the Gaza Strip, though it may also include the West Bank.

If no such announcement is made by the end of 2025-12-25, the question resolves No. Delayed events or announcements made after 2025-12-25 will not count towards a Yes resolution, and the question will resolve No in such cases. 

Primary resolution sources will include official statements published on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs websites of Qatar (https://www.mofa.gov.qa/) or Egypt (https://mfa.gov.eg/), as well as credible reporting confirming the official announcements from major news agencies such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) or the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/). If these specific websites become unavailable, archived versions or equivalent official statements distributed to international press will be used.
subquestions.rationale: Hamas explicitly ties the issue of its weapons and potential disarmament to an 'internal Palestinian dialogue' and the establishment of a unified Palestinian government, refusing to yield to foreign authorities. Therefore, before Hamas can officially announce any form of disarmament by the ultimate question's deadline of December 31, it must first establish this internal consensus with Fatah. Tracking whether this political agreement is reached by December 25 provides a high-value early indicator: failure to reach a governance agreement makes it highly improbable they will agree to disarm by December 31. Conversely, if an agreement is reached, it clears the primary internal hurdle Hamas has cited, significantly increasing the probability of a subsequent disarmament announcement.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official announcement by Hamas AND Fatah representatives (or mediating country government) of a finalized formal agreement to form a unified government, administration, or joint committee to govern Gaza Strip, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-25. Statements about ongoing talks, drafts under review, or contingent agreements do NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Hamas Fatah unified government agreement Gaza 2025' (to find any agreement announced in the window); 2) 'Palestinian Authority Hamas reconciliation deal December 2025' (to find reconciliation announcements); 3) 'Hamas Fatah Cairo meeting agreement technocratic committee Gaza governance' (to find specific governance committee deals); 4) 'Palestinian national reconciliation unity government announcement 2025' (to find unity announcements); 5) 'Palestinian factions unity deal Egypt Qatar mediation December 2025' (to find mediated agreements).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) Fatah spokesman Abdel Fattah Daula announced on Dec 9 that a technocratic committee formation is 'likely imminent' but noted no exact date, multiple conditions still needed (factional adherence, guarantees, consensus on powers, US position) — REJECTED as not a finalized agreement. (b) Hamas and Palestinian factions preparing 'comprehensive national meeting' in Cairo with Fatah expected to attend (Dec 9 reporting) — REJECTED as merely preparation for a meeting, not a finalized agreement. (c) A 42-member technocratic committee reportedly 'approved by Hamas, Fatah, and Egypt' mentioned in Dec 17 report by Asharq Al-Awsat — this is the closest candidate but the report frames it as preparation for phase 2 beginning in January 2026, not a formal official announcement by Hamas and Fatah of a joint governance agreement. (d) US-Qatar-Egypt-Turkey Miami meeting (Dec 19) issued joint statement urging restraint, noted 'little progress' — REJECTED as not a Hamas-Fatah agreement. (e) Turkish FM meeting Hamas delegation on Dec 24 discussing reconciliation among Palestinian factions — REJECTED as discussions, not a finalized agreement.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that explicitly satisfies ALL criteria: (1) official announcement by representatives of BOTH Hamas AND Fatah (or official mediating government statement), (2) confirming a FINALIZED agreement (not pending, contingent, or in progress), (3) to form a unified government/administration/joint committee, (4) to govern Gaza Strip, (5) within the window. The Asharq Al-Awsat Dec 17 report mentions a '42-member technocratic committee approved by Hamas, Fatah, and Egypt' but this appears in secondary reporting as background context for phase 2 planning, not as an official announcement of a finalized Hamas-Fatah governance agreement. Multiple sources explicitly state that as of late December 2025, no technocratic government had been established, no peace council existed, and the second phase remained unfinalized. [Source: Asharq Al-Awsat Dec 6](https://english.aawsat.com/node/5216452) states 'no peace council, no technocratic government, no police force, and no stabilization force.' [Source: Yeshiva World Dec 19](https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/israel-news/2488132/witkoff-meeting-gaza-mediators-in-miami-as-white-house-grows-impatient-with-israel-and-hamas) confirms 'none of these steps had meaningfully occurred.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no qualifying event was found within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event was found at all within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources from throughout the window (Nov 30 – Dec 25, 2025) consistently confirm: (1) talks are ongoing but not finalized; (2) Phase 2 governance is stalled; (3) Hamas has not agreed to disarm or relinquish governance; (4) the technocratic committee list is still being vetted; (5) the Miami meeting on Dec 19 yielded 'little progress'; (6) Trump's Board of Peace announcement was pushed to January 2026; (7) as of Dec 24, Israeli-Hamas ceasefire tensions persist with no governance breakthrough. No contradictory evidence (i.e., no source claiming a finalized Hamas-Fatah governance agreement was announced). The Dec 17 Asharq Al-Awsat report about a '42-member committee approved by Hamas, Fatah, and Egypt' is the closest possible qualifier but it is framed as preparation for phase 2 starting in January 2026 and was mentioned by a third-party mediator/analyst (Bishara Bahbah), not as an official joint announcement by Hamas and Fatah representatives. This does not meet the resolution criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying Hamas-Fatah formal agreement to form a unified government or joint committee to govern Gaza was officially announced between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-25. All evidence points to ongoing negotiations, preparations, and discussions — with multiple sources explicitly confirming no finalized governance agreement existed within the window. Resolution: No, with resolution_datetime = 2025-12-25T23:59:59Z (window closed with no qualifying event).

question: Elon no longer world's richest before 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Elon Musk is any rank other than #1 on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index at any point between June 30, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the Bloomberg Billionaires Index (https://www.bloomberg.com/billionaires/). If this source becomes permanently unavailable in that time period, the Forbes Real-Time Billionaires List will be used (https://www.forbes.com/real-time-billionaires/#6aa3f0213d78). subquestions.question: Will Tesla Inc. (TSLA) stock close at a price at least 10% lower than its first September 2025 trading day closing price on any day before October 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of August 2025, Elon Musk remains the world's richest person with a net worth hovering between $371 billion and $410 billion, depending on daily market fluctuations (https://www.forbes.com/real-time-billionaires/). However, his wealth has experienced extreme volatility throughout 2025, dropping by over $60 billion earlier in the year primarily due to swings in Tesla's stock price and external political pressures concerning electric vehicle subsidies (https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/40209873/elon-musks-wealth-takes-more-than-60-billion-hit-in-2025-as-bill-gates-also-sees-huge-losses-but-one). Meanwhile, his closest rivals—Larry Ellison and Mark Zuckerberg—have fortunes around $277 billion and $254 billion respectively, driven by robust tech and AI stock performances (https://townflex.com/top-20-richest-people-in-the-world-2025-forbes-real-time-billionaires-list/). Because Musk's number one ranking heavily depends on his massive holdings in Tesla, an acute downward trend in TSLA stock is the most likely driver for him losing his top spot on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. 

Sources:
Forbes Real-Time Billionaires List: https://www.forbes.com/real-time-billionaires/
Benzinga - Elon Musk Wealth Hit: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/40209873/elon-musks-wealth-takes-more-than-60-billion-hit-in-2025-as-bill-gates-also-sees-huge-losses-but-one
Townflex - Top 20 Richest: https://townflex.com/top-20-richest-people-in-the-world-2025-forbes-real-time-billionaires-list/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the official closing price of Tesla Inc. (TSLA) stock on the NASDAQ exchange is at least 10.00% lower than its official closing price on the first trading day of September 2025 (expected to be September 2, 2025) on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). To determine resolution, the resolver will calculate the threshold: [First Sept 2025 Trading Day Closing Price] * 0.90. If the closing price on any subsequent trading day within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window is less than or equal to this threshold, the question resolves Yes. Intraday drops that recover before the market closes do not count; only the official end-of-day closing price is considered. The primary data source will be Yahoo Finance historical data for TSLA (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/history/). If Yahoo Finance is unavailable, Google Finance (https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) will serve as the fallback. If TSLA stock splits or issues dividends during this period, adjusted closing prices will be used to accurately reflect the 10% drop in valuation.
subquestions.rationale: Elon Musk's wealth is highly concentrated in Tesla. A substantial 10% drop in Tesla's stock price over the span of a single month would wipe out tens of billions of dollars from his net worth. Observing such downward volatility in the near term acts as an excellent early indicator (crux) that Musk's buffer over fast-rising competitors like Ellison or Zuckerberg is deteriorating, increasing the probability that he will lose the #1 rank before the end of the year.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: TSLA closing price on any trading day from Sept 1–Oct 1, 2025 must be ≤ (Sept 2 closing price × 0.90). September 2, 2025 is the first trading day of September (Labor Day Sept 1 is a market holiday). Observable evidence: Explicit closing prices from reliable financial sources throughout September 2025. Key entities: TSLA stock on NASDAQ. Key threshold: [Sept 2 close] × 0.90. Timing: Sept 1–Oct 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Tesla TSLA stock closing price September 2025' (to find price levels throughout the month); 2) 'TSLA stock price September 2 2025 first trading day' (to find the benchmark closing price); 3) 'Tesla TSLA stock drop decline September 2025 lowest price' (to find if any day dropped significantly); 4) 'Tesla TSLA stock closed $329.36 September 2 2025' (to verify the opening price); 5) 'Tesla TSLA stock price below $296 $297 September 2025' (to specifically check if the threshold was ever breached); 6) 'Tesla TSLA lowest closing price September 2025 first week trading' (to check early September specifically).
evidence.step3_event_detection: The Markets Daily (published Sept 2, 2025) explicitly states TSLA 'closing at $329.36' on September 2, 2025, down 1.4% from prior close of $333.87. This establishes the September 2 close. The 10% threshold = $329.36 × 0.90 = $296.42. Subsequent closing prices found: Sept 4 = $338.53; Sept 10 = $347; Sept 11 = $354.82–$368.81; Sept 12 = $390.88; Sept 13 = $395.94; Sept 15 = $410.26; Sept 18 = $416.87; Sept 22 = $434.21; Sept 25 = $427.83; Sept 30 = ~$440. All subsequent prices are significantly ABOVE the September 2 close, let alone the 10%-below threshold of $296.42. Teslarati confirms 'has not been below $333 since early September 2025.' Multiple sources confirm TSLA gained 30-32% during September 2025 — the opposite of a 10% decline.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The criteria require TSLA to close at or below $296.42 (≤ $329.36 × 0.90) on any day in the Sept 1–Oct 1 window. Based on explicit evidence from [The Markets Daily](https://www.themarketsdaily.com/2025/09/02/tesla-nasdaqtsla-shares-down-1-4-whats-next.html) (Sept 2 close = $329.36), [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3125918/tesla-tsla-soars-over-30-in-september-amid-ai-ambitions) (surged over 30% in September), [ABC Money](https://www.abcmoney.co.uk/2025/09/tesla-stock-surges-32-in-september-on-ai-hype-and-delivery-optimism/) (September close at $412.50, up 32% for the month), and [Teslarati](https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-tsla-stock-another-firm-boost-price-target-buy-rating-canaccord/) ('has not been below $333 since early September 2025'), the price never came close to the $296.42 threshold. No day in the window saw a close at or below $296.42.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 2, 2025 closing price = $329.36 (explicitly stated in The Markets Daily article published 2025-09-02). The 10% threshold = $296.42. The window ended on 2025-10-01 with no price below this threshold. Since the condition was never met, the relevant timestamp for resolution_datetime is 2025-10-01 (end of window with no qualifying event).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (price ≤ $296.42) was found at any point in the window. TSLA's lowest closing price in September after Sept 2 appears to have been around $329–$338 (the first few days), but even those are above the threshold. After September 4, prices only increased significantly.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources confirm TSLA rose ~30-32% during September 2025, from ~$329 to ~$440. This is the opposite direction of what would be required for resolution. Key verification: (1) Teslarati article from Sept 30 states 'has not been below $333 since early September 2025' — confirming no close below $333, far above the $296.42 threshold. (2) GuruFocus, ABC Money, and Investing.com all confirm 30%+ monthly gain. (3) Multiple daily price data points show consistent upward trajectory throughout September. No contradictory evidence found suggesting any day with a close below $296.42.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The September 2, 2025 closing price was $329.36 (explicitly stated). The 10% below threshold = $296.42. TSLA never closed at or below $296.42 during the Sept 1–Oct 1 window. Instead, the stock rose approximately 30–32% during September, closing near $440 by month end. The question resolves No. The window closed on October 1, 2025 with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: Will USA win the 2025 Ryder Cup?
description:
In the 2025 Ryder Cup, scheduled for September 25-28, 2025.

If Team USA wins the 2025 Ryder Cup by finishing with more total points than Team Europe, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If the Ryder Cup is postponed, this market will remain open until the tournament has been completed.

If the Ryder Cup is canceled entirely, with no make-up tournament, this market will resolve “Tie”.

subquestions.question: Will Team USA win the Friday morning opening session (Session 1) at the 2025 Ryder Cup?
subquestions.background_information: The 2025 Ryder Cup will be played at the Bethpage Black Course in Farmingdale, New York, from September 26-28, 2025. The format consists of 28 match-play contests over three days. The competition kicks off on Friday, September 26, with the opening session in the morning, which traditionally features four foursomes (alternate shot) matches. Each match is worth one point, with a tie awarding a half-point to each side. Momentum in the Ryder Cup is highly influential, and the winner of the opening session often gains a significant psychological advantage. For the United States, utilizing the home-course advantage at Bethpage Black to jump out to an early lead against Team Europe could be pivotal. Team USA must score 14.5 points in total to reclaim the trophy. Sources: 1. Official Ryder Cup Website (https://www.rydercup.com), 2. PGA Tour (https://www.pgatour.com), 3. Yahoo Sports (https://sports.yahoo.com/golf/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if Team USA scores strictly more points than Team Europe in the Friday morning session (Session 1) of the 2025 Ryder Cup. The qualifying events for this resolution must occur between the start date of 2025-09-01 and the end date of 2025-09-26. Specifically, Session 1 must be completed by the end of the day on 2025-09-26, and Team USA must earn strictly more points than Team Europe in that session alone (e.g., scoring at least 2.5 points out of 4 available). If Team USA scores equal to or fewer points than Team Europe, or if the session is cancelled or not completed on or before 2025-09-26, the question resolves 'No'. Resolution will be based on the official Ryder Cup website (https://www.rydercup.com) or ESPN golf leaderboards (https://www.espn.com/golf/).
subquestions.rationale: Winning the opening session of the Ryder Cup is a critical early indicator of team form, strategy, and momentum. If Team USA secures an outright win in the Friday morning session, it will strongly increase the probability that they will win the entire 2025 Ryder Cup. Conversely, a poor start would negatively update forecasts for their ultimate victory.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition for Yes is: Team USA scores strictly more than Team Europe in Friday morning Session 1 (foursomes) at the 2025 Ryder Cup (at least 2.5 out of 4 points). The event must occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26. Observable evidence: explicit match results showing USA won 3 or 4 of the 4 foursomes matches.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) '2025 Ryder Cup Friday morning session 1 results' - to find completed match results; 2) 'Ryder Cup 2025 foursomes morning session Europe wins USA loses' - to find session outcome; 3) 'Michael Jordan Ryder Cup 2025 brutal morning session USA loses' - to find reaction articles confirming USA loss; 4) 'Ryder Cup 2025 day one score Europe 3 USA 1 Friday' - to confirm exact score
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key candidate event: The Friday morning foursomes session at Bethpage Black on September 26, 2025. Golf Digest article (2025-09-26) explicitly states 'the U.S. lost three of the four opening foursomes, with Europeans winning 4&3, 5&3 and 5&4, and that only Xander Schauffele and Patrick Cantlay earned a crucial point against Viktor Hovland and Robert MacIntyre.' NZ Herald article confirms 'Europe grabbed a 3-1 lead' with specific match results: Fitzpatrick/Aberg beat Scheffler/Henley 5&3, Rahm/Hatton won 4&3, and Schauffele/Cantlay won 2-up for the only USA point.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require Team USA to score STRICTLY MORE than Team Europe in Session 1. The evidence from [Golf Digest](https://www.golfdigest.com/story/michael-jordan-us-ryder-cup-team-bethpage-black-friday-foursomes-reaction) and [NZ Herald](https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/golf/ryder-cup-europe-grabs-3-1-lead-as-us-seeks-trump-boost-at-bethpage-black/3YHCJ6CTZBGLZGGRDT4A4AHC5U/) explicitly confirms Europe won 3 of 4 foursomes matches (3 points to 1 point). Team USA earned only 1 point vs Europe's 3 points — this does NOT satisfy the resolution criteria for 'Yes'. Therefore, the resolution is 'No'.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Golf Digest article was published on 2025-09-26, confirming the Friday morning session was completed on that date. The NZ Herald article covers the completed foursomes session results on September 26, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is the only occurrence of Session 1 at the 2025 Ryder Cup. The event happened on 2025-09-26 and the outcome (Europe 3, USA 1) definitively forecloses any 'Yes' resolution.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources confirm Europe won the morning foursomes session 3-1: Golf Digest (published 2025-09-26) reports Michael Jordan's reaction noting 'the U.S. lost three of the four opening foursomes'; NZ Herald confirms 'Europe grabbed a 3-1 lead' with specific match scores. No contradictory evidence was found. The only USA win was Schauffele/Cantlay beating MacIntyre/Hovland 2-up, consistent across all sources.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Team USA lost the Friday morning Session 1 foursomes at the 2025 Ryder Cup by a score of 1-3 (USA 1 point, Europe 3 points). Team USA did NOT score strictly more than Team Europe in Session 1. The question resolves 'No'. The definitive No moment was when the last match of Session 1 was completed on 2025-09-26, with Europe winning 3-1.

question: Nothing Ever Happens: Khamenei
description:
This market will resolve to “No” if any of the following conditions are met between market creation and March 31, 2026, 11:59 ET:

- Khamenei out as Supreme Leader of Iran
- Khamenei leaves Iran

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “Yes”.

Khamenei out as Supreme Leader of Iran:
This market will resolve to "No" if Iran's Supreme Leader, Ali Khamenei, is removed from power for any length of time during this market’s above-specified time frame. Khamenei will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as Supreme Leader of Iran within this market's timeframe. The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

Khamenei leaves Iran:
This market will resolve to "No" if it is confirmed that Ali Khamenei has left Iran for any length of time during this market’s above-specified time frame. In cases where Ali Khamenei may have exited Iranian airspace on a plane, he must be confirmed to have exited the plane in a country other than Iran for this market to resolve to "No". If Ali Khamenei exits Iranian maritime territory on a boat to international waters, this market may resolve to "No". The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States officially confirm conducting a kinetic military strike on Iranian territory between February 5, 2026, and February 26, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Iran is currently experiencing widespread anti-government protests, severe economic instability, and a violent government crackdown that has reportedly led to thousands of deaths [https://www.news.com.au/world/middle-east/iranian-leader-hiding-son-left-in-charge]. Amid this unrest, the United States has deployed significant naval forces to the Middle East, including the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier group. U.S. leadership has threatened military action if the violent crackdown continues, with officials noting a 'massive flotilla' heading toward the region [https://www.republicworld.com/world-news/middle-east/khamenei-reportedly-sheltering-in-underground-bunker-as-us-naval-forces-head-to-middle-east]. Due to fears of a U.S. military strike, Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei has reportedly relocated to a fortified underground bunker in Tehran and delegated day-to-day governance to his son, Masoud [https://www.breitbart.com/middle-east/2026/01/26/report-irans-khamenei-flees-to-fortified-bunker-fearing-u-s-strike]. A U.S. kinetic strike on Iranian soil would represent a massive escalation that could destabilize the regime and precipitate Khamenei's removal or flight.

Sources:
News.com.au - Iranian leader hiding, son left in charge: https://www.news.com.au/world/middle-east/iranian-leader-hiding-son-left-in-charge
Republic World - Khamenei Reportedly Sheltering in Underground Bunker: https://www.republicworld.com/world-news/middle-east/khamenei-reportedly-sheltering-in-underground-bunker-as-us-naval-forces-head-to-middle-east
Breitbart - Report: Iran's Khamenei Flees to 'Fortified' Bunker: https://www.breitbart.com/middle-east/2026/01/26/report-irans-khamenei-flees-to-fortified-bunker-fearing-u-s-strike
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the United States government officially confirms that U.S. military forces have conducted a kinetic strike (e.g., using aircraft, drones, or missiles) against a target located within the internationally recognized land territory or territorial waters of Iran between 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive).

To resolve Yes, the official confirmation must be issued by the US Department of Defense (DoD), US Central Command (CENTCOM), or the White House via an official press release, public statement, or press briefing published on their respective official websites (https://www.defense.gov/, https://www.centcom.mil/, or https://www.whitehouse.gov/) within the resolution window.

The strike itself must occur between 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-26. Non-kinetic actions (such as cyberattacks or electronic warfare), or strikes on Iranian proxies, personnel, or assets located outside of Iran's internationally recognized borders (e.g., in Syria, Iraq, Yemen, or international waters) will not count for a Yes resolution. If no such official confirmation of a qualifying strike is made by the U.S. government between 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-26, the question will resolve No. If the event is postponed or confirmation is delayed beyond 2026-02-26, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The possibility of a US military strike is cited as the primary reason Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has reportedly relocated to an underground bunker and delegated daily powers to his son. A kinetic U.S. strike would severely test the regime's grip on power during ongoing mass protests, dramatically increasing the probability that Khamenei loses his position or is forced to flee (e.g., to Russia). Tracking the materialization of this specific threat provides a strong early indicator of the conditions required for the ultimate question to resolve 'No' (meaning Khamenei is out).

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: US DoD, CENTCOM, or White House officially confirms a kinetic strike (aircraft/drones/missiles) on targets within Iran's internationally recognized borders/territorial waters, with the strike occurring AND confirmation issued between 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-26. Observable evidence: Official press release, statement, or briefing on defense.gov, centcom.mil, or whitehouse.gov explicitly confirming a kinetic strike on Iranian territory.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'United States military strike Iran 2026' (Feb 5-26) - to find any confirmed strikes; 2) 'US military attack Iran territory February 2026' (Feb 5-26) - variations; 3) 'US strike Iran confirmed Pentagon CENTCOM February 2026' (Feb 20-26) - official confirmations; 4) 'Iran nuclear deal diplomacy talks February 2026 outcome' (Feb 20-26) - diplomatic context; 5) 'US Iran Geneva talks February 26 2026 outcome result' (Feb 25-26) - final day events; 6) 'US military strike attack Iran February 26 2026 bombing' (Feb 25-26) - any last-minute strikes; 7) 'CENTCOM Pentagon White House Iran strike confirmed official statement' (Feb 5-26) - official statements
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: Extensive US military buildup (two aircraft carrier strike groups, 150+ fighter jets, Patriot/THAAD systems deployed); Three rounds of indirect nuclear talks (Feb 6 Muscat, Feb 17-18 Geneva, Feb 26 Geneva); Trump set 10-15 day deadline on Feb 19; Feb 26 Geneva talks concluded with 'significant progress' per Oman mediator, technical talks scheduled in Vienna; No kinetic US military strike on Iranian territory was identified in any article from the resolution window. All rejected as qualifying events: All military movements were preparations/positioning, not actual strikes. All diplomatic events were negotiations, not military actions.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article within the Feb 5-26 window reports an official US confirmation of a kinetic strike on Iranian territory. On Feb 26, multiple sources ([AP](https://apnews.com/article/iran-us-war-geneva-talks-nuclear-c1eb17f570b059f34071937c3f310fb6), [The Star](https://www.thestar.com/news/world/middle-east/us-and-iran-wrap-up-another-round-of-indirect-nuclear-talks-as-american-forces-mass/article_c3295ad9-f78f-5aca-be53-918df0f5b66c.html), [WRAL](https://www.wral.com/news/ap/c1eb1-mediator-cites-progress-as-indirect-nuclear-talks-between-the-us-and-iran-wrap-up/)) confirm the third round of nuclear talks took place and concluded with 'significant progress' - the US was still in diplomatic talks on the last day of the window. A Feb 27 article ([SHTF Plan](https://www.shtfplan.com/war/now-we-wait-for-war-with-iran-to-begin-as-a-rare-6-planet-parade-and-a-blood-moon-eclipse-loom)) confirms no strike had occurred by that date either, and Trump was still deciding on scope. The resolution criteria explicitly require an official US government confirmation of a kinetic strike - none found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a qualifying US kinetic strike on Iran can be extracted, because no such strike occurred within the window. The window closed on 2026-02-26T23:59:59Z with ongoing diplomacy.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence of a US kinetic military strike on Iranian territory was found at any point in the resolution window (Feb 5-26, 2026). The searches found only military preparations, diplomatic talks, threats, and warnings - not actual strikes.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: Multiple independent sources (AP, AFP, The Star, WRAL, Asharq Al-Awsat) confirm the February 26 Geneva talks concluded with 'significant progress' and technical talks were scheduled in Vienna the following week - indicating diplomacy was still ongoing at the end of the window. A post-window article (Feb 27, SHTF Plan) reports the Geneva talks 'yielded no results' and Trump was convening advisers on Friday (Feb 27) to decide on strike scope - confirming no strike had occurred within the window. Defense stocks fell on Feb 25 due to 'progress' in nuclear talks. No DoD/CENTCOM/White House official confirmation of any strike was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence conclusively shows that no US kinetic military strike on Iranian territory occurred within the Feb 5-26, 2026 window. Throughout this period, the US was engaged in massive military buildup and three rounds of indirect nuclear talks with Iran. The final day (Feb 26) saw the third round of Geneva talks conclude with 'significant progress' and plans for follow-on technical talks in Vienna. No official DoD, CENTCOM, or White House press release confirming a kinetic strike on Iranian territory was found in any search. The question resolves No.

subquestions.question: Will the Milwaukee Bucks have a regular season win percentage of .500 or higher at the end of the day on January 3, 2026?

A key threshold for demonstrating competitiveness is returning to a .500 win percentage. If the Bucks fail to improve their standing, the pressure to trade Antetokounmpo before the February 2026 deadline will escalate significantly.

question: NYSE marketwide circuit breaker in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a marketwide circuit breaker is triggered on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) at any time between January 1 and market close on December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A marketwide circuit breaker is defined as a trading halt that is initiated due to significant declines in the S&P 500 Index, specifically a Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3 halt as per NYSE rules.
