subquestions.question: Will the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) close at or above 45.00 on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question evaluates if a marketwide circuit breaker will be triggered on the NYSE in 2025. Circuit breakers halt trading during rapid market declines and are triggered when the S&P 500 drops by 7% (Level 1), 13% (Level 2), or 20% (Level 3) in a single day. In April 2025, the stock market experienced severe sell-offs due to reciprocal tariffs and inflation concerns, with the S&P 500 falling almost 6% in one session—coming very close to the 7% circuit breaker threshold (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/circuit-breaker-heres-trading-halted-20250410.html).

The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) measures the stock market's expectation of volatility based on S&P 500 index options. High VIX values indicate extreme fear and large expected price swings, which are prerequisites for marketwide circuit breakers. Historically, VIX levels above 40 reflect severe market turmoil. During the March 2020 crash, when the last marketwide circuit breakers were triggered, the VIX closed at a record high of 82.69 (https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/16/wall-street-fear-gauge-hits-highest-level-ever.html). Therefore, monitoring whether the VIX surges above 45.00 in September 2025 acts as a highly informative crux for predicting if the extreme volatility needed to trigger a circuit breaker will persist or escalate before the year ends.

Sources:
Yahoo! Finance: What is a circuit breaker? - https://finance.yahoo.com/news/circuit-breaker-heres-trading-halted-20250410.html
CNBC: Wall Street's 'fear gauge' hits highest level ever - https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/16/wall-street-fear-gauge-hits-highest-level-ever.html
CBOE VIX Index - https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) official closing price is 45.00 or higher on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

The primary resolution source will be historical data from Yahoo Finance for the VIX index (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/history/). The "Close" column for the specified dates will be used for resolution. Intraday highs that exceed 45.00 but close below 45.00 will not count towards a "Yes" resolution. 

In the event Yahoo Finance data is unavailable, data directly from the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) (https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/) or another credible financial data provider (such as Bloomberg, MarketWatch, or Reuters) will be used as a fallback. 

If the specified window passes without the VIX closing at or above 45.00, or if all major exchanges are closed for the entirety of this period preventing the index from being calculated, this question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A marketwide circuit breaker requires a sudden and severe 7% drop in the S&P 500. The VIX index directly measures anticipated stock market volatility and fear. A VIX closing value above 45.00 in September is a strong signal of panic and extreme distress in the market. Since circuit breakers correlate strongly with immense VIX spikes (as seen in March 2020), tracking if the VIX surpasses 45.00 in the short term serves as a robust leading indicator for the ultimate question without merely being a restatement of it.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: CBOE VIX official closing price ≥ 45.00 on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Observable evidence required: explicit VIX closing price data from credible financial news sources. Key entities: CBOE VIX index; threshold: 45.00; timing: September 1 – October 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'VIX CBOE Volatility Index closing price September 2025' — to find daily closing data; 2) 'VIX index high spike 45 above September 2025' — to find any qualifying event; 3) 'VIX volatility index market crash spike September 2025' — to detect any crash events; 4) 'Stock market crash extreme volatility September October 2025' — to check for macro events that could spike VIX above 45.

All values are far below 45.00. No articles report any sudden VIX spike anywhere near 45 during this period. No qualifying events found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the reported VIX closings approached 45.00. Per [Yahoo Finance Sep 25 article](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/stock-market-news-sep-25-075300739.html), VIX dropped 2.8% to 16.18 on Sep 25. Per [Benzinga Sep 18](https://www.benzinga.com/etfs/specialty-etfs/25/09/47747431/why-volatility-etfs-are-among-2025s-worst-performers), VIX was at 15.7 and down 9.5% YTD after the Fed cut. Per [Markets Insider Sep 26](https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/closing-bell-movers-oracle-ticks-higher-as-trump-rescues-tiktok-in-us-1035209775), VIX 'approached 18, the highest level in three weeks' — still far below 45. Per [Motley Fool Sep 5](https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/09/05/stock-market-bull-signal-17-times-big-gains-next/), VIX peaked at 45.3 on April 4, 2025 and then fell to 14.2 by August 22, 2025 — well before the window. No article reports any VIX close ≥ 45.00 during the September 1–October 1 window.

subquestions.background_information: The ultimate question asks whether the 10-year Treasury yield will hit 5.0% in 2025. A major driver for long-term Treasury yields is inflation, which dictates the Federal Reserve's monetary policy and influences the term premium demanded by bond investors. In mid-2025, inflation was hovering slightly above the Fed's 2% target, with the year-over-year CPI for May 2025 reported at 2.4% (https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news). If inflation begins to accelerate or remains sticky at elevated levels, it reduces the likelihood of near-term Federal Reserve rate cuts, pushing long-term Treasury yields higher. Therefore, the August 2025 CPI release serves as a critical crux. If the 12-month percentage change climbs back to 2.5% or higher, it indicates re-accelerating or persistent inflation, providing a strong signal that the 10-year yield is on track to approach or reach the 5.0% mark later in the year. Sources: Investing.com Economy News (https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news), US Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index (https://www.bls.gov/cpi/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports that the 12-month percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), All items, not seasonally adjusted, is 2.5% or higher for the month of August 2025. The data must be officially published in the BLS 'Consumer Price Index Summary' news release between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The resolution will be determined strictly based on the initial release of the August 2025 data available on the BLS website (https://www.bls.gov/cpi/news.htm). Any subsequent revisions to the data will not affect the resolution. If the data for August 2025 is not published during the resolution window between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question will resolve as unresolvable (N/A).
subquestions.rationale: Inflation data is a primary leading indicator for long-term Treasury yields. The August CPI report, which is released in September, will provide crucial insight into the inflation trend entering the final quarter of the year. An inflation reading of 2.5% or higher would signal to markets that inflation remains sticky, forcing the Federal Reserve to maintain higher interest rates and making a 5.0% 10-year Treasury yield significantly more probable.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: BLS must report that the 12-month % change in CPI-U (All items, not seasonally adjusted) for August 2025 is ≥2.5%, published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Subsequent reporting in August 2025 indicated that a detailed prospectus known as the 'GREAT Trust' had been circulating within the U.S. administration, aiming to temporarily or permanently relocate residents into transit areas or third countries (https://www.washingtonpost.com/). Israel has actively sought third-party nations to host relocated Palestinians, with reports highlighting talks with South Sudan to establish mass resettlement camps (https://apnews.com/). Despite Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's endorsement, global human rights groups have strongly opposed the plan, and finding willing host nations remains the primary bottleneck. Securing international bilateral agreements is a necessary precursor to large-scale relocations. Sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/) | Washington Post (https://www.washingtonpost.com/) | AP News (https://apnews.com/)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), an official representative or an official press release from the government of Israel, the United States, or a receiving third-party country publicly announces that a finalized agreement has been reached for the receiving sovereign nation to host, resettle, or process at least 10,000 Palestinians relocating from the Gaza Strip. The announcement must confirm that the agreement is finalized or signed; announcements of ongoing talks, proposals, or exploratory feasibility studies do not qualify. Transfers strictly to the West Bank do not count, as the destination must be a distinct third-party sovereign nation. If the official government announcement does not explicitly specify a number, credible reporting from major news outlets (such as AP News or Reuters) confirming that the agreement covers 10,000 or more individuals will be sufficient to meet the threshold. Primary resolution sources will include official press statements from the U.S. State Department (https://www.state.gov/press-releases/) or the Israeli Prime Minister's Office (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office/news), corroborated by credible international news sources (https://apnews.com/). subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question requires 500,000 Gazans to be relocated by December 31, 2025. Moving half a million people is an immense logistical operation that fundamentally requires large-scale destinations willing to accept them. As of August 2025, no official mass resettlement agreements have been confirmed. For 500,000 people to be successfully moved by year-end, formal bilateral host agreements must be established rapidly. If October 1 arrives without any third-party nation formally agreeing to take a significant cohort (10,000+), the logistical window to hit the 500,000 threshold by December 31 effectively closes, making this a highly informative crux for forecasters.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official announcement from Israel, US, or receiving third-party country that a FINALIZED agreement has been reached for a sovereign nation to host/resettle/process at least 10,000 Palestinians from Gaza. [South Sudan denial](https://www.arabnews.com/node/2614154/middle-east) confirmed 'There is no discussions on that and there is no deal that has been signed.' The US 21-point peace plan [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/revealed-us-21-point-plan-for-ending-gaza-war-creating-pathway-to-palestinian-state/) explicitly encourages Palestinians to REMAIN in Gaza and prohibits forced displacement, the opposite of what the question requires. The Trump 20-point plan [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2023407) 'explicitly prohibits forced relocation of Palestinians from Gaza.' None of these qualify as a finalized agreement for a third-party sovereign nation to accept 10,000+ Palestinians.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp exists. The only relevant timestamps are: Sept 4-5 (South Sudan denial), Sept 11-12 (Israeli internal discussions with no finalized deals), Sept 27-30 (US peace plan that prohibits displacement). evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout September 2025, Israel discussed voluntary emigration plans but no agreements were finalized with any country. question: Fed rate cut by October 2025 meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is decreased at any point between September 18 and the completion of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for October 2025, currently scheduled for October 28–29. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If no relevant statement is released for this meeting by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, and no qualifying rate cut is announced, this market will resolve to "No". Emergency rate cuts will qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the official U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) for September 2025 be reported at 4.3% or higher in the initial BLS release?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. Federal Reserve considers both labor market conditions and inflation when making its monetary policy decisions, balancing its dual mandate of full employment and price stability. In recent months, Fed officials have signaled increasing attention to downside risks in the labor market. As of mid-2025, the unemployment rate has hovered in a narrow band between 4.0% and 4.2%. A rising unemployment rate, particularly breaking above 4.2%, would indicate further labor market softening, creating stronger pressure for the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to lower the target federal funds rate at its upcoming October 2025 meeting. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) typically releases the Employment Situation summary for September on the first Friday of October, providing a critical data point before the Fed's October meeting.

Sources:
BLS Employment Situation News Release: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) initially reports a seasonally adjusted U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) of 4.3% or higher for the month of September 2025. This initial publication must occur between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18 (inclusive).

The primary resolution source will be the official BLS Employment Situation news release (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm).
- The resolution will be based strictly on the headline seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for September 2025 as published in the initial release during the specified timeframe.
- If the initially reported value is exactly 4.3% or greater, the question resolves Yes. If it is 4.2% or lower, the question resolves No.
- Any subsequent revisions to the September 2025 unemployment data made after the initial release will not be considered for resolution.
- Delayed events: If the BLS postpones the release of the September 2025 employment data beyond the resolution window (i.e., it is not published between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18), the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: The BLS employment report is a critical macroeconomic indicator used by the Federal Reserve to guide monetary policy. A jump in the unemployment rate to 4.3% or higher would signal a meaningful deterioration in the labor market compared to previous months. This would strongly increase the probability that the Fed acts to cut interest rates at the October 2025 FOMC meeting to fulfill the employment side of its dual mandate, making it an excellent leading indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes condition: BLS must officially publish a seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate of 4.3% or higher for September 2025 between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18 inclusive. Observable evidence: Official BLS Employment Situation press release showing September 2025 U-3 ≥ 4.3%. Key entities: BLS, Employment Situation Summary (empsit.nr0.htm). Threshold: U-3 ≥ 4.3%. Timing: Must occur within resolution window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'BLS unemployment rate September 2025 initial release' (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-18) - looking for the actual release. 2) 'Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation October 2025 September jobs report' (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-18) - looking for publication. 3) 'BLS jobs report released government shutdown ended October 2025' (2025-10-08 to 2025-10-18) - checking if shutdown ended. 4) 'September 2025 unemployment rate BLS published released' (2025-10-08 to 2025-10-18) - direct evidence search. 5) 'government shutdown ended spending bill signed October 2025' (2025-10-14 to 2025-10-18) - checking shutdown end. 6) 'BLS employment situation report September 2025 delayed shutdown status' (2025-10-14 to 2025-10-18) - verifying continued delay.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No qualifying event found. The September 2025 BLS Employment Situation Report was originally scheduled for October 3, 2025 (first Friday of October), but the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025 prevented its release. The BLS furloughed nearly all staff on October 1. Multiple sources (The Hill, Washington Examiner, BLS statement, Yahoo Finance, Seeking Alpha, Reuters) confirm the September jobs report was NOT released. The only BLS exception during the shutdown was the September CPI report, scheduled for October 24 (outside the resolution window). As of October 16-17, 2025 (the last confirmed dates within the window), the shutdown was still ongoing (day 16), with the Senate adjourned and no deal reached. All sources confirm the September employment situation report remained unreleased.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require the BLS to publish the September 2025 U-3 unemployment rate between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18. Multiple authoritative sources confirm this did NOT happen: [The Hill](https://thehill.com/business/5531272-government-shutdown-delays-jobs-report/) 'The U.S. monthly jobs report for September will not be released this week due to a federal government shutdown'; [Investing.com UK](https://uk.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-to-release-september-inflation-data-despite-shutdown-93CH-4300183) 'The September employment report, originally scheduled for October 4, 2025, has already been delayed due to the shutdown... No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services'; [Quartz](https://qz.com/government-shutdown-fomc-fed-meeting-jobs-report-inflation) 'The shutdown has prevented the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) from releasing the September jobs report'; [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/5553684-inflation-data-used-to-set-2026-social-security-cola-coming-oct-24/) 'other BLS reports, including the September jobs report, remain on hold'; [FrankNez Media](https://franknezmedia.com/senate-democrats-now-block-gop-plan-to-end-the-shutdown/) 'The Senate adjourned for a long weekend, with no session scheduled until October 20' (as of Oct 16). No criteria match found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for the BLS September 2025 Employment Situation report being published within the window, because it was not published. The shutdown prevented publication. The BLS explicitly stated only the CPI would be released (October 24, outside window). The most recent evidence (October 16-17, 2025) confirms the shutdown was still ongoing and the jobs report had not been released.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event occurred within the window at all.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence: Searched for any indication the shutdown ended before October 18 or that the BLS released the report under special circumstances. Found none. The Independent article from October 16 confirms the shutdown was in its third week. The Senate adjourned for a long weekend with no vote scheduled until October 20. BLS explicitly stated only CPI would be released during shutdown. Multiple authoritative sources (Reuters/Investing.com factbox from Oct 13, Powell's Oct 14 speech, Quartz Oct 16 article) all confirm the September jobs report remained unreleased throughout the window. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BLS September 2025 Employment Situation Report was NOT published within the resolution window (2025-09-18 to 2025-10-18). The U.S. government shutdown began October 1, 2025, preventing BLS from releasing the report originally scheduled for October 3, 2025. The shutdown was still ongoing as of October 16-17, 2025, with no end in sight before October 18. The BLS explicitly stated no reports other than CPI would be released during the shutdown, and the CPI itself wasn't scheduled until October 24. Per the resolution criteria: 'If the BLS postpones the release of the September 2025 employment data beyond the resolution window (i.e., it is not published between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18), the question should be considered unresolvable.' The question is therefore unresolvable.

subquestions.question: Will Mexico's Ministry of the Interior (SEGOB) report 350,000 or more Mexican nationals repatriated from the United States in calendar year 2025, in data published between January 29, 2026, and February 26, 2026?
subquestions.background_information: The ultimate question asks whether ICE removed 750,000 or more non-citizens in the 2025 fiscal year. Because official ICE deportation data can be delayed, independent tracking by receiving countries serves as an excellent early indicator. Historically, Mexican nationals make up a large percentage of total U.S. deportations. Mexico's Unidad de Politica Migratoria, Registro e Identidad de Personas (UPMRIP), under the Secretariat of the Interior (SEGOB), independently tracks and publishes the number of Mexican nationals repatriated from the United States ('Eventos de repatriacion de mexicanos desde Estados Unidos'). For context, in 2023, SEGOB reported approximately 214,849 repatriations of Mexicans from the U.S. If U.S. deportations surged to meet or exceed the 750,000 threshold across all nationalities in 2025, it is highly probable that repatriations of Mexican nationals would correspondingly surge to 350,000 or more. Monitoring SEGOB's calendar year 2025 statistics provides a strong, independent early indicator of ICE's overall deportation volume before the ICE Annual Report is fully processed and published. Sources: 1) ICE Annual Report FY 2024 (https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf) 2) Mexico UPMRIP Boletines (http://portales.segob.gob.mx/es/PoliticaMigratoria/Boletines_Estadisticos).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive), Mexico's Unidad de Politica Migratoria, Registro e Identidad de Personas (UPMRIP) or the Secretariat of the Interior (SEGOB) publishes official data indicating that the total number of 'Eventos de repatriacion de mexicanos desde Estados Unidos' (Events of repatriation of Mexicans from the United States) for the full calendar year 2025 was 350,000 or greater. The primary resolution source will be the official UPMRIP statistical bulletins or data tables available at http://portales.segob.gob.mx/es/PoliticaMigratoria/Boletines_Estadisticos. If the reported total for the 2025 calendar year is exactly 350,000 or greater, it resolves Yes. If the reported total is less than 350,000, it resolves No. If the final data for the full calendar year 2025 is not published within this exact resolution window (by 2026-02-26 at 11:59 PM UTC), the question will be considered unresolvable and should resolve as Ambiguous/Unresolved.
subquestions.rationale: Mexico is historically the largest country of origin for deportees from the U.S. Using an independent dataset from the Mexican government tracking incoming deportees provides a highly correlated proxy for U.S. ICE numbers that cannot be obfuscated by U.S. domestic agency delays. Since Mexicans typically comprise 40-50% of U.S. deportations, seeing 350,000 or more Mexican repatriations strongly points toward total ICE removals approaching or exceeding 750,000, providing forecasters with actionable evidence before the ultimate ICE report.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: SEGOB/UPMRIP publishes official data between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26 showing total 'Eventos de repatriacion de mexicanos desde Estados Unidos' for full calendar year 2025 ≥ 350,000. Observable evidence: Official bulletin on portales.segob.gob.mx or UPMRIP statistical tables showing the figure. Key entities: Mexico SEGOB, UPMRIP, Mexican nationals repatriated from US. Threshold: 350,000 events. Window: 2026-01-29 to 2026-02-26.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Mexico SEGOB UPMRIP repatriation statistics 2025 Mexican nationals United States' (Jan-Feb 2026) - to find official data publication; 2. 'Mexico repatriacion mexicanos Estados Unidos 2025 estadisticas SEGOB' (Jan-Feb 2026) - same in Spanish; 3. 'Mexico 146000 repatriated deported 2025 SEGOB official figures' - to find specific numbers; 4. 'Mexico deportation repatriation 2025 annual total statistics 350000' - to check for threshold; 5. 'portales segob gob mx PoliticaMigratoria Boletines Estadisticos 2025' - to directly find UPMRIP bulletin; 6. 'Mexico te Abraza deportados mexicanos 2025 estadisticas gobierno'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) BorderReport (Feb 12, 2026): states 'Mexico recorded 146,000 of its citizens expelled from the U.S. in 2025' - this is within the resolution window and represents Mexican government data; (2) Mexico Business News (Feb 11, 2026): 'Federal data show 146,000 Mexican migrants were deported from the U.S. in 2025'; (3) KVIA article (Jan 22, 2026): references 'Quinto Elemento Lab' data showing deportations to Mexico declined in 2025; (4) Mexico Ambassador quote (Jan 28, 2026): Mexico te Abraza program helped ~150,000 since 2024 launch (not just 2025). No evidence found of UPMRIP bulletin showing ≥350,000 or any figure close to threshold. The 146,000 figure is far below 350,000.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The reported Mexican government figure of 146,000 repatriated Mexican nationals from the US in 2025 does NOT meet the 350,000 threshold required for Yes resolution. Sources: [BorderReport](https://www.borderreport.com/regions/mexico/migrant-tents-dismantled-as-mass-deportations-dont-materialize/) states 'Mexico recorded 146,000 of its citizens expelled from the U.S. in 2025.' [Mexico Business News](https://mexicobusiness.news/talent/news/state-mexico-scales-job-programs-returning-migrants) states 'Federal data show 146,000 Mexican migrants were deported from the U.S. in 2025.' Neither is the specific UPMRIP bulletin from portales.segob.gob.mx, but both cite Mexican federal government data published within or near the resolution window. The question also requires the data to come specifically from UPMRIP statistical bulletins. No direct evidence of the UPMRIP bulletin itself was found in this search.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The figure of 146,000 Mexican repatriations in 2025 appears in: (1) BorderReport published 2026-02-12 (within window); (2) Mexico Business News published 2026-02-11 (within window). However, no explicit UPMRIP bulletin publication with a specific timestamp was identified.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest explicit references to the 146,000 figure for Mexican repatriations in 2025 appear in articles dated 2026-02-11 and 2026-02-12. Earlier articles from January 2026 reference declining deportations generally without the specific annual total.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification: The 146,000 figure for Mexican repatriations from the US in 2025 is consistently reported by multiple sources. This figure is far below (approximately 58% less than) the 350,000 threshold required for Yes resolution. The question requires specific UPMRIP official data, which was not directly located in news searches. However: (1) Multiple sources cite 'federal data' for this figure, which could be from UPMRIP; (2) The BorderReport article specifically references 'the Mexican government' as the source; (3) Even if UPMRIP's specific bulletin was published in the window, the underlying number (146,000) is well below 350,000. No evidence was found suggesting any figure near 350,000 for Mexican repatriations in 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Multiple sources within or adjacent to the resolution window consistently report that Mexico recorded approximately 146,000 Mexican nationals repatriated/expelled from the United States in 2025. This is far below (roughly 41.7% of) the 350,000 threshold required for Yes resolution. While the specific UPMRIP bulletin was not directly accessed, the underlying data from Mexican government sources is consistently below the threshold. The condition for Yes (≥350,000 'Eventos de repatriacion de mexicanos desde Estados Unidos' for calendar year 2025) was definitively not met. Given that border crossings fell to historic lows under Trump's 2025 immigration policies, and the consistent reporting of ~146,000 figure from federal data, this is definitively a No. The resolution_datetime is set to 2026-02-26 as the end of the window, since no specific earlier 'decisive No moment' can be established from an official UPMRIP publication.

description:

subquestions.question: Will the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), NIH, or CDC publicly release a formal written report or study concerning the causes of autism between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In late August 2025, Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced during a Cabinet meeting that his department had identified "certain interventions" that are "almost certainly causing autism." He pledged that a full public announcement, alongside related research and data, would be released in September 2025. Previously, in May 2025, he had pushed his original September deadline back to March 2026, but his recent August remarks reinstated the September timeline. The NIH has also been directed to conduct studies pinpointing these supposed causes. Tracking whether a formal written report or study is actually published by HHS or NIH in September serves as a concrete, observable indicator of whether RFK Jr. is on track to definitively name a cause of autism before November.

Sources:

UPI - https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/08/27/rfk-jr-autism-report/
The Independent - https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/rfk-jr-autism-cause-timeline-b2721835.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), the National Institutes of Health (NIH), or the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) officially publishes a formal written report, study, white paper, or official dataset specifically investigating or addressing the causes of autism (including potential "interventions" or "environmental toxins") between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

- The document must be officially published or hosted on an official .gov website associated with HHS (https://www.hhs.gov/), NIH (https://www.nih.gov/), or CDC (https://www.cdc.gov/), or be formally distributed via an official press release from these agencies linking to the written document.
- The document does not need to declare a definitive cause to count, as long as its primary subject matter is the investigation of autism's causes or links to interventions/toxins.
- Verbal statements, interviews, press conferences, or social media posts by RFK Jr. or other officials do not count for this subquestion unless they are accompanied by the public release of a formal written report or study as described above.
- Leaked documents that are not officially released or acknowledged by the agencies do not qualify.
- If the document is delayed and no such qualifying release occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 at 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion tracks an observable administrative milestone—the publication of a formal written report or study by federal health agencies—rather than a verbal claim of finding a 'definitive cause'. Since RFK Jr. explicitly promised to release his research in September 2025, the actual publication of this document is a crucial leading indicator. If the agencies publish the report by October 1, it is highly likely RFK Jr. will use it to formally announce a definitive cause, resolving the ultimate question to 'Yes'. Conversely, if no official document materializes in September, it strongly suggests another delay in his timeline, making a definitive announcement before November unlikely.

subquestions.question: Will the ECB's December 2025 macroeconomic projections forecast euro area annual HICP inflation for 2026 at 1.9% or higher?

The ECB is scheduled to release its next monetary policy decision alongside updated Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections on December 18, 2025. Previous projections had 2026 inflation at 1.7%, but market analysts anticipate a slight upward revision, though generally expecting it to remain below 2%. If the 2026 inflation forecast is revised to 1.9% or higher, it would signal that inflation expectations are uncomfortably close to the ECB's ceiling. This would directly influence the governing council's assessment, potentially prompting a rate hike or hawkish pivot at the subsequent February 2026 meeting rather than maintaining a 'no change' stance.

A higher inflation projection in December 2025 would serve as a strong crux indicating that the ECB may deviate from a 'no change' policy and instead opt for a rate adjustment at the February 2026 meeting to address persistent inflation risks.

Announcements of violations or partial returns falling short of the threshold will not be sufficient to resolve "Yes".
subquestions.rationale: The return of the living hostages is the most immediate and critical condition of the ceasefire agreement established on October 9, 2025. If Hamas successfully releases a significant number of living hostages (at least 10), it strongly indicates that the initial phase of the ceasefire is being implemented, building the necessary trust to prevent a cancellation. Conversely, failure to release the hostages would be a major violation of the newly signed terms, making it highly probable that Israel would announce the cancellation of the ongoing ceasefire before December 31. Such a motion must be proposed by at least one-tenth of the Deputies (35 members). Given Sánchez's refusal to resign, a motion of no confidence represents the primary institutional mechanism the opposition could use to attempt to force him from power during the critical autumn legislative session.

subquestions.question: Will the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) estimate the U.S. federal budget deficit for Fiscal Year 2025 to be $1.85 trillion or more in its Monthly Budget Review released between October 1 and October 18, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
According to a September 2025 report by the Congressional Budget Office (CBO), the United States accumulated a $2 trillion federal budget deficit over the first 11 months of Fiscal Year 2025. Because September typically sees a surplus due to quarterly tax receipts, the CBO projected the total deficit for the full fiscal year (ending September 30, 2025) to be $1.8 trillion. Meanwhile, the gross national debt surpassed $37 trillion in mid-August 2025, growing at a historically rapid pace of roughly $1 trillion every five months. The annual budget deficit directly drives the borrowing needs of the Treasury. If the final FY 2025 deficit comes in significantly higher than the $1.8 trillion projection (e.g., $1.85 trillion or more), it would indicate that government spending outpaced revenues by more than expected in the final month. This accelerated pace of deficit spending acts as a critical indicator that the total national debt is accumulating faster than forecasted, thereby increasing the likelihood that it will breach the $38 trillion mark before the end of calendar year 2025.

Sources:
Congressional Budget Office - Monthly Budget Review: https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/monthly-budget-review
Report: U.S. racked up $2 trillion deficit over past 11 months (KPVI): https://www.kpvi.com/news/national_news/report-u-s-racked-up-2-trillion-deficit-over-past-11-months/article_ed1c23a8-4e8b-59d4-8d48-3a9d4a413d11.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) publishes a Monthly Budget Review (or official equivalent release estimating the full FY 2025 deficit) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-18 (inclusive) stating that the total federal budget deficit for Fiscal Year 2025 (October 2024 through September 2025) was $1.85 trillion or greater (i.e., $1,850 billion or more).

The primary source for this resolution is the official CBO website, specifically the Monthly Budget Review publications page (https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/monthly-budget-review). 

To resolve the question, the specific numerical value provided in the summary table for the FY 2025 total deficit (typically listed in billions of dollars) will be used. If the text and table differ, the table's exact figure will take precedence. If a range is provided rather than a point estimate, the midpoint of the range will be used. 

If the reported deficit is strictly less than $1,850 billion, the question resolves 'No'. 

If the CBO does not release its FY 2025 full-year deficit estimate between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-18 at 11:59 PM ET, the question will be considered unresolvable and should be canceled.
subquestions.rationale: The U.S. national debt is heavily influenced by the federal budget deficit. By the end of August 2025, the national debt topped $37 trillion, and the CBO projected a full-year FY 2025 deficit of $1.8 trillion. If the final FY 2025 deficit reported in early October exceeds expectations and hits $1.85 trillion or more, it implies that recent borrowing was higher than forecasted. This accelerated pace of debt accumulation serves as a strong leading indicator for whether the national debt will surpass the ultimate threshold of $38 trillion by the end of 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) CBO releases a Monthly Budget Review between Oct 1–18, 2025; (2) The reported FY2025 total federal deficit is $1,850 billion or more. Both conditions must be met simultaneously.

evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Condition 1 (CBO release within window): SATISFIED. The CBO released its Monthly Budget Review on October 8, 2025, within the Oct 1–18, 2025 window. subquestions.question: Will OpenAI officially announce plans to introduce advertisements into ChatGPT or its general-purpose GPT models between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05?

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question resolves only upon the actual integration and release of advertisements. Tracking whether an announcement is made by early January provides a strong early crux for forecasters: if OpenAI publicly confirms ad testing or plans in this window, the likelihood of a public rollout by March 31 increases dramatically.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: OpenAI makes an official public announcement (blog post, official X post, or C-level executive statement) explicitly confirming plans to integrate advertisements into ChatGPT or GPT models between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05. 'Exploring' or investigating does not qualify — confirmation of plans being actively tested or slated for release is needed.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'OpenAI ChatGPT advertisements ads announcement official' (Dec 6 - Jan 5); 2) 'OpenAI advertising plans GPT monetization 2025' (Dec 6 - Jan 5); 3) 'OpenAI official statement ads advertising ChatGPT spokesperson confirmation' (Dec 6 - Jan 5); 4) 'Sam Altman OpenAI ads advertising announcement December 2025' (Dec 6 - Jan 5); 5) 'OpenAI officially announce ads advertising plans confirmed January 2026' (Dec 6 - Jan 5); 6) 'OpenAI exploring what ads ads in our product official statement' (Dec 6 - Jan 5).

However, this statement describes exploration — not confirmed plans to integrate, active testing, or a slated release date. Multiple sources explicitly state 'OpenAI has not officially announced an advertising strategy.' evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence shows OpenAI is exploring advertising concepts internally, and an OpenAI spokesperson acknowledged this exploration with vague language ('exploring what ads in our product could look like'). subquestions.question: Will US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin hold an in-person meeting in Budapest, Hungary, between November 11, 2025, and December 11, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question concerns whether any major disruptive military or geopolitical events will occur by the end of 2025, including a "US-Russia nuclear deal" or "Ukraine agrees to give up the rest of Donbas." According to reports from mid-October 2025, US President Donald Trump announced plans to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Budapest, Hungary, facilitated by his relationship with Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban. During a meeting at the White House, Trump mentioned that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's attendance at this potential Budapest summit is "to be determined" (https://www.devdiscourse.com/). Furthermore, Russian President Vladimir Putin has publicly praised Trump's peace efforts and expressed a strong desire to extend the 2010 New START nuclear arms treaty, which Trump has reportedly called "a good idea" (https://www.pbs.org/). The New START treaty limits deployed nuclear weapons, and an extension or replacement is a critical component of US-Russia relations. An in-person meeting between Trump and Putin in Budapest would serve as a critical negotiating forum for both a nuclear arms treaty and the ongoing Ukraine war. Therefore, whether this meeting actually takes place in the near term is a strong early indicator of the likelihood of a US-Russia nuclear deal or a major territorial concession by Ukraine before the end of the year.

Sources:
Devdiscourse: https://www.devdiscourse.com/
PBS: https://www.pbs.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-11 (inclusive), US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin hold an in-person meeting in Budapest, Hungary. The meeting can be bilateral or part of a larger summit, provided both leaders are physically present in the same room and engage in a recognized diplomatic discussion or meeting. 

Resolution will be based on official press releases or statements from the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or the Kremlin (http://en.kremlin.ru/), or corroborated reporting from at least three major reliable news agencies (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/, AP News: https://apnews.com/). 

If the meeting is canceled, held exclusively in a city other than Budapest, or postponed such that it does not occur before the end of 2025-12-11, this question resolves No. Virtual, telephonic, or video-conference meetings do not qualify for a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: An in-person summit in Budapest between Trump and Putin is the likeliest venue for negotiating a US-Russia nuclear deal or a Ukraine peace agreement (such as one involving the concession of Donbas). If this planned meeting happens by December 11, it strongly increases the probability of one of the ultimate question's resolution conditions being met before December 31, 2025. If it does not occur, time will be running out for such complex geopolitical agreements to be reached before the ultimate question's deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) Trump and Putin physically present in the same room, (2) in Budapest, Hungary specifically, (3) between November 11–December 11, 2025, (4) engaging in a recognized diplomatic discussion. Evidence must come from White House/Kremlin press releases or corroborated reporting from at least three major news agencies.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump Putin meeting Budapest Hungary 2025' (Nov–Dec 2025) — to find any completed meeting. Query 2: 'Trump Putin summit in-person November December 2025' — to find any completed meeting. Query 3: 'Trump Putin Budapest meeting canceled November 2025' — to confirm cancellation. Query 4: 'Trump Putin actual meeting held December 2025' — to find any meeting that occurred.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) Trump canceled a planned Budapest meeting with Putin in October 2025 (around Oct 22, 2025) — BEFORE the question window; (b) Trump-Orban White House meeting on Nov 7, 2025, where Trump said there's 'very good chance' of future Budapest meeting — not a Trump-Putin meeting; (c) Putin-Orban meeting at Kremlin on Nov 28, 2025 — not Trump-Putin; (d) Putin met with Trump's envoy Witkoff and Jared Kushner at the Kremlin in Moscow on Dec 2, 2025 — in Moscow, not Budapest, and not Trump personally; (e) Kremlin stated on Dec 5, 2025 that a Putin-Trump meeting 'may take place in the near future.' evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event matches all criteria. The Budapest meeting was canceled by Trump in October 2025 before the question window. During the window: Trump and Putin never met in person in Budapest. Putin met Witkoff/Kushner in Moscow on Dec 2, 2025 — wrong location (Moscow not Budapest), wrong person (Witkoff not Trump). Multiple sources confirm no Trump-Putin in-person meeting in Budapest or elsewhere occurred during the window. [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/11/28/8009391/) confirms the Budapest meeting was cancelled by Trump on November 23, 2025 (for preparatory meetings), with no new meeting scheduled. [Kremlin](http://en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/78577) Nov 28 statement shows Putin only discussed potential future Budapest venue with Orban. [APA](https://en.apa.az/cis-countries/kremlin-says-a-putin-trump-meeting-may-take-place-in-the-near-future-485537) Dec 5 states a future meeting 'may take place' — not that it has occurred.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a Trump-Putin Budapest meeting because no such meeting occurred within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at any point in the window. The question resolves No.
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checked multiple sources: The Budapest summit was explicitly canceled (Oct 22, 2025). As of Dec 5, 2025, a future Putin-Trump meeting was still being discussed as future/hypothetical. No contradictory evidence suggests a Budapest meeting actually took place. evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition (Trump and Putin in-person meeting in Budapest between Nov 11–Dec 11, 2025) was definitively never met. question: NATO x Russia military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between September 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will NATO or any NATO member state officially announce a policy to intercept Russian aerial targets over Ukrainian territory between September 24, 2025, and October 24, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 9-10, 2025, a swarm of Russian drones entered Polish airspace during a bombardment of Ukraine, prompting Polish, Dutch, and Italian fighter jets to shoot down multiple drones over Poland (https://apnews.com/). This unprecedented incident marked the first time NATO forces directly engaged Russian munitions within allied airspace. Following the incursion, Poland invoked Article 4 of the NATO treaty, and the incident spurred urgent discussions about NATO's deterrence posture. According to policy experts, there have been growing calls for NATO to consider extending air-defense coverage into western Ukraine to intercept Russian drones and missiles before they breach allied borders (https://ecfr.eu/). Such a policy shift would actively involve NATO forces in the defense of Ukrainian airspace and has been framed as a vital step to enforce deterrence by punishment against Russia (https://cepa.org/).

Sources:
AP News: https://apnews.com/
European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR): https://ecfr.eu/
Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA): https://cepa.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-24 (inclusive), NATO as an organization or the national government of any NATO member state officially announces a policy, decision, or agreement to use its military forces to intercept, shoot down, or otherwise neutralize Russian missiles, drones, or aircraft while those targets are in Ukraine's internationally recognized airspace.

The announcement must be made publicly by an official government or military representative (e.g., a head of state, defense minister, or NATO Secretary General) and be available via credible media outlets or official government websites (such as the Polish Ministry of National Defence at https://www.gov.pl/web/national-defence or NATO's official press portal at https://www.nato.int/). Statements from anonymous sources, rumors, or unconfirmed leaks do not qualify.

The interception policy must explicitly authorize the targeting of Russian aerial assets over Ukraine. If the announcement only reaffirms authorizations for intercepts strictly within NATO airspace, or only involves donating air defense equipment to Ukraine without NATO personnel operating it, the question will not resolve Yes.

If no such official announcement is made between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-24 at 11:59 PM ET, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether there will be a direct military clash between NATO and Russia by the end of 2025. Extending NATO air defense to intercept targets over Ukraine would be a significant escalation, placing NATO operators in a direct combat role against Russian strike packages. This policy shift would heavily increase the risk of Russia retaliating against NATO air defense batteries or a NATO jet accidentally engaging a Russian manned aircraft. Therefore, an official announcement of this policy serves as a highly informative early indicator (crux) of an impending clash.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: NATO organization OR national government of any NATO member state officially announces a policy authorizing its military to intercept/shoot down Russian missiles, drones, or aircraft WHILE those targets are in Ukraine's internationally recognized airspace. Must be: (1) publicly stated by official government/military representative, (2) available via credible media or official government websites, (3) explicitly authorizing targeting over Ukraine (not just NATO airspace), (4) occurring between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-24 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'NATO member state intercept Russian missiles drones Ukraine airspace policy announcement' (Sept 24 - Oct 24, 2025). Query 2: 'NATO shoot down Russian aircraft missiles Ukraine territory official announcement 2025'. Query 3: 'Poland Germany France UK intercept shoot down Russian missiles drones OVER Ukraine territory authorization'. Query 4: 'NATO ministers Brussels October 2025 decision intercept Russian aerial Ukraine'. Query 5: 'close Ukrainian airspace NATO decision shoot down Russia over Ukraine October 2025'. Query 6: 'Poland Sikorski intercept missiles Ukraine airspace NATO collective decision October 2025'. Query 7: 'NATO official announcement policy intercept Russia missiles drones Ukrainian territory airspace 2025'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) NATO defense ministers meeting in Brussels Oct 15, 2025 - discussed rules of engagement for NATO airspace, not Ukraine airspace. (2) Lithuania easing drone shooting rules (Sept 28, 2025) - covers Lithuanian airspace only. (3) Poland shooting down drones over Polish airspace (Sept 10, 2025) - over Poland, not Ukraine. (4) NATO announcing 'Eastern Sentry' operation - covers NATO territory. (5) Zelensky proposing joint aerial defense shield (Sept 29, 2025) - proposal by Ukraine, not a NATO member government committing to act. (6) Poland FM Sikorski stating Poland WON'T intercept over Ukraine without NATO collective consent (Oct 10, 2025) - explicitly NEGATIVE evidence. ALL REJECTED as not meeting the key criterion of authorizing intercepts over Ukrainian territory.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that matches the resolution criteria. Key finding: [Poland FM Sikorski, TASS Oct 10 2025](https://tass.com/world/2028149) explicitly stated 'Poland will not intercept Russian missiles or drones over Ukraine without the collective approval of NATO.' The NATO Brussels defense ministers meeting ([Firstpost, Oct 15 2025](https://www.firstpost.com/world/amid-russian-incursions-nato-holds-meeting-to-discuss-shooting-russian-aircraft-ukraine-aid-13942379.html)) focused on standardizing rules for NATO airspace engagement, with no decision on Ukraine territory. The [Foreign Policy article, Oct 22 2025](https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/10/22/russia-poland-nato-drones-airspace-planes/) confirmed that NATO has failed to establish clear public rules of engagement and advocates for such rules — indicating they don't yet exist. All drone wall and aerial shield discussions pertained to NATO territory or future proposals, not current authorization over Ukraine.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with a timestamp exists within the window. The most relevant timestamp is Oct 10, 2025 (Sikorski statement that Poland WILL NOT act unilaterally over Ukraine), which constitutes negative evidence.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence found because no qualifying event occurred at any point during the window. The condition was never met.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) Reports about NATO/member states shooting down Russian targets all relate to NATO airspace (Poland, Lithuania, etc.), NOT Ukraine. (2) All discussions of intercepting over Ukraine were proposals FROM Ukraine or Ukrainian officials, not commitments from NATO/member state governments. (3) Poland's Sikorski explicitly confirmed the absence of such a policy when asked on Oct 10. (4) The October 15 NATO defense ministers meeting produced no such announcement. (5) The broader 'drone wall' is a future concept, not an immediate intercept authorization over Ukraine. No contradictory evidence found that would support a Yes resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Extensive search found no official announcement by NATO or any NATO member state government authorizing the interception of Russian aerial targets over Ukrainian territory between September 24 and October 24, 2025. All relevant announcements, policies, and discussions pertained to: (a) intercepting Russian aircraft over NATO member airspace, (b) future drone wall concepts, (c) proposals from Ukraine (not binding NATO commitments), or (d) explicitly excluded interception over Ukraine (Sikorski Oct 10). The window closed without the condition being met.

question: Will the EU impose new tariffs on US goods in 2025?
description:

Any tariff which is officially enacted within the market's time frame will qualify, regardless of when the tariff goes into effect.

subquestions.question: Will the European Commission formally propose new tariffs targeting the United States, or will an EU legislative body vote on such a proposal, between October 31 and November 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In August 2025, the U.S. and the EU reached a framework trade agreement wherein the U.S. applied a 15% tariff on most EU goods, and in return, the EU committed to eliminating tariffs on U.S. industrial goods. The U.S. continues to hold a 27.5% tariff on European automobiles as leverage until the EU enacts these legislative cuts. Tensions remain high due to unpredictable U.S. trade policies, including recent 10% global tariffs affecting over 60 countries. Within the European Union, implementing new tariffs requires a distinct, consensus-driven procedure. The European Commission must first formally propose the trade measure, which is then subject to approval by the member states. The EU maintains a policy of strategic autonomy and separates unilateral sanctions from standard tariff procedures. Given this bureaucratic timeline, any retaliatory or new tariffs fully enacted by the EU against the U.S. by the end of December 2025 would almost certainly need to be formally proposed by the European Commission, or actively voted on, weeks in advance. Therefore, tracking whether the Commission officially proposes tariffs targeted at the U.S. in November serves as a highly informative leading indicator for the ultimate outcome.

Sources:
U.S. and EU flesh out trade commitments under new framework deal: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-eu-flesh-out-trade-commitments-2025.html
US keeping lofty EU car tariffs until levies on American goods cut: https://nypost.com/2025/08/21/business/us-keeping-lofty-eu-car-tariffs-until-levies-on-american-goods-cut/
Tariffs not a cure-all: https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202510/16/WStariffs.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29 (inclusive), the European Commission formally adopts and publishes a legislative proposal, draft implementing act, or draft delegated act to impose new or increased tariffs (or customs duties) specifically targeting the United States. If such a proposal was already published prior to 2025-10-31, this question will also resolve Yes if the Council of the European Union or the European Parliament formally votes on or approves the proposal during the resolution window.

To qualify, the proposed measure must explicitly target imports originating from the United States. Proposals for global tariffs or safeguard measures applied to imports from all countries (such as the recently proposed EU global steel quotas) do not count.

The official action must be publicly announced via an official press release on the European Commission's Press Corner (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en), the Council of the EU's press page (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/), or published in the Official Journal of the European Union (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/oj/direct-access.html) during the resolution window.

subquestions.rationale: Because the European Union requires consensus among member states and a formal process to enact new tariffs, the European Commission must first issue a formal proposal, followed by legislative voting. Conversely, the absence of a proposal or vote makes it logistically difficult and politically unlikely for new tariffs to be fully enacted by the December 31 ultimate deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) The European Commission formally adopts and publishes a legislative proposal, draft implementing act, or draft delegated act to impose NEW OR INCREASED tariffs specifically targeting the United States between Oct 31 and Nov 29, 2025; OR (2) If such a proposal was already published before Oct 31, 2025, the Council of the EU or European Parliament formally votes on or approves such a proposal during the window. (3) Reports of EU concerns about US tariffs on steel/aluminum — EU was seeking relief, not imposing counter-tariffs. (4) General discussion of safeguard mechanisms in the trade deal — these are contingency measures, not new tariff proposals targeting US. All candidate events REJECTED because they involved the EU reducing tariffs on US goods or implementing a trade deal favorable to the US, not imposing new/increased tariffs on US imports. No evidence found of any formal EC proposal or Council/Parliament vote to impose new tariffs specifically targeting the United States.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Council of the EU action on November 28 [Consilium press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2025/11/28/eu-us-trade-relations-council-moves-forward-in-implementing-the-tariff-elements-of-the-joint-statement/) involved adopting negotiating mandates that ELIMINATE remaining customs duties on US industrial goods and REDUCE tariffs for certain US seafood and agricultural products — this is the opposite of imposing new tariffs on US goods. evidence.step7_verification: Verification confirms no qualifying event. All evidence consistently shows that during this period: (a) The EU and US had a trade agreement from July/August 2025 where the EU was committed to reducing tariffs on US goods; (b) The EU Council on Nov 28 voted to advance implementation by adopting negotiating mandates that eliminate tariffs on US industrial goods; (c) The EU was pressing the US to reduce tariffs on EU steel/aluminum, not imposing new tariffs on US goods; (d) EU concerns were about potential US violations of the trade deal, not about retaliating with new tariffs. The article about 'retaliatory measures' mentioned the possibility of reimposing suspended balancing measures as a threat if negotiations failed (from April 2025 context), but no such formal proposal was made during the Oct 31 – Nov 29 window. No contradictory evidence suggesting a formal proposal of new tariffs targeting the US was published.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution = No. The window closed on November 29, 2025 with no qualifying event. The entire EU-US trade dynamic during this period was focused on implementing and advancing the July/August 2025 trade deal which involved the EU REDUCING tariffs on US goods, not imposing new ones. subquestions.question: Will the U.S. government explicitly confirm or condemn the execution of any Iranian protesters between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-19?
subquestions.background_information:
In late 2025 and early 2026, nationwide protests erupted in Iran, reportedly triggered by economic hardship and followed by a severe security crackdown. By mid-January 2026, reports indicated nearly 2,600 deaths associated with the unrest. Amidst these tensions, U.S. President Donald Trump voiced support for the Iranian demonstrators, explicitly warning Tehran that the U.S. would take 'very strong action' if protesters are executed. Concurrently, the U.S. has advised some personnel at the Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar to evacuate or reposition, citing threats from Iranian forces. Because the U.S. administration has drawn a clear red line regarding the execution of protesters, official confirmation or condemnation of such executions by the U.S. government would serve as a strong leading indicator of impending military action or strikes against Iran.

The statement must explicitly acknowledge that the Iranian government has 'executed', 'hanged', or 'put to death' individuals in connection with the recent or ongoing nationwide protests. The statement must refer to the actual carrying out of the execution, not merely the handing down of a death sentence.

If no such qualifying statement or post is issued between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-19, the question will resolve 'No'. If a scheduled official press briefing or announcement regarding this specific matter is officially postponed beyond the resolution window, the question should be considered unresolvable. Delayed confirmations published after the resolution window will not count toward a 'Yes' resolution. In the event that the primary websites are down, official archives or widely reported video evidence of such press briefings (e.g., C-SPAN) may be used as fallback criteria.

U.S. Department of State Press Releases: https://www.state.gov/press-releases/

subquestions.question: Will a poll published by the Public Policy Institute of California (PPIC) or UC Berkeley IGS between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 show support for California Proposition 50 at 50% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
California's Proposition 50 is a legislatively referred constitutional amendment on the November 4, 2025 ballot. The measure would allow the state legislature to temporarily replace the state's independent redistricting commission and redraw congressional maps for the 2026, 2028, and 2030 elections (Los Angeles Magazine, https://lamag.com). A Berkeley IGS poll conducted August 11-17, 2025, found that 48% of registered voters supported the measure, 32% opposed it, and 20% were undecided (Medium, https://medium.com). Whether the "Yes" campaign can cross the majority threshold in leading independent state polls leading up to the election is a crucial early indicator of its ultimate passage. The Public Policy Institute of California (PPIC) and UC Berkeley's Institute of Governmental Studies (IGS) are California's premier nonpartisan polling organizations.

Medium: https://medium.com

Berkeley IGS: https://igs.berkeley.edu/igs-poll/current-and-past-polls

This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the Public Policy Institute of California (PPIC) or the UC Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies (IGS) officially publishes a statewide poll regarding the November 2025 special election, and the topline result for Proposition 50 (or the referenced 'redistricting constitutional amendment') shows 50.0% or higher support (e.g., 'Yes', 'Favor', or 'Support').

Specific conditions:
- The support level will be evaluated based on the primary sample reported in the poll's headline, press release, or executive summary (e.g., Likely Voters if reported; if not, Registered Voters).
- The required threshold is 50.0%. If the poll reports integer percentages, 50% counts as Yes. If decimals are provided, it must be 50.0% or higher (e.g., 49.8% resolves No).
- If multiple qualifying polls are published by these organizations within the timeframe, the question resolves Yes if AT LEAST ONE poll meets or exceeds the 50.0% threshold.
- If neither organization publishes a poll explicitly asking about Proposition 50 within the resolution window, or if no such poll reaches the 50.0% threshold, the question resolves No.
- Delayed events: If a poll is announced or conducted in the timeframe, but the results are published after 2025-10-01, it will not count towards resolution.

Data sources to be used for resolution:
- Official releases on PPIC's website (https://www.ppic.org/polling/)
- Official releases on Berkeley IGS's website (https://igs.berkeley.edu/igs-poll/current-and-past-polls)
subquestions.rationale: Polling is the most direct indicator of voter sentiment for state ballot measures. A mid-August Berkeley IGS poll showed support at 48%, slightly below the majority needed for passage but with 20% undecided. If a highly-rated California pollster demonstrates that support has crossed the critical 50% threshold by October, it would serve as a robust crux indicating that the "Yes" campaign is capturing sufficient undecided voters, heavily increasing the probability that the referendum ultimately passes on November 4.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: PPIC or UC Berkeley IGS publishes a statewide poll between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) showing ≥50.0% support for California Proposition 50 (redistricting constitutional amendment) in the November 2025 special election. Observable evidence: press release or published poll results from ppic.org or igs.berkeley.edu showing topline support ≥50% for Prop 50. Key entities: PPIC, UC Berkeley IGS. Threshold: 50.0%. 'California November 2025 special election redistricting constitutional amendment poll' (Sept 1-Oct 1) - to find any qualifying polls; 4. 'UC Berkeley IGS poll 48 percent support September 2025' - to identify the specific IGS poll and when it was published; 5. 'Berkeley IGS poll DiCamillo Proposition 50 August September 2025 results' - to identify the timing of the Berkeley poll; 7. 'Berkeley IGS poll September 2025 new California proposition 50 redistricting survey released' - to find any NEW Berkeley poll in window; 8. 'PPIC Public Policy Institute California poll Proposition 50 redistricting survey results' (Aug-Oct 15) - to find any PPIC poll.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: Berkeley IGS poll showing 48% support — conducted Aug 11-17, published ~Aug 22, 2025 (The Hill, Aug 22). This is BEFORE the September 1 window. REJECTED as outside window. Candidate event 2: Multiple September 2025 articles reference the SAME August Berkeley IGS poll (48%) — not a new poll. REJECTED as not a new poll within window. The Newsweek article [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/california-redistricting-proposition-50-10832504) confirms 'UC Berkeley's Institute of Governmental Studies found slightly lower support at 48% in August 2025.' Times survey' showing a closer race but does not report new ≥50% IGS numbers. No criteria-matching event found.

subquestions.question: Will a fourth round of direct peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine be officially announced or commence before the end of November 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Direct peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine have seen intermittent progress throughout 2025. Following a highly publicized summit between U.S. and Russian leaders in Alaska, a third round of direct talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations was held in Istanbul on July 23, 2025. These talks addressed political, military, and humanitarian issues, including the transfer of deceased soldiers' bodies and prisoner exchanges. Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky stated that the occurrence of a fourth round of negotiations would depend on the implementation of these agreements. However, as of October 2025, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin claimed the positive momentum was fading and that Ukraine was not serious about making a deal, although communication lines remain open. At the same time, diplomatic pressure regarding territorial swaps has intensified; Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the Donetsk region, while Ukraine continues to hold a pocket of territory in Russia's Kursk Oblast. For any diplomatic agreement to be reached where Ukraine cedes the Russian territory it controls by the end of December 2025, formal negotiations must resume.

Sources:
TASS (Russian News Agency): https://tass.com/politics
Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
Euractiv: https://www.euractiv.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a fourth round of direct peace negotiations (or an equivalent formal bilateral peace summit) between official delegations of the Russian Federation and Ukraine is officially announced OR officially commences between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive).

- The negotiations must involve official government delegations from both Russia and Ukraine meeting either in-person or in a formally organized, officially recognized online session aimed at a peace settlement or territorial agreement.
- Routine low-level communications, prisoner exchanges, or working groups strictly limited to humanitarian issues (such as body transfers) do not qualify, unless they are explicitly designated by both parties as part of a formal resumption of peace negotiations or a comprehensive peace negotiation framework.
- If the talks are announced before 2025-10-31, the question will only resolve Yes if the talks actually commence between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30.
- If the talks are announced between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 but are scheduled for a date after 2025-11-30, the question will still resolve Yes, as the milestone of an official announcement within the window was met.
- Official confirmation must come from the Ukrainian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://mfa.gov.ua/en), the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://mid.ru/en/), or an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting from major news outlets (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/, AP News: https://apnews.com/).
subquestions.rationale: For Ukraine to officially agree to cede Russian territory in Kursk as part of a diplomatic agreement by December 31, 2025, formal diplomatic negotiations between Russia and Ukraine must take place. Following the third round of direct talks in July 2025, negotiations stalled. The announcement or commencement of a fourth round of talks in November 2025 would serve as a critical leading indicator that a comprehensive peace or territorial deal is actively being negotiated, significantly increasing the probability of a 'Yes' resolution on the ultimate question. Conversely, if no formal negotiations are announced or held by November 30, the timeline for reaching a finalized agreement by the end of December becomes highly improbable.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official announcement OR commencement of a fourth round of direct bilateral peace negotiations between official Russian and Ukrainian delegations, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30. Must be formal bilateral peace negotiation framework, not prisoner exchanges, multilateral meetings, or indirect talks.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Russia Ukraine peace negotiations fourth round 2025' — to find any fourth round; 2) 'Russia Ukraine direct talks peace summit November 2025' — to find bilateral meetings; 3) 'Ukraine suspends peace talks Russia Istanbul fourth round announcement' — to find suspension events; 4) 'Russia Ukraine bilateral direct negotiations official delegation November 2025' — to find any official bilateral contacts; 5) 'Zelensky Turkey Istanbul visit Russia Ukraine talks November 19 2025' — to assess Zelensky Turkey visit; 6) 'Ukraine Russia direct meeting Umerov Medinsky peace negotiations November 2025' — to find any direct bilateral meeting.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Turkey's offer to host fourth round (Nov 1) — rejected: Turkey's offer, not an official announcement from Russia/Ukraine. (2) Ukraine's official suspension of talks (Nov 12) — relevant as negative evidence. (3) Russia's claimed readiness to resume Istanbul talks (Nov 12) — rejected: unilateral signal only, Ukraine suspended and didn't accept. (4) Zelensky's Turkey visit (Nov 19) — rejected: Russia explicitly declined to attend per Kremlin confirmation. (5) Geneva talks (Nov 23-24) — rejected: explicitly US-Ukraine-Europe only, Russia did NOT participate. (6) Ukrainian decree establishing delegation for talks 'with Russia' (Nov 22/28) — does not indicate actual commencement of bilateral talks. (7) Ukrainian delegation to US (Nov 29-30) — rejected: US-Ukraine meeting, not bilateral Russia-Ukraine.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No identified event satisfies the criteria of a direct bilateral Russia-Ukraine peace negotiation. The Geneva talks ([Reuters via ukrinform.net](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/4062020-new-round-of-negotiations-on-peace-plan-between-ukraine-us-europe-begins-in-geneva.html)) were explicitly US-Ukraine-Europe, with Russia absent. The Turkey visit ([TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2045069)) confirmed 'Russia will not participate in talks with Ukraine scheduled for November 19, 2025, in Istanbul.' Ukraine officially suspended talks per [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2042933) and [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/ukrainian-deputy-foreign-minister-says-kyiv-suspended-peace-talks-with-russia/3742359). A US-Russia meeting was planned for 'early next week' after Nov 27, meaning after the November 30 window closes per [RT](https://www.rt.com/russia/628550-no-russia-us-deal-ukraine-putin/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Ukraine's official suspension of talks: November 12, 2025 (18:02 per TASS). No bilateral Russia-Ukraine peace negotiations commenced or were officially announced within the window. No qualifying event timestamp exists for a Yes resolution.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying bilateral Russia-Ukraine fourth round peace negotiation was found at any point in the October 31–November 30, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Ukraine's decree appointing delegation for talks 'with Russia and the US' does not constitute commencement or announcement of bilateral Russia-Ukraine talks. The Geneva talks were explicitly multilateral (US-Ukraine-Europe) and Russia did not attend. Multiple sources confirm no direct Russia-Ukraine bilateral meeting occurred in this period: 'no formal negotiations have taken place between Ukrainian President Zelensky and Russian President Putin as of November 25, 2025' ([agcnews.eu](https://www.agcnews.eu/ukrainerussiawar-accordi-di-pace-in-alto-mare-il-27-novembre-putin-termina-visita-in-kirghizstan-pokrovsk-e-circondata-manovra-di-accerchiamento-per-lyman/)). German Chancellor Merz noted 'the next step must be: Russia must come to the table' on Nov 24, indicating Russia had NOT yet joined talks.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly confirms that no fourth round of direct bilateral Russia-Ukraine peace negotiations was officially announced or commenced between October 31 and November 30, 2025. Ukraine formally suspended the Istanbul process on November 12. Russia signaled readiness but Ukraine declined. The Geneva talks (Nov 23-24) were US-Ukraine-Europe only — Russia was absent. Zelensky's Turkey visit (Nov 19) also excluded Russia. The Ukrainian delegation traveled to the US (Nov 29-30) for US-Ukraine talks, not bilateral Russia-Ukraine talks. The planned US-Russia meeting was scheduled for after November 30. The question therefore resolves No. The window closed on November 30 with no qualifying event having occurred or been announced.
