subquestions.question: Will a federal lawsuit be filed by Lisa Cook, the Federal Reserve, or the Trump administration regarding Cook's removal from the Federal Reserve Board before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 26, 2025, President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that he had fired Federal Reserve Board member Lisa Cook, citing "gross negligence" and "potentially criminal" actions related to alleged mortgage fraud. Cook and her legal team stated she will not resign and that Trump lacks the authority to remove her, as Federal Reserve governors can only be removed "for cause" under the Federal Reserve Act. The Fed indicated it might pursue legal action to prevent the president's "attempted illegal action" (The Independent, https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-lisa-cook-federal-reserve-b2601718.html). Because Trump has also heavily criticized Fed Chair Jerome Powell, the legal and political fallout from his attempt to fire Cook serves as a direct precedent. The outcome of this standoff—specifically whether it escalates into a formal court battle—will act as a strong indicator of Trump's willingness and legal capability to challenge the Fed's independence and potentially target Powell next.

Sources:
CBS News - https://www.cbsnews.com/
The Independent - https://www.independent.co.uk/
Mediaite - https://www.mediaite.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), a lawsuit or formal legal complaint is filed in a United States federal court by Lisa Cook, the Federal Reserve (or its representatives), Donald Trump, or the US federal government (e.g., the Department of Justice) that explicitly seeks to enforce, block, or clarify the legal status of Lisa Cook's removal from the Federal Reserve Board of Governors. The filing must be docketed within this exact time window. Resolution will be determined by reviewing official federal court dockets via the Public Access to Court Electronic Records (PACER) system (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/) or through a consensus of credible reporting from major financial and political news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, https://www.bloomberg.com/; Reuters, https://www.reuters.com/). If no such lawsuit is docketed between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 at 11:59 PM ET, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The unprecedented attempt to remove Governor Lisa Cook is a clear test of the president's power to fire independent Fed officials "for cause." If the dispute escalates into a formal lawsuit within the next month, it demonstrates that Trump's administration is actively litigating the boundaries of Fed independence, increasing the probability he will formally move against Jerome Powell. Conversely, if no legal action is taken and the firing remains a social media statement without legal enforcement, it signals a lower probability that Trump will take formal, legally binding action to fire Powell.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: A lawsuit or formal legal complaint filed between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) in a US federal court by Lisa Cook, the Federal Reserve, Donald Trump, or the US federal government that explicitly seeks to enforce, block, or clarify the legal status of Lisa Cook's removal from the Federal Reserve Board. The filing must be docketed within that exact window. Key entities: Lisa Cook, Federal Reserve, Trump administration/DOJ. Key threshold: filing must be docketed in the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve removal lawsuit federal court' (Sept 1 - Oct 1 2025) - to find lawsuits within the window; 2) 'Lisa Cook Trump fired Federal Reserve Board Governor' (July-Oct 2025) - to find background and initial filing dates; 3) 'Lisa Cook lawsuit filed date August 28 federal court DC' - to confirm the filing date of the original lawsuit; 4) 'Trump administration DOJ Supreme Court application Lisa Cook September 2025' - to find Trump admin filings in the window; 5) 'Lisa Cook lawsuit filed August 28 docketed federal court DC' - to confirm pre-window filing
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Lisa Cook filed lawsuit in US District Court for DC on August 28, 2025 - REJECTED as outside window (before September 1). (2) Cook's lawyers filed additional civil action/filings on September 3, 2025 - within window, but these appear to be supplemental filings/briefs in the existing case, not new lawsuits. (3) Trump administration filed with DC Court of Appeals requesting stay on approximately September 11-15, 2025 - within window, emergency stay applications in existing case. (4) DOJ/Solicitor General filed emergency application with the US Supreme Court on September 18, 2025 - within window, filed by US federal government (DOJ), in a US federal court (SCOTUS), explicitly seeking to enforce Cook's removal.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria states the filing must be by 'Lisa Cook, the Federal Reserve (or its representatives), Donald Trump, or the US federal government (e.g., the Department of Justice)' and must 'explicitly seek to enforce, block, or clarify the legal status of Lisa Cook's removal.' The DOJ/Solicitor General's September 18, 2025 Supreme Court application ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/18/trump-supreme-court-lisa-cook-fed.html), [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5510206-trump-supreme-court-fed/), [Louisiana Illuminator](https://lailluminator.com/2025/09/18/repub/federal-reserve-cook/)) was filed by the US federal government's DOJ/Solicitor General in the US Supreme Court (a federal court) and explicitly sought to lift the injunction blocking Cook's removal - directly seeking to enforce the legal status of Cook's removal. This matches the criteria. Additionally, the Trump administration filed with the DC Circuit Court on September 11 and 15, 2025 ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/11/trump-lisa-cook-fed-lawsuit-fomc.html), [The Federalist](https://thefederalist.com/2025/09/15/rests-on-a-series-of-legal-errors-trump-admin-appeals-court-order-blocking-removal-of-fed-governor-lisa-cook/)) - also within the window and matching the criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Trump administration's Supreme Court application was filed on September 18, 2025, as reported by multiple sources including CNBC ('The Trump administration has filed an application with the Supreme Court'), The Hill ('On September 18, 2025, the Justice Department asked the Supreme Court'), and Louisiana Illuminator ('On September 18, 2025, the Trump administration filed a 41-page appeal with the U.S. Supreme Court'). The DC Circuit appeals were filed approximately September 11 and 15, 2025. All within the September 1-October 1 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying filing within the September 1-October 1 window by any named party was the Trump administration's filing with the DC Court of Appeals around September 11, 2025 (Trump filed a stay request with the Court of Appeals, as confirmed by CNBC on September 11). evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Lisa Cook's original lawsuit was filed August 28 - before the window - but the resolution criteria is broad enough to encompass subsequent filings by any named party within the window. No contradictory evidence found suggesting these filings didn't occur. The resolution criteria does not require a 'new' lawsuit - it requires 'a lawsuit or formal legal complaint' that seeks to 'enforce, block, or clarify the legal status of Lisa Cook's removal.' The Trump administration's SCOTUS application qualifies.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Yes. Multiple filings within the September 1-October 1, 2025 window satisfy the resolution criteria. The Trump administration/DOJ filed emergency applications in the DC Circuit Court of Appeals (around September 11-15, 2025) and the US Supreme Court (September 18, 2025), all explicitly seeking to enforce Cook's removal by lifting court-ordered injunctions blocking it. These are formal legal filings by the US federal government in US federal courts explicitly seeking to enforce/clarify the legal status of Cook's removal. The earliest qualifying filing within the window appears to be around September 3, 2025 (Cook's attorneys' additional filing), followed by the Trump administration's September 11 DC Circuit filing. The first occurrence within the window was Cook's attorneys' September 3 filing (supplemental civil action), though the Trump administration's September 11 and 18 filings also independently qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the daily closing market capitalization of either Apple (AAPL) or Microsoft (MSFT) exceed that of Nvidia (NVDA) on any trading day between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13?
subquestions.background_information:
Nvidia has seen unprecedented growth due to its dominance in AI hardware. As of September 30, 2025, Nvidia reached a record market capitalization of $4.53 trillion, securing its position as the world's most valuable company, ahead of Apple and Microsoft. For Nvidia to finish the year as the second-largest company by market cap, it would need to be surpassed by at least one of its major rivals (most likely Apple or Microsoft). The tech sector often experiences significant volatility around quarterly earnings reports, and both Apple and Microsoft typically report earnings in late October. Tracking whether either company can temporarily or permanently overtake Nvidia in market cap during the mid-October to mid-November window provides a clear indicator of the competitive dynamics and Nvidia's likelihood of dropping to the number two spot by the end of December.

Sources:
Yahoo Finance NVDA: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA
Yahoo Finance AAPL: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL
Yahoo Finance MSFT: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MSFT
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

(AAPL) or Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) is strictly greater than the daily closing market capitalization of Nvidia Corporation (NVDA) on any regular U.S. stock market trading day between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 (inclusive). 

The resolution will be based on the official daily closing market capitalization data provided by Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MSFT) as of the close of regular trading (4:00 PM ET). Intraday market cap fluctuations do not count; only the final closing value for the day is considered. In the event of data discrepancies or if Yahoo Finance is unavailable, alternative credible financial data providers such as YCharts (https://ycharts.com) or standard Bloomberg terminal data will be used as a fallback. If neither Apple nor Microsoft closes with a higher market cap than Nvidia during the defined period, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For Nvidia to resolve as the 'second-largest' company at the end of the year, it must relinquish its current position as the largest company. If Apple or Microsoft overtakes Nvidia in market cap between mid-October and mid-November (a period often catalyzed by Q3 earnings reports), it proves Nvidia's lead is vulnerable, significantly increasing the probability that Nvidia might finish the year in the number two spot. Conversely, if Nvidia maintains its lead through its rivals' earnings season, its chances of remaining the largest company through year-end are much higher.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: AAPL closing market cap > NVDA closing market cap OR MSFT closing market cap > NVDA closing market cap on any trading day between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 inclusive. question: GOP uses 'Nuclear Option' to break filibuster by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US Senate passes a motion to invoke cloture and end debate on any part of the legislative process, with such a cloture motion receiving Yea votes from fewer than three-fifths of the Senators by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve "No".

Confirmations are considered part of the Senate’s “advice and consent” function, not part of the Senate’s “legislative process,” and will therefore not count towards this market's resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the U.S. government.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Senate successfully invoke cloture on a government funding bill with 60 or more Yea votes between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. federal government is currently in a shutdown that has lasted at least 21 days as of late October 2025, tying it for the second-longest in history (https://baynews9.com). In response to the legislative deadlock, several House Republicans, such as Rep. Chip Roy and Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, have called for the Senate to invoke the "nuclear option"—changing Senate rules to bypass the 60-vote filibuster threshold and pass a Continuing Resolution (CR) with a simple majority (https://thehill.com, https://easternprogress.com). While Senate Republicans recently used the nuclear option in September 2025 to streamline the confirmation of Trump administration executive nominees (https://washingtontimes.com), Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Speaker Mike Johnson have thus far opposed using it for legislation, with Thune warning that the legislative filibuster "makes the Senate the Senate" (https://baynews9.com).

The ultimate question is whether the GOP will eliminate the legislative filibuster by December 31, 2025. If the Senate is able to reach a bipartisan agreement and invoke cloture on a funding bill with the standard 60 votes by November 30, the immediate shutdown crisis will be resolved conventionally, significantly lowering the odds of the nuclear option being deployed for legislation this year. Conversely, if no such 60-vote threshold is met, the continuing shutdown will maximize pressure on GOP leadership to change the rules.

Sources:
Spectrum News Bay News 9: https://baynews9.com
The Hill: https://thehill.com
Washington Times: https://washingtontimes.com
Eastern Progress: https://easternprogress.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the U.S. Senate holds a successful roll call vote to invoke cloture on a bill, joint resolution, or continuing resolution that provides appropriations for the federal government, and the cloture motion receives 60 or more "Yea" votes, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive).

The primary resolution source will be the official U.S. Senate roll call vote tracker (https://www.senate.gov/legislative/votes_new.htm). 

The legislative item in question must provide continuing or regular appropriations to fund federal government operations (e.g., a Continuing Resolution or a regular appropriations bill). Cloture votes on other unrelated legislation do not count towards resolution.

If no such successful cloture vote with 60 or more Yea votes occurs on a funding bill between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, the question resolves "No". Furthermore, if the funding dispute is resolved via unanimous consent, a voice vote, or by the Senate invoking the nuclear option (which would allow cloture to be invoked with fewer than 60 votes), this question will also resolve "No".
subquestions.rationale: The primary catalyst right now for potentially using the legislative nuclear option is the ongoing government shutdown. If the Senate successfully invokes cloture on a funding bill with the standard 60 votes, it demonstrates that a bipartisan consensus was reached, removing the immediate crisis pushing the GOP to change the legislative filibuster rules. This event would heavily update forecasters toward a 'No' on the ultimate question. Alternatively, a failure to reach 60 votes implies either a prolonged shutdown or a procedural rule change, increasing the probability of a 'Yes' outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The U.S. Senate must hold a successful roll call cloture vote on a government funding/appropriations bill with 60+ Yea votes between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), NOT via unanimous consent, voice vote, or nuclear option. Observable evidence: official roll call vote record showing 60+ Yea votes on a cloture motion for a continuing resolution or appropriations bill. Key entities: U.S. Senate, H.R. 5371, cloture motion. Threshold: exactly 60 or more Yea votes.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Senate cloture vote government funding bill November 2025' — to find any cloture votes on funding bills; Query 2: 'Senate continuing resolution appropriations cloture 60 votes 2025' — to confirm 60-vote threshold met; Query 3: 'Senate cloture HR 5371 November 9 2025 roll call 60 votes' — to confirm specifics of vote; Query 4: 'Senate cloture H.R. 5371 continuing appropriations bill exact date time November 2025' — to extract precise timestamp.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Primary candidate: Cloture vote on H.R. 5371 (Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act) on the night of November 9, 2025, resulting in a 60-40 vote. This vote is confirmed by multiple independent sources (Al Jazeera, ABA Banking Journal, JD Supra, National Law Review, Gateway Pundit, Coinspeaker, Townhall, Santa Fe New Mexican). Earlier failed cloture attempts (November 4: 54-44; earlier on November 9: 54-44) are rejected as they did not reach the 60-vote threshold. A second qualifying cloture vote on November 16 also passed 60-40 per the Santa Fe New Mexican 'How they voted' article, but the first occurrence on November 9 is the controlling event.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: ✅ Successful cloture vote: 60-40 [ABA Banking Journal](https://bankingjournal.aba.com/2025/11/senate-takes-first-step-to-end-government-shutdown/); ✅ Government funding bill: H.R. 5371 is 'Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act' [JD Supra](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/senate-advances-funding-bill-to-end-1619210/); ✅ 60+ Yea votes: exactly 60 Yea, 40 Nay [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/10/us-senate-shutdown-vote-what-happened-who-voted-to-end-it-whats-next); ✅ Within window: November 9, 2025 is between October 31 and November 30, 2025; ✅ Standard roll call (not unanimous consent, voice vote, or nuclear option): nuclear option was rejected by Thune [NewsMax](https://www.newsmax.com/newsfront/senate-filibuster-obamacare/2025/11/05/id/1233322/), vote was a standard 60-vote cloture roll call.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Gateway Pundit article states 'Senator John Cornyn cast the final vote shortly after 10:45 p.m.' on November 9, 2025. Multiple sources describe this as a 'late-night Senate vote on November 9, 2025.' Converting 10:45 PM ET to UTC: approximately 2025-11-10T03:45:00Z. This is the most precise timestamp available from reported sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Earlier cloture attempts on H.R. 5371 on November 4 (54-44) and earlier on November 9 (54-44) both FAILED to reach 60 votes. The November 9 late-night vote (60-40) is the first successful cloture vote with 60+ Yea votes on a government funding bill within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent, high-quality sources (Al Jazeera, ABA Banking Journal, JD Supra, National Law Review, Coinspeaker, Santa Fe New Mexican) all consistently report the same outcome: 60-40 cloture vote on H.R. 5371 on November 9, 2025. No contradictory evidence found. Nuclear option was explicitly NOT used. The vote was a standard 60-vote roll call cloture. H.R. 5371 is explicitly a government funding/appropriations bill (continuing appropriations + three full-year appropriations bills). The bill's purpose (funding federal government operations) unambiguously satisfies the resolution criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. Senate successfully invoked cloture on H.R. 5371 (Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act) by a 60-40 roll call vote on the night of November 9, 2025 (approximately 10:45 PM ET / 2025-11-10T03:45:00Z UTC). This vote is the first occurrence of a successful 60+ vote cloture on a government funding bill within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window. All resolution criteria are satisfied. Resolution: YES.

question: Will the federal government be shut down for 10–29 days in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve according to how many days the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announces that the U.S. federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse in appropriations by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM.

Days are counted based on notices checked at 10:00 AM ET each day. If the Office of Personnel Management announces a partial shutdown, this will count; however, announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather will not qualify. 

If there are multiple government shutdowns during the relevant period, this market only applies to the first shutdown, as the market will resolve after the end of the first shutdown. Notices of emergency furloughs or impacted government operations count toward the shutdown days.  

If no shutdown occurs during the period, this market will resolve to "No shutdown".

The resolution source for this market will be the website of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. President sign a Continuing Resolution (CR) or other appropriations legislation into law between September 17, 2025 and September 30, 2025, to avert an October 1 government shutdown?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. fiscal year ends on September 30, 2025. Congress must pass new appropriations to fund the federal government for Fiscal Year 2026. According to the National Law Review, as of early September 2025, lawmakers are behind schedule: the Senate has passed only three of twelve appropriations bills, and the House only two. If a Continuing Resolution (CR) or other comprehensive funding legislation is not signed into law by midnight on September 30, 2025, a partial federal government shutdown will occur starting October 1, 2025. A shutdown would furlough hundreds of thousands of non-essential federal employees and suspend non-essential operations. Prediction markets have recently shown a 43% chance of a government shutdown by the end of 2025, highlighting the severe risk of political gridlock. This subquestion focuses on whether Congress and the President can successfully enact a stopgap or permanent funding measure before the deadline.

Sources:
Over 43% chance of U.S. government shutdown in 2025: Polymarket (TheStreet) - https://www.thestreet.com/
When could a government shutdown occur? How would it affect you? (Aol) - https://www.aol.com/
Potential Outcomes If Congress Misses the Federal Funding Deadline (The National Law Review) - https://www.natlawreview.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a Continuing Resolution (CR) or any other comprehensive appropriations legislation that provides funding for the federal government past October 1, 2025, is signed into law by the President of the United States on or before 11:59 PM ET on September 30, 2025. 

The legislation must prevent a lapse in appropriations for all regular federal agencies on October 1, 2025. The overall resolution window during which qualifying events and confirmation can occur is between the subquestion start date of 2025-09-17 and the end date of 2025-10-02.

The primary resolution sources will be the official legislation tracker on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/) and official statements from the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/legislation/).

If the President signs qualifying legislation funding the government past October 1, 2025 within the specified window, the question resolves Yes. If the deadline of 11:59 PM ET on September 30, 2025 passes without such legislation being signed, triggering a lapse in appropriations for the start of the fiscal year, the question resolves No. If legislation is passed by Congress but not signed by the President by the 11:59 PM ET September 30 deadline, it does not count and the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The failure to pass a funding bill by September 30 is the direct trigger for an October 1 shutdown. If a bill is signed into law, an October 1 shutdown is averted, which significantly reduces the probability of a 10-29 day shutdown occurring in 2025 (though a shutdown could theoretically happen later if a CR expires in late 2025). Conversely, if no bill is signed, a shutdown begins immediately, drastically increasing the likelihood that the ultimate 10-29 day shutdown threshold will be met.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: U.S. President signs a CR or comprehensive appropriations legislation funding the federal government past October 1, 2025, on or before 11:59 PM ET on September 30, 2025. Observable evidence: White House signing statement, Congress.gov bill signing record, contemporaneous news reporting of a signed bill. Key entities: President Trump, Senate (needed 60 votes), House (passed H.R. 5371 on September 19 by 217-212). Key timing: 11:59 PM ET September 30, 2025 (= 2025-10-01T03:59:00Z).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Continuing Resolution signed law government shutdown October 2025' — to find evidence of a signing event; 2) 'government shutdown October 1 2025 averted funding' — to check if shutdown was averted; 3) 'Trump signs continuing resolution appropriations bill September 30 2025' — direct evidence of signing; 4) 'government shutdown ended reopened funding bill signed October 2025' — to check if shutdown ended quickly after October 1.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) House passed H.R. 5371 (clean CR through November 21) on September 19, 2025 — REJECTED as qualifying event because it was not signed into law. (2) Senate voted 55-45 on September 30 to reject H.R. 5371 — confirms no signing. (3) Senate also rejected Democratic alternative — confirms no signing. (4) OMB directed agencies to 'execute plans for an orderly shutdown' on September 30/October 1 — confirms no signing before deadline. (5) Government entered shutdown at 12:01 AM ET October 1, 2025 — explicitly confirms deadline passed without qualifying legislation signed.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple high-quality sources confirm no CR or appropriations legislation was signed by President Trump before the September 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET deadline. [TimesNow](https://www.timesnownews.com/world/us/us-news/us-government-shutdown-2025-what-is-a-continuing-resolution-article-152924791): 'The United States government entered a partial shutdown at 12:01 AM on Wednesday, October 1, 2025, after the Senate failed to pass a funding measure.' [Newsmax/OMB Memo](https://www.newsmax.com/politics/omb-memo-government/2025/09/30/id/1228516/): OMB Director Russell Vought directed agencies to 'execute their plans for an orderly shutdown,' confirming no bill was signed. [Reuters via JP](https://jp.reuters.com/world/us/PQI7KPQ3JBMNZAHYBR6BLYRNBE-2025-10-01/): 'On October 1, 2025, a partial shutdown of U.S. government agencies began due to a failure by Congress and the White House to reach an agreement on a temporary funding bill.' [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/senate/3830473/senate-dueling-funding-bills-government-shutdown-midnight/): Senate rejected both the Republican CR (55-45) and the Democratic alternative (47-53) on September 30, setting up midnight shutdown. None of these events constitutes a signing of legislation; all confirm the opposite.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The definitive No moment is 11:59 PM ET September 30, 2025 = 2025-10-01T03:59:00Z, when the funding deadline passed. The shutdown was confirmed to have begun at 12:01 AM ET October 1, 2025 = 2025-10-01T05:01:00Z. The OMB memo was issued on September 30/October 1, explicitly stating funding 'will expire at 11:59 p.m. on September 30, 2025.' These timestamps are explicit and reliable.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying signing event was found. The House passed H.R. 5371 on September 19, but the Senate never passed it, so the President had no bill to sign. The resolution window opened September 17, 2025, and no qualifying signing occurred at any point before the deadline.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence (late-breaking signing, last-minute deal): None found. All sources — including Reuters, The Hill, Washington Examiner, AP, Newsmax, OAN, and dozens of others — confirm the government shut down at midnight October 1, 2025. The OMB explicitly directed agencies to prepare for shutdown. Senate votes on both September 30 and October 1 failed to reach the 60-vote threshold. No source reports any bill being signed by the President before the deadline. The shutdown was still ongoing as of October 2, 2025 (within the resolution window), with no end-of-shutdown legislation signed.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The U.S. President did not sign any Continuing Resolution or appropriations legislation into law before 11:59 PM ET on September 30, 2025. The government entered a shutdown at 12:01 AM ET on October 1, 2025, confirmed by multiple high-quality news sources. The Senate failed twice (September 30 and October 1) to advance the House-passed CR with the needed 60 votes. The definitive No moment is 2025-10-01T03:59:00Z (11:59 PM ET September 30, 2025), when the deadline passed.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) publicly announce it is withholding or delaying the release of any Epstein-related documents citing an ongoing investigation between November 30, 2025, and December 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
President Donald Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act into law on November 20, 2025, which legally obligates the Department of Justice to release all unclassified investigative materials related to Jeffrey Epstein by December 19, 2025 (https://www.chicagotribune.com). This release is expected to include FBI reports, witness transcripts, flight logs, and internal communications. Although the law forbids redactions intended solely to protect the reputations of public figures, the DOJ retains the authority to withhold files if their release would jeopardize an active investigation (https://globalnews.ca). Attorney General Pam Bondi recently launched a new investigation into Epstein's associates and political adversaries, which could serve as a justification for the DOJ to temporarily delay or withhold significant portions of the files (https://www.pbs.org). Prediction markets and the public are heavily speculating on which high-profile names, including Michael Jackson, will appear in the new documents, though Jackson was previously named in earlier releases without allegations of wrongdoing (https://www.financialexpress.com). The completeness of the December document dump is central to whether novel information about Jackson will be published.

Sources:
Global News - The Epstein files: What to know ahead of their release (https://globalnews.ca)
PBS - 7 things to know about the Justice Department's Epstein files (https://www.pbs.org)
Chicago Tribune - What to know about the Justice Department's Jeffrey Epstein files (https://www.chicagotribune.com)
The Financial Express - Epstein Files: From Elon Musk to Leonardo DiCaprio (https://www.financialexpress.com)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), the Attorney General, or an official spokesperson for the DOJ publicly announces or confirms in a legal filing, press release, or public statement that it is withholding or delaying the release of one or more documents related to Jeffrey Epstein, specifically citing an ongoing or active investigation as the reason, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-15 (inclusive). The announcement must occur within this specified time window. A general statement that the DOJ 'might' withhold documents does not count; the DOJ must affirmatively state that they are withholding or delaying specific documents, a category of documents, or the entire release due to an ongoing investigation (such as the newly launched probe by Attorney General Pam Bondi). If the release is delayed or withheld for other reasons (e.g., technical difficulties, privacy redactions of victims) without citing an ongoing investigation, this question resolves No. If the deadline passes without any such announcement, it resolves No. Delayed events: if the DOJ makes this announcement after 2025-12-15, it will not count toward resolution and the question resolves No. Authoritative sources for resolution include official DOJ press releases (https://www.justice.gov/news/press-releases) and court filings via PACER (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/), supplemented by credible reporting from major news outlets such as the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/).
subquestions.rationale: The Epstein Files Transparency Act mandates the release of all unclassified Epstein files by December 19, 2025. The ultimate question resolves Yes if Michael Jackson is named in newly released files by December 31, 2025. A major crux for this outcome is whether the DOJ will fully comply with the December 19 deadline or use exceptions to withhold documents. The recently announced investigation by AG Pam Bondi provides a legal mechanism for the DOJ to withhold materials. If the DOJ announces it will withhold documents due to this active investigation before December 15, the scope of the new document release will be significantly reduced or delayed, heavily decreasing the likelihood that novel documents naming Michael Jackson will be released by the end of the year. Conversely, no such announcement strongly implies the impending release of the full corpus of documents.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: The DOJ/AG/official spokesperson must publicly announce (in press release, legal filing, or public statement) that it is AFFIRMATIVELY withholding or delaying specific Epstein documents, citing an ONGOING or ACTIVE investigation as the specific reason. The announcement must occur between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-15 (inclusive). A general statement that DOJ 'might' withhold does not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'DOJ Department of Justice withholding Epstein documents ongoing investigation 2025' (Nov 30–Dec 15) — to find direct DOJ announcements. 2) 'Epstein files release delay DOJ announcement December 2025' — to find any delay announcements. 3) 'DOJ Pam Bondi announce withholding Epstein files active investigation December 2025' — to find Bondi statements. 4) 'DOJ statement Epstein documents withheld ongoing investigation Bondi press release' — to find official statements. 5) 'DOJ officially announces withholding Epstein files investigation December 2025' — broader search. 6) 'Epstein files DOJ court filing withhold delay active investigation SDNY December 2025' — to find court filings. 7) 'DOJ Bondi affirmatively states withholds Epstein documents active investigation announcement' — explicit statement search. 8) 'Epstein files DOJ Maxwell retrial withhold FOIA exemption 7A investigation announcement' — alternative withholding basis.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) DOJ cited FOIA Exemption 7(A) / Maxwell retrial possibility as reason to withhold records — this occurred before the window as part of prior proceedings. (2) NYMag article (Dec 12) says the DoJ 'has invoked' the active investigation exception — this is analytical/commentary, not a DOJ press release or official announcement. (3) Legal experts (Lisa Rubin on Dec 3, law professor) warned DOJ COULD use investigation as pretext — these are experts speaking, not DOJ officials. (4) USA Today (Dec 11) noted 'concerns remain' that DOJ may invoke exceptions — speculation, not an affirmative DOJ announcement. (5) DOJ spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre only 'confirmed receipt' of a congressional letter and 'declined further comment' — not an affirmative withholding announcement. (6) DOJ was actively REQUESTING courts to unseal records during this window (Florida approved Dec 5, Maxwell case approved Dec 9, Epstein 2019 case ordered Dec 12) — the DOJ's posture during the window was toward release, not withholding. All candidates rejected as not meeting the criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of the DOJ making an affirmative, explicit public announcement that it IS withholding specific Epstein documents citing an active investigation during Nov 30–Dec 15, 2025. The [AOL article](https://www.aol.com/articles/epstein-island-photos-released-maxwell-221915214.html) notes 'The Justice Department cited the possibility of a retrial as a reason to withhold records under FOIA Exemption 7(A)' but this is contextual background from prior proceedings. The [NYMag article](https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/what-you-will-and-wont-find-in-the-epstein-file-dump.html) states 'the DoJ has invoked' the active investigation exemption, but this is analytical commentary without citing a specific DOJ press release or official statement within the window. The [Alternet/Rubin article](https://www.alternet.org/lisa-rubin-epstein-trump/) features a legal expert warning this COULD happen — not an official DOJ statement. The [AP article](https://apnews.com/article/epstein-justice-department-trump-fbi-files-7b7e45b283a8344b05f3a47640a960ae) describes what the DOJ is releasing, not withholding. Criteria not met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. The DOJ's actions during this window were toward releasing documents (seeking court orders to unseal in Florida and New York), not officially announcing withholding citing an active investigation.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: During the window, the DOJ actively sought to unseal grand jury records in Florida (approved Dec 5), the Maxwell case (approved Dec 9), and Epstein's 2019 case (ordered Dec 12). This posture is inconsistent with an affirmative withholding announcement. While analysts and legal experts speculated that the DOJ MIGHT use the active investigation exception as a pretext, no explicit DOJ public statement or court filing within the window confirms this. The DOJ spokesperson declined to comment on the congressional letter rather than making an announcement. The window closes December 15, before the December 19 filing deadline, meaning any formal withholding announcement (if it came at all) would more likely have occurred at or after the deadline.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is NO. Within the Nov 30–Dec 15, 2025 window, the DOJ did not publicly announce it was affirmatively withholding or delaying specific Epstein-related documents citing an ongoing investigation. The DOJ's actual posture was to seek court orders to unseal records. While legal experts and commentators speculated that the DOJ COULD invoke the active investigation exception, no explicit DOJ announcement, press release, or court filing to that effect was found within the window. The window ended December 15, before the December 19 statutory deadline, so any such announcement would be expected to come at or after that deadline (if at all).

question: U.S. Government funding lapse on October 1?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a U.S government funding lapse occurs on October 1, 2025, 12:00 AM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A funding lapse is defined as the President failing to sign the relevant bill(s) extending government funding by September 30, 11:59 PM ET. If a bill extending the funding of the U.S. government is passed and signed by the acting President before October 1, 2025, 12:00 AM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes" any funding lapse will count. If only a portion of the US government is covered by any signed bill(s) extending funding of the US government, and a portion of the US government goes unfunded, this market will still resolve to "Yes".

The primary resolution for this source will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass a continuing resolution (CR) or any bill extending federal government funding beyond September 30, 2025, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26?
subquestions.background_information: Congress faces a September 30 deadline to pass funding legislation for the new fiscal year beginning October 1, 2025, or face a partial government shutdown. As of late August 2025, the House has passed only a few appropriations bills, and a stopgap continuing resolution (CR) is expected to be necessary to avoid a lapse in funding (https://thehill.com). Democratic leaders Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries recently sent a letter to GOP leaders urging immediate 'four corners' negotiations for a stop-gap measure. Furthermore, Representative Steve Womack noted that the chances for a shutdown are very high given the few session days remaining (https://talkbusiness.net). Passing a CR or a funding package in the House is a crucial step; if the House has not passed any funding extension by September 26, the timeline to get a bill through the Senate and signed by the President before October 1 becomes extremely tight, significantly increasing the probability of a shutdown. Sources: The Hill (https://thehill.com), Talk Business & Politics (https://talkbusiness.net), Military Times (https://www.militarytimes.com).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes a bill that extends funding for the federal government (such as a Continuing Resolution or an omnibus appropriations package covering the majority of federal agencies) for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2025, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26 (inclusive). Passage must occur before 11:59 PM ET on September 26, 2025. Resolution will be determined by official roll call vote or voice vote records from the Office of the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives (https://clerk.house.gov/Votes) or Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov). To qualify, the bill must be specifically intended to prevent a lapse in appropriations on October 1, 2025 (e.g., providing funding past September 30, 2025). If no such bill is passed by the House between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26, the question resolves No. If passage is delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A funding bill must be passed by both chambers of Congress before being signed by the President. If the House passes a funding extension by September 26, the chances of avoiding a shutdown increase substantially because the legislative process is moving forward. If they fail to do so, the timeline to avert an October 1 shutdown becomes extremely compressed, making this a strong early indicator.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The U.S. House of Representatives must pass (by roll call or voice vote) a bill extending federal government funding beyond September 30, 2025, between September 1-26, 2025 (inclusive, before 11:59 PM ET September 26). Observable evidence: official vote record showing House passage of a CR or omnibus covering majority of federal agencies for FY2026. Key entities: U.S. House of Representatives, bill number, vote count, date.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'House of Representatives continuing resolution government funding September 2025' — to find any CR passage; 2. 'government shutdown continuing resolution CR vote September 2025' — to find shutdown-related votes; 3. 'House vote HR 5371 continuing resolution September 19 2025 roll call' — to find specific bill and vote details; 4. 'House passed continuing resolution government funding October 2025 before September 19' — to check for earlier qualifying events.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Primary candidate: House passage of H.R. 5371 (clean continuing resolution) on September 19, 2025, vote 217-212, extending federal funding through November 21, 2025. Rejected candidate: Procedural vote on September 17 (216-210) — this was only to advance debate/open floor consideration, not to pass the CR itself. No earlier House passage of a CR extending funding past September 30 was found in the September 1-18 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: H.R. 5371 explicitly matches all criteria: (1) It is a Continuing Resolution [WacoTrib](https://wacotrib.com/news/nation-world/government-politics/article_25e81cc7-6ba9-59a6-8564-9539763093dc.html); (2) It extends funding through November 21, 2025 — past September 30, 2025 [HotAir](https://hotair.com/john-s-2/2025/09/19/house-passes-bill-to-avoid-government-shutdown-n3806975); (3) It was passed by the U.S. House of Representatives [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/house-passes-trump-backed-plan-avert-government-shutdown); (4) Vote was 217-212 by roll call [E&E News](https://www.eenews.net/articles/congress-leaving-for-recess-with-no-deal-to-avoid-shutdown/); (5) Date: September 19, 2025 — within the September 1-26 window; (6) Specifically intended to prevent lapse in appropriations on October 1, 2025 [Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/2025/09/house-passes-short-term-continuing-resolution/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Date: September 19, 2025. Multiple sources explicitly state 'On September 19, 2025, the House passed...' The vote occurred on a Friday (confirmed by multiple articles referencing 'Friday'). Exact time of vote not specified in articles, but the date September 19, 2025 is unambiguous and within the resolution window (September 1-26, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier House passage of a CR extending government funding past September 30, 2025 was found between September 1-18, 2025. The September 17 vote (216-210) was a procedural vote to advance debate (rule vote), not passage of the CR itself. This is confirmed by the Epoch Times article: 'The House of Representatives advanced a measure on September 17 that will open debate on a continuing resolution.' The September 19 vote is the first and only qualifying House passage in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: None found. All 7+ independent sources (Fox News, WacoTrib, HotAir, E&E News, Breaking Defense, Epoch Times, Dallas Morning News, KOLOTV) agree the House passed the CR on September 19, 2025. The Senate's subsequent rejection (September 19-20) does not affect the resolution criteria, which only requires House passage. The bill clearly covers the majority of federal agencies (it is a government-wide CR). The question only asks about House passage, not enactment into law.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R. 5371, a clean continuing resolution extending federal government funding through November 21, 2025 (past September 30, 2025), on September 19, 2025, by a roll call vote of 217-212. This falls squarely within the September 1-26, 2025 window. All resolution criteria are satisfied. Resolution: Yes.

question: 5kt meteor strike in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a natural meteoroid (bolide) explodes in Earth's atmosphere with a total impact energy greater or equal to 5 kilotons of TNT equivalent between May 28, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The object must be classified as a natural meteoroid; events involving artificial objects or reentry vehicles do not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/. The relevant field for determining impact energy is the “Impact Energy (kt)” column. If this dataset has not been updated to include all relevant dates by February 28, 2026, or if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository becomes permanently unavailable, this market may resolve based on a consensus of credible sources including the European Space Agency (ESA), the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN), the U.S. Department of Defense, or credible reporting of a scientific consensus, such as a NASA press release.

subquestions.question: Will the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository record at least 3 distinct fireball events occurring between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Fireballs and bolides are exceptionally bright meteors resulting from meteoroids entering Earth's atmosphere. NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) maintains a public repository of these events (https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/), documenting their date, time, and calculated impact energy. The frequency of smaller, detectable meteor events acts as a proxy for the baseline influx of meteoroids and the current sensitivity of Earth's detection networks. On average, the CNEOS database logs approximately 30 to 40 fireball events annually, which equates to roughly 2 to 4 events per month. For example, recent news highlighted a 1.6 kiloton fireball over southern Japan on August 19, 2025, demonstrating ongoing active detections (https://watchers.news). Because meteoroid sizes roughly follow a power-law distribution, an increased or average baseline count of smaller fireballs can indicate whether Earth is passing through higher-density debris fields, which provides context for the likelihood of a much larger (≥5 kt) meteor impact later in the year.

Sources:
NASA JPL Fireball Database: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/
Watchers News (August 2025 Event): https://watchers.news
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository (https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/) records at least 3 distinct fireball events with a 'Date/Time (UT)' occurring between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive of both dates). The events must be officially listed in the 'Date/Time (UT)' column of the database. The resolution will be based on the data available on the CNEOS repository as of the end of the resolution window. If the NASA JPL repository is permanently unavailable or not updated by the end date, the question may resolve based on a consensus of credible alternatives tracking the same metrics, such as the European Space Agency (ESA) or the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN). Events involving artificial objects or space debris do not count toward this total.
subquestions.rationale: Forecasting the ultimate outcome of a 5 kt impact depends heavily on understanding the current rate of meteoroid influx and the operational reliability of atmospheric detection networks. Tracking the general count of smaller fireball events over a one-month window serves as an observable, near-term metric for baseline meteoroid activity without simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline or tighter energy constraint. A healthy detection rate indicates that sensor systems are online and functioning normally, while a potential spike could indicate a dense debris stream.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition: At least 3 distinct fireball events recorded in NASA JPL CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data repository (cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/) with 'Date/Time (UT)' between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). subquestions.question: Will the COMEX Gold Continuous Contract (GCW00) close below $4,000 per troy ounce on any trading day between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI officially announce definitive agreements to restructure away from its non-profit board control by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
OpenAI is currently attempting to restructure its unusual corporate setup—where a non-profit board controls a capped-profit entity—into a more conventional for-profit or public benefit corporation. According to reports, this structural transition is a prerequisite for CEO Sam Altman to be granted an equity stake. Currently, Altman holds no direct equity in OpenAI and earns an annual salary of $76,001 (https://fortune.com/2025/08/21/openai-sam-altman-equity-salary-most-valuable-startup/). 

In August 2025, news surfaced that OpenAI was negotiating a new contract with Microsoft that could shift its 2026 restructuring plan, aiming to replace the existing profit-sharing structure with traditional equity ownership for investors (https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/08/40546555/whats-going-on-with-microsoft-stock-wednesday-microsoft-nasdaqmsft). Reuters has previously reported that Altman would receive his equity grant following the completion of this nonprofit-to-for-profit restructuring. Given the legal and regulatory complexities (including approvals from state attorneys general), finalizing the restructuring agreements is the main bottleneck. Tracking whether this is agreed upon in October provides a crucial indicator of whether Altman can legally receive equity before the end of 2025.

Sources:
Fortune: https://fortune.com
Benzinga: https://www.benzinga.com
Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if OpenAI publicly announces, or if a consensus of credible top-tier financial reporting (e.g., Reuters [https://www.reuters.com], Bloomberg [https://www.bloomberg.com], or The Wall Street Journal [https://www.wsj.com]) confirms that OpenAI has formally signed definitive agreements to restructure its corporate entity to remove its non-profit board control in favor of a standard for-profit or public benefit corporate structure. 

The announcement or confirming reports must occur between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z (inclusive). 

The restructuring does not need to be fully finalized, closed, or legally cleared by regulators within this window, but the definitive agreements among key stakeholders (like Microsoft and the OpenAI board) must be explicitly reported as 'agreed upon' or 'signed'. If no such announcement or definitive reporting occurs within the specified resolution window, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Sam Altman currently does not hold equity, and reports indicate that he will only receive an equity grant after OpenAI restructures its non-profit governance model into a for-profit framework. Because completing a corporate restructuring takes time, achieving definitive agreements in October 2025 is a critical milestone if Altman is to receive his equity by December 31, 2025. If the restructuring is significantly delayed past October, the likelihood of an equity grant happening within 2025 drops precipitously.

evidence.step1_decompose: The resolution criteria requires: (1) OpenAI publicly announces OR credible top-tier financial reporting confirms (2) formally signed definitive agreements (3) to restructure to REMOVE non-profit board control (4) in favor of a standard for-profit or public benefit corporate structure, (5) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. The critical phrase is 'remove its non-profit board control.'
evidence.step2_search_queries: (1) 'OpenAI restructure non-profit board for-profit definitive agreement 2025' — to find core event; (2) 'OpenAI corporate restructuring announcement October 2025' — to find timing and details; (3) 'OpenAI restructure public benefit corporation non-profit foundation board control October 28 2025' — to verify board control status; (4) 'OpenAI Microsoft definitive agreement signed restructuring Reuters Bloomberg WSJ October 2025' — to find top-tier source confirmation; (5) 'OpenAI non-profit foundation retains control board appoints directors PBC structure October 2025' — specifically to check whether non-profit board control was removed or retained.
evidence.step3_event_detection: On October 28, 2025, OpenAI announced restructuring into a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) called 'OpenAI Group PBC.' Microsoft and OpenAI signed a 'new definitive agreement' (explicitly stated by Benzinga, Investing.com, connect.de, Business Insider). Multiple top-tier sources (AP, Reuters via Investing.com, WSJ as cited in Korean outlet Chosun) confirmed the signed agreement on October 28, 2025. However, crucially, multiple sources also confirm the OpenAI Foundation (the renamed nonprofit) RETAINS control over the PBC, specifically retaining the right to appoint all board members. This is a critical fact that affects criteria matching.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria explicitly requires removal of non-profit board control. However: [AP](https://apnews.com/article/openai-chatgpt-nonprofit-microsoft-c661df3242766d6b0ddbab401ad1fd84): 'converting into a public benefit corporation while remaining under the control of its nonprofit parent'; [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/openai-restructuring-company-structure-chatgpt-invest-own-rcna240138): 'the nonprofit will have special voting and governance rights to appoint all members of the for-profit's board'; [Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/10/28/business/openai-restructures-for-profit-company/): 'original nonprofit, which retains control via its board'; [Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/openai-and-microsoft-sign-agreement-to-restructure-openai-into-a-public-benefit-corporation-with-microsoft-retaining-27-percent-stake-non-profit-open-ai-foundation-to-oversee-open-ai-pbc): 'non-profit OpenAI Foundation to oversee OpenAI PBC'; [Winbuzzer](https://winbuzzer.com/2025/10/29/openai-eyes-ipo-after-securing-californias-blessing-for-corporate-restructuring-xcxwbn/): 'the nonprofit retaining control of the board.' The restructuring created a PBC structure BUT the non-profit Foundation retains the power to appoint all PBC board members. This does NOT satisfy the resolution criteria of removing non-profit board control.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The restructuring announcement was made on October 28, 2025 — within the resolution window (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-31). The exact timestamp from multiple sources is October 28, 2025. This is within the window, but the criteria matching fails.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event (i.e., no prior announcement of signed definitive agreements to remove non-profit board control) was found. October 28, 2025 is the first and only relevant announcement. However, the event does not satisfy the criteria because it retained rather than removed non-profit board control.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find evidence that non-profit board control was removed: All sources consistently confirm the opposite — the OpenAI Foundation retains board appointment rights. Even critics arguing the nonprofit's control is 'illusory' (Public Citizen's Weissman) acknowledge the formal structure retains nonprofit governance. The LessWrong analysis notes 'the nonprofit's power to hire and fire directors is weakened by board overlap' but still formally exists. The restructuring moved from a capped-profit nonprofit hybrid to a PBC where the nonprofit Foundation owns equity and retains board appointment power — a shift in legal form but not elimination of non-profit board control. The resolution criteria specifically requires 'remove its non-profit board control,' which was not achieved.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The definitive agreements signed on October 28, 2025 are within the resolution window and were reported by credible top-tier sources. However, the agreements restructured OpenAI into a PBC while RETAINING non-profit board control (the OpenAI Foundation appoints all PBC board members). The resolution criteria requires removing non-profit board control. Since the non-profit Foundation explicitly retains the power to appoint all board members of the new PBC, the specific condition of 'remove its non-profit board control' was not met. The question resolves No.

subquestions.question: Will the prosecution formally demand a prison sentence of 5 years or more for Kim Keon Hee in her corruption trial by January 2, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:

Under South Korean criminal procedure, a trial concludes with a final hearing where the prosecution summarizes its case and officially requests a specific sentence (a procedure known as 'guyhyeong'). Given the severity of the charges, which include violating the Capital Markets Act and the Political Funds Act, she faces potentially lengthy prison time, with reports indicating she could face sentences of 5 years or longer (https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/). 

A sentencing demand of 5 years or more by the prosecution would signal a strong case for significant prison time, increasing the likelihood of a guilty verdict and a prison sentence. Because a judge's verdict typically follows the prosecution's demand by two to four weeks, a final hearing held by early January 2026 is a crucial milestone for ensuring the actual sentencing occurs well before the ultimate March 31, 2026 deadline.

This makes a guilty verdict and a prison sentence highly likely to happen well before the ultimate question's March 31, 2026 deadline. Conversely, a delayed final hearing or a lenient sentencing demand would lower the probability of her receiving a prison sentence by the target date.

One such potential candidate is Michael Anton, a former senior national security official who served in the first Trump administration.

If Michael Anton is to be appointed by the December 31, 2025 deadline, it is highly likely his name will be surfaced by major political reporting outlets as being on the shortlist or under consideration. Tracking these leaks and reports provides a verifiable, early indicator of whether Anton is seriously in the running before the ultimate appointment is made.

subquestions.question: Will the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) adopt a resolution authorizing or establishing a multinational stabilization force for the Gaza Strip before November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

To monitor the implementation of the agreement, the U.S. deployed roughly 200 military personnel to Israel to form a Civil-Military Coordination Center. Concurrently, discussions are actively underway to deploy an international stabilization force into Gaza. U.S. and European officials have advanced a UN Security Council draft resolution to establish this international stabilization force under Egyptian leadership, while Arab nations are pushing for a UN mandate to define the legal authority of the broader mission. Although the U.S. currently maintains that American troops will not physically enter Gaza, the establishment of an official UN-mandated force architecture—co-managed by U.S. coordination cells in Israel—would dramatically alter the military landscape. Monitoring whether the UNSC successfully passes such a resolution provides critical insight into how quickly the international military framework in Gaza will be established, which is a necessary precursor for any potential U.S. military entry (e.g., for oversight, emergency response, or engineering support) before the end of 2025.

ynetnews: https://www.ynetnews.com/
News18: https://www.news18.com/

To resolve Yes, the adoption of the resolution must occur within the specified time window (between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30) and be officially documented on the UN Security Council's Resolutions page (https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/content/resolutions-0) or confirmed by an official UN press release (https://press.un.org/en/content/security-council).

The text of the adopted resolution must explicitly mention Gaza or the Gaza Strip and the establishment, authorization, or endorsement of a multinational or international military/stabilization force. It is not required that the United States directly contributes troops to this specific force under the resolution.

If a draft resolution is proposed but vetoed, or otherwise fails to be adopted by the UNSC within the resolution window, it will not count towards a Yes resolution. If no qualifying resolution is adopted by 11:59 PM UTC on November 30, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A UN Security Council resolution authorizing an international force in Gaza is a critical precursor to the deployment of foreign militaries into the territory. While current diplomatic plans exclude U.S. troops from entering Gaza directly, the formal establishment of a multinational force—especially one coordinated by the newly deployed U.S. military personnel in Israel—increases the likelihood of U.S. regular forces eventually crossing into Gaza for logistical, engineering, or emergency support. Conversely, if no such UN mandate is passed by the end of November, the stabilization effort may stall, severely reducing the conditions under which U.S. forces would enter Gaza by the end of 2025.

Resolution identified as 2802 (2025) by UN News. No candidate events were rejected — all sources are consistent. An earlier draft was circulated on November 4, 2025, but this was not yet a resolution. Vote was held at 5:00 PM New York time on November 17, 2025.

evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: November 17, 2025, at 5:00 PM New York time (22:00 UTC), as confirmed by UN News pre-vote announcement and multiple post-vote confirmations. This is within the resolution window (2025-10-31 to 2025-11-30).

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. government publish a formal proposal, Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, or Notice of Inquiry in the Federal Register regarding semiconductor tariffs or domestic-to-import chip ratios between October 24, 2025, and November 23, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: In August and September 2025, President Trump frequently threatened to impose a 100% tariff or a fairly substantial tariff on imported semiconductors, aiming to force companies to build manufacturing plants in the U.S. Alternatively, the Commerce Department, under Secretary Howard Lutnick, has reportedly weighed a plan requiring a 1:1 domestic-to-imported chip ratio, penalizing non-compliant companies with tariffs. However, enacting such tariffs usually requires formal administrative procedures, such as a Section 232 investigation by the Commerce Department or a Section 301 investigation by the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR), both of which involve publishing formal notices and allowing for public comment. Tracking whether a formal administrative process is initiated in the Federal Register is a crucial early indicator of whether the administration is on track to enact legally sound tariffs by December 31, 2025. Sources: Economic Times (https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/), Malay Mail (https://www.malaymail.com/), Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. government publishes a formal document (such as a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, Notice of Inquiry, or official Request for Comments) in the Federal Register that explicitly proposes, investigates, or outlines a structure for tariffs or import quotas/ratios specifically targeting semiconductors. This publication must occur between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23 (inclusive). The primary resolution source will be the official Federal Register website (https://www.federalregister.gov/). The search will specifically look for documents issued by the Department of Commerce, the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR), or the Executive Office of the President. General tariffs (e.g., across-the-board tariffs on all goods from a country) do not count; the notice must specifically highlight semiconductors or related integrated circuits. If the administration bypasses the notice-and-comment process and enacts an Executive Order directly enforcing the tariff within this window, the question will also resolve Yes provided the Executive Order is published in the Federal Register between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23. Otherwise, if no such qualifying document is published in the stated window, it resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks if tariffs will be enacted by the end of 2025. Standard federal rulemaking and trade investigations require a notice and comment period, which typically must be initiated months in advance. If the administration intends to formally enact these tariffs through standard regulatory frameworks by December 31, a formal notice must appear in the Federal Register by late November. If no such notice appears by November 23, forecasters should update towards a No on the ultimate question, as it implies a lack of necessary administrative groundwork.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) A formal government document (NPRM, ANPRM, Notice of Inquiry, Request for Comments, or Executive Order) published in the Federal Register between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23 (inclusive); (2) The document must specifically target semiconductors or related integrated circuits (not general tariffs); (3) The document must be issued by DOC, USTR, or the Executive Office of the President; (4) It must propose, investigate, or outline a structure for tariffs OR import quotas/ratios specifically targeting semiconductors.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Federal Register semiconductor tariffs Notice of Proposed Rulemaking 2025' (Oct 24-Nov 23) — to find qualifying publications; Query 2: 'semiconductor chip tariffs Executive Order Federal Register October November 2025' (same range) — to find EO-based resolution; Query 3: 'Section 232 semiconductor tariff notice inquiry rulemaking Department of Commerce October November 2025' — to find Section 232-specific filings; Query 4: 'semiconductor tariffs 300% Federal Register publication formal notice 2025' — to find high-profile chip tariff notices; Query 5: 'chip tariff ratio domestic import Federal Register NPRM ANPRM notice inquiry Commerce USTR 2025' — to find ratio-related rulemaking; Query 6: 'semiconductor tariff on hold delayed no formal notice rulemaking November 2025' — to find evidence of NON-resolution.

No Federal Register publication found. REJECT — No qualifying publication. REJECT — Pre-existing investigation, no new Federal Register notice. (C) U.S.-China trade deal (Oct 30-Nov 2, 2025): Federal Register statement on pausing tariffs published (as referenced by TASS) — but this concerns general tariff pauses, NOT a proposal for semiconductor-specific tariffs. REJECT — Not a semiconductor-specific tariff proposal; also reduces tariffs rather than proposes them. (D) FCC FNPRM seeking input on semiconductors (Oct 2025): FCC issued a 'Second Report and Order and Second Further Notice of Proposed Rulemaking' seeking input on extending a national security ban to components 'such as semiconductors, firmware, and optical transceivers.' However, this is an FCC supply-chain security measure, not a tariff/import quota proposal from DOC/USTR/Executive Office, and is not about tariffs on chip imports. REJECT — Wrong agency (FCC, not DOC/USTR), wrong subject matter (supply chain security, not import tariffs). REJECT — Not a qualifying Federal Register publication. evidence.step8_final_decision: Based on comprehensive searching, no formal Federal Register publication (NPRM, ANPRM, Notice of Inquiry, or Executive Order) specifically targeting semiconductor tariffs or domestic-to-import chip ratios was published between October 24 and November 23, 2025. subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of the Treasury officially announce a partnership or contract with a cryptocurrency exchange, custodian, or blockchain infrastructure provider between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?

To execute this, they partnered with blockchain infrastructure providers and major cryptocurrency exchanges (Coinbase, Gemini, and Kraken) to purchase digital currency for network transaction fees, also known as gas (https://bravenewcoin.com/). Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick indicated this model would eventually expand to the entire federal government (https://www.business-standard.com/). The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. Treasury will officially send funds or assets via a blockchain by the end of 2025. Because the Treasury does not currently have established infrastructure to directly send cryptocurrency natively, entering into a partnership or vendor agreement with a crypto exchange, wallet provider, or infrastructure company is a necessary precursor. Sources: Decrypt (https://decrypt.co/), Business Standard (https://www.business-standard.com/), Brave New Coin (https://bravenewcoin.com/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of the Treasury officially announces a partnership, contract, or formal agreement with a cryptocurrency exchange, digital asset custodian, or blockchain infrastructure provider between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The announcement must be made via an official press release on the U.S. Treasury website (https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases) or formally announced by a verified Treasury representative, such as the Secretary of the Treasury. The partnership must be for the purpose of facilitating blockchain operations, digital asset custody, or on-chain transactions. Mere exploratory committees or research papers without a specific vendor partnership do not count. Announcements made by other departments that explicitly include the Treasury as a joint partner in contracting the vendor will count. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, or no such announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The Commerce Department recently utilized crypto exchanges to pay gas fees for on-chain data publishing, signaling the administration's willingness to use third-party crypto vendors. For the Treasury to send funds or assets on a blockchain in an official, non-exploratory capacity, they will likely need to formalize a similar vendor relationship to custody or transmit those assets. An official partnership announcement serves as a direct, highly informative leading indicator that the Treasury is building the operational capacity required to trigger the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: U.S. Department of the Treasury (not SEC/CFTC/other agencies) officially announcing (via home.treasury.gov press release or verified Treasury representative) a partnership/contract/formal agreement with a crypto exchange, digital asset custodian, or blockchain infrastructure provider between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, specifically for the purpose of blockchain operations, digital asset custody, or on-chain transactions. Regulatory rulemakings, exploratory committees, and research papers do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'U.S. Treasury Department cryptocurrency exchange partnership contract 2025' (general search for Treasury-crypto partnerships). 2. 'Treasury Department blockchain digital asset custodian agreement announcement' (custodian-specific search). 3. 'Treasury Department strategic Bitcoin reserve custody Coinbase Anchorage Fireblocks contract award' (custody contract search). 8. 'US Treasury GENIUS Act stablecoin cryptocurrency exchange formal agreement vendor September 2025' (GENIUS Act vendor agreements).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) US-UK Transatlantic Taskforce for Markets of the Future (Sept 22, 2025) - Treasury co-chairs with UK Treasury, involves crypto industry representatives but is an intergovernmental regulatory task force, not a vendor contract. REJECTED - purely regulatory rulemaking, no vendor contract. (3) H.R. 5166 Strategic Bitcoin Reserve feasibility mandate - Congressional mandate for Treasury to study Bitcoin reserve. REJECTED - study/feasibility report, not an announced partnership. (4) Existing US Marshals Service/Coinbase Prime custody relationship mentioned in one article. REJECTED - pre-existing arrangement, no new Treasury announcement in window. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate events match the required criteria. The US-UK Transatlantic Taskforce [Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-uk-digital-asset-task-force-regulation) is an intergovernmental regulatory coordination body—not a contract with a private crypto exchange or infrastructure provider. The GENIUS Act ANPRM [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2025/09/19/u-s-treasury-takes-next-step-in-turning-genius-act-into-stablecoin-regulations) is a regulatory rulemaking process seeking public comment—not a vendor agreement. Resolution: No.

subquestions.question: Will any sovereign nation officially announce a quantified troop or financial commitment to the Gaza International Stabilization Force (ISF) between January 5 and January 13, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:

The plan includes the establishment of a "Board of Peace" to govern Gaza and a 20,000-member Temporary International Stabilization Force (ISF) to handle security and demilitarization. While the US expects to unveil the Board of Peace soon, establishing the ISF is a critical prerequisite for the Board's operational success. The US has ruled out deploying American troops and has been actively negotiating with nations including Indonesia, the UAE, Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey for troop and financial contributions. Initially, the formal announcement of the Board of Peace was expected around late December 2025 during a meeting between President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. Given that we are now in early January 2026, formalizing troop and financial commitments from international partners is a key indicator of whether the overarching peace plan and the Board of Peace are moving forward toward implementation or stalling due to regional complexities.

Sources:
AP News: https://apnews.com/
Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/
The Times of Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com/
