A 'quantified commitment' requires a specific numerical figure to be stated by an official representative (e.g., 'we will send 1,000 troops' or 'we are committing $50 million'). Vague statements of 'support', 'endorsement', or 'willingness to participate' that do not include specific numbers or amounts do not count toward a Yes resolution.

The announcement must be made publicly by an official government authority (e.g., Head of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Defense, or an official spokesperson) of the committing nation. The United States is excluded from this resolution criteria regarding financial commitments, as the question seeks to measure allied international buy-in.

Resolution will be determined using official government press releases and a consensus of credible mainstream reporting from sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), and Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com).

If no such official, quantified announcement occurs between the start date of 2026-01-05 and the end date of 2026-01-13, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The Board of Peace is the transitional governing body for Gaza under the Trump administration's plan, while the ISF is its required security mechanism. Progress on establishing the Board is heavily dependent on the operationalization of the ISF, which relies on international troop and financial contributions. Since negotiations for these contributions have been ongoing since November 2025, an official, quantified commitment by a sovereign nation acts as a highly costly, observable signal that the administrative and logistical hurdles of the plan are being successfully navigated. Positive movement on the ISF strongly indicates that the Board of Peace itself is likely to be officially established by the ultimate March 2026 deadline.

subquestions.question: Will the Government of India officially confirm the resumption of rare earth shipments from China between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: On April 4, 2025, China restricted the export of several rare earth metals and magnets (https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/13/business/china-rare-earths-exports.html). Following diplomatic meetings in August, reports indicated that Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi assured India that export restrictions on items like rare earth minerals and tunnel-boring machines would be eased. However, as of mid-September 2025, Indian importers and EV manufacturers had not received any supplies, and Beijing had issued no official statement confirming the resumption of shipments or expedited applications (https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/). Indian officials were reportedly planning to approach the Chinese Commerce Ministry to enforce the pledge. Because India is actively pressing for these supplies, an official confirmation from the Indian government regarding the resumption of physical shipments would serve as a crucial early indicator that China is actively rolling back its April 4 export ban in practice. Sources: New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/13/business/china-rare-earths-exports.html | Ministry of External Affairs, India: https://www.mea.gov.in/ | The Hindu Business Line: https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a named official or official publication from the Indian Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) (https://www.mea.gov.in/) or the Indian Ministry of Commerce and Industry (https://commerce.gov.in/) publicly states that imports of rare earth elements, minerals, or magnets from China have resumed or been received. The qualifying statement must be issued and reported between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). Statements by unnamed sources, anonymous officials, or unverified claims by private companies do not count toward resolution. The statement must confirm the active resumption or physical receipt of the restricted materials, not merely an assurance of future resumption. Resolution will rely on official press releases or transcripts from the MEA or Ministry of Commerce, as well as credible news reporting that explicitly quotes a named official from these ministries confirming the receipt. If no such official confirmation is made within the specified window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: China's restriction on rare earths was followed by diplomatic promises to India that have yet to materialize into physical shipments. If the Indian government officially confirms that China has actually resumed supplying these critical materials, it acts as a highly reliable signal that China is making material exceptions to or rolling back its April 4 ban in practice. This increases the probability of a formal lifting or reduction of the ban globally by the end of the year.

evidence.step1_decompose: EXACT CONDITION FOR YES: A named official from India's MEA (mea.gov.in) or Ministry of Commerce and Industry (commerce.gov.in) must publicly state — between October 1-31, 2025 — that imports/shipments of rare earth elements, minerals, or magnets from China have been actively resumed or physically received. OBSERVABLE EVIDENCE: An official press release, media briefing transcript, or credible news report that explicitly quotes a named MEA or Ministry of Commerce official confirming that physical rare earth imports have actually arrived in India or that imports are actively underway. KEY CONSTRAINT: The statement must confirm active resumption or physical receipt, NOT merely licenses, assurances, or future capability to import.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'India China rare earth shipments resumption 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find general news on the topic; 2. 'India Ministry of Commerce rare earth minerals China imports official confirmation' (Oct 1-31) — to find official statements; 3. 'MEA Randhir Jaiswal rare earth magnets confirmation October 30 2025' (Oct 29-31) — to find specific MEA briefing; 4. 'India Ministry External Affairs MEA official statement rare earth imports received China October 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find official confirmations; 5. 'India rare earth magnets physical receipt shipment arrived October 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to determine if physical receipt was confirmed; 6. 'MEA Randhir Jaiswal rare earth received resumed October 30 2025' (Oct 29-31) — to check exact wording of MEA statement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: PRIMARY CANDIDATE EVENT: On October 30, 2025, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal (a named official from the Indian Ministry of External Affairs) confirmed at a weekly media briefing that 'some Indian companies have received licences for importing rare earth magnets from China.' Multiple credible outlets confirmed this including The Times of India, Economic Times, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, NDTV, Business Standard, The Tribune, Zee News, MoneyControl, and Firstpost. SPECIFIC COMPANIES NAMED: Continental India, DE Diamond, Hitachi, and Jay Ushin. REJECTION ANALYSIS: The key question is whether 'received licences for importing' satisfies the criteria of 'active resumption or physical receipt.' The MEA confirmed licenses (authorization to import), not physical shipments having arrived. Articles use forward-looking language: 'resumption of imports is EXPECTED to ease bottlenecks' — indicating physical imports had not yet occurred at time of statement.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: ANALYSIS OF FIT: The resolution criteria requires confirmation of 'active resumption or physical receipt of the restricted materials, not merely an assurance of future resumption.' The MEA statement confirmed receipt of IMPORT LICENSES — a legal authorization enabling future imports. This is materially different from confirmation that physical shipments have arrived or that imports are actively occurring. Evidence from [Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/some-indian-cos-have-received-licenses-to-import-rare-earth-magnets-from-china-external-affairs-ministry/articleshow/124960729.cms) states 'the resumption of imports from China is EXPECTED to ease production bottlenecks' — future tense, indicating physical receipt had not yet occurred. [Hindustan Times](https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/china-eases-restrictions-grants-licences-to-indian-firms-to-import-rare-earth-magnets-101761845190440.html) quotes Jaiswal: 'some Indian companies have received licences for importing rare earth magnets from China' — confirming licenses, not physical goods. The resolution criteria also refers to 'imports of rare earth elements, minerals, or magnets from China have resumed or been received' — implying physical goods movement, not the administrative authorization to move goods. CONCLUSION: The MEA statement does NOT satisfy the resolution criteria because it confirms only license receipt, not active resumption or physical receipt of rare earth materials.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The MEA media briefing by Randhir Jaiswal confirming the licenses occurred on October 30, 2025. Multiple sources confirm this date (Economic Times, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, NDTV, etc.). No more precise UTC timestamp is available from the search results, though MEA weekly briefings typically occur mid-morning IST (approximately 03:30-04:30 UTC). The date itself (October 30, 2025) is confirmed by multiple high-quality sources. However, since the underlying event (physical shipment receipt) was NOT confirmed, timestamp extraction for the qualifying event is moot.
evidence.step7_verification: CONTRADICTORY EVIDENCE CHECK: The October 28, 2025 article from Hindu BusinessLine confirms that as of two days before the MEA announcement, India was 'still in talks' with China on end-user conditions — suggesting no physical imports had occurred yet. The October 10, 2025 article notes China sought guarantees from India about non-diversion to the US, and India 'has not yet agreed to China's request.' The October 30 MEA statement itself (licenses granted, not shipments confirmed) is consistent with this timeline — licenses came first, physical goods would follow. The critical distinction between 'licenses received' and 'shipments received/resumed' is clear and well-supported across multiple sources. The resolution criteria explicitly excludes statements that do not confirm active resumption or physical receipt, making this a clear No.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The MEA (through named spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal) made an official statement on October 30, 2025 — within the qualifying window — confirming that Indian companies have received import licenses for rare earth magnets from China. However, the resolution criteria requires confirmation of 'active resumption or physical receipt of the restricted materials, not merely an assurance of future resumption.' Import licenses are an authorization to import, not confirmation that imports have physically occurred. This critical distinction means the MEA statement, while official and named, does not satisfy the precise resolution criteria. No evidence found of any MEA or Ministry of Commerce statement confirming that physical rare earth shipments had actually arrived in India or that active imports were underway during October 2025. Therefore, this question resolves No.

question: Will the Fed cut-pause-pause in 2025?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings in 2025 (September 16-17, October 28-29, and December 9-10).

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered. 

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the December meeting by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the median projection for the federal funds rate at the end of 2025 be 4.1% in the FOMC's September 2025 Summary of Economic Projections?
subquestions.background_information:
As of July 2025, the target range for the federal funds rate is 4.25% to 4.50%, with a midpoint of 4.375% (typically represented as 4.4% in Federal Reserve projection tables). The ultimate question asks whether the Fed will execute a "cut-pause-pause" sequence across its final three meetings of 2025 (September, October, and December). At the September 16-17, 2025 meeting, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will release its Summary of Economic Projections (SEP), which includes the "dot plot" detailing policymakers' expectations for the federal funds rate at year-end.

If the Fed expects to execute exactly one 25-basis-point cut for the remainder of 2025 (matching the "cut-pause-pause" sequence), the projected end-of-2025 target range would be 4.00% to 4.25%. The midpoint of this range is 4.125%, which is conventionally rounded and displayed as 4.1% in the SEP tables. Therefore, a median projection of 4.1% for 2025 in the September SEP is a direct, observable leading indicator that the FOMC plans exactly one more cut for the year, perfectly aligning with the ultimate question's required trajectory.

Sources:
1. Federal Reserve Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
2. FOMC Calendars & Statements: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the "Summary of Economic Projections" (SEP) released by the FOMC shows a "Median" value of exactly 4.1% (or exactly 4.125% if unrounded) for the "Federal funds rate" for the year 2025 in Table 1 (or the equivalent main projections table) between 2025-09-05 and 2025-10-05 inclusive.

This question resolves No if the median projection for 2025 is any other value (e.g., 3.9%, 4.4%), or if no SEP is published within the resolution window.

The official resolution source is the Projection Materials PDF provided for the September 16-17, 2025 FOMC meeting on the Federal Reserve website: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

To resolve, resolvers should navigate to the specific FOMC meeting on the calendar, open the "Projection Materials" PDF, locate "Table 1. Economic projections of Federal Reserve Board members and Federal Reserve Bank presidents" (or equivalent table), and find the intersection of the "Federal funds rate" row and the "2025" column under the "Median" heading. If the publication format changes but an equivalent median projection for the year-end 2025 federal funds rate is released in official Fed materials within the timeframe, that figure will be used.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on the Fed delivering exactly one rate cut over the final three meetings of 2025 (cutting in September, then pausing in October and December). The September SEP 'dot plot' directly reveals the committee's median expectation for the end-of-year rate. A median of 4.1% explicitly signals a consensus for exactly one 25 bps cut from the current 4.25-4.50% range. If the Fed cuts in September and concurrently projects a 4.1% year-end rate, it essentially confirms their intention to pause at the subsequent two meetings, making this projection a highly informative crux for forecasters.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: The FOMC's September 2025 SEP, released between 2025-09-05 and 2025-10-05, must show a median federal funds rate of exactly 4.1% (or 4.125% unrounded) for the year 2025 in the projections table. Observable evidence: the published SEP document and news reports citing the specific median value. Key entities: FOMC, Federal Reserve, September 16-17 2025 meeting. Threshold: exactly 4.1% or 4.125%.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'FOMC September 2025 Summary of Economic Projections federal funds rate median' — to find reports on the SEP's content. Query 2: 'Federal Reserve dot plot September 2025 interest rate projections' — to find dot plot details. Query 3: 'FOMC September 2025 SEP dot plot median federal funds rate 3.6% 3.625% 2025' — to verify the specific value. Query 4: 'Federal Reserve September 2025 projections materials 4.1% median rate' — to check if any source reports 4.1%.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: FOMC September 16-17, 2025 meeting released the SEP on September 17, 2025. Multiple sources report the median projection for end-2025 federal funds rate as 3.6% (midpoint of 3.50%-3.75% range), with one source (Seeking Alpha/Wolf Street) specifically citing 3.625% unrounded. No source reports a 4.1% median. The value 3.9% was the June 2025 SEP median (pre-revision). All sources are consistent: the September 2025 SEP shows 3.6%, not 4.1%.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require exactly 4.1% or 4.125% as the 2025 median federal funds rate. Sources consistently report 3.6% (3.625% unrounded): [Santa Clarita Valley Signal](https://signalscv.com/2025/09/federal-reserve-cuts-interest-rates-for-first-time-in-2025/) reports '3.6% by year-end'; [Seeking Alpha/Wolf Street](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4823870-this-fed-meeting-must-have-been-circus) reports '3.625%'; [Asia Times](https://asiatimes.com/2025/09/whither-us-interest-rates-but-how-far-and-how-fast/) reports 'median projection of 3.6% federal funds rate by year-end 2025'; [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/fed-signals-2-more-cuts-in-2025-raises-gdp-forecast-for-the-year-183031677.html) reports 'fed funds rate falling to 3.6% this year'; [ActionForex](https://www.actionforex.com/live-comments/612276-fed-cuts-25bps-projections-signal-two-more-moves-this-year/) reports 'median federal funds rate falling to 3.6% by year-end'. This does NOT match the required 4.1% or 4.125%. Criteria not satisfied → resolves No.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The September 2025 SEP was released on September 17, 2025, the second day of the FOMC meeting (September 16-17, 2025). Multiple sources published on 2025-09-17 confirm the SEP release with a 3.6% median. Exact timestamp: 2025-09-17 (afternoon EST, standard FOMC press release time ~2:00 PM ET = 2025-09-17T18:00:00Z).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence exists. The SEP was first published on September 17, 2025. No other SEP was published within the resolution window with a 4.1% median — in fact, no source reports any 4.1% median value for the September 2025 SEP.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The June 2025 SEP showed 3.9% as the median. The September 2025 SEP revised this downward to 3.6% (after the 25bps cut plus two more projected cuts). The question asks about 4.1%, which would have implied no cuts from the then-current 4.1% midpoint (4.25%-4.50% range), inconsistent with what actually happened. Multiple independent, high-quality sources (Morningstar, Yahoo Finance, Seeking Alpha, Asia Times, ActionForex, Anadolu Ajansı, Benzinga) all agree the September 2025 SEP median is 3.6% for end-2025. No source reports 4.1% as the September 2025 SEP median.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The September 2025 FOMC SEP was published on September 17, 2025, within the resolution window. The median federal funds rate projection for end-2025 is clearly 3.6% (3.625% unrounded), not 4.1% (or 4.125%). The Yes condition is definitively not met. The question resolves No as of September 17, 2025, when the SEP was published with a 3.6% median value.

subquestions.question: Will Russia capture the entirety of the settlement of Novoekonomichne by September 25, 2025?

Because Novoekonomichne sits strategically on the eastern approach to Myrnohrad, its complete capture by Russian forces would serve as a key leading indicator of Russian momentum. DeepStateMap: https://deepstatemap.live/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The ISW interactive map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) shades the entirety of Novoekonomichne's built-up area red (indicating Russian control), or the ISW publishes a written daily campaign assessment on https://www.understandingwar.org/ explicitly stating that Russian forces have captured the entirety of Novoekonomichne.

If neither source confirms the full capture of the settlement by September 25, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves "No". If one source confirms it but the other does not, the question resolves "Yes" based on the first reliable confirmation. In the event of temporary map glitches or rollbacks that are corrected within 48 hours, the corrected version of the map will be used.
subquestions.rationale: Novoekonomichne is a contested settlement on the immediate eastern approach to Myrnohrad. Its complete capture is a practical prerequisite and a strong proxy for Russia's ability to maintain enough offensive momentum to push into Myrnohrad proper and capture the specified intersection (Vatutina and Puhachova) by the end of September.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: ISW or DeepStateMap must confirm, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-25, that Russia fully captured/occupied all of Novoekonomichne, Donetsk Oblast. Observable evidence: ISW written assessment explicitly stating full Russian capture, or DeepStateMap marking entire settlement as occupied (red/Russian-controlled).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Novoekonomichne Russia captured Donetsk 2025' (to find Russian capture reports); 2) 'Novoekonomichne Ukraine liberated 425th regiment August 2025' (to confirm control timeline); 3) 'ISW assessment Novoekonomichne Russia captured September 2025' (ISW-specific); 4) 'DeepStateMap Novoekonomichne occupied Russian control September 2025' (DeepState-specific); 5) 'Novoekonomichne Russia recaptured occupied September 2025' (disproof check).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key findings: (1) Ukrainian 425th Skelia Regiment liberated Novoekonomichne on August 31, 2025, raising the Ukrainian flag — confirmed by General Staff, Ukrinform, Ukrainian Pravda (published Sept 1, 2025). (2) Ukrainian General Staff reports from Sept 6, 9, 20, 22, 24 mention active Russian assault attempts near/in Novoekonomichne being repelled by Ukrainian forces. (3) DeepState updates in September reported Russian advances only in other oblasts (Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia) — no mention of Novoekonomichne falling to Russia. (4) No ISW or DeepState source reports Russian capture of Novoekonomichne in September 2025. All candidate events are of Ukrainian control or contested status, not Russian capture.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require ISW or DeepStateMap to confirm full Russian capture of Novoekonomichne. Multiple sources confirm: [Ukrinform](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/4031788-ukrainian-forces-liberate-novoekonomichne-in-donetsk-region.html) — Ukraine liberated Novoekonomichne on Aug 31. [Ukrainian Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/09/1/7528827/) — DeepState noted the liberation. [Ukrinform Sept 9](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/4034645-69-clashes-on-frontline-fighting-continues-in-six-sectors.html) — Russian forces made 35 attempts to advance near Novoekonomichne, with 27 repelled. [Ukrainian Pravda Sept 22](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/09/22/7531888/) — Ukrainian forces stopped 49 Russian assaults including near Novoekonomichne. No source confirms full Russian capture. Criteria are NOT met for Yes.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a Russian capture of Novoekonomichne during the window, because no such event occurred. The relevant timestamp is August 31, 2025 (Ukrainian liberation), which is before the resolution window and is the opposite direction.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event (Russian full capture of Novoekonomichne confirmed by ISW or DeepState) occurred at any point during September 1–25, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Active fighting reports throughout September (Sept 6, 9, 20, 22, 24) with Ukrainian forces repelling Russian attacks near Novoekonomichne confirm that Ukraine maintained control. DeepState's September updates do not mention Novoekonomichne falling to Russia. No contradictory evidence suggesting Russian capture was found. The evidence is consistent and mutually reinforcing across multiple independent sources.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Russia did NOT capture Novoekonomichne during September 1–25, 2025. Instead, Ukrainian forces liberated it on August 31 and defended it throughout September. Neither ISW nor DeepStateMap reported full Russian capture during the resolution window. The question resolves No. The window closed on September 25, 2025 with no qualifying event.

subquestions.question: Will a US Congressional committee or Ghislaine Maxwell's legal team publicly announce an agreement for her to testify before Congress by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In July 2025, the US House Committee on Oversight and Accountability subpoenaed Ghislaine Maxwell to testify regarding Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking network. However, Maxwell's attorneys stated she would invoke her Fifth Amendment rights unless several demands were met, such as being granted formal immunity, receiving questions in advance, and moving the deposition outside her prison facility (CNN, https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/29/politics/maxwell-offers-testify-congress-immunity/index.html). Congressional members have been hesitant to grant immunity, leading to a legal and political standoff. Additionally, the Department of Justice announced intentions to meet privately with Maxwell, adding another layer of complexity to her potential Congressional appearance (WSET, https://wset.com/news/nation-world/gop-might-anger-trump-in-bid-to-subpoena-ghislaine-maxwell-amid-epstein-files-spectacle). Reaching a formal agreement on these conditions is generally seen as a necessary precursor for any substantive testimony to occur.

Sources:
CNN: https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/29/politics/maxwell-offers-testify-congress-immunity/index.html
WSET: https://wset.com/news/nation-world/gop-might-anger-trump-in-bid-to-subpoena-ghislaine-maxwell-amid-epstein-files-spectacle
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if either of the following conditions occurs between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive):
1. A US Congressional committee (from either the House or Senate), its leadership, or Ghislaine Maxwell's legal representatives publicly announce that an agreement has been reached for Maxwell to provide testimony or answer substantive questions before a Congressional committee.
2. Ghislaine Maxwell provides live or recorded testimony to a Congressional committee where she answers substantive questions without exclusively invoking her Fifth Amendment rights.

To count toward resolution, the qualifying event must occur and be publicly reported between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. Evidence must come from official Congressional press releases (e.g., https://oversight.house.gov/) or reports from at least two credible news organizations (e.g., Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), or CNN (https://www.cnn.com/)). If neither condition is met within this time window, or if an agreement is only announced after 2025-10-31, the question resolves No. If Maxwell appears before Congress during this window but exclusively pleads the Fifth Amendment to substantive questions, and no agreement to answer questions is otherwise announced, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Maxwell has made her testimony conditional on significant concessions from Congress, most notably immunity. The announcement of an agreement between her lawyers and Congress is a distinct, critical milestone that would serve as a strong leading indicator of her actually providing substantive testimony. Resolving this crux early provides major evidence regarding whether she will overcome the Fifth Amendment hurdle and testify before the ultimate resolution date.

evidence.step1_decompose: Resolution requires: (1) A public announcement of an agreement between Congress and Maxwell's legal team for her to testify, OR (2) Maxwell actually providing substantive testimony to a Congressional committee — both must occur between Oct 1–31, 2025. Key entities: House Oversight Committee (Chair Comer, Ranking Member Garcia), Maxwell's legal team (attorney Markus). The bar is an 'agreement reached,' not merely demands or contact.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: 'Ghislaine Maxwell Congress testimony 2025' (Oct 1–31), 'Ghislaine Maxwell Congressional committee agreement testify' (Sep–Oct 2025), 'Maxwell testimony agreement Congress deposition October 2025' (Oct 1–31), 'Maxwell House Oversight Committee deposition scheduled date' (Oct 1–31), 'Maxwell Congressional testimony agreement confirmed scheduled November 2025' (Oct 20–31), 'House Oversight Epstein Maxwell deposition update October 30 31 2025' (Oct 25–31).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Oct 7, 2025 — SCOTUS rejected Maxwell's appeal, clearing legal path for testimony. (2) Oct 9–10, 2025 — House Oversight Committee contacted Maxwell's attorneys; committee said update 'soon'; Rep. Garcia stated 'a date is being set.' (3) Oct 10, 2025 — Garcia demanded 'immediate testimony.' (4) Oct 30, 2025 — Garcia still demanding Maxwell testify, calling situation a 'criminal cover up.' All rejected as qualifying events: none constitutes an 'agreement reached and publicly announced.' Contact and demands are not agreements. Committee said update coming 'soon' but no update confirming agreement was found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence of a publicly announced agreement. [Forbes, Oct 9](https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2025/10/09/will-ghislaine-maxwell-speak-with-congress-supreme-court-rejection-clears-way-for-her-to-testify/) reports committee will give update 'soon' — prospective, not an agreement. [Washington Examiner, Oct 10](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/house/3845304/oversight-committee-ghislaine-maxwell-testify/) confirms committee 'contacted' Maxwell's attorneys — contact, not agreement. [The Hill, Oct 7](https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5543253-garcia-trump-ghislaine-maxwell-pardon/) states 'a date is being set' — ongoing process. [Alternet, Oct 30](https://www.alternet.org/epstein-maxwell-johnson/) still shows Garcia 'demanding' Maxwell testify — no agreement reached by Oct 30. No evidence Maxwell actually appeared before Congress. Maxwell's prior immunity request was rejected by the committee per [TheBlaze, Oct 7].
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found with a reliable timestamp within the window. The closest events (committee contact, Oct 9-10) do not meet the criteria of a publicly announced agreement.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at all within the October 1–31, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove No conclusion by searching for any late-October agreement announcements. The Oct 30, 2025 Alternet article still shows Garcia demanding Maxwell testify — confirming no agreement was reached by that date. The government shutdown (begun Oct 1, 2025) complicated committee operations throughout the month. DOJ was not responding to subpoenas during the shutdown per [Ukraine Today, Oct 17]. No credible source reports Maxwell appearing before Congress or any agreement being finalized.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly shows that while Congress was actively pursuing Maxwell's testimony throughout October 2025 — with subpoenas, committee contact with her attorneys, and Democratic demands — no agreement was publicly announced and Maxwell did not appear before any Congressional committee during the October 1–31 window. The resolution criteria require an explicit, public announcement of an agreement or actual testimony, neither of which occurred. Resolution: No, with resolution_datetime at the end of the window since no earlier definitive No moment (like a formal refusal) was reported.

subquestions.question: Will Elon Musk's X account (@elonmusk) reply to, repost, or quote any post from Nikita Bier (@nikitabier) between October 15, 2025 and November 14, 2025?

Futurism: https://futurism.com
Mashable: https://mashable.com

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

If @elonmusk does not reply to, repost, or quote any post from @nikitabier during this period, the question resolves No. If either account is suspended, deleted, or otherwise completely inaccessible for the entirety of the resolution window, preventing any interactions, the question resolves No.

subquestions.rationale: Nikita Bier secured his executive position largely through his prolific posting and public interactions with Elon Musk on X. A complete cessation of public engagement from Musk toward Bier's account over a month-long period would be a strong leading indicator of internal friction, alienation, or an impending departure. evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: @elonmusk (Elon Musk's official X account) must reply to, repost, or quote-tweet a post by @nikitabier (Nikita Bier) between 2025-10-15T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-14T23:59:59Z. evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Elon Musk reply repost quote Nikita Bier X Twitter 2025' (general interaction search); 2) '@elonmusk @nikitabier interaction tweet October November 2025' (specific window search); 3) 'Elon Musk reply Nikita Bier YouTube creator payments X October 2025' (specific event); 4) 'Elon Musk YouTube does a much better job Nikita Bier creator payout' (key quote search); 5) 'Nikita Bier creator payout does more harm than good X tweet date' (confirming event date).

evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Benzinga article [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/25/10/48256944/elon-musk-recommends-a-competitor-youtube-does-a-much-better-job) explicitly states: 'Elon Musk...publicly praised YouTube...stating in a reply to X Head of Product Nikita Bier on October 16, 2025.' Multiple other sources (Teslarati, Times of India, TimesNow, Mashable India) all published on October 16-17, 2025 confirm Musk replied to Bier's post. This is a 'reply' interaction which directly matches the resolution criteria. The interaction is between @elonmusk and @nikitabier on X. October 16, 2025 falls within the window (Oct 15 – Nov 14, 2025).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The most explicit timestamp comes from the Benzinga summary: 'in a reply to X Head of Product Nikita Bier on October 16, 2025.' The Benzinga article itself was published on October 16, 2025. Multiple other articles from October 16-17, 2025 corroborate the event occurred on or just before October 16, 2025. Given the window opens on October 15, 2025, and the article was published October 16, 2025, the reply occurred on October 15 or 16, 2025 — within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence found. evidence.step8_final_decision: Multiple credible news sources published on October 16-17, 2025 explicitly state that Elon Musk (@elonmusk) replied to a post by Nikita Bier (@nikitabier) on X, saying 'YouTube does a much better job.' This reply occurred on October 15 or 16, 2025, within the resolution window. The interaction was a direct reply, which qualifies under the resolution criteria. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo be traded this season?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed NBA player is traded from their current team to another NBA team before the 2025-2026 NBA trade deadline. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The NBA trade deadline for the 2025-2026 season is scheduled for February 5, 2026.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA; however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will there be credible reporting that Giannis Antetokounmpo has formally requested a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks between December 4, 2025, and January 3, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Giannis Antetokounmpo's future with the Milwaukee Bucks has become a major focal point of the 2025-2026 NBA season. The Bucks have struggled early on, posting a 9-13 record. Recently, Antetokounmpo removed nearly all Bucks-related content from his social media accounts, sparking widespread trade speculation. According to reports from ESPN, Antetokounmpo and his agent, Alex Saratsis, have initiated discussions with the Bucks regarding his long-term fit, with a resolution expected soon. Although Antetokounmpo is under contract, a formal trade request would force Milwaukee's hand ahead of the February 5, 2026 NBA trade deadline. Determining whether Giannis applies direct pressure via a trade request is a critical early indicator of an impending blockbuster move.

Sources:
ESPN NBA: https://www.espn.com/nba/
Bleacher Report NBA: https://bleacherreport.com/nba
RealGM NBA News: https://basketball.realgm.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 (inclusive), a credible sports news outlet (such as ESPN, The Athletic, Bleacher Report, or Yahoo Sports) or one of their verified lead NBA reporters publishes a report stating that Giannis Antetokounmpo or his representatives have formally requested or demanded a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks. To qualify, the report must definitively state that a trade request or demand has been communicated to the team's front office. General speculation, rumors of dissatisfaction, or reports stating he is merely 'open to a trade' do not qualify. Direct public statements from Giannis Antetokounmpo or his agent confirming a trade request between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 also qualify for a Yes resolution. If no such qualifying report or statement is made by 2026-01-03 at 23:59:59 UTC, the question resolves No. Note that if Antetokounmpo is traded during this window without a qualifying report of a prior or simultaneous trade request, this question will resolve No, as it strictly tracks the reporting of a request. Verification will rely on official articles and verified social media posts from authoritative outlets.

Primary resolution sources:
ESPN: https://www.espn.com/nba/
The Athletic: https://theathletic.com/nba/
Yahoo Sports: https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/
subquestions.rationale: A formal trade request is the clearest early indicator of an impending blockbuster trade in the NBA. Superstars of Giannis Antetokounmpo's caliber are rarely traded mid-season unless they explicitly apply pressure on the front office. Resolving whether a request is made a month before the trade deadline acts as a strong crux: if he demands a trade, the probability of an actual trade by February 5 skyrockets. If he does not, the Bucks are highly likely to wait until the offseason to assess their options, thereby drastically lowering the probability of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition for Yes requires: A credible sports news outlet (ESPN, The Athletic, Bleacher Report, Yahoo Sports, etc.) or their verified lead NBA reporters must publish a report between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 (inclusive) stating that Giannis Antetokounmpo or his representatives have FORMALLY requested or demanded a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks — communicated to the team's front office. General speculation, rumors of dissatisfaction, or 'open to a trade' reports do not qualify. Key entities: Giannis Antetokounmpo, his agent Alex Saratsis, Milwaukee Bucks front office. Threshold: formal/definitive trade request/demand communicated to front office. Window: 2025-12-04 to 2026-01-03.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Giannis Antetokounmpo trade request Milwaukee Bucks 2025' (Dec 4 - Jan 3) — to find any formal trade request reports; 2) 'Giannis trade demand Milwaukee Bucks formal request' (Dec 4 - Jan 3) — to find demand-specific reporting; 3) 'Giannis Antetokounmpo formal trade request confirmed January 2026' (Dec 15 - Jan 3) — to check if anything happened after mid-December; 4) 'Giannis Antetokounmpo trade update Milwaukee Bucks December January' (Dec 20 - Jan 3) — to check the latest developments.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple articles from Dec 4-Jan 3 discuss trade speculation. Key findings: (1) Doc Rivers repeatedly stated 'Giannis has never asked to be traded. Ever.' (Dec 4, 2025) per multiple sources; (2) ESPN's Shams Charania reported on discussions about Giannis's 'future' with the team and his agent having conversations, but did not report a formal trade request; (3) Marc Stein (Dec 13): 'He has to firmly say it, and that has not happened'; (4) Jake Fischer (Dec 17): 'Giannis has not yet asked out'; (5) Giannis himself (Dec 18-19): 'I personally have not had that conversation with the Bucks'; (6) Giannis (Dec 28): Called trade questions 'disrespectful,' stated 'I'm here. I'm here. I'm here.'; (7) Jan 2, 2026: Reports that Giannis may delay any request until summer; (8) Dec 31: ESPN sources indicate a 'forceful' trade request from Giannis would be necessary but has not occurred. No article identified a qualifying event of a formal trade request being communicated to the Bucks front office.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the articles found report that Giannis Antetokounmpo or his representatives formally requested or demanded a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks. All credible sources ([Journal Sentinel](https://eu.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2025/12/04/did-giannis-request-trade-what-is-real-what-is-not-milwaukee-bucks-star/87607643007/), [NBC Sports](https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/bucks-players-coach-doc-rivers-downplay-buzz-around-giannis-antetokounmpo-trade-rumors), [Yahoo Sports](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/amid-being-top-subject-discussions-111857054.html), [NBC Sports Dec 15](https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/nba-trade-rumors-2025-26-giannis-antetokounmpo-trade-update), [Sporting News Dec 17](https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/milwaukee-bucks/news/bucks-giannis-antetokounmpo-trade-request/877a1f43d3ef9e187513c47e), [Real GM Dec 18](https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/283174/Giannis-Antetokounmpo-Confirms-He-Hasnt-Spoken-To-Bucks-About-Future), [Sports Illustrated Dec 28](https://www.si.com/nba/giannis-antetokounmpo-shuts-down-question-bucks-trade-speculation-im-here), [Yardbarker Jan 2](https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/giannis_antetokounmpo_trade_talks_could_shift_to_summer_as_bucks_weigh_their_options/s1_17009_43277009)) consistently report that NO formal trade request was made. The Sporting News article from Dec 4 mentions 'expressed a desire to be traded' but this contradicts all other sourcing and is classified by other outlets as speculation/mischaracterization. The dominant reporting from authoritative sources is consistently that no formal trade request was made.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying Yes event because no such event occurred within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found anywhere in the Dec 4, 2025 – Jan 3, 2026 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempts to disprove No conclusion: One article (Sporting News Dec 4) mentions Shams Charania 'confirmed' a trade request, but this is contradicted by: (a) Bucks coach Doc Rivers explicitly denying it (Dec 4), (b) Giannis himself stating Dec 18-19 he hasn't spoken to the Bucks about his future, (c) Marc Stein (Dec 13) saying 'He has to firmly say it, and that has not happened,' (d) Jake Fischer (Dec 17) saying 'Giannis has not yet asked out,' (e) Giannis on Dec 28 calling trade questions 'disrespectful' and reaffirming 'I'm here.' The consensus among authoritative sources (ESPN reporters, The Athletic, NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Bleacher Report's Jake Fischer) is unambiguous: no formal trade request was communicated during this window. The Sporting News Dec 4 summary appears to mischaracterize Charania's actual reporting, which described 'discussions about future' rather than a formal request. The overwhelming weight of credible evidence confirms no formal trade request.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All credible evidence within the Dec 4, 2025 – Jan 3, 2026 window consistently and explicitly confirms that Giannis Antetokounmpo did NOT formally request a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks. Authoritative NBA reporters (Shams Charania, Marc Stein, Jake Fischer, Chris Haynes), Doc Rivers, and Giannis himself all indicated no formal trade request was made. As of Jan 2-3, 2026, reports were discussing whether Giannis might delay a possible request until summer. The window closed without a qualifying event. Resolution: No.

question: Will Italy win the third most gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the third most gold medals at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most gold medals won will use most overall medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most gold medals won, and Norway wins more overall medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the gold medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

subquestions.question: Will Italy reach a cumulative total of at least 4 gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics by February 16, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2026 Winter Olympics are taking place in Milano-Cortina, Italy, from February 4 to February 22, 2026. For the host nation to secure the third most gold medals, they would need an exceptionally strong performance, likely surpassing traditional powerhouses like Canada, Switzerland, and either the US or Germany, who are heavily favored behind Norway. In the 2022 Beijing Games, the third-place nations (USA and China) won 9 gold medals each. Historically, host nations enjoy a medal bump; Italy won 5 gold medals when they previously hosted the Winter Games in Turin 2006 (https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/torino-2006/medals). Tracking Italy's total gold medal count by the midpoint of the Games provides a crucial indicator of whether they possess the momentum to challenge for a top-3 finish.

Sources:
IOC - Turin 2006 Medal Table: https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/torino-2006/medals
CBS Sports - 2026 Winter Olympics medal count: https://www.cbssports.com/olympics/news/2026-winter-olympics-medal-count/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the official International Olympic Committee (IOC) medal table credits Italy with a cumulative total of 4 or more gold medals at any point between 2026-02-07 and 2026-02-16T23:59:59Z (inclusive). The official resolution source is the IOC website (https://www.olympics.com/). The determination will be based on the official medal standings as they appear during the resolution window. If Italy does not reach a total of at least 4 gold medals by the end of 2026-02-16T23:59:59Z, the question resolves No. Medals awarded, reallocated, or stripped after 2026-02-16T23:59:59Z will not be considered. If the Games are canceled or postponed during this window, the question resolves based on the official count at the time of cancellation.
subquestions.rationale: To finish with the third most gold medals, a nation typically needs around 8 to 12 golds (e.g., 9 golds secured third place in 2022). Monitoring whether Italy can accumulate 4 gold medals by the midpoint of the Games is a strong indicator of their overall pace. If they fail to reach this threshold by February 16, it is highly unlikely they will gather enough medals in the remaining days to place third overall, efficiently updating forecasters on the ultimate question's outcome.

question: Will Rodrigo Paz Pereira win by 15–20%?
description:
A second-round (runoff) vote for the Bolivia Presidential election is scheduled to take place on October 19, 2025 

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the 2025 Bolivian Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the 'margin of victory' is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first and second-place candidate. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the second round of the Bolivian Presidential Election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the results of the election aren’t known by March 31, 2026 ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve solely based on the first official vote count released by the Bolivian Government, specifically the Plurinational Electoral Body (Órgano Electoral Plurinacional, OEP) (https://www.oep.org.bo/).

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

subquestions.question: Will Samuel Doria Medina publicly endorse Rodrigo Paz Pereira for the Bolivian presidential runoff between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In the first round of the Bolivian presidential election on August 17, 2025, centrist Rodrigo Paz Pereira secured first place with 32.1% of the vote, while right-wing candidate Jorge 'Tuto' Quiroga came in second with 26.9%. The two will compete in a runoff election scheduled for October 19, 2025. Samuel Doria Medina, a conservative billionaire and third-place finisher, captured 20% of the vote. The distribution of Doria Medina's voters will be crucial in determining the margin of victory in the runoff. According to the Americas Society/Council of the Americas, Paz Pereira 'may get a boost in the runoff due to the endorsement of third-place finisher Samuel Doria Medina.' If Paz Pereira receives this endorsement, he is much more likely to expand his 5.2% first-round lead into the 15-20% margin required for the ultimate question to resolve positively.

Sources:
AS/COA: https://www.as-coa.org/
Counter Punch: https://www.counterpunch.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Samuel Doria Medina publicly and explicitly endorses Rodrigo Paz Pereira for the October 19, 2025, Bolivian presidential runoff between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). 

An 'endorsement' is defined as a public, unambiguous statement by Samuel Doria Medina (or an official press release from his campaign/party) explicitly urging voters, supporters, or the general public to vote for Rodrigo Paz Pereira in the second round. Statements that merely express a personal preference, a personal intention to vote for Paz Pereira without encouraging others, or general opposition to Jorge Quiroga without an explicit call to vote for Paz Pereira, will not count towards a Yes resolution. 

The resolution will rely on reports from credible Bolivian or international news organizations (such as El Deber at https://eldeber.com.bo/ or La Razón at https://www.la-razon.com/) or direct statements published on Samuel Doria Medina's official verified social media accounts (e.g., X/Twitter at https://x.com/SDoriaMedina). If no qualifying endorsement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question resolves No. If he explicitly endorses Jorge Quiroga or calls for null/blank votes during this window without subsequently endorsing Paz Pereira within the window, the question will also resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: Rodrigo Paz Pereira led the first round by a margin of 5.2% over Jorge Quiroga. For the ultimate question (a Paz Pereira victory margin of 15–20%) to resolve Yes, Paz Pereira needs to capture a very large share of the voters who did not support him in the first round. Samuel Doria Medina won 20% of the vote, making him the most significant kingmaker. An explicit endorsement from Doria Medina would be a strong early indicator that Paz Pereira can consolidate enough of the conservative and centrist electorate to win by a 15–20% margin. Without it, the race is likely to remain tighter.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Samuel Doria Medina must make a public, unambiguous statement explicitly urging voters/supporters/the general public to vote for Rodrigo Paz Pereira in the October 19, 2025 runoff, during the window 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Observable evidence: credible news article or official social media post documenting such a statement with a timestamp in that window. Key entities: Samuel Doria Medina, Rodrigo Paz Pereira; threshold: explicit call to vote, not merely personal preference; timing: strictly within Sep 1 - Oct 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Samuel Doria Medina endorses Rodrigo Paz Pereira Bolivia runoff 2025' (Sep-Oct window) — to find direct endorsement evidence. Query 2: 'Bolivia presidential runoff segunda vuelta October 2025 Paz Pereira Quiroga' (Sep-Oct window) — to find runoff context and any endorsement mentions. Query 3: 'Doria Medina apoyo endoso segunda vuelta Bolivia 2025' (Sep-Oct window) — Spanish-language search for endorsement. Query 4: 'Samuel Doria Medina Bolivia election second round endorsement' (Aug-Oct window) — wider date range to find when endorsement first occurred. Query 5: 'Doria Medina endorsement support Paz Pereira runoff Bolivia August 2025' (Aug 17 - Sep 1) — to find pre-window endorsement. Query 6: 'SDoriaMedina Bolivia runoff endorsement campaign September 2025' (Sep-Oct window) — to find any September endorsement. evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) AFP article (Aug 18, 2025): 'Doria Medina immediately threw his support behind Paz, citing the need for change in the country' — This is a strong endorsement but dated August 17-18, 2025, BEFORE the resolution window. (2) Adnkronos article (Aug 18, 2025): 'Entrepreneur Samuel Doria Medina has announced his support for Paz Pereira in the second round' — Also before the window. (3) AS/COA article (Aug 19, 2025): References 'endorsement of third-place finisher Samuel Doria Medina' — Also before window. (4) TASS article (Aug 18, 2025): Doria Medina said 'I promise to support any initiative that will help the country emerge from the crisis' — Vaguer, also before window. No qualifying events found within the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window. All endorsement activity discovered occurred in August 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The endorsements documented by [AFP](https://afp.com/), [Adnkronos](https://www.adnkronos.com/internazionale/akieng/bolivia-elections-there-will-be-a-runoff-challenge-between-rodrigo-paz-and-tuto-quiroga_44zMKQaP0EXCxNrALcsIzC), and [AS/COA](https://www.as-coa.org/articles/three-things-know-about-bolivias-2025-first-round-election-results) appear to meet the substantive criteria for an endorsement (explicit support/urging to vote for Paz Pereira in the runoff), but they all occurred on August 17-18, 2025 — BEFORE the question's resolution window of September 1, 2025. No qualifying endorsement was found within the Sep 1 - Oct 1, 2025 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The endorsement events are dated August 17-18, 2025 (election night and day after). Multiple AFP and Adnkronos articles published August 18, 2025 document the endorsement. No endorsement with a timestamp in the September 1 - October 1 window was found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first occurrence of Doria Medina's endorsement of Paz Pereira was on August 17-18, 2025 (election night), which is outside (before) the resolution window. No qualifying first occurrence within the window was identified.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly shows that Doria Medina's public endorsement of Paz Pereira occurred on August 17-18, 2025 — before the resolution window of September 1, 2025. No qualifying endorsement event was found within the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window. The question specifically requires the endorsement to occur within that window. question: Will India strike Pakistan by Dec 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if India initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Pakistani territory by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Indian military forces that impact Pakistani territory (e.g., if an Indian missile or drone hits a target within Pakistan’s borders, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted before reaching Pakistani territory, as well as surface-to-air missile strikes, will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether debris lands on Pakistani soil or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or any operation conducted by Indian ground forces will not qualify as a strike under this market.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a terrorist attack resulting in at least 3 fatalities occur in India and be publicly attributed to Pakistan or Pakistan-based groups by the Indian government between November 14 and December 14, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tensions between India and Pakistan have severely escalated throughout 2025 following the devastating April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, which resulted in the deaths of 26 Indian civilians. In response, India launched 'Operation Sindoor', a major cross-border military campaign that targeted terrorist infrastructure and military assets deep within Pakistani territory. Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have publicly stated that India will not hesitate to act again if further provoked. Recently, security agencies have warned of a rising terror threat, particularly in Punjab and Jammu & Kashmir, highlighted by a surge in drone-facilitated arms smuggling, including assault rifles and rocket-propelled grenades (RPGs) originating from Pakistan. Since previous military strikes against Pakistan have been directly triggered by mass-casualty terrorist attacks attributed to Pakistan-based groups, monitoring whether a new deadly attack occurs provides a critical early indicator for whether India will initiate another strike by the end of the year.

Sources:
Firstpost - https://www.firstpost.com/india/we-didnt-kill-pakistani-citizens-rajnath-singh-operation-sindoor-13833212.html
The Tribune - https://www.tribuneindia.com/
The Print - https://theprint.in/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if a militant or terrorist attack occurs within the internationally recognized borders of India (or Indian-administered territories), resulting in the confirmed deaths of at least three (3) individuals (excluding the attackers/perpetrators), AND an official representative or body of the Government of India publicly attributes the attack, or the organization responsible for it, to Pakistan or Pakistan-based entities, between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 (inclusive, in UTC).

Qualifying victims include Indian civilians, law enforcement, or military personnel. The public attribution must be made by a relevant government authority (e.g., Ministry of External Affairs, Ministry of Defence, Prime Minister's Office, or senior military commands) via an official statement, press conference, or press release.

Both the attack itself and the official government attribution must take place between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14.

Resolution will be determined by reviewing official press releases from the Indian Ministry of External Affairs (https://www.mea.gov.in/press-releases.htm), the Press Information Bureau of India (https://pib.gov.in/), or a consensus of credible reporting from major news outlets (e.g., The Hindu - https://www.thehindu.com/, Hindustan Times - https://www.hindustantimes.com/) confirming both the casualty threshold and the government's official attribution. If these conditions are not met within the resolution window, the question resolves 'No'. If an attack occurs within the window but the government delays attribution until after 2025-12-14, the question will resolve 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Historically, major Indian military operations against Pakistan (such as the 2019 Balakot strikes and the recent Operation Sindoor) have been launched as direct retaliations for mass-casualty terror attacks on Indian soil attributed to Pakistan-based militant groups. The occurrence of a new, deadly attack that the Indian government explicitly blames on Pakistan serves as a highly informative crux: a 'Yes' outcome significantly elevates the probability of an Indian retaliatory strike by December 31, while a 'No' outcome implies that the immediate geopolitical status quo remains relatively stable, reducing the likelihood of an unprovoked Indian strike.

evidence.step1_decompose: Requires: (1) terrorist/militant attack within India (including Indian-administered territories) between Nov 14-Dec 14, 2025; (2) at least 3 civilian/security fatalities (excluding attackers); (3) official Indian government attribution of the attack OR its responsible organization to Pakistan or Pakistan-based entities; (4) both attack AND attribution must occur within the window. Observable evidence: official press releases from MEA, PIB, or credible news reports of Indian government statements explicitly attributing a qualifying attack to Pakistan. Key threshold: 3+ non-attacker deaths.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'terrorist attack India Pakistan attributed fatalities 2025' [general search for qualifying events]; 2. 'militant attack India Kashmir killed November December 2025' [search for attacks within window]; 3. 'Delhi Red Fort car bomb attack India Pakistan attribution November 2025' [specific to the nearest qualifying event]; 4. 'India government official statement Pakistan terror attack attribution November December 2025' [search for official attribution]; 5. 'India official attribution Red Fort blast Pakistan Jaish-e-Mohammed NIA government statement' [specific attribution search]; 6. 'India terror attack Kashmir killed Pakistan attribution official statement December 2025' [broader search for any qualifying attack]; 7. 'India government blamed Pakistan attack fatalities December 2025' [search for attribution in December].
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Delhi Red Fort car bomb (Nov 10, 2025) — killed 10-15 people, linked to Jaish-e-Mohammed; REJECTED because attack occurred BEFORE the window (Nov 10, before Nov 14). (B) Nowgam police station explosion (Nov 14, 2025, ~11:20 PM) — killed 8-9 police/forensic officials; REJECTED because Indian police explicitly stated this was an ACCIDENTAL detonation, not a terrorist attack, and no official attribution to Pakistan was made. (C) No other qualifying attacks within India during Nov 14 - Dec 14, 2025 period were found. The searches revealed multiple terror attacks in Pakistan (by TTP, BLA) but none in India that met both criteria of (a) being a terrorist attack within the window and (b) being officially attributed to Pakistan.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Delhi Red Fort attack (Nov 10) fails on timing — it occurred before the Nov 14 window start date. The Nowgam explosion (Nov 14-15) fails on two counts: (1) Indian police explicitly stated it was NOT a terrorist attack but an accidental explosion; (2) no attribution to Pakistan was made. Multiple sources confirm India deliberately refrained from officially attributing the Red Fort blast to Pakistan within the window: [CSIS](https://www.csis.org/analysis/understanding-red-fort-attack-new-delhi): 'India's government has declared the event an act of terrorism...though it has not officially named JeM or Pakistan'; [RT](https://www.rt.com/india/627882-delhi-blast-suicide-attack/): 'As of November 17, 2025, New Delhi had not attributed responsibility for the Red Fort blast to Islamabad'; [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/south-asia/is-india-changing-its-pakistan-playbook): 'his government has refrained from directly blaming Pakistan'; [Express Tribune](https://tribune.com.pk/story/2581174/indias-commitment-trap): 'but did not accuse Pakistan.' No qualifying attack with official attribution to Pakistan was found within the Nov 14 - Dec 14 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Red Fort attack: Nov 10, 2025, approximately 6:52 PM IST — BEFORE the window. The Nowgam explosion: Nov 14, 2025, approximately 11:20 PM IST (possibly Nov 15 UTC depending on time zone) — within the window start date, but classified as accidental not terrorist, and no Pakistan attribution. No qualifying event with exact timestamp within the window could be identified.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (terrorist attack in India with 3+ fatalities AND official Indian government attribution to Pakistan) was found within the Nov 14 - Dec 14, 2025 window. The closest event was the Red Fort attack (Nov 10), but it occurred before the window and, critically, India's government deliberately refrained from officially attributing it to Pakistan.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent, high-quality sources corroborate that India deliberately maintained a non-accusatory stance toward Pakistan regarding the Red Fort blast throughout the Nov 14 - Dec 14 window: CSIS analysis, AFP reporting, Straits Times analysis, The Express Tribune (Pakistan perspective), RT India reporting, and HW News opinion all consistently report no official Indian government attribution to Pakistan for the Red Fort attack. India's Cabinet adopted a 'non-accusatory resolution' on Nov 12. The India-Germany JWG meeting (Nov 28) condemned both Pahalgam (April 22) and Red Fort (Nov 10) attacks without attributing the Nov 10 attack to Pakistan. No contradictory evidence was found indicating an official Indian government attribution to Pakistan for a qualifying attack within the resolution window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Within the Nov 14 - Dec 14, 2025 window: (1) The Delhi Red Fort attack (10+ fatalities, linked to Jaish-e-Mohammed/Pakistan-based handlers) occurred BEFORE the window (Nov 10); (2) The Nowgam police station explosion (8-9 fatalities, Nov 14-15) was officially classified as ACCIDENTAL and not attributed to Pakistan; (3) No other qualifying terrorist attack in India with 3+ fatalities AND official Indian government attribution to Pakistan occurred within the window. India deliberately maintained diplomatic restraint and did not officially blame Pakistan for any attack during this period. The window closed on Dec 14, 2025 with the condition never being met.

question: Will Norway win the second most gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?

subquestions.question: Will NASA successfully complete a wet dress rehearsal for the Artemis II mission before February 16, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
NASA rolled out the Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft to Launch Pad 39B at the Kennedy Space Center on January 17, 2026. The next critical milestone before the crewed launch is a 'wet dress rehearsal' (WDR). During the WDR, the rocket is fully loaded with super-cold cryogenic propellants (liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen) and the launch team simulates a full countdown sequence. The WDR is currently targeted for on or around February 2, 2026. According to NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, no official launch date will be announced until the WDR is successfully completed. A successful WDR is a strict prerequisite for the mission. Delays or failures during the WDR, such as the hydrogen leaks experienced during the Artemis I campaign, could require the rocket to be rolled back to the Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB) and push the launch out of the February window. Thus, completing the WDR by mid-February is a crucial indicator for whether the Artemis II mission can launch by the end of February.

Sources:
NASA Artemis Blog: https://blogs.nasa.gov/artemis/
CBS News Space: https://www.cbsnews.com/space/
SciTechDaily Space News: https://scitechdaily.com/news/space/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if NASA officially announces the successful completion of a wet dress rehearsal (WDR) for the Artemis II mission between 2026-01-21 and 2026-02-16T00:00:00Z (inclusive). A 'successful completion' is defined as NASA confirming that they have loaded the Space Launch System (SLS) with cryogenic propellants, executed the simulated countdown sequence to the planned cutoff point, and declared the test complete such that no additional full WDR is required before launch. Resolution will be determined by official press releases, blog posts, or video statements from NASA (e.g., https://blogs.nasa.gov/artemis/ or https://www.nasa.gov/). If NASA requires an additional WDR that is not completed by the end date, or if the test is postponed past the resolution window, the question resolves No. If NASA formally cancels the WDR requirement entirely and clears the vehicle for launch within the resolution window, this will also resolve as Yes.
subquestions.rationale: The wet dress rehearsal is the most critical hurdle remaining before the Artemis II launch. Artemis I experienced multiple WDR failures and rollback delays due to propellant leaks. Successfully passing the WDR by mid-February is a strong indicator of whether the vehicle is healthy enough to launch before February 28. If the WDR fails or is delayed past this date, a February launch becomes highly improbable due to the time required to analyze data, address anomalies, and reset ground systems.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: NASA officially announces successful WDR completion between 2026-01-21 and 2026-02-16T00:00:00Z (inclusive), defined as: (1) SLS loaded with cryogenic propellants, (2) simulated countdown executed to planned cutoff point, AND (3) NASA declares no additional full WDR required before launch. Observable evidence: Official NASA press release, blog post, or statement confirming all three criteria.

question: Will Israel annex West Bank territory in 2025?

Annexation is defined as an official declaration or legal act by the Israeli government claiming sovereignty over territory in the West Bank they were not claiming at the time of this market's creation.

Qualifying examples of annexation include the 1980 Jerusalem Law, and the Golan Heights Law, however instances where Israeli settlers claiming administrative control over land in the West Bank without a formal annexation will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Israeli government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu publicly announce an intention to annex or "apply sovereignty" to any territory in the West Bank between September 2, 2025, and October 2, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In late August and early September 2025, reports emerged that the Israeli government is considering the annexation of parts of the occupied West Bank. This move is reportedly being weighed as a response to anticipated declarations by France, the UK, Australia, and Canada to formally recognize a Palestinian state at the UN General Assembly summit in September 2025 (https://www.al-monitor.com). According to Israeli media, the security cabinet scheduled discussions on this matter in early September, and Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar has reportedly informed U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Israel intends to announce annexation 'soon' (https://www.middleeasteye.net). Because a formal annexation or 'application of sovereignty' requires extensive legislative or executive procedures, a public declaration by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would likely precede the final legal act. Tracking whether Netanyahu makes such a declaration during the critical September UN General Assembly window provides a highly informative early indicator of whether formal legal annexation will actually take place by the end of 2025.

Middle East Eye - https://www.middleeasteye.net
Al-Monitor - https://www.al-monitor.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-02 and 2025-10-02 (inclusive), Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu makes a public statement explicitly declaring that his government intends to, or has decided to, "annex" or "apply Israeli sovereignty" to any portion of the West Bank (often referred to by the Israeli government as Judea and Samaria). The statement must be made publicly by Netanyahu himself, such as in a speech, press conference, television broadcast, on his official verified social media accounts, or in an official press release from the Prime Minister's Office. Internal anonymous leaks, unconfirmed reports, or statements by other cabinet ministers (e.g., Gideon Sa'ar or Bezalel Smotrich) do not count toward a Yes resolution unless Netanyahu explicitly confirms them publicly within the resolution window. The primary resolution sources will be the official website of the Israeli Prime Minister's Office (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office/govil-landing-page) and a consensus of reporting from major credible news organizations such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) and The Times of Israel (https://www.timesofisrael.com).
subquestions.rationale: A public commitment by Prime Minister Netanyahu is a critical and highly visible precursor for the Israeli government to formally execute a controversial and legally complex move like annexation. Given that the immediate motivation for annexation is reportedly a response to the UN General Assembly summit in September, if Netanyahu does not publicly announce this intent by early October, it strongly suggests the plans have been delayed or shelved, substantially reducing the probability of a formal legal annexation occurring by the end of 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Netanyahu himself publicly declares his government intends to or has decided to 'annex' or 'apply Israeli sovereignty' to any portion of the West Bank, between 2025-09-02 and 2025-10-02 inclusive. Must be a public statement (speech, press conference, social media, official PMO release). Statements by other ministers or anonymous leaks do not count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Netanyahu annex West Bank sovereignty announcement 2025' (Sep 2 - Oct 2). Query 2: 'Israel apply sovereignty Judea Samaria West Bank September 2025' (Sep 2 - Oct 2). Query 3: 'Netanyahu statement declare sovereignty West Bank announcement September October 2025' (Sep 2 - Oct 2). Query 4: 'Netanyahu apply sovereignty OR annex West Bank speech press conference October 2025' (Sep 25 - Oct 2). Query 5: 'Netanyahu Trump White House meeting West Bank sovereignty outcome September 29 October 2025' (Sep 29 - Oct 2). Query 6: 'Netanyahu no Palestinian state sovereignty announcement official declaration West Bank 2025' (Sep 2 - Oct 2).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Netanyahu dropped sovereignty from ministerial agenda on Sep 4 after UAE warning [Yahoo/Worthy Christian News, Sep 4]. (2) Netanyahu signed E1 settlement expansion on Sep 11, declared 'there will be no Palestinian state' [Times of Israel, Sep 11] — does not explicitly state annexation intent. (3) Netanyahu declared 'no Palestinian state west of the Jordan' on Sep 21-22 — expansion pledge, not annexation declaration. (4) Netanyahu's UN speech Sep 26 — focused on Gaza/Hamas, no annexation declaration. (5) Netanyahu met settler leaders Sep 28-29, pledged to raise sovereignty issue with Trump but acknowledged 'complicated reality.' (6) Trump-Netanyahu White House meeting Sep 29 — no annexation announcement; plan includes prohibition on annexation. All candidate events involving Netanyahu himself either: (a) relate to different cabinet ministers (Smotrich, Ben-Gvir) calling for annexation; (b) are Netanyahu's 'no Palestinian state' statements which don't explicitly declare annexation intent; or (c) show Netanyahu shelving or softening annexation push due to US and UAE pressure.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No found statement by Netanyahu himself explicitly declares intent to annex or apply sovereignty to the West Bank within the window. Key distinctions: (a) 'There will be no Palestinian state' [Times of Israel, Sep 11](https://www.timesofisrael.com/there-will-be-no-palestinian-state-pm-signs-plan-cementing-e1-settlement-expansion/) is not the same as announcing annexation/sovereignty application. (b) Netanyahu shelved annexation from ministerial agenda Sep 4 [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/netanyahu-drops-w-bank-sovereignty-105013264.html). (c) Netanyahu met settler leaders Sep 28-29 but said annexation faces 'complicated reality' and did not publicly declare intent [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/netanyahu-meets-settler-leaders-pledges-to-raise-west-bank-sovereignty-with-trump-report/).
