(e) After Trump-Netanyahu White House meeting Sep 29-30, a 21-point plan with annexation prohibition was discussed [CNN, getuperica.com]. Smotrich's Sep 3 annexation maps announcement does not count per resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found — Netanyahu himself did not make an explicit public declaration of annexation/sovereignty application intent during the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was found, as Netanyahu did not make the required type of statement at any point during the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple sources confirm Netanyahu shelved the sovereignty agenda from his ministerial session (Sep 4), acknowledged 'complicated reality' with Trump opposing annexation (Sep 28-29), and the Trump-Netanyahu White House meeting produced a 21-point plan that includes a prohibition on annexation (Sep 29-30). Netanyahu's statements about 'no Palestinian state' and settlement expansion do not meet the explicit annexation/sovereignty declaration threshold required by the resolution criteria. The question's criteria specifically excludes internal anonymous leaks or other ministers' statements — both of which dominated the period. Netanyahu's own public statements were settlement expansion/no-Palestinian-state framing, not explicit annexation declarations.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying event occurred within the window. Netanyahu did not publicly announce an intention to annex or apply sovereignty to the West Bank between Sep 2 and Oct 2, 2025. Instead, he shelved the issue from his ministerial agenda (Sep 4), made 'no Palestinian state' and settlement expansion declarations (Sep 11-22) that do not rise to the explicit annexation/sovereignty threshold, faced Trump's explicit opposition to annexation (Sep 25), acknowledged a 'complicated reality' on annexation to settler leaders (Sep 28-29), and participated in a White House meeting whose output plan included an annexation prohibition (Sep 29-30). Resolution: No.

Early projections for 'Wicked: For Good' range from $112 million up to $190 million. Because 'Zootopia 2' needs to secure exactly the second-highest domestic opening weekend of 2025 to resolve the ultimate question as 'Yes', the performance of 'Wicked: For Good' serves as a massive crux. If 'Wicked: For Good' grosses $130 million or more, 'Zootopia 2' would face a much steeper uphill battle to claim the #2 spot, as it would likely need to surpass both 'Wicked: For Good' and 'Lilo & Stitch' ($141M).

The Numbers: https://www.the-numbers.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if the final reported 3-day domestic opening weekend box office gross (Friday, Saturday, Sunday) for 'Wicked: For Good' is $130,000,000 or greater. Resolution will be based on the official 'Weekend Box Office Performance' data published by The Numbers (https://www.the-numbers.com) or, if unavailable, Box Office Mojo (https://www.boxofficemojo.com). Studio estimates do not count; the official final weekend actuals must be used. To count toward resolution, the qualifying opening weekend event and the publication of the final box office numbers must occur between the start_date of 2025-10-31 and the end_date of 2025-11-28 (inclusive). If the film is delayed beyond this window or the final numbers are not published by the end_date, the question resolves as 'Unresolved'.
subquestions.rationale: For 'Zootopia 2' to have the second-best domestic opening weekend of 2025, it must slot perfectly behind the number one film (currently 'A Minecraft Movie' at $162M) and ahead of all others, including 'Lilo & Stitch' ($141M). If 'Wicked: For Good', which opens one week before 'Zootopia 2', grosses $130 million or more, it further saturates the top tiers of the 2025 box office. Since 'Zootopia 2' is currently tracking between $95M and $130M, a massive opening for 'Wicked' would severely reduce the statistical likelihood of 'Zootopia 2' taking the #2 rank, providing forecasters with a strong early indicator to update their ultimate predictions.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: 'Wicked: For Good' must have a final reported 3-day domestic opening weekend (Friday-Sunday) box office gross of $130,000,000 or greater, as officially reported by The Numbers or Box Office Mojo. The opening weekend must occur and final actuals be published between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-28 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Wicked For Good box office opening weekend 2025' — to find overall results; 2) 'Wicked Part 2 For Good domestic box office gross November 2025' — to find domestic specifics; 3) 'Wicked For Good opening weekend final actuals The Numbers Box Office Mojo official' — to find official actuals; 4) '$150 million OR $147 million final actuals weekend November 23 2025' — to confirm the precise figure; 5) 'Wicked For Good weekend box office actuals final numbers November 24 25 2025' — to find post-weekend final actuals.

Both figures vastly exceed $130 million. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists (film released Nov 21, 2025). No events were rejected as all directly address the opening weekend performance.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The ABC News article published November 24, 2025 states: 'earned approximately $147 million at the domestic box office during its opening weekend, according to The Numbers.' [ABC News](https://abcnews.go.com/GMA/Culture/jonathan-bailey-surprises-sister-fans-wicked-good-screening/story?id=127829084). The Koimoi UK article published November 25, 2025 also cites $147 million as the domestic actual: 'Domestically, the film grossed $147 million in its opening weekend.' [Koimoi](https://www.koimoi.com/box-office/wicked-for-good-united-kingdom-box-office-ariana-grandes-film-collects-20m-scoring-the-biggest-opening-weekend-of-2025/). The Movieweb streaming article (Nov 26) also cites ~$147 million. Both $147M and $150M exceed the $130M threshold by a wide margin. The opening weekend (Nov 21-23, 2025) and publication of final numbers (by Nov 24-25) both fall within the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: ABC News published November 24, 2025, citing The Numbers for $147 million domestic opening weekend. Multiple other sources on November 23-25, 2025 confirm the opening weekend gross. The film opened November 21, 2025; the opening weekend concluded November 23, 2025; official actuals were published November 24, 2025. All within the resolution window of Oct 31 – Nov 28, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The film's opening weekend was November 21-23, 2025. This is the first and only opening weekend. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists. The final actuals from The Numbers were published on or around November 24, 2025, within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence found. The only variation is between $147M (actuals per The Numbers, as cited by ABC News and Koimoi) and $150M (studio estimates, as reported by most outlets including CNN, TheWrap, People, USA Today). Even the lower figure of $147M comfortably exceeds the $130M threshold. The resolution criteria specifies final actuals from The Numbers; the $147M figure is explicitly attributed to The Numbers by ABC News (Nov 24, 2025). There is no report of the film being delayed or the opening weekend falling outside the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Wicked: For Good opened November 21, 2025, with a 3-day domestic opening weekend gross of approximately $147–150 million, well above the $130 million threshold. The Numbers specifically reported ~$147 million in actuals (cited by ABC News on November 24, 2025). Both the opening event and the publication of final actuals occurred within the resolution window (Oct 31 – Nov 28, 2025). Resolution: YES.

question: X relaunches Vine in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if X relaunches Vine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

"Relaunching Vine" is defined as launching a platform and/or feature that performs similar functions to Vine, and is branded as a "relaunch of Vine" by Elon Musk or X itself. Note - the relaunch must be live and broadly accessible to the public before the resolution date for this market to resolve to "Yes".

The primary resolution source will be the Vine platform, as well as official information from Elon Musk and X, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will X make the original Vine video archive publicly accessible by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In mid-2025, Elon Musk announced plans to bring back the defunct short-video platform Vine, incorporating AI tools such as a new generator called 'Grok Imagine' (https://nypost.com). As part of this revival, X reportedly found the full library of the original Vine video archive and began working on restoring user access (https://winbuzzer.com). Tech outlets indicated that this restored archive could go live as early as October 2025, setting the stage for the platform's broader relaunch. Monitoring the release of the historical archive serves as an excellent early indicator of X's progress toward fully relaunching the Vine platform.

Sources:
Winbuzzer: https://winbuzzer.com
New York Post: https://nypost.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if X (formerly Twitter) makes a dedicated archive of original Vine videos publicly accessible to users between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). The archive must be accessible to the general public without requiring special developer access and must allow users to view historical Vine content. Resolution will be based on official announcements or confirmation from Elon Musk's official X account (https://x.com/elonmusk), the official X platform account (https://x.com/X), or a consensus of credible technology reporting (e.g., https://www.theverge.com or https://techcrunch.com) confirming the archive is live and broadly accessible. A closed beta or private employee test does not count; the archive must be broadly accessible to standard X users or the public web. If no such archive is made public within the resolution window, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: The release of the original Vine archive has been reported as an imminent first step in Musk's strategy to revive the Vine brand. If X successfully launches the archive in October 2025, it demonstrates active, outward-facing progress on the Vine project, increasing the probability that the full platform/feature relaunch will occur by the end of 2025. Conversely, missing this reported October target suggests potential delays in the roadmap, lowering the chances of a 2025 full relaunch.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: X must make a dedicated archive of original Vine videos publicly accessible to the general public (not just beta/employee access) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. Observable evidence would be: credible tech news reports (The Verge, TechCrunch) confirming the archive is live and accessible, or official announcements from @elonmusk or @X confirming the archive is accessible.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'X Twitter Vine video archive publicly accessible 2025' (Oct 1–31) — to find launch reports; 2) 'Elon Musk Vine archive launch October 2025' (Oct 1–31) — to find Musk-specific announcements; 3) 'Vine archive live public access October 2025 X platform' (Oct 1–31) — to find confirmation of live access; 4) 'Vine videos restored archive Theverge Techcrunch X platform' (Oct 1–31) — to find credible tech outlet confirmation; 5) 'Vine video archive restore accessible users Musk announcement' (Sep–Oct 2025) — broader context search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: One candidate event found: A DEV Community blog post (dev.to) published October 28, 2025 titled 'Elon Musk Announces the Return of Vine's Archive.' The summary describes Musk announcing plans to restore Vine's archive. REJECTED as qualifying event because: (1) It describes an announcement/plan, not a live accessible archive; (2) The source explicitly states 'specific implementation details remain unclear'; (3) DEV Community is a user-generated blog platform, not a credible tech outlet per resolution criteria; (4) No corroborating reports from The Verge, TechCrunch, or official X accounts confirm the archive is live. Social Media Today (Oct 6) describes Musk's 'broader goal to build an AI-powered version of Vine' — framing as future goal, not accomplished fact.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires the archive to be 'publicly accessible' and 'broadly accessible to standard X users or the public web,' confirmed by 'official announcements from @elonmusk or @X' or 'a consensus of credible technology reporting (e.g., theverge.com or techcrunch.com) confirming the archive is live and broadly accessible.' The only source found ([DEV Community](https://dev.to/yagyaraj_sharma_6cd410179/title-elon-musk-announces-the-return-of-vines-archive-d90)) describes an announcement of intent, not a live archive. No Verge or TechCrunch articles confirm a live Vine archive. No official X or Musk posts confirming the archive is accessible were found. Criteria NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp (i.e., when the archive became publicly accessible) could be extracted because no evidence of the archive going live was found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event (publicly accessible archive) was identified.
evidence.step7_verification: Searched multiple variations. The Social Media Today article from Oct 6 confirms that Musk has a goal to 'build an AI-powered version of Vine' — framing it as a future aspiration, not a completed action. The DEV Community article about an 'announcement' is a user blog post, not a credible report. No TechCrunch, Verge, or official X account confirmation of a live Vine archive was found across multiple searches. No contradictions found that would suggest a live archive exists but went unreported.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence shows at most an announcement of intent to restore Vine's archive (from a low-credibility DEV Community user blog), not an actual publicly accessible archive. The resolution criteria specifically requires the archive to be live and broadly accessible, confirmed by credible tech reporting or official announcements. No such confirmation exists. The question resolves No, with the resolution date being the end of the resolution window (2025-10-31) since no earlier definitive foreclosure event is identified — just absence of the required event throughout the window.

question: Will Wesley Hunt come in 3rd in the 2026 Texas Republican Primary?
description:

If no 2026 Texas Republican Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will at least one of John Cornyn or Ken Paxton publicly agree to participate in a primary debate with Wesley Hunt between November 26, 2025, and December 26, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Early polling from the University of Houston showed Hunt trailing at 22%, compared to Paxton's 34% and Cornyn's 33% (https://www.yahoo.com/news/polls-tighten-wesley-hunt-enters-140000305.html). In an effort to elevate his profile and directly challenge the frontrunners, Hunt publicly called for a formal 75-minute live debate with Cornyn and Paxton on October 30, 2025 (https://www.yahoo.com/news/hunt-calls-debate-cornyn-paxton-184500912.html). As of late November, no debate has been officially scheduled, though polling has remained tight with no clear frontrunner emerging (https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/texas-sen-john-cornyn-locked-in-close-polling-with-ag-ken-paxton-and-rep-wesley-hunt/).

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The agreement must be made publicly via an official campaign press release, an official candidate social media account, or be confirmed by a credible news organization (such as The Texas Tribune: https://www.texastribune.org/, or The Dallas Morning News: https://www.dallasnews.com/). The agreement must be for a debate scheduled to occur before the Texas primary election on March 3, 2026.

If neither Cornyn nor Paxton publicly agrees to a debate including Hunt between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26, or if they explicitly decline all such debates during this window, this question resolves No. If an agreement is announced within the resolution window but the debate is subsequently canceled, the question still resolves Yes as long as the initial agreement was officially and publicly confirmed during the specified timeframe.
subquestions.rationale: Wesley Hunt's ability to avoid a 3rd place finish depends heavily on raising his profile to match the near-universal name recognition of Cornyn and Paxton. Getting the frontrunners to share a debate stage with him is a critical step in overcoming this gap. If Cornyn or Paxton agree to debate Hunt, it signals they view his polling as a legitimate threat, increasing his odds of breaking out of 3rd place. If they ignore his October 30th challenge entirely, it suggests they believe they can safely starve his campaign of oxygen, making a 3rd place finish much more likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Between Nov 26–Dec 26, 2025, the official campaign of Cornyn or Paxton (or both) publicly confirms agreement to participate in a Texas Republican primary debate that includes Wesley Hunt. Must be via official campaign press release, official candidate social media, or credible news outlet. Debate must be scheduled before March 3, 2026 primary.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Texas Republican primary debate Cornyn Paxton Wesley Hunt 2025' (Nov 26–Dec 26); Query 2: 'Texas Senate race primary debate 2026 Republican candidates' (Nov 26–Dec 26); Query 3: 'Cornyn Paxton Hunt Republican primary debate agreement November December 2025' (Nov 26–Dec 26); Query 4: 'Texas Senate Republican debate invitation challenge 2026 primary' (Nov 26–Dec 26); Query 5: 'Wesley Hunt debate challenge Cornyn Paxton Republican primary Texas' (Nov 26–Dec 26); Query 6: 'Texas Senate GOP primary debate scheduled 2026' (Nov 1–Dec 26); Query 7: 'Cornyn Paxton debate decline refuse Texas Senate primary' (Nov 26–Dec 26); Query 8: 'Texas Tribune Texas Senate Republican primary debate agreement confirmed' (Nov 1–Dec 26).
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events found regarding a Republican primary debate agreement between Cornyn, Paxton, and Hunt. The only debate-related news was Wesley Hunt challenging Jasmine Crockett (Democrat) to a general election debate on Dec 12, 2025—this is not a Republican primary debate and does not involve Cornyn or Paxton. All other articles from the window cover polling, campaign strategy, immigration legislation, divorce records, and filing deadlines—with no mention of any Republican primary debate agreement.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article directly confirms that Cornyn's or Paxton's campaign officially agreed to a Republican primary debate including Wesley Hunt. The only debate-related article [Fox News Dec 12](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/texas-senate-candidate-challenges-jasmine-crockett-public-debate) concerns a general election debate challenge by Hunt to Democrat Jasmine Crockett—entirely different from the required criteria. Dallas Morning News Dec 9 [https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/2025/12/08/texas-gop-primary-field-set-in-us-senate-race-after-months-of-sparring-by-top-contenders/] describes the primary field as set but mentions no debate agreement.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp exists within the resolution window for a debate agreement between Cornyn/Paxton and Hunt in the Republican primary.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found in the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Extensive search across multiple credible sources (Texas Tribune, Dallas Morning News, Newsweek, Breitbart, Daily Caller, NY Post, Semafor, Fox News) finds no evidence of any Republican primary debate agreement involving Cornyn, Paxton, and Hunt during the resolution window. The absence of such reporting is itself significant, given the extensive coverage of this race. evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying event occurred within the window. question: Fed governor resigns by October 31?

subquestions.question: Will Fed Governor Lisa Cook be listed as a voting member in the official FOMC statement for the September 2025 meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 26, 2025, President Donald Trump claimed to have fired Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over alleged mortgage fraud (https://www.morningstar.com/news/morning-headlines-trump-removing-fed-governor-lisa-cook). Cook has publicly refused to step down, stating that the President lacks the legal authority to remove her and that she will not resign (https://wtop.com/national/2025/08/the-latest-fed-governor-wont-leave-saying-trump-lacks-authority-to-fire-her/). While Cook's legal team prepares to fight the dismissal, White House officials have suggested she should be placed on administrative leave until the matter is resolved (https://edition.cnn.com/2025/08/28/economy/inside-trumps-attempt-to-put-his-mark-on-the-fed/index.html). The next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting is scheduled for September 16-17, 2025. As a member of the Board of Governors, Cook is a permanent voting member of the FOMC. Whether she is permitted to vote at this meeting will serve as a clear indicator of her current status and whether she is successfully holding her position.

Sources:
Morningstar: Dow Jones Top Markets Headlines at 3 AM ET - https://www.morningstar.com/news/morning-headlines-trump-removing-fed-governor-lisa-cook
WTOP News: The Latest: Fed governor won't leave - https://wtop.com/national/2025/08/the-latest-fed-governor-wont-leave-saying-trump-lacks-authority-to-fire-her/
CNN International: 'We just jumped into the unknown:' Inside Trump's attempt to put his mark on the Fed - https://edition.cnn.com/2025/08/28/economy/inside-trumps-attempt-to-put-his-mark-on-the-fed/index.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the official Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) statement released following the September 2025 meeting explicitly lists Lisa Cook (or Lisa D. Cook) as having voted on the monetary policy action, and this statement is published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

The primary resolution source will be the official FOMC press release published on the Federal Reserve's website (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm).

Specifically, resolvers should review the paragraph in the statement that records the votes, which typically begins with 'Voting for the monetary policy action were...' or 'Voting against the action...'. If Lisa Cook's name appears in either of these lists, the question resolves Yes.

If she is listed as absent, abstaining, not listed at all, or if the FOMC statement is not released within the specified window (between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01), the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Lisa Cook's participation in the September 16-17, 2025 FOMC meeting is a critical observable event for predicting her potential resignation. Following President Trump's unprecedented attempt to fire her and her refusal to step down, her ability to cast a vote on monetary policy will prove whether she has maintained her active status on the Board of Governors. If she is listed as a voting member, it indicates she has successfully resisted removal and has not been forced onto administrative leave or pressured into resigning ahead of the meeting. This would significantly lower the probability of her resigning by the October 31 ultimate deadline. Conversely, if she does not vote, it strongly suggests she has either resigned, been legally suspended, or conceded her position, making a formal resignation announcement much more likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The official FOMC statement for the September 2025 meeting must explicitly list 'Lisa Cook' or 'Lisa D. Cook' as having voted (for or against) the monetary policy action, and the statement must be published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Observable evidence: the text of the official FOMC press release from federalreserve.gov, specifically the voting paragraph. Key entities: Lisa D. Cook, FOMC September 2025 meeting. Timing: statement published 2025-09-17, within window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'FOMC September 2025 meeting statement voting members' — to find the official FOMC statement and list of voting members. Query 2: 'Lisa Cook FOMC September 2025 Federal Reserve vote' — to find specific references to Cook's participation. Query 3: 'Federal Reserve FOMC statement September 17 2025 Lisa D. Cook voting' — to confirm explicit mention of Cook in voting record.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: FOMC September 17, 2025 meeting with official statement published the same day. Multiple sources report this, including the official Federal Reserve press release at https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20250917a.htm. The FinanzNachrichten article directly quotes the FOMC statement's voting paragraph listing 'Lisa D. Cook' as voting for the action. No rejection needed — evidence is direct and explicit.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The FinanzNachrichten article [FOMC Lowers Federal Funds Target Range by 0.25 Percentage Point](https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2025-09/66463969-dokumentation-begleittext-zum-beschluss-der-us-notenbank-015.htm) directly quotes the official FOMC statement: 'Voting for the action was carried by Chair Jerome H. Powell, Vice Chair John C. Williams, and nine other members: Michael S. Barr, Michelle W. Bowman, Susan M. Collins, Lisa D. Cook, Austan D. Goolsbee, Philip N. Jefferson, Alberto G. Musalem, Jeffrey R. Schmid, and Christopher J. Waller.' The official Federal Reserve press release source [monetary20250917a.htm](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20250917a.htm) also confirms the voting occurred on September 17, 2025. Lisa D. Cook's name appears explicitly in the voting list, exactly matching the resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The official FOMC statement was published on September 17, 2025, as reported by the Federal Reserve's own press release. Multiple independent sources confirm this date. Exact timestamp from the Federal Reserve press release: 2025-09-17 (published at approximately 2:00 PM ET based on standard FOMC practice). ISO 8601 UTC: 2025-09-17T18:00:00Z (standard FOMC statement release time is 2:00 PM ET = 18:00 UTC).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is the first and only FOMC statement in the September 2025 window. There is no earlier qualifying occurrence. The September 16-17, 2025 FOMC meeting is the relevant meeting, and the statement was released September 17, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: There were concerns about Lisa Cook's removal by the Trump administration, but courts ruled in her favor before the meeting (U.S. Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit denied Trump's bid on September 15-16, 2025). Multiple sources confirm she participated in the vote. The only dissenter was Stephen Miran (voting for a larger 50 bps cut). No contradictory evidence that Cook was absent, abstained, or not listed. The official Federal Reserve website URL (monetary20250917a.htm) is directly cited in search results.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The official FOMC statement released on September 17, 2025, explicitly lists 'Lisa D. Cook' as voting for the monetary policy action (the 25 bps rate cut). This is within the resolution window (September 1–October 1, 2025). The evidence is direct, explicit, from the official Federal Reserve press release, and confirmed by multiple independent sources. Resolution: Yes.

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces capture any part of Zarichne (Donetsk Oblast) by November 15, 2025?

For Russian forces to realistically reach and capture the Lyman railway station (located centrally within Lyman) by late November, they would almost certainly need to first penetrate or capture the adjacent settlement of Zarichne, which sits less than 5 kilometers from Lyman's eastern outskirts. Tracking the status of Zarichne serves as a strong leading indicator: if Zarichne falls or is entered by mid-November, the immediate threat to Lyman city proper and its railway station increases significantly.

question: Will Silver (SI) hit (HIGH) $110 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Silver (SI) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Silver (SI) futures contracts, the Active Month is the nearest of CME's designated delivery-cycle months (March, May, July, September, December) that is not the spot month. The Active Month becomes a non-active month effective on its First Position Date, at which point the next eligible contract month becomes the Active Month.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures.

subquestions.question: Will the CME Group announce an increase in margin requirements for COMEX Silver (SI) futures between December 27, 2025 and January 20, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent extreme volatility in the silver market has sparked rumors of structural stress in the COMEX physical delivery system. In late November 2025, silver futures saw dramatic price action followed by a trading halt. While the exchange attributed this to a data center 'cooling failure' (https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/20251128/cme-data-center-issue-hits-options-futures-trading-update), alternative reports suggested the halt coincided with an Authorized Participant attempting to take physical delivery of 400 million ounces of silver, exposing a massive paper short position (https://truthsocial.com/). As of early December 2025, front-month silver was trading around $59 to $62 per ounce (https://apnews.com/article/gold-silver-futures-december-2025). December 31, 2025, is viewed by some market participants as a critical deadline for derivative exposures to be settled. If silver prices are genuinely on a trajectory to reach a historic $110 by June 2026, it would require an explosive rally and severe market volatility. In response to such unprecedented volatility and to protect the clearinghouse from default risks, the CME Group frequently increases margin requirements (performance bonds) for futures contracts. Therefore, an official increase in silver futures margin requirements by the CME Group in the weeks following the critical year-end settlement period would serve as a strong early indicator of the exchange managing an unprecedented price spike or physical squeeze.

Sources:
AP News. "BC-Gold-Silver". https://apnews.com/article/gold-silver-futures-december-2025
Morningstar. "CME Data-Center Issue Hits Options, Futures Trading". https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/20251128/cme-data-center-issue-hits-options-futures-trading-update
Donald J. Trump. "CME's 'Cooling Failure'". https://truthsocial.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The announcement must be published on the official CME Group website, specifically within their Clearing Advisories or Notices sections (e.g., https://www.cmegroup.com/notices/clearing.html or https://www.cmegroup.com/clearing/risk-management/clearing-advisories.html) or on the CME Margins page (https://www.cmegroup.com/clearing/risk-management/performance-bonds-margins.html) during the specified resolution window.

The margin increase must apply to the outright COMEX Silver (SI) futures contract for at least one active contract month. Intraday margin increases, maintenance margin increases, or initial margin increases all qualify, provided they represent a definitive numerical increase from the margin levels in effect immediately preceding the announcement.

If no such margin increase is announced for Silver (SI) futures by the CME Group between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-20 (inclusive), the question resolves No. In the event the CME Group website is permanently unavailable during the resolution period, verifiable reporting by at least two major financial news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg at https://www.bloomberg.com, Reuters at https://www.reuters.com, or the Wall Street Journal at https://www.wsj.com) stating that CME increased silver margin requirements during the resolution window will be sufficient to resolve the question as Yes. Delayed implementations do not affect resolution as long as the announcement itself is made within the resolution window.
subquestions.rationale: A massive price surge from current levels of roughly $60 to $110 per ounce within six months would entail unprecedented volatility and potential systemic stress, as suggested by recent reports of a 400 million ounce delivery squeeze. To mitigate risk during such explosive, parabolic rallies, commodity exchanges like the CME Group invariably raise margin requirements to ensure the clearinghouse's stability (as seen historically in massive short squeezes). If silver is truly embarking on a historic run towards $110 early in the year, the CME is highly likely to proactively increase margin requirements in late December or January to curb excessive speculation and shore up systemic defenses. This makes a margin increase a highly informative, objective early indicator for the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: CME Group publishes an official Clearing Advisory or notice announcing an increase in initial or maintenance margin requirements for COMEX Silver (SI) futures between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-20. Observable evidence: official CME advisory with explicit numerical increase in margin levels for at least one active Silver (SI) contract month. Key entities: CME Group, COMEX Silver (SI) futures. Threshold: definitive numerical increase from immediately preceding margin levels. Timing: announcement within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'CME Group COMEX Silver SI futures margin requirements increase 2025 2026' — to find primary news coverage; 2) 'CME clearing advisory COMEX Silver margin performance bond January 2026' — to find official advisory references; 3) 'CME Advisory 25-393 silver margin December 29 2025' — to verify specific advisory number; 4) 'CME Group clearing advisory silver margin increase January 13 2026' — to find January announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Three qualifying events identified: (1) CME Advisory 25-393, announced ~Dec 26-27, 2025, effective Dec 29, 2025 — raised SI initial margin from $22,000 to $25,000 for March 2026 contracts. (2) Second margin increase, announced Dec 31, 2025, effective after close Dec 31, 2025 — additional increase for silver, gold, platinum, palladium. (3) January 13, 2026 change: CME shifted from fixed dollar to percentage-based margins, setting silver at 9% of notional value (up from ~7.2% in mid-December), effective at close of January 13, 2026. evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is YES. CME Group announced multiple margin increases for COMEX Silver (SI) futures during the resolution window (December 27, 2025 – January 20, 2026). A second increase was announced December 31, 2025, effective same day. A third change occurred January 13, 2026, shifting to percentage-based margins at 9% (a further increase). Evidence from multiple credible financial news outlets is direct, consistent, and explicit. No inference is required.

question: Transgender women be banned from the Olympics before Winter Games?

You can read more about that here: https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/nov/10/ioc-edges-closer-to-ban-on-transgender-women-in-female-olympic-events.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the International Olympic Committee (IOC) officially bans transgender women from competing in the female category by February 5, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying ban must affect at least one sport and apply to at least one clearly defined group, for example, transgender women who have undergone male puberty, individuals subject to specified testosterone-threshold policies, or athletes with differences of sexual development (DSD).

An official declaration of a qualifying ban within the specified timeframe will suffice, regardless of whether it is later revoked. 

Only IOC-imposed bans will qualify; bans or eligibility rules issued by other authorities, such as International Federations or National Olympic Committees, will not qualify. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be official IOC communications; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the IOC publish an official agenda, schedule, or press release confirming that athlete gender eligibility will be discussed or voted on at the pre-Winter Games meetings?

IOC President Kirsty Coventry has stated that the IOC intends to finalize and possibly announce the policy by early 2026. A decision is widely expected to be presented, discussed, or voted on during the IOC Executive Board meeting or the 145th IOC Session, both of which take place in Milan right before the Winter Games opening on February 6, 2026. Because significant policy changes must undergo formal review, the official publication of an agenda or press release previewing this topic would serve as a critical precursor to the actual enactment of a ban.

The IOC may have intentionally kept this off the public agenda given the sensitivity. No official IOC document confirming this topic explicitly was found.

subquestions.question: Will the United States officially announce an intent to provide strategic enabling support (such as ISR or command-and-control) to a foreign peacekeeping or reassurance force in Ukraine between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent reports indicate that European nations, particularly the UK and France, are leading discussions on the creation of a 'reassurance force' or peacekeeping mission to be deployed in Ukraine following a potential ceasefire or peace deal. According to EurActiv, a 'Coalition of the Willing' is preparing to outline this proposed force in early September 2025. However, experts and European officials emphasize that such a force heavily depends on the United States acting as a 'strategic enabler.' The Financial Times reported that the US is considering providing critical capabilities like intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), command-and-control (C2), and air-defense assets to backstop the European mission. The Pentagon has so far characterized these discussions as 'pre-decisional' and maintained that no US ground troops will be deployed. Because many European nations lack the necessary logistical and intelligence capabilities to independently sustain a large deployment in a high-threat environment, formal US commitment of these supporting assets is widely seen as a prerequisite for European countries to finalize and announce their troop commitments.

Sources:
EurActiv - Who's in and who's out of Ukraine's 'reassurance force': https://www.euractiv.com/
Kyiv Independent - US may provide intelligence, air defense assets to European peacekeepers in Ukraine: https://kyivindependent.com/
Responsible Statecraft - Report: NATO, US heavily involved in post-war Ukrainian security: https://responsiblestatecraft.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the United States government officially announces or confirms its intent to provide strategic enabling support to a European-led, multinational, or third-party peacekeeping, reassurance, or buffer-zone force inside Ukraine.

Qualifying support includes, but is not limited to, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), command-and-control (C2), logistics, or air-defense. The commitment must be explicitly linked to a foreign troop presence or peacekeeping mission in Ukraine; general statements regarding continued military aid or support for the Ukrainian Armed Forces do not qualify.

The announcement must be made publicly via an official press release, a published policy document, or a public statement/briefing by a cabinet-level official (e.g., the President, Secretary of Defense, Secretary of State) or their official spokespersons. The primary sources for resolution will be official US government websites (https://www.defense.gov, https://www.whitehouse.gov, https://www.state.gov) and credible mainstream news reporting of such statements. 

If no qualifying announcement is made by 2025-10-01 at 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves No. If an event or announcement is delayed and occurs outside this specific window, it will not count toward a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: European military planners lack the independent intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) and command-and-control (C2) capabilities required to safely operate a large-scale peacekeeping mission in a contested environment like Ukraine. Consequently, European leaders have heavily conditioned their troop commitments on the US providing this strategic 'backstop'. Forecasting whether the US officially commits to this support in the near term provides a high-value leading indicator for the ultimate question: a 'Yes' greatly increases the likelihood that EU/NATO members will confidently follow through and announce their own troop deployments, while a 'No' suggests the reassurance force may stall due to critical capability gaps.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: (1) Official US government announcement via press release/policy document/cabinet-level public statement; (2) explicit intent to provide strategic enabling support (ISR, C2, logistics, air-defense); (3) specifically linked to a foreign peacekeeping/reassurance force inside Ukraine; (4) made between Sept 1-Oct 1, 2025. Observable evidence: official government press releases, published policy documents, or recorded cabinet-level statements.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) US strategic enabling support peacekeeping Ukraine 2025; 2) US ISR intelligence surveillance reconnaissance peacekeeping Ukraine announcement; 3) Rubio Hegseth White House official statement Ukraine peacekeeping September 2025; 4) US security guarantees Ukraine peace deal announcement ISR intelligence support official; 5) Trump Zelensky UN General Assembly security guarantees intelligence sharing Sept 23 2025; 6) US backstop Ukraine peacekeeping ISR confirmed official; 7) von der Leyen US command control intelligence surveillance; 8) US strategic enablers Ukraine peacekeeping confirmed official.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (a) Al Jazeera Sept 2 reporting 'US officials promised strategic enablers' — REJECTED: secondary reporting referencing pre-window promises; (b) OilPrice Sept 1 citing von der Leyen saying US 'would provide C2, ISR' — REJECTED: European official characterizing US position, not US official statement; (c) Macron Sept 4 saying US 'very clear' on security guarantees — REJECTED: French president reporting Trump's position, not official US statement; (d) Macron saying US would 'finalize support in coming days' — REJECTED: conditional/future, not confirmed US announcement; (e) Trump meeting Zelensky at UNGA Sept 23, discussing security guarantees — REJECTED: no official announcement of specific enabling support linked to peacekeeping force; (f) Boston Globe Sept 25 explicitly noting 'no new military support for Ukraine' announced. No qualifying official US government statement found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the found events satisfy all resolution criteria simultaneously. European leaders and secondary sources reference US pledges, but the resolution criteria require an official US government announcement (whitehouse.gov, defense.gov, state.gov, or cabinet-level public statement) explicitly linking strategic enabling support to a foreign peacekeeping/reassurance force in Ukraine. The closest — Macron's Sept 4 statement and von der Leyen's Sept 1 statement — are European officials characterizing US intentions, not official US government announcements. Trump's statements at UNGA were vague and conditional. The Boston Globe (Sept 25) explicitly stated 'no new call for a ceasefire or peace agreement, no new sanctions, no new deadlines and no new military support for Ukraine, beyond the weapons NATO buys from the United States.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found for an official US government announcement within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence found. All US-attributed statements were either secondhand reports of prior discussions (pre-window August summit), vague/conditional, or not explicitly linked to a peacekeeping force.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources confirm that as of September 4, the 'exact American contribution will be clarified in the coming days' (Zelensky) and the US role remained unspecified. The US was actually cutting some security assistance to Eastern European countries (Section 333 funding). The UNGA meeting (Sept 23-24) focused on vague security guarantee discussions with no specific C2/ISR/peacekeeping commitment announced officially.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying official US government announcement was made within the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window. The resolution criteria require an explicit official US commitment specifically linked to a foreign peacekeeping/reassurance force in Ukraine, made publicly via official channels. All evidence shows the US role remained ambiguous, conditional, and unspecified throughout September 2025, with the 'exact American contribution' still to be clarified. The window closed without a qualifying announcement.

subquestions.question: Will the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) or the White House officially announce an agreement in principle or the signing of a bilateral free trade agreement with Argentina between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: U.S.-Argentina economic relations have intensified significantly in late 2025. On October 9, 2025, the U.S. Treasury announced a $20 billion currency swap with Argentina to stabilize its markets, accompanied by high praise from U.S. officials for Argentine President Javier Milei. A bilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and President Milei was scheduled for October 14, 2025 (https://www.as-coa.org/articles/tracking-trump-and-latin-america-trade). Concurrently, global trade dynamics are rapidly shifting, with the European Union looking to finalize its long-delayed Mercosur trade agreement—of which Argentina is a key member—by December 5, 2025 (https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-mercosur-trade-deal-december-5/). Given the U.S. administration's aggressive trade timeline and recent proactive financial measures with Argentina, a U.S. bilateral agreement could be fast-tracked to counter EU influence. For a comprehensive U.S.-Argentina trade agreement to potentially become U.S. law by December 31, 2025 (the ultimate question's deadline), the two nations would almost certainly need to announce an agreement in principle or officially sign the deal by late November to allow time for executive enactment or congressional review. Sources: [1] Americas Society/Council of the Americas (AS/COA), Tracking Trump and Latin America: Trade (https://www.as-coa.org/articles/tracking-trump-and-latin-america-trade) --- [2] Politico, Brussels aims to sign Mercosur trade deal on Dec. 5 (https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-mercosur-trade-deal-december-5/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) or the White House publishes an official statement, press release, or document explicitly announcing that the United States has signed a free trade agreement (FTA) with Argentina, or reached a finalized "agreement in principle" on a free trade agreement with Argentina. The primary sources for resolution will be the official press release sections of the USTR (https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases) and the White House Briefing Room (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/). To qualify, the announcement must explicitly state that negotiations have concluded, a deal has been reached, or a trade pact has been signed. Announcements of mere intent to negotiate, preliminary trade dialogues, working groups, or unrelated financial agreements (such as currency swaps) do not qualify. Delayed events: If the official announcement occurs after 2025-11-30, the question resolves No. Fall-back criteria: If either specified government website becomes permanently unavailable, credible reporting from at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/ or Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com/) confirming that the official U.S. government announcement was made within the resolution window will suffice.
subquestions.rationale: A free trade agreement requires extensive legal review, congressional notification, or rapid executive processing before it can be enacted into law. If the ultimate outcome is to be achieved by the end of 2025, substantive negotiations must be concluded and formally announced to the public by the end of November 2025 at the latest. This subquestion isolates the crucial diplomatic announcement milestone, providing a highly informative early indicator for whether the December 2025 legislative enactment is possible.

question: U.S. enacts AI safety bill in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will either the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate pass a federal bill containing at least one of the specified AI safety provisions between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. federal government has faced mounting pressure to regulate Artificial Intelligence. In mid-2025, state-level regulations accelerated; California enacted SB 53, Illinois passed the Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act, and Texas passed SB 815, among others. Meanwhile, the Trump administration has taken a deregulatory approach to AI, rescinding Biden-era safety measures in favor of the 'AI Action Plan' intended to promote open-source AI and reduce regulatory barriers (https://www.lexology.com). Despite this, there has been bipartisan interest in AI legislation, such as the AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act (Hawley-Blumenthal) and the No Adversarial AI Act (Krishnamoorthi-Moolenaar) (https://www.lexology.com). Congress also recently removed a 10-year ban on state-level AI regulation from the One Big Beautiful Bill (https://wztv.com). For a federal AI safety bill to be signed into law by December 31, 2025, it would likely need to make significant legislative progress, such as passing at least one chamber of Congress by late October 2025. This subquestion tracks whether either chamber of the U.S. Congress passes a bill that includes specific AI safety provisions (Prohibition on Creation/Release, Training Restrictions, Usage Restrictions, or Human-in-the-Loop Requirements) during October 2025.

subquestions.question: Will the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository record at least one meteor event with an impact energy of 0.1 kt or greater occurring between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Earth is constantly bombarded by small space debris, which burn up in the atmosphere as meteors or bolides. Their explosive energy is measured in kilotons (kt) of TNT equivalent. According to recent reports, a 1.6 kt fireball was recorded over southern Japan on August 19, 2025 (https://watchers.news), while a smaller 0.02 kt (20 tons) meteor exploded over Georgia in June 2025 (https://fark.com). Monitoring the frequency and size of these smaller impacts acts as a baseline indicator for near-Earth object activity. Furthermore, NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) maintains the primary repository for this data (https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/). Tracking whether smaller (>= 0.1 kt) events are actively recorded during September tests both the operational integrity of the database—which is the primary resolution source for the ultimate 10 kt question—and whether Earth is currently passing through any localized regions of denser space debris. 

Sources:
NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/
Watchers News on Japan Fireball: https://watchers.news
Fark News on Georgia Meteor: https://fark.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The occurrence date is determined strictly by the 'Date/Time (UT)' column in the dataset.

Because of natural delays in sensor data processing and reporting, resolution will be determined by checking the repository on October 15, 2025, at 12:00 PM UTC. If the specific NASA JPL dataset has not reported any qualifying event that occurred within the defined time window by this check date, or if the repository is permanently unavailable on this date, the question will resolve No. Events officially noted by CNEOS or NASA as involving artificial objects or space debris reentry are excluded.
subquestions.rationale: Tracking smaller bolide impacts (0.1 kt+) over a one-month window serves two distinct functions. First, it establishes the ongoing operational status, sensitivity, and reporting latency of the CNEOS database, which is the sole primary source for the ultimate 10kt question. Second, an elevated rate of smaller impacts could suggest Earth is passing through a denser cluster of debris, slightly elevating the probability of a larger event. Conversely, a lack of reported events might indicate a quiet period or a database reporting outage, either of which would downwardly update expectations for a positively recorded 10 kt+ event by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository (cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/) to officially log at least one event with Impact Energy ≥ 0.1 kt in the Date/Time column between 2025-09-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC. Observable evidence would be a news report or direct reference to the CNEOS database recording an event with ≥ 0.1 kt in that period. Key entities: NASA CNEOS/JPL, fireball/bolide data, impact energy ≥ 0.1 kt, September 2025 date window. Events involving artificial objects are excluded.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'NASA JPL fireball bolide data September 2025 impact energy' — to find any CNEOS records for Sep 2025; 2) 'meteor fireball impact energy kiloton September 2025' — to find large meteor events; 3) 'fireball Argentina September 13 2025 0.38 kilotons NASA CNEOS' — to verify the specific Argentina event and its energy attribution; 4) 'NASA CNEOS fireball bolide 0.38 kt September 2025 impact energy' — to confirm the CNEOS database attribution; 5) 'NASA fireball database bolide September 2025 large energy explosion atmosphere' — to find any additional qualifying events.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: Argentina (La Pampa) fireball on September 13, 2025 — energy 0.38 kt according to NASA's CNEOS. Confirmed by: [The Most Important News article](http://themostimportantnews.com/archives/the-earth-has-been-shaken-by-466742-earthquakes-so-far-in-2025) published Sept 19, 2025, explicitly stating 'A bright fireball over central Argentina on September 13 released an estimated 0.38 kilotons of energy, according to NASA's CNEOS.' Supported by [LatestLY article](https://www.latestly.com/socially/world/argentina-bright-fireball-streaks-across-night-sky-in-la-pampa-video-goes-viral-7109698.html) confirming a fireball over La Pampa, Argentina on September 13, 2025. No indication this was artificial/space debris. Candidate event 2: Delhi-NCR bolide on September 20, 2025 — described as a bolide but no specific energy figure reported; later identified by India Today as possibly Chinese rocket debris, which would exclude it. Candidate event 3: Bay Area fireball on September 25-26 — confirmed to be Starlink satellite re-entry, excluded as artificial object.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Argentina fireball on September 13, 2025 satisfies all criteria: (1) Date: September 13, 2025 — within the Sept 1–Oct 1, 2025 window [LatestLY](https://www.latestly.com/socially/world/argentina-bright-fireball-streaks-across-night-sky-in-la-pampa-video-goes-viral-7109698.html); (2) Impact energy: 0.38 kt ≥ 0.1 kt threshold [The Most Important News](http://themostimportantnews.com/archives/the-earth-has-been-shaken-by-466742-earthquakes-so-far-in-2025); (3) Source: Explicitly attributed to 'NASA's CNEOS' — the same agency that operates the JPL Fireball repository; (4) Not artificial: The event is described as a natural meteor/fireball with a viral video of the event, with no indication of space debris. The 0.38 kt value is well above the 0.1 kt threshold.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The event date is September 13, 2025 as explicitly stated in both sources. No precise UTC time is available from the news articles, but the date is clearly within the resolution window (Sept 1–Oct 1, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The September 13, 2025 Argentina fireball is the earliest qualifying event found in the search results. No earlier events within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window with reported energy ≥ 0.1 kt were identified. The Perth, Australia fireball reported on September 1, 2025 was described as 'cricket ball sized' with no energy figure approaching 0.1 kt.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) The Delhi-NCR fireball on September 20, 2025, which was later identified as potentially Chinese rocket debris (Long March 3B), would be excluded per resolution criteria if confirmed artificial. (2) The Bay Area fireball was explicitly confirmed as Starlink satellite re-entry — excluded. (3) The Argentina event has no mention of artificial origin; LatestLY reported it as a 'bright fireball, described as meteor-like' with viral video, consistent with a natural event. (4) The CNEOS attribution in The Most Important News article appears to be citing the same CNEOS/JPL database that serves as the resolution source. The source (The Most Important News) has a sensationalist tone, but the specific factual claim about Argentina fireball energy is consistent with other reporting of the event and specific enough to be credible as a CNEOS data citation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: A natural fireball event over central Argentina (La Pampa) on September 13, 2025, with an impact energy of 0.38 kilotons as reported by NASA's CNEOS, satisfies all resolution criteria: the event falls within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window, the energy (0.38 kt) exceeds the 0.1 kt threshold, the data source is NASA CNEOS (which operates the JPL Fireball repository), and the event is a natural meteor — not an artificial object. This event is explicitly confirmed across multiple news sources, with the energy figure specifically attributed to NASA CNEOS. The question resolves Yes.

question: Will any of the stolen Louvre jewels be returned by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any of the jewels stolen from the Louvre’s Galerie d’Apollon are officially recovered by the listed date ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

A single item (e.g., one earring) will suffice regardless of if it is missing a diamond or other element; however, recovery of only a fragment or part of an item (for example, a loose stone or a piece of a crown) will not suffice

The primary resolution source will be official statements from the Louvre or the French government; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will authorities announce the arrest or formal charging of at least one suspect in connection with the October 2025 Louvre jewel heist between October 21 and November 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 19-20, 2025, a highly coordinated heist at the Louvre Museum in Paris resulted in the theft of eight historic French crown jewels from the Galerie d'Apollon. The thieves, operating in under seven minutes, stole irreplaceable items such as Empress Eugénie's diadem and an emerald set once worn by Empress Marie-Louise. Art recovery experts, such as Chris Marinello, warn that without rapid police action, the jewels are highly likely to be dismantled, melted down, and recut to obscure their origins within 24 to 48 hours. Therefore, the swift identification and arrest of the perpetrators—reported to be a four-person team—is viewed as a critical step toward recovering any of the jewels intact. The Paris public prosecutor’s office is directing the investigation, with alerts issued to Interpol and neighboring countries to monitor black-market activity.

Sources:
Burglars Just Broke Into the Louvre and Stole Historic Crown Jewels in a Daring Daylight Heist - https://www.smithsonianmag.com
Expert Says Stolen Louvre Jewels Need to Be Recovered in 24-to-48 Hours Or They're 'Long Gone': Report - https://people.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if a recognized French governmental authority (e.g., the Paris public prosecutor's office, Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Interior, or National Police), or a foreign/international law enforcement agency (e.g., Interpol, Europol), officially announces that at least one individual has been arrested, detained (placé en garde à vue), or formally charged (mis en examen) in direct connection with the October 2025 Louvre jewel heist between 2025-10-21 and 2025-11-20T23:59:59Z (inclusive). The official announcement must occur and be publicly reported within this time window. A consensus of credible reporting from major news agencies (such as Reuters: https://www.reuters.com, France 24: https://www.france24.com, or Le Monde: https://www.lemonde.fr) quoting official law enforcement statements will suffice for resolution. If an individual is originally arrested for an unrelated crime, the question will only resolve 'Yes' if they are explicitly charged or officially detained for their involvement in the Louvre heist within the specified resolution window. If no such announcement occurs between 2025-10-21 and 2025-11-20T23:59:59Z, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Art recovery experts note that stolen historic jewels are typically dismantled and melted down rapidly to hide their origins and avoid detection. If authorities fail to make any arrests or identify suspects within the first month of the heist, it strongly implies the thieves have successfully escaped and fenced or destroyed the items, making the recovery of any intact jewel by the end of December highly improbable. Conversely, an early arrest increases the probability of interrogating suspects, disrupting the fencing network, and locating at least one intact piece.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: French governmental authority (or international law enforcement) officially announces that at least one individual was arrested, detained (placé en garde à vue), or formally charged (mis en examen) in direct connection with the October 2025 Louvre jewel heist between 2025-10-21T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-20T23:59:59Z. Observable evidence: official statement from Paris prosecutor's office or equivalent authority, corroborated by credible major news sources. Key entity: Paris public prosecutor Laure Beccuau. Heist occurred October 19, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Louvre jewel heist October 2025' — to confirm the heist occurred and find arrest info; 2) 'Louvre robbery theft arrest 2025' — to find arrest reporting; 3) 'Louvre heist suspects formally charged mis en examen November 2025' — to find formal charging; 4) 'Louvre robbery arrest October 26 2025 Paris prosecutor announcement' — to verify official announcement date and first occurrence.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) October 25-26, 2025: Two suspects arrested — one at CDG Airport attempting to flee to Algeria, one in Seine-Saint-Denis. Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau confirmed arrests on October 26, 2025. (2) ~October 29-30, 2025: Two earlier suspects formally charged (mis en examen) with organized theft and criminal conspiracy, both partially admitted involvement. (3) October 29-30, 2025: Five additional suspects arrested in and around Paris. (4) November 1, 2025: Two more suspects formally charged. All events are within the resolution window. No events rejected — all directly satisfy criteria.

Criteria satisfied: (a) recognized French governmental authority (Paris public prosecutor's office); (b) official announcement; (c) at least one individual arrested/detained; (d) directly in connection with October 2025 Louvre heist; (e) announcement within window (Oct 26 is between Oct 21 and Nov 20); (f) reported by major credible news agencies.

evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: None found. All sources consistently report October 25-26 arrests with prosecutor confirmation. evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is YES. This is within the resolution window (2025-10-21 to 2025-11-20T23:59:59Z). The announcement was made by a recognized French governmental authority (Paris public prosecutor's office) and was widely reported by major credible news agencies. Subsequent formal charges (mis en examen) on October 29-30 and November 1, 2025 provide further confirming evidence.

question: U.S. x Iran Military Engagement by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Iran between market creation and the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Iranian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots, artillery fire into uninhabited areas, or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Iranian land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage.

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; the Iranian Law Enforcement Command is a branch of the Iranian Armed Forces; all sub-branches of the Artesh, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (including the Basij), and Law Enforcement Command are part of the Iranian Armed forces.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) or the Department of Defense officially announce the use of kinetic force (e.g., warning shots, drone/missile interceptions, or direct strikes) by U.S. forces against Iranian military assets between February 6, 2026, and February 25, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
On February 4, 2026, a U.S. Navy F-35C stealth fighter jet shot down an Iranian Shahed-139 drone that aggressively approached the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier in the Arabian Sea (Source: https://defensescoop.com/). On the same day, Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) boats and a Mohajer drone harassed the U.S.-flagged tanker M/V Stena Imperative in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting the guided-missile destroyer USS McFaul to intervene and provide escort (Source: https://lloydslist.maritimeintelligence.informa.com/). These incidents occurred amidst a broader U.S. military buildup in the Middle East, including the deployment of the Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group and additional destroyers, in response to rising regional tensions. Diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran are reportedly scheduled in Oman, but the recent military skirmishes threaten to derail them (Source: https://www.bne.eu/). Tracking whether tactical, non-engagement uses of force (like drone interceptions and warning shots) continue in the coming weeks provides crucial insight into the trajectory of U.S.-Iran relations and the potential for a larger conflict.

Sources:
bne IntelliNews - https://www.bne.eu/
DefenseScoop - https://defensescoop.com/
Lloyd's List - https://lloydslist.maritimeintelligence.informa.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) or the U.S. Department of Defense officially announces that U.S. military forces used kinetic force (including but not limited to warning shots, interceptions or shoot-downs of drones/missiles/aircraft, or direct strikes) against assets explicitly identified as belonging to Iran or the Iranian military (e.g., IRGC, Iranian Navy, Iranian Armed Forces), and the incident occurs between 2026-02-06 and 2026-02-25 (inclusive). 

The official announcement must be published by CENTCOM or the DoD, for example via official press releases (https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/ or https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/) or their official social media accounts (e.g., https://x.com/CENTCOM). The targeted asset must be explicitly attributed to the state of Iran; actions against Iranian-backed proxies (e.g., Houthi or Hezbollah forces) without direct attribution of the asset to the Iranian state do not qualify.

This question resolves Yes if the qualifying event occurs between 2026-02-06 and 2026-02-25. If no such announcement is made regarding an event occurring within this time window, or if the event is delayed or postponed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question resolves 'Yes' if there is a direct military engagement by June 30, 2026, but it explicitly excludes drone interceptions and warning shots from triggering a 'Yes' resolution. However, tracking whether the U.S. continues to engage in these lower-level tactical skirmishes (like the February 4 drone shootdown) serves as an excellent early indicator. If U.S. forces continue to intercept Iranian drones or fire warning shots between February 6 and February 25, it demonstrates sustained, high-level military friction that significantly increases the probability of a miscalculation or escalation into a full military engagement by June 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: CENTCOM or DoD officially announces U.S. military used kinetic force against assets explicitly attributed to the Iranian state (IRGC, Iranian military), occurring between 2026-02-06 and 2026-02-25. Observable evidence: Official CENTCOM/DoD press release, social media post, or statement attributed to official spokesperson confirming shoot-down of Iranian drone/missile, or direct strike on Iranian military asset within the window.

evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Feb 3/4 2026: F-35C shot down Iranian Shahed-139 near USS Abraham Lincoln — confirmed by multiple sources but BEFORE the window. (B) Asia Times (published Feb 6) states 'shot down an Iranian drone...on February 6' — possibly within window but likely refers to or conflates with Feb 3/4 incident. CENTCOM spokesperson Capt. Tim Hawkins cited. This falls within the window. Note: Hindustan Times (Feb 13) states drone was shot down 'the previous week', which conflicts. The National Interest Feb 13 article also erroneously claims it was 'the first time an Iranian drone has been destroyed by U.S. forces in 2026', contradicting the Feb 3/4 events.
