Tim Hawkins making a public statement. The drone is explicitly attributed to Iran (identified as Iranian, Shahed-129 loitering munition). The action (F-35C shoot-down) constitutes kinetic force (drone interception). CENTCOM officially confirmed it. The date (February 13) falls within the Feb 6-25 window. However, conflicting evidence from Hindustan Times (same day, Feb 13) says the drone was shot down 'the previous week', suggesting the article may be recounting the earlier Feb 3/4 incident. The National Interest article's characterization as 'first time in 2026' is clearly erroneous given established Feb 3/4 events, which raises questions about reliability.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: February 13, 2026 — from National Interest articles published February 13, 2026, explicitly stating the shoot-down occurred 'on February 13, 2026'. However, Hindustan Times (also Feb 13) contextualizes the drone shoot-down as having occurred 'the previous week', creating a conflict.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: If the Feb 13 event is valid, it would be a second incident (the first being Feb 3/4, before the window). If Asia Times is correct about Feb 6, that would be the first within the window. There is conflicting evidence making it difficult to confirm with certainty whether there was a distinct Feb 6 or Feb 13 incident separate from the Feb 3/4 event.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradiction: Hindustan Times (Feb 13) explicitly says 'U.S. forces shot down an Iranian drone the previous week' — implying the shoot-down was before Feb 13, consistent with Feb 3/4. The National Interest articles (Feb 13) say the event was on Feb 13 and was 'the first time in 2026' (which is clearly wrong). The Will Goodhind/ABC7 AP story (Feb 13) and WRAL AP story (Feb 13) both say 'U.S. forces shot down an Iranian drone' without a specific date, possibly referencing the earlier event. The Asia Times (Feb 6) says the event was 'on February 6.' The Simple Flying article (Feb 12) confirms the Feb 3 date for the first shoot-down. The conflicting dates across sources make definitive resolution uncertain. However, CENTCOM official confirmation of at least one qualifying event within the window (via the Asia Times Feb 6 reference, which explicitly states Feb 6, and the National Interest Feb 13 reference) exists.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is conflicting. Multiple high-quality sources (Hindustan Times, Simple Flying, AFP) confirm the primary drone shoot-down was February 3, 2026, BEFORE the window. The National Interest articles explicitly state a February 13 incident with CENTCOM confirmation, but this conflicts with other Feb 13 sources saying it was 'the previous week.' The Asia Times article (published Feb 6) says the shoot-down occurred 'on February 6' with CENTCOM confirmation — this would fall within the window on its first day. Given the conflicting evidence, I cannot definitively confirm a qualifying event occurred within the window without ambiguity. However, the weight of evidence — particularly the Asia Times (Feb 6 with CENTCOM stated as source), the National Interest (Feb 13 with CENTCOM spokesperson cited), and the TimesNow (Feb 7 date) — suggests at least one qualifying event occurred within the window. The resolution criteria require CENTCOM official announcement, and CENTCOM is cited as confirming these events. Given that the question requires precision, and there is direct evidence of a CENTCOM-confirmed Iranian drone shoot-down on February 13, 2026 (within window), despite some conflicting contextual evidence, I resolve Yes.

question: Will there be exactly 1 earthquake of magnitude 7.0 or higher worldwide by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of earthquakes with a magnitude of 7.0 or higher that occur anywhere on Earth between October 13, 2025, 12:00 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source for this market is the United States Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Hazards Program (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php#sigdef).

If an earthquake of substantial size has occurred within this market's timeframe but not yet appeared on the resolution source, this market may remain open until January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or until the earthquake in question otherwise appears on the resolution source. If such an earthquake has not appeared on the resolution source by that date, another credible resolution source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the USGS record 10 or more earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 or higher worldwide between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-09?
subquestions.background_information:
According to historical U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) data, there are typically about 130 to 150 earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 to 6.9 worldwide per year, which averages to roughly 11 to 12 per month. Global seismic activity can occasionally fluctuate above or below this baseline; for example, reports from late October 2025 highlight significant ongoing activity, including a magnitude 6.7 in the Banda Sea and frequent aftershocks in Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula following an 8.8-magnitude quake in July 2025. Because magnitude 7.0+ earthquakes are relatively rare (averaging around 10 to 20 per year), forecasters often rely on the frequency of magnitude 6.0+ earthquakes over a shorter time window as a proxy to model the current global seismic baseline rate.

Sources:
USGS Earthquake Statistics: https://www.usgs.gov/programs/earthquake-hazards/lists-maps-and-statistics
USGS Earthquake Search: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/
Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/
VolcanoDiscovery: https://www.volcanodiscovery.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the United States Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Hazards Program records 10 or more earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 or higher worldwide between 2025-11-13 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-09 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive.

The official resolution source will be the USGS Earthquake Catalog Search (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/). To verify resolution:
1. Access the USGS Earthquake Catalog Search.
2. Set the 'Magnitude' parameter to a minimum of 6.0.
3. Set the 'Date & Time' parameter to start on 2025-11-13 00:00:00 and end on 2025-12-09 23:59:59 (UTC).
4. Set the 'Geographic Region' to 'World'.
5. Count the total number of resulting earthquakes.

If the resulting count is 10 or greater, the question resolves Yes. If the count is 9 or fewer, it resolves No. In the event of an earthquake's magnitude being revised by the USGS prior to resolution (the data will be checked on 2025-12-12 to account for slight delays in final measurements), the revised magnitude will be used. If the USGS catalog is unavailable or ceases to function permanently, the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) catalog (https://www.emsc-csem.org/Earthquake/) will be used as a fallback source.
subquestions.rationale: The frequency of magnitude 6.0+ earthquakes acts as a reliable proxy for short-term global seismic activity rates. Understanding the current Poisson rate of earthquakes is crucial for forecasting whether 'exactly 1' magnitude 7.0+ earthquake will occur by the end of December. If the baseline rate of 6.0+ earthquakes is unusually high (potentially pushing the number of 7.0+ earthquakes to 2 or more) or unusually low (potentially keeping the number of 7.0+ earthquakes at 0), this subquestion provides valuable, measurable evidence to update probabilities for the ultimate question.

question: US congress stock trading ban in 2025?
description:

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will either chamber of the US Congress hold a roll call vote on legislation banning sitting members of Congress from trading individual stocks by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
There has been growing pressure to ban members of Congress from trading individual stocks, fueled by recent public scrutiny and high-profile returns from some lawmakers' portfolios. Several bills have been introduced in both chambers, including the End Congressional Stock Trading Act (H.R. 1908) and the PELOSI Act. On August 29-30, 2025, Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL) announced her intention to file a discharge petition to force a House floor vote on H.R. 1908, a maneuver that requires 218 signatures to bypass House leadership. Meanwhile, the Senate has seen similar pushes, with the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee advancing a stock trading ban bill. Congress returns from recess in September 2025 with a packed schedule, primarily focused on avoiding a government shutdown by the September 30 deadline. Whether a stock trading ban can secure a floor vote amid these competing priorities will be a strong indicator of its chances to become law in 2025.

Sources:
One America News Network: https://www.oann.com/newsroom/rep-luna-introduces-resolution-to-advance-the-end-congressional-stock-trading-act/
Associated Press: https://apnews.com/article/congress-government-shutdown-stock-trading-7f8e9d
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the US House of Representatives or the US Senate holds a floor roll call vote on the passage of a bill, or on the adoption of an amendment, that would prohibit sitting members of the US Congress from trading individual stocks. The vote must occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

The primary sources for resolution will be the official roll call vote records of the US House of Representatives (https://clerk.house.gov/Votes) and the US Senate (https://www.senate.gov/legislative/votes_new.htm). 

Legislation that requires members to place individual stocks in a qualified blind trust or divest them entirely qualifies as a ban for the purposes of this question. Voice votes, unanimous consent agreements, and committee-level votes do not count. Furthermore, procedural votes (such as cloture votes, motions to proceed, motions to table, or votes on a special rule or discharge petition) do not count; the vote must be a direct roll call vote on the passage of the qualifying bill or the adoption of the qualifying amendment. If no such roll call vote occurs within the specified window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A floor vote in September 2025 would demonstrate that the push for a stock trading ban has overcome significant committee and leadership hurdles. If a roll call vote occurs, it signals high momentum (likely driven by the discharge petition or bipartisan pressure), increasing the likelihood of the ban becoming law by the end of 2025. If no vote is held by October 1, it indicates that the legislation remains stalled despite the aggressive discharge petition effort, sharply lowering the probability of passage before the end of the year.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: floor roll call vote (not procedural, not committee) in House or Senate on bill banning Congress members from trading individual stocks, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive. Observable evidence: official roll call records from clerk.house.gov or senate.gov, or news reports confirming such a vote occurred.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Congress roll call vote stock trading ban members 2025' (Sept-Oct window); 2) 'STOCK Act ban Congress members trading individual stocks vote 2025'; 3) 'discharge petition stock trading ban vote Anna Paulina Luna September 2025'; 4) 'Restore Trust Congress Act floor vote House Senate September 2025'; 5) 'congressional stock trading ban vote September 2025 House floor vote passed'; 6) 'discharge petition stock trading ban 218 signatures Congress vote late September 2025'; 7) 'Restore Trust Congress Act roll call vote passed September October 2025'; 8) 'congressional stock trading ban vote failed stalled Johnson September 2025'; 9) 'stock trading ban Congress vote late September Mike Johnson floor September 25-30 2025'; 10) 'Luna discharge petition stock trading signatures September 30 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Introduction of Restore Trust in Congress Act on Sept 3, 2025 - REJECTED (introduction, not a vote); (2) Rep. Luna's discharge petition filing - REJECTED (procedural mechanism, not a floor vote on the bill itself); (3) Speaker Johnson expressing tentative support - REJECTED (not a vote); (4) End-of-September deadline set by Luna - articles show this was a threat/deadline, not confirmation a vote occurred. No articles reported an actual floor roll call vote on the stock trading ban within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of a qualifying floor roll call vote. Multiple sources ([The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5482647-house-members-introduce-stock-trading-ban/), [CNN](https://us.cnn.com/2025/09/03/politics/stock-trade-ban-congress), [ktxs.com](https://ktxs.com/news/nation-world/lawmakers-try-to-find-consensus-in-push-to-ban-congressional-stock-trading)) describe introduction of the bill and pressure to vote, but none report an actual roll call vote occurring. Late September coverage focused entirely on government shutdown negotiations.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying vote because no qualifying vote was reported to have occurred within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at all within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence suggesting a vote did occur - none found. Multiple late-September articles (Sept 22-30) still describe the bill as being pushed toward a vote, not having been voted on. The government shutdown dominated congressional attention in the final week of September. Luna's end-of-month deadline appears to have passed without a floor vote being scheduled. The discharge petition (even if it reached 218 signatures) would require additional legislative days and would trigger procedural votes first, not a direct floor vote within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Restore Trust in Congress Act was introduced on Sept 3, 2025, gained bipartisan support, and faced pressure from Rep. Luna's discharge petition threat. However, no floor roll call vote on the legislation occurred within the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window. Congressional attention shifted to government shutdown negotiations by late September, and no reporting confirms a qualifying vote took place. The question resolves No, with the window closing on October 1, 2025.

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve announce a reduction in the target range for the federal funds rate at or before the conclusion of its October 2025 FOMC meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question resolves to "No" if any of four conditions are met, one of which is that the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates twice between September 23, 2025, and December 31, 2025. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) has a scheduled policy meeting on October 28-29, 2025. Because there is only one other scheduled meeting in 2025 (in December), a rate cut at the October meeting is a critical stepping stone for the "Fed cuts twice" condition to be fulfilled. If the Fed does not cut rates in October, fulfilling the condition would require an emergency inter-meeting cut or multiple cuts at a single meeting in December. Market expectations leading up to the meeting point to a 0.25-percentage-point cut in the fed funds rate, though recent data and potential disruptions such as a government shutdown add uncertainty to the Fed's decision-making process.

Sources:
Investopedia: Next Fed Meeting: When It Is In October And What To Expect - https://www.investopedia.com/
Federal Reserve FOMC Calendar - https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announces a reduction in the target range for the federal funds rate between 2025-10-27 and 2025-11-05 (inclusive).

The primary source for resolution will be the official press releases issued by the Federal Reserve, available on their official website (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm and https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases.htm). 

If the stated target range (or single target rate, in the event the Fed modifies its targeting framework) for the federal funds rate announced at the conclusion of the October 2025 FOMC meeting (or an emergency announcement prior to the end date) is lower than the target range in effect immediately prior to 2025-10-27, the question resolves Yes.

If the FOMC announces no change, an increase, or does not issue any decision to lower the target range between 2025-10-27 and 2025-11-05, the question resolves No. If the scheduled October meeting is delayed beyond the end date of 2025-11-05 without any rate cut announcement occurring within the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A rate cut at the October 2025 FOMC meeting serves as an important crux for the ultimate question. Since the ultimate question looks for two rate cuts between September 23 and December 31, an October rate cut is practically necessary for this condition to be met. Establishing whether this first cut happens provides strong early evidence of whether the 'Nothing Ever Happens' outcome will be invalidated by the Fed's monetary policy path.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition for Yes: The FOMC must announce a REDUCTION in the target range for the federal funds rate between 2025-10-27 and 2025-11-05 (inclusive). Observable evidence: An official Federal Reserve press release announcing a lower federal funds rate target range. Key threshold: The new rate must be lower than the rate in effect immediately prior to 2025-10-27 (which was 4.00%–4.25%). Timing: October 28–29 FOMC meeting, with decision announced on October 29, 2025.

All sources consistently report the same decision, amount, new range, and date. No candidates were rejected.

question: Will there be at least 500 measles cases in the U.S. in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there have been the specified amount or more confirmed cases of Measles (Rubeola) in humans in the territory of the United States of America in 2026 according to the CDC case counter between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the CDC Measles (Rubeola) counter (see: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html) at the resolution time. If the counter becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

Note: Only cases reported by the CDC Measles (Rubeola) counter will qualify, regardless of reports from U.S. State agencies or other sources.

subquestions.question: Will the CDC report a cumulative total of 50 or more distinct measles outbreaks in the U.S. for the year 2025 by January 1, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The United States is currently experiencing its worst measles year in decades, with over 1,700 confirmed cases reported by November 2025. While the overall number of cases is an important metric, the geographic dispersion and number of distinct transmission chains are crucial indicators of the virus's momentum. The CDC reported 45 distinct measles outbreaks as of November 13, 2025, which is a massive increase compared to the 16 outbreaks recorded in all of 2024. The CDC typically defines a measles outbreak as a cluster of 3 or more related cases. 

A continuously rising number of outbreaks indicates that the virus is establishing new transmission chains in different communities rather than remaining confined to localized events (such as the massive Texas outbreak earlier in 2025). Tracking whether the U.S. reaches 50 or more outbreaks before the end of 2025 serves as an early indicator of how widely dispersed the virus will be heading into 2026. This metric is especially relevant given declining national MMR vaccination rates (currently around 92.5%, below the 95% herd immunity threshold) and warnings from the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) regarding the potential loss of the U.S. measles elimination status in early 2026.

Sources:
CDC Measles Data - https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html
The Boston Globe - https://www.bostonglobe.com
SheKnows - https://www.sheknows.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports a cumulative total of 50 or more measles outbreaks in the United States for the year 2025, in any official data update or press release published between 2025-12-02 and 2026-01-01 (inclusive). 

The primary resolution source will be the official CDC Measles (Rubeola) Data and Statistics page (https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html). Official CDC press releases, health advisories, or Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Reports (MMWR) published within the resolution window will also qualify. 

If the CDC ceases to publish or update the national count of outbreaks during this window due to budget cuts or other disruptions, the question will resolve No unless the threshold of 50 was explicitly met and published by the CDC prior to the stoppage but within the resolution window. An 'outbreak' is defined by the CDC parameters (typically 3 or more related cases); however, for resolution, whatever number of distinct outbreaks the CDC officially states as the cumulative total for 2025 will be taken as authoritative regardless of their internal classification changes. Delayed reports published after 2026-01-01 will not be considered.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. will see 500+ cases in 2026. The number of active or total outbreaks at the end of 2025 is a powerful leading indicator for 2026 case volume. More distinct outbreaks mean the virus is geographically dispersed and actively circulating in multiple independent communities. If the U.S. crosses the 50-outbreak threshold by the end of December 2025, it signals that public health interventions are failing to contain geographic spread, strongly predicting multiple uncontained seed points heading into 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: CDC must officially report ≥50 distinct measles outbreaks in the U.S. for 2025, in an official data update or press release published between 2025-12-02 and 2026-01-01 inclusive. Key threshold: 50 outbreaks (CDC definition: 3+ related cases). Evidence required: CDC publication explicitly stating cumulative count ≥50.

All explicitly match the ≥50 threshold and cite CDC as source.

question: Next BLS jobs report during government shutdown?

Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Partial shutdowns are considered shutdowns, whereas announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as shutdowns.

Both a full release of the monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate) and an official release of the underlying data by the Bureau of Labor Statistics will count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

subquestions.question: Will the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announce that the U.S. federal government is no longer shut down between October 8, 2025 and November 1, 2025?

The ultimate question asks whether the BLS will release the Employment Situation report before the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces that the government is no longer shut down. Given that the BLS is closed during the shutdown, if the shutdown ends and the OPM announces it, the BLS will likely reopen and release the report shortly after, resulting in a 'No' for the ultimate question. However, if the shutdown drags on significantly, there may be increasing pressure from financial markets and policymakers to grant the BLS a special exemption or targeted funding to release the data during the shutdown. This subquestion asks whether the shutdown will end, as announced by the OPM, by November 1, 2025.

Sources:

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) officially announces that the federal government is no longer shut down, or that normal operations have resumed following the lapse in appropriations, between 2025-10-08 and 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z. If no such announcement is made by 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z, this question resolves 'No'. If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: If the government shutdown ends by November 1, 2025, the BLS will reopen and release the jobs report after the OPM's announcement. This timeline would naturally trigger a 'No' resolution for the ultimate question. Conversely, if the shutdown continues into November, the likelihood of an emergency data release of the jobs report during the shutdown (a 'Yes' resolution for the ultimate question) increases significantly due to the prolonged absence of critical economic data and mounting pressure from the Federal Reserve and markets.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: OPM officially announces the federal government is no longer shut down (or normal operations resumed) between 2025-10-08T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z. question: Will Italy win the second most medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most medals won will use most gold medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most medals won, and Norway wins more gold medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

Additionally, a U.S. government shutdown has hindered the release of key economic data, complicating the Fed's outlook (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/powells-december-warning-exposes-hardening-divisions-at-fed-20251030/). For the ultimate question's "Pause-Pause-Pause" scenario to resolve 'Yes', the Fed must first choose to pause at its December 9-10, 2025 meeting. The CME FedWatch Tool is widely used to gauge market expectations of FOMC policy changes by calculating probabilities based on 30-Day Fed Funds futures pricing data. If the market assigns a >50% probability to a pause just days before the December meeting, forecasters can significantly update their models toward a 'Yes' on the first leg of the ultimate question.

question: Will Trump act to ban mail-in voting or voting machines in 2025?
description:
On August 18, 2025, President Donald J. Trump announced his commitment to eliminate mail-in voting and voting machines in U.S. elections, ahead of the 2026 midterms.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that inhibits mail-in voting or voting machines from use for the 2026 midterm election by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any executive action or legislation that restricts, limits, or prohibits the use of mail-in voting or voting machines in any way will qualify, even if the action is delayed, suspended, or subsequently blocked by judicial or other actions.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration officially establish a new federal commission, task force, or advisory board focused on "election integrity," mail-in voting, or voting machines between November 30, 2025, and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In August 2025, President Donald Trump repeatedly announced his intent to sign an executive order to ban mail-in voting and voting machines before the 2026 midterms, claiming the order was 'being written right now by the best lawyers in the country.' However, legal experts and election administrators note that Article I, Section 4 of the U.S. Constitution grants states the authority to administer elections, meaning a direct federal ban by the president would face severe legal hurdles. Earlier in April 2025, a federal judge blocked a similar Trump executive order requiring proof of citizenship for federal elections, citing that election regulation is a state and congressional power. 

Given these constitutional constraints, an outright ban via executive order may be legally unworkable in the short term. The administration might instead opt to establish a federal commission, task force, or advisory board to investigate mail-in voting and voting machines as a precursor to future action—similar to the Presidential Advisory Commission on Election Integrity established during Trump's first term in 2017. Tracking whether such a commission is established provides a strong indicator of the administration's approach: forming a study commission suggests a delay in immediate restrictive actions, whereas skipping this step might indicate an imminent, direct executive order is still planned for 2025.

Sources:
Al Jazeera Online: 'Trump to order voter ID for every vote, no exceptions' - https://www.aljazeera.com
KOMO: 'Election officials speak out as Trump pushes to eliminate mail-in voting' - https://komonews.com
USA Today: 'Trump says he will issue executive order mandating voter ID requirement' - https://www.usatoday.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), the White House, the Department of Justice (DOJ), or another U.S. federal agency officially establishes a new commission, task force, advisory board, or specialized unit whose stated mandate includes investigating, reviewing, or reforming 'election integrity,' mail-in voting, or electronic voting machines.

- 'Officially establishes' means the action is formalized via a signed executive order, presidential memorandum, or official agency directive. 
- The action must be published or officially announced on an authoritative U.S. government website, such as the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov), the DOJ website (https://www.justice.gov), or the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov).
- Mere verbal promises or statements of intent during speeches or interviews without an accompanying signed directive or official press release announcing the formal creation of the body do not qualify.
- The mandate of the body must explicitly relate to election administration, voter fraud, mail-in ballots, or voting machines.
- If an executive order is signed that directly restricts or bans mail-in voting/voting machines AND ALSO creates a task force within the same document, this question resolves Yes. If it solely restricts/bans without creating such a body, it resolves No.
- Any action taken before 2025-11-30 or after 2025-12-29 will not count toward a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A direct federal ban on mail-in voting via executive order is legally complex and likely to face immediate injunctions, as states possess constitutional authority over election administration. If the Trump administration recognizes an immediate ban is unfeasible by the end of 2025, they may pivot to establishing a federal commission or task force to 'investigate' mail-in voting and voting machines as an interim step. If such a commission is formed in December, it indicates a longer-term strategy, reducing the likelihood that Trump will issue a direct, inhibiting executive action before December 31, 2025. Conversely, the absence of a commission may indicate that the administration intends to proceed directly with a blunt executive order to fulfill Trump's August 2025 promises before the end of the year.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: Between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29, the Trump administration must officially establish (via signed executive order, presidential memorandum, or official agency directive, published on an authoritative U.S. government website) a new commission, task force, advisory board, or specialized unit whose stated mandate explicitly includes investigating, reviewing, or reforming 'election integrity,' mail-in voting, or electronic voting machines.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump administration election integrity commission task force 2025' (Nov 30–Dec 29) — to find any formal body created; 2) 'Trump executive order election integrity advisory board December 2025' — to find any EO signed; 3) 'Trump Election Integrity Task Force Tulsi Gabbard working group December 2025' — to investigate specific claims from fringe sources; 4) 'DOJ election integrity task force voting machines mail-in ballots December 2025' — to find DOJ-specific actions; 5) 'Alex Jones Todd Blanche election integrity task force blocking 2025' — to investigate specific claims; 6) 'Trump election integrity commission formal creation November December 2025 White House federal register' — authoritative source check; 7) 'Trump voting machines mail-in voting executive order new task force December 2025' — to find specific EO.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (A) References by Roger Stone (Dec 19) and Alex Jones (Dec 26-27) to a 'Trump admin's Election Integrity Commission' and an 'Election Integrity Task Force' — but these come from fringe InfoWars/conspiracy sources and describe an informal 'working group' allegedly authorized by Trump but not formally established via executive order or official directive. Alex Jones even complained the Task Force was being 'blocked' by DAG Todd Blanche, suggesting it was not fully operational. (B) Trump's March 2025 EO 'Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections' — predates the question window. (C) DOJ lawsuits against states for voter roll data (Dec 11-19) — these are enforcement actions, not the creation of a new body. (D) Food Supply Chain Security Task Force (Dec 6-7) — unrelated to election integrity. (E) AI Litigation Task Force (Dec 11-12) — unrelated to election integrity. All formal task force/commission creations during this window related to food supply chains and AI, not election integrity.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of an officially established (via signed EO, presidential memorandum, or official agency directive published on whitehouse.gov, justice.gov, or federalregister.gov) new commission, task force, advisory board, or specialized unit with a stated mandate explicitly related to election administration, voter fraud, mail-in ballots, or voting machines within the November 30 – December 29, 2025 window. The references to an 'Election Integrity Task Force' or 'Election Integrity Commission' come exclusively from unverified claims by Roger Stone [freerepublic.com/focus/f-news/4358163/posts] and Alex Jones [rawstory.com/alex-jones-jd-vance/] on fringe platforms (InfoWars). These are not authoritative U.S. government sources, and the descriptions explicitly suggest the body was not fully functional (Jones said DAG Blanche was 'blocking it'). No official White House, DOJ, or Federal Register announcement was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No reliable timestamp for a qualifying event could be extracted. The only references to an election integrity body are from conspiracy commentators making claims about informal/alleged activities, not official government announcements.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was found within the window. The March 2025 EO on election integrity predates the window, and no new body was formally established within the November 30 – December 29, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: (1) Alex Jones explicitly states the Election Integrity Task Force is being 'blocked' by DAG Blanche, contradicting any claim that it was formally established. (2) Roger Stone's description of a 'working group led by Tulsi Gabbard' appears to describe an informal arrangement, not a formally signed executive order or directive. (3) No mainstream or government news sources reported the formal creation of an election integrity commission or task force during this window. (4) The Trump administration's documented formal actions during this window focused on food supply chains, AI regulation, proxy advisory firms, and DOJ lawsuits against states — none related to establishing a new election integrity body.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. The window closed (December 29, 2025) without any formally established (via signed executive order, presidential memorandum, or official agency directive published on an authoritative U.S. government website) commission, task force, advisory board, or specialized unit with a stated mandate explicitly related to election integrity, mail-in voting, or voting machines. All claims of such a body came from fringe sources (Alex Jones, Roger Stone on InfoWars), were contradicted by statements that the body was being 'blocked,' and were not corroborated by any authoritative government source. The March 2025 EO on election integrity predates the window.

question: Will US GDP growth in Q3 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP "Advance Estimate" release for Q3 of 2025 scheduled for October 30, 2025.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's GDPNow model estimate for Q3 2025 real GDP growth be 2.5% or higher in its final update of September 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's GDPNow model provides a running, real-time estimate of real gross domestic product (GDP) growth based on the latest available economic data for the current measured quarter. As the ultimate question asks whether Q3 2025 GDP will land exactly between 2.0% and 2.5%, tracking the GDPNow estimate at the end of September (the close of the third quarter) is highly informative. According to recent news reports, the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) revised Q2 2025 GDP growth up to 3.3%, up from the advance estimate of 3.0%. This growth was driven largely by strong AI-related investments and a sharp drop in imports ahead of tariff hikes. However, economists caution that tariff-induced drags could slow future growth down closer to 1.5%. By late September, the GDPNow model will have incorporated roughly two months of Q3 data, including July and August figures for retail sales, industrial production, and trade balances. A GDPNow reading of 2.5% or higher at the end of September would indicate that the economy maintained strong momentum through Q3, making a final BEA print inside the narrow 2.0-2.5% range less likely by suggesting a potential overshoot.

Sources:
Atlanta Fed GDPNow: https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow
BEA GDP Data: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's GDPNow model estimate for Q3 2025 real seasonally adjusted annual rate GDP growth is 2.5% or higher, according to the final update published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive). 

Resolution will be based on the official 'Latest estimate' figure posted on the Atlanta Fed GDPNow website (https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow). The resolver will check the headline number provided in the final model update released on or before 2025-09-30. If the value is 2.5% or greater (e.g., 2.5%, 2.6%), the question resolves Yes. If the value is 2.4% or lower, it resolves No. 

If the GDPNow model is discontinued or no updates are published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question will resolve based on the last available estimate published prior to 2025-10-01. Any updates or revisions made to the GDPNow model on or after 2025-10-01 will not be considered for the resolution of this subquestion.
subquestions.rationale: The Atlanta Fed GDPNow is a premier real-time tracking model for US GDP. Its final update in September will incorporate the majority of the quarter's actual data. If this estimate is 2.5% or above, it acts as a strong crux indicating Q3 momentum is too hot to safely land in the 2.0% - 2.5% target bracket, heavily updating forecasts for the ultimate BEA release in October.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Atlanta Fed GDPNow model's final published estimate for Q3 2025 real seasonally adjusted annual rate GDP growth must be 2.5% or higher, based on the final update published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30. Key threshold: ≥2.5%. Key entity: Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank GDPNow model. Timing: final update on or before September 30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Atlanta Fed GDPNow Q3 2025 GDP estimate September 2025' (to find all September updates); 2) 'GDPNow model estimate real GDP growth third quarter 2025' (broader search); 3) 'Atlanta Fed GDPNow September 26 2025 final update estimate' (targeting late September); 4) 'GDPNow Q3 2025 3.9% September 29 30 final' (targeting the last updates); 5) 'Atlanta Fed GDPNow latest estimate September 30 2025' (targeting final update date); 6) 'GDPNow 3.9 OR 4.0 September 29 30 2025' (checking for any further update).
evidence.step3_event_detection: The following GDPNow updates were identified during September 2025: (a) ~Sept 2: 2.2% (from a Williams-Sonoma report, likely the August 29 or Sept 2 update); (b) Sept 4: 3.0% (InstaForex, CalculatedRisk, multiple sources); (c) Sept 10: 3.1% (InstaForex); (d) Sept 16: 3.4% (InstaForex); (e) Sept 17/24: 3.3% (multiple sources referencing the Sept 17 update); (f) Sept 26: 3.9% (InstaForex — explicitly stated as revised from 3.3% to 3.9%); (g) Sept 30: 3.9% (CFO Dive and Investing.com articles confirm 3.9% as the Atlanta Fed's Q3 forecast). No subsequent update changing the 3.9% figure was found before September 30. The Investing.com India article dated September 30 (evening) still lists GDPNow Q3 at 3.9% for October 1 events. This strongly indicates 3.9% was the final September estimate.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple sources explicitly confirm the Atlanta Fed GDPNow model raised its Q3 2025 estimate to 3.9% on September 26, 2025: [InstaForex Sept 26](https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2756812) states 'The Atlanta Federal Reserve's GDPNow model has raised its third-quarter U.S. growth forecast from 3.3% to 3.9%, a 0.6-percentage-point increase reported on September 26, 2025.' [CFO Dive Sept 30](https://www.cfodive.com/news/consumer-confidence-slumps-five-month-low-inflation-jobs-outlook/761529/) states 'The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta raised its third-quarter GDP forecast to 3.9% from 3.3%.' [Investing.com Sept 30](https://www.investing.com/analysis/probable-shutdown-adds-risk-while-us-economy-nears-economic-nirvana-200667763) states 'the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow projecting a 3.9% annual growth rate.' [Investing.com India Sept 30 for Oct 1](https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/adp-jobs-data-manufacturing-pmi-and-crude-oil-inventories-in-focus-wednesday-93CH-5026594) states 'The Atlanta Fed GDPNow forecast remains at 3.9% for the current quarter.' This confirms 3.9% as the final September 2025 GDPNow update. 3.9% is well above the 2.5% threshold for Yes resolution.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The September 26, 2025 update (3.9%) is explicitly documented. Articles published on September 27, 28, 29, 30, and even the October 1 economic calendar (published September 30 evening) all reference 3.9% as the current/latest GDPNow estimate, confirming no subsequent update changed the figure before September 30.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first update meeting the ≥2.5% threshold in September 2025 was the September 4, 2025 update at 3.0%. All subsequent September updates (3.1%, 3.4%, 3.3%, 3.9%) also exceeded 2.5%. The final update in September appears to be 3.9% from September 26, 2025, with no further changes observed through September 30.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: One article (Williams-Sonoma report, Sept 2) cited GDPNow at 2.2%, which may reflect an earlier August estimate before the full PCE and trade data were incorporated. By September 4, it had risen to 3.0% per multiple independent sources. No articles show GDPNow falling below 2.5% during September 2025. Multiple independent sources (InstaForex, CFO Dive, Investing.com, Yahoo Finance, CNBC, CalculatedRisk, Capital Economics via Yahoo Finance) confirm the September estimates were consistently above 2.5%, culminating at 3.9% as the final September update. No conflicting evidence found for the final September value.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Atlanta Fed GDPNow model's final update in September 2025 showed a Q3 2025 real GDP growth estimate of 3.9% (updated September 26, 2025, and confirmed unchanged through at least September 30). This is well above the 2.5% threshold specified in the resolution criteria. The question resolves Yes. The resolution datetime is set to September 26, 2025, when the 3.9% figure was first published (though the question asks about the FINAL update, which is also 3.9%).

question: GTA 6 launch postponed?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if by May 26, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, Rockstar Games or its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, officially announces that Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) will not be released by May 26, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Grand Theft Auto VI is otherwise not released in the US by May 26, 2026, 11:59 PM ET this will qualify as a postponement.

For the purposes of this market, "release" refers to the game becoming publicly available for purchase or download in the US. Early access, beta versions, other forms of pre-release availability, or leaks will not count as an official release. If the release is only for certain consoles (e.g. Xbox Series X/S) it will count.

The resolution source will be official information from Rockstar Games or its parent company, Take-Two Interactive.

subquestions.question: Will a major gaming news outlet report that Grand Theft Auto VI is delayed beyond May 26, 2026, between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Despite Take-Two Interactive confirming a May 26, 2026, release date for Grand Theft Auto VI at a September 2025 shareholder meeting (https://www.sportskeeda.com/gta/why-shouldn-t-pay-attention-gta-6-delay-rumors), industry insiders remain skeptical. Since official announcements at earnings calls are frequently preceded by leaks to major journalists, October 2025 is a critical window. If the game is indeed facing an internal delay to be announced in November, it is highly likely that major outlets like Bloomberg or Insider Gaming will break the news in October. Sources: Sportskeeda - https://www.sportskeeda.com/gta/why-shouldn-t-pay-attention-gta-6-delay-rumors | Gameranx - https://gameranx.com/updates/id/insider-believes-a-grand-theft-auto-vi-delay-announcement-will-come-this-november/ | Mashable - https://mashable.com/article/gta-vi-delay-what-we-know-so-far
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), an article is published on any of the following websites reporting that Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) has been internally delayed, or is planned to be delayed, beyond its publicly announced May 26, 2026 release date: https://www.bloomberg.com, https://insider-gaming.com, https://www.ign.com, https://www.eurogamer.net, https://www.gamespot.com, https://www.polygon.com, or https://kotaku.com. The report must definitively state that the release has been delayed or that a delay is planned/scheduled based on internal sources, leaks, or official confirmation. Reports stating only that a delay is 'possible,' 'being considered,' 'feared,' or 'at risk' will not trigger a Yes resolution. Opinion pieces and speculative commentary (e.g., 'I think Rockstar will delay the game') do not count. If Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive officially announces a delay during this window on their official websites (https://www.rockstargames.com or https://www.take2games.com), the question will also resolve 'Yes'.
