subquestions.rationale: If the rumors of a November 2025 delay announcement are true, it is highly probable that well-connected gaming journalists will uncover and report the delay in the weeks leading up to the earnings call. An October leak confirming a delay would drastically increase the likelihood of the ultimate question resolving Yes, while a lack of leaks during this critical window would suggest the May 2026 date is still firm, reducing the probability of an impending delay announcement.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes resolution, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), one of the following must happen: (1) An article on bloomberg.com, insider-gaming.com, ign.com, eurogamer.net, gamespot.com, polygon.com, or kotaku.com definitively reports that GTA VI has been internally delayed or is planned to be delayed beyond May 26, 2026, with a new release window strictly after that date — based on internal sources, leaks, or official confirmation; OR (2) Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive officially announces a delay on their official websites. Reports of 'possible' delays, speculation, opinion pieces, or fear of delay do NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Grand Theft Auto VI GTA 6 delayed beyond May 2026' (Oct 2025) — to find any qualifying delay report; 2) 'GTA VI delay 2026 Rockstar Games announcement' (Oct 2025) — to find official announcements; 3) 'GTA 6 delay Bloomberg Jason Schreier October 2025' — to find Bloomberg-sourced reports; 4) 'GTA 6 delay IGN Kotaku Eurogamer Polygon GameSpot report October 2025' — to find qualifying outlet reports; 5) 'GTA 6 officially delayed Fall 2026 announcement Take-Two Rockstar' — to find official delay announcements; 6) 'GTA 6 Insider Gaming Tom Henderson delay confirmed 2026' — to find Insider Gaming confirmations.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (A) Game Rant (Oct 1) article saying delay is 'basically confirmed' based on insiders suggesting delay is 'possible' — this is NOT from a qualifying outlet and is speculative; (B) Kotaku (Oct 1) article about TikToker harassing Rockstar devs — not a delay report; (C) Polygon (Oct 3) article confirming May 26, 2026 release date (no delay beyond that date); (D) Multiple articles noting insiders like Tom Henderson have 'speculated' a delay may come — language of speculation/possibility only; (E) No article from bloomberg.com, insider-gaming.com, ign.com, eurogamer.net, gamespot.com, polygon.com, or kotaku.com definitively reporting a confirmed delay beyond May 26, 2026; (F) No official statement from Rockstar or Take-Two announcing a delay. The Polygon article confirmed May 26, 2026 as the current date. Multiple sources noted Tom Henderson of Insider Gaming 'speculated' a delay might happen but this is framed as speculation/possibility — not confirmation. Game Rant (not a qualifying outlet) summarizes these speculative statements.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No qualifying article was found. The Polygon article [polygon.com](https://www.polygon.com/gta-6-release-date/) published Oct 3 confirms May 26, 2026 release date — no delay. The Kotaku article [kotaku.com](https://kotaku.com/tiktok-creator-flies-to-scotland-to-yell-at-gta-6-devs-outside-their-office-2000630715) is about fan harassment, not a delay report. The GameSpot article is about GTA Online Halloween — not a delay report. Tom Henderson of Insider Gaming's statements are characterized as 'speculation' that a delay 'may' happen — not a definitive delay report. No article from any qualifying outlet states that GTA VI HAS BEEN or IS PLANNED TO BE delayed beyond May 26, 2026 based on internal sources.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found, so no timestamp to extract for a Yes resolution.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at all during the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked multiple angles: official announcements (none found), qualifying outlet articles (none definitively reporting a delay beyond May 26, 2026), Insider Gaming (Tom Henderson framed as speculative — 'may announce delay in February 2026' — not a current confirmed delay), Bloomberg (Jason Schreier mentioned in secondary coverage only as speculating about delay possibility). All sources consistently show the official release date remained May 26, 2026 through October 2025, with no qualifying outlet definitively reporting a confirmed delay beyond that date during the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence consistently shows: (1) The official GTA VI release date remained May 26, 2026 throughout October 2025; (2) No qualifying outlet (bloomberg.com, insider-gaming.com, ign.com, eurogamer.net, gamespot.com, polygon.com, kotaku.com) published a definitive report stating the game was delayed or planned to be delayed beyond May 26, 2026 during the window; (3) Mentions of insider speculation about a possible future delay do not meet the criteria (must 'definitively state' a delay has occurred/is planned); (4) No official announcement from Rockstar or Take-Two of any delay was found. Resolution is No. Since the window closed without any qualifying event occurring, the resolution_datetime is 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z.

question: Will US GDP growth in 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted real GDP growth rate for the United States in 2025, as reported in the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) "Advance Estimate" release for Q4 of 2025, scheduled for January 29, 2026.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: The relevant data will be the full-year real GDP growth rate as stated in the advance estimate, typically expressed as the percentage change from the annual level in 2024 to the annual level in 2025. Any revisions to this figure made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the final estimate of U.S. real GDP growth for the third quarter of 2025 be 4.2% or lower?
subquestions.background_information:
According to recent reports, the U.S. economy grew at an annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter of 2025 based on the initial estimate from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) (https://www.hindustantimes.com/). This followed a 3.8% growth rate in Q2 and a contraction in Q1, resulting in a 2.5% annualized growth rate for the first three quarters of 2025 combined (https://www.foxbusiness.com/). Due to a government shutdown, the BEA delayed its releases and the final estimate for Q3 2025 is scheduled for release on January 22, 2026 (https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product). For the full-year 2025 GDP growth to land between 2.0% and 2.5%, the Q4 figure will need to be relatively low, or prior quarters will need to see downward revisions. Therefore, a downward revision to the Q3 GDP growth estimate (to 4.2% or lower) would mathematically increase the likelihood that the full-year 2025 GDP growth remains within the 2.0%-2.5% range.

Sources:
BEA GDP Data: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
Hindustan Times: https://www.hindustantimes.com/
Fox Business: https://www.foxbusiness.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reports a final estimate of real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth for the third quarter (Q3) of 2025 that is 4.2% or lower (e.g., 4.2%, 4.1%, etc.). The resolution window for this question is between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-29 (inclusive).

The value used for resolution will be the "seasonally adjusted at annual rates" percent change from the preceding quarter for Real Gross Domestic Product, specifically for Q3 2025, as published in the BEA's final GDP release for that quarter (scheduled for January 22, 2026). The official release will be accessed at the BEA's website: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product.

If the reported value is 4.3% or higher, the question resolves No. If the final estimate for Q3 2025 is not published by the BEA on or before January 29, 2026, the question resolves as unresolvable. Any subsequent revisions to the Q3 2025 GDP data made after January 29, 2026, will not be considered for resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The full-year 2025 GDP growth outcome depends on the growth rates of all four quarters. Currently, the first three quarters suggest a running average of 2.5%. For the ultimate question (full-year GDP between 2.0% and 2.5%) to resolve Yes, the average must not exceed 2.5%. A downward revision of the Q3 GDP growth from its initial estimate of 4.3% to 4.2% or lower would reduce the running average, giving more room for Q4 growth before exceeding the 2.5% upper bound, making a full-year result of 2.0% to 2.5% more likely. It is therefore a strong early indicator.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: BEA's final estimate for Q3 2025 real GDP (seasonally adjusted annual rate, percent change from preceding quarter) must be ≤4.2%. Observable evidence: BEA press release published between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-29. Key threshold: 4.2% or lower = Yes; 4.3% or higher = No. Scheduled release: January 22, 2026.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'BEA Bureau of Economic Analysis GDP Q3 2025 final estimate third quarter' (2025-12-30 to 2026-01-29) — to find the official release; Query 2: 'US real GDP growth third quarter 2025 final release January 2026' (2025-12-30 to 2026-01-29) — to find news coverage of the release; Query 3: 'BEA Q3 2025 GDP second estimate OR final estimate OR third estimate January 22 2026' (2026-01-20 to 2026-01-29) — to confirm the type of estimate and exact value.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Primary candidate: BEA Q3 2025 GDP release on January 22, 2026, showing 4.4%. Supported by 10+ sources including AFP, FXStreet, Fox Business, ABA Banking Journal, Firstpost, The Star, Zero Hedge, Seeking Alpha, Breitbart, TalkMarkets. One InstaForex article (secondary, low-quality) mentioned 4.5%/4.6% but is contradicted by all major sources and rejected. The January 22, 2026 release is explicitly described as replacing the 'third estimate' (which was originally scheduled for December 19, 2025 but delayed by the government shutdown), making it the final estimate for resolution purposes.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The BEA released the final Q3 2025 real GDP estimate on January 22, 2026, at 4.4% annualized SAAR — [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2026/01/23/us-q3-gdp-growth-revised-upward-growth-benefits-unevenly-distributed) calls it a 'final reading'; [Firstpost](https://www.firstpost.com/business/us-gdp-grows-at-4-4-in-q3-final-reading-spotlight-on-fed-rate-cut-outlook-13971431.html) calls it 'the final estimate'; [ABA Banking Journal](https://bankingjournal.aba.com/2026/01/gdp-growth-remains-robust-in-q3-updated-estimate/) calls it 'the final revised estimate'; [TalkMarkets](https://talkmarkets.com/content/real-gdp-rose-a-revised-44-percent-in-the-third-quarter?post=552239) notes it 'replaces the originally scheduled third estimate due to the 2025 government shutdown.' The value 4.4% is above the 4.2% threshold, so Yes condition is NOT satisfied. Since 4.4% ≥ 4.3%, the question resolves No.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: January 22, 2026. FXStreet URL contains timestamp 202601221337, indicating approximately 13:37 UTC on January 22, 2026. Multiple independent sources published on the same date confirm this.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event within the resolution window (2025-12-30 to 2026-01-29). The January 22, 2026 release is the first and only BEA final GDP release for Q3 2025 within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: All major news sources (AFP, Fox Business, FXStreet, ABA Banking Journal, Firstpost, The Star, Zero Hedge, Breitbart, Seeking Alpha, TalkMarkets) consistently report 4.4%. The question requires the value to be ≤4.2% for Yes, but the reported value of 4.4% exceeds this threshold. The release occurred within the resolution window (January 22, 2026 is between December 30, 2025 and January 29, 2026). One InstaForex article mentioned 4.5%/4.6%, but this is a low-quality outlier contradicted by all credible sources. The resolution criteria specify the 'final estimate' published by January 29, 2026 — this was published on January 22, 2026, within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BEA published its final Q3 2025 real GDP estimate on January 22, 2026, showing 4.4% annualized growth — clearly above the 4.2% threshold required for Yes resolution. Since 4.4% ≥ 4.3%, the question resolves No. The definitive No moment is January 22, 2026, when the BEA report was published.

question: Will Tulsi Gabbard be the first to leave the Trump Cabinet before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve based on the next individual announced to leave the Trump Cabinet, or who otherwise ceases to be a member of the administration. If no one leaves by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “None before 2027”.

An announcement of an individual's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the resignation/removal takes effect.

If multiple individuals announce departures or are removed at the same time, the market will resolve to the individual who actually leaves office first. If they leave simultaneously, the market will resolve to the individual whose last name comes first alphabetically.

For the purposes of this market, the Cabinet includes Vice President, the heads of the 15 executive departments, as well as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the President’s Chief of Staff, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Ambassador to the United Nations, the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA). Acting officials serving in these roles are not included. The Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) is not considered Cabinet-level under the current Trump administration and is excluded from this market.

An individual will be considered to have left the Cabinet if they resign from or are removed from any Cabinet-level position, even if they are subsequently appointed to a different Cabinet-level role.

If a candidate who is not already listed, assumes a listed cabinet position they will be added to the market. However, candidates who have merely been nominated for a cabinet position will not be considered to have left, even if their nomination is rejected or withdrawn.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible reopening may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem announce her departure or be removed from her Cabinet position before February 1, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
To forecast whether Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard will be the first to leave the Trump Cabinet, we must monitor the status of other highly vulnerable Cabinet members. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem has been widely reported to be on the verge of being ousted. According to December 2025 reports, Noem is on 'thin ice' and is expected to be replaced in 2026 due to personal scandals, her employment of controversial adviser Corey Lewandowski, and President Trump's reported desire for a 'clean slate' for mass deportations in the new year (https://www.rawstory.com/trump-embarrassment-dead-beat-cabinet/). If Noem or any other Cabinet member is announced to be leaving the administration before Gabbard, then Gabbard cannot be the 'first' to leave. 

Sources:
Raw Story (Dec 15, 2025): https://www.rawstory.com/trump-embarrassment-dead-beat-cabinet/
Raw Story / The Bulwark (Dec 7, 2025): https://www.rawstory.com/key-trump-cabinet-member-booted-soon/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if, between 2026-01-05 and 2026-02-01 (inclusive), there is an announcement that Kristi Noem has resigned, been fired, or will otherwise cease to be the Secretary of Homeland Security. The announcement must be made within this time window, even if the actual departure is scheduled for a later date. Valid primary sources for resolution include official White House press releases (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), official Department of Homeland Security statements (https://www.dhs.gov/news-releases), or direct statements from President Trump or Kristi Noem via verified official social media accounts. If no such announcement occurs between 2026-01-05 and 2026-02-01, the question resolves 'No'. If she leaves her position to assume a different Cabinet-level role, it still counts as departing her current position for the purposes of this question.
subquestions.rationale: Kristi Noem is currently considered one of the most likely Trump Cabinet members to be ousted first, given multiple reports of her precarious standing in late 2025. If Noem leaves the Cabinet before Tulsi Gabbard, Gabbard cannot be the first to leave, which would essentially resolve the ultimate question to 'No'.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: An official announcement between 2026-01-05 and 2026-02-01 (inclusive) that Kristi Noem resigned, was fired, or would otherwise cease to be DHS Secretary. Observable evidence: White House press release, DHS statement, or direct statement from Trump or Noem via verified official social media. Key entities: Kristi Noem, President Trump, DHS. Timing constraint: announcement must occur within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Kristi Noem resignation fired removed Homeland Security Secretary 2026' (Jan 5 - Feb 1). Query 2: 'Kristi Noem departure Cabinet DHS Secretary January 2026' (Jan 5 - Feb 1). Query 3: 'Kristi Noem steps down resigns fired DHS Secretary announcement' (Jan 5 - Feb 1). Query 4: 'Trump fires Noem cabinet secretary replacement DHS January February 2026' (Jan 5 - Feb 1). Query 5: 'Kristi Noem still DHS Secretary status February 2026' (Jan 29 - Feb 5). Query 6: 'Noem fired removed departed Homeland Security February 2026' (Jan 29 - Feb 5).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Multiple calls for resignation from Democrats and Republicans (Jan 7-31) — REJECTED: these are calls for removal by others, not resignation/firing announcements; (2) Trump stating 'No' when asked if Noem would resign on January 27 — REJECTED as a qualifying event (this confirms she is NOT departing); (3) Trump backing Noem on Truth Social on January 31 — REJECTED (confirms she is staying); (4) Noem attending Cabinet meeting on January 29 — REJECTED (confirms she is staying); (5) Noem actively functioning as DHS Secretary on February 2-4 (body camera announcement, Arizona border visit) — REJECTED as outside the window but confirms no departure occurred within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event within the window of 2026-01-05 to 2026-02-01 matches the resolution criteria. President Trump explicitly stated 'No' when asked if Noem would resign [New York Post](https://nypost.com/2026/01/27/us-news/trump-addresses-requests-to-fire-dhs-secretary-kristi-noem-with-one-word-response/). Trump backed Noem publicly on Truth Social on January 31 [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5716159-trump-backs-noem-homeland-security/). Noem participated in Cabinet meetings and continued in her role throughout the window [The Hill](https://thehill.com/video-clips/5712325-watch-live-white-house-cabinet-meeting-trump-dhs-ice/). After the window closed, Noem was still actively serving and making DHS announcements [FOX 10](https://www.fox10phoenix.com/news/kristi-noem-dhs-secretary-arizona-visit-u-s-mexico-border).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying departure event because no such event occurred within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (resignation, firing, or departure announcement) was found at any point within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contrary evidence checked: Multiple articles confirm Noem was still DHS Secretary throughout the window and continued to serve after it closed (February 2-4, 2026 activities). No contradictory evidence suggesting she departed was found. All evidence consistently shows she remained in her position despite political pressure. The Redstate article explicitly notes Trump's Cabinet had 'not seen any resignations, firings, or role changes since its formation' as of January 27, 2026. The Alternet January 31 article discusses the 'real reason Trump didn't fire Noem,' confirming she was not fired.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution is No. Despite intense bipartisan calls for Kristi Noem's resignation or firing throughout the resolution window, President Trump explicitly refused to fire her, she refused to resign, and she continued to actively serve as DHS Secretary through the end of the window (February 1, 2026) and beyond. The question definitively resolves No as of the close of the resolution window on February 1, 2026, since no qualifying announcement occurred during the window.

question: Will MrBeast post another video on a weekday by September 30?
description:
On August 1, 2025, a Friday, MrBeast posted a video on his main YouTube channel, which breaks his usual pattern (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z4hVGCWH1Kc).

This market will resolve to “Yes” if MrBeast posts a YouTube video on a weekday (Monday - Friday, ET) between August 19 and September 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market is MrBeast's main YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast).

Note: This market refers to MrBeast's regular posted videos. Shorts, previews, or videos on platforms other than YouTube will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will MrBeast post a regular video on a weekend (Saturday or Sunday) on his main YouTube channel between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-21?
subquestions.background_information:
MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson) traditionally posts his high-production videos on his main YouTube channel on weekends. However, on Friday, August 1, 2025, he broke this longstanding pattern by uploading a regular video on a weekday (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z4hVGCWH1Kc). MrBeast has recently been highly active with external projects, including completing filming for "Beast Games" Season 2 (https://www.yahoo.com) and running the massive #TeamWater charity campaign throughout August (https://www.forbes.com). 

The ultimate question asks whether he will post on a weekday by September 30. Observing whether he reverts to his traditional weekend schedule during the first three weeks of September serves as a powerful crux. If he posts on a weekend, it signals a return to his standard upload pattern, potentially indicating the Friday post was an anomaly. 

Sources:
MrBeast Main Channel: https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast
Forbes: https://www.forbes.com
Yahoo: https://www.yahoo.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a new regular video is published on MrBeast's main YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast) on a Saturday or Sunday (Eastern Time) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-21.

- The overall resolution window begins exactly on 2025-09-01 at 00:00:00 ET and ends on 2025-09-21 at 23:59:59 ET.
- A qualifying "weekend" publication is defined as a video published between Saturday 00:00:00 ET and Sunday 23:59:59 ET during the resolution window.
- The video must be a regular, long-form upload. YouTube Shorts, live streams, community posts, trailers/previews, or uploads to any of his secondary channels (e.g., MrBeast Gaming, Beast Reacts) do not count.
- The publication time will be determined by the official publication timestamp accessible via the YouTube API or platform, converted to Eastern Time (ET).
- If MrBeast publishes at least one regular video on a weekend during this period, the question resolves Yes. If he only publishes on weekdays during this period, or if no regular videos are published at all within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-21 window, it resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion tests whether MrBeast is reverting to his historical norm of weekend uploads. If he publishes on a weekend by September 21, forecasters should likely decrease their probability for the ultimate question, as it implies his August 1st weekday upload was a one-off exception rather than a permanent schedule shift. Conversely, if he uploads on a weekday during this time, the ultimate question is automatically satisfied, making this a highly informative crux.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A regular long-form video published on MrBeast's main YouTube channel (@MrBeast) on a Saturday or Sunday ET between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-21. Weekend days in window: Sep 6-7, Sep 13-14, Sep 20-21. Must not be a Short, livestream, community post, trailer, or secondary channel upload.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: 'MrBeast YouTube video September 2025'; 'MrBeast new video upload September 2025 weekend'; 'MrBeast main YouTube channel video published September 6 7 2025'; 'MrBeast YouTube video Saturday Sunday September 13 14 2025'; 'MrBeast new video upload long-form challenge September 2025'; 'MrBeast YouTube channel upload schedule posting video 2025'; 'MrBeast video released September 20 21 14 7 2025'; 'MrBeast NFL broadcast video YouTube September 5 2025 regular upload'; 'MrBeast new video September 2025 YouTube longform'; 'MrBeast video published I Bought The NFL channel September 2025'; 'MrBeast video September 20 21 2025 Saturday Sunday upload'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Sep 3 (Wed): 'I Bought The NFL' video uploaded — Wednesday, not a weekend. (2) Sep 5 (Fri): NFL Chiefs vs Chargers livestream on YouTube — livestream, not a regular upload; also Friday. (3) Sep 6 (Sat): NFL broadcast aftermath coverage — this was a livestream event, not a regular video upload. (4) Sep 13 (Sat): Tyson punch video/stunt — shared on X/Instagram/TikTok, not confirmed as a regular YouTube channel upload. No articles explicitly report a long-form regular video published on MrBeast's main YouTube channel on a Saturday or Sunday in the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No found article explicitly states a regular, long-form video was published on MrBeast's main YouTube channel on a Saturday or Sunday during the resolution window. The 'I Bought The NFL' upload was September 3 (Wednesday). The NFL game on September 5 was a livestream (explicitly excluded). The Tyson punch content was shared on X and Instagram, with no explicit confirmation it was uploaded to his main YouTube channel as a regular video on Sep 13 (Saturday). No direct YouTube API timestamp or news report confirms a qualifying weekend upload.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact publication timestamp for a qualifying regular long-form YouTube video on a weekend could be extracted from available evidence.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Cannot be performed — no qualifying event was found in the first place.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked multiple sources across the entire window. The NFL-related content was a promotional clip (Sep 3, Wednesday) and a livestream (Sep 5, Friday). The Tyson punch was social media content (X/Instagram). No source confirms a regular long-form YouTube upload on a weekend. However, absence of news coverage of a weekend upload does not definitively prove none occurred — MrBeast uploads frequently and not all uploads generate major news coverage. Evidence is insufficient to confirm Yes, but also insufficient to definitively confirm No.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence gathered does not contain explicit confirmation of a regular long-form video published on MrBeast's main YouTube channel on a qualifying weekend day. However, I also cannot definitively confirm that no such video was published. The resolution cannot be determined with the required precision from available evidence alone.

question: Will the US capture Khamenei before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if U.S. government personnel (including U.S. military, CIA, or any U.S. federal law enforcement agency) directly participate on the ground in an operation that results in the capture of Supreme Leader of Iran Ali Khamenei by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, “capture” means Khamenei is taken into physical custody and detained (including arrest, detention, or seizure) such that he is no longer free to leave at will, even if only temporarily. Voluntary surrender may qualify if it results in immediate detention/custody.

U.S. personnel must directly participate on the ground to qualify. Intelligence, surveillance, planning, logistics, transport, support, funding, training, or advisory roles alone will not count, even if they materially contribute to the operation. If U.S. personnel are physically present in the operational area and take direct action (e.g., raiding, detaining, securing, physically transferring custody), it will qualify. U.S. government contractors will be considered to be U.S. personnel if they are confirmed to be acting under the direction of U.S. government authorities.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the US government publicly confirm conducting kinetic military strikes on Iranian sovereign territory between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-25?
subquestions.background_information: Since late December 2025, Iran has been engulfed in massive anti-government protests, leading to thousands of deaths and a severe regime crackdown. In response to the unrest and threats to regional stability, the US has deployed a significant naval armada, including the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group, to the Middle East, alongside strategic bombers and surveillance aircraft. US officials have openly considered military options against Iran, including strikes on Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) bases or decapitation operations targeting Iran's leadership. According to CBS News, options range from targeted strikes to operations mirroring the US capture of Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro. Gulf allies have initiated diplomatic efforts to avert direct US-Iran military conflict. Khamenei has reportedly been moved to underground bunkers. Whether the US takes the extraordinary step of launching direct military strikes on Iranian soil in the near term is a critical indicator of whether the administration is willing to risk an all-out conflict, which would be a necessary precursor to or component of any operation to capture the Supreme Leader. Sources: CBS News: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/iran-protests-us-response-options/ ; Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/02/01/khamenei-warns-us-of-regional-war-if-iran-is-attacked
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if the United States Department of Defense (DoD), the White House, or another official US government agency publicly confirms that US forces have conducted intentional kinetic military strikes (e.g., airstrikes, missile strikes, or ground combat operations) against targets located within the internationally recognized sovereign borders of Iran between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-25 (inclusive of both dates). 'Kinetic military strikes' includes the use of explosive munitions, missiles, drone strikes, or direct ground fire. Cyberattacks, electronic warfare, or psychological operations do not count. The strikes must be officially acknowledged by the US government on the record (e.g., via a press release on https://www.defense.gov/News/Press-Releases/ or an official statement on https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/). Anonymous leaks or unconfirmed reports do not qualify. Strikes on Iranian proxies (e.g., in Iraq, Syria, or Yemen) or on Iranian naval vessels in international waters do not count. The target must be within Iran's terrestrial borders or its territorial waters. If the US government announces a strike that occurred within the date range, but the announcement is delayed until after February 25, the question will still resolve 'Yes' so long as the actual strike occurred between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-25 and is confirmed by the resolution date.
subquestions.rationale: An operation to capture the Supreme Leader of Iran on Iranian soil would represent an unprecedented escalation and would almost certainly be accompanied or preceded by broader US military action against Iran's air defenses, IRGC bases, and military infrastructure. If the US initiates direct kinetic strikes on Iranian territory in February 2026, it signals a collapse of de-escalation efforts by Gulf allies and a willingness by the US administration to execute extreme military options. If no strikes occur, it suggests diplomacy or deterrence is holding, drastically lowering the probability of an eventual capture raid.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The US DoD, White House, or official US agency publicly confirms kinetic military strikes (airstrikes, missiles, drones, ground fire) on targets within Iran's sovereign territory between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-25. Observable evidence: Official press release on defense.gov or whitehouse.gov. Key entities: DoD/Pentagon, White House. Timing: Strikes must occur within the window; announcements may be delayed but strikes must have actually happened in-window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'US military strikes Iran 2026' (Feb 8–25) — to find any confirmed strike reporting; 2. 'United States airstrikes Iran February 2026' (Feb 1–25) — broader window; 3. 'US strikes Iran confirmed Pentagon DoD announcement February 2026' — looking for official confirmation; 4. 'US attack Iran nuclear facilities military operation February 21-25 2026' — targeting specific dates; 5. 'Iran nuclear negotiations Geneva February 26 2026' — to check if diplomacy continued past window; 6. 'US war Iran started began bombed' — to disprove the null hypothesis.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No articles found confirming actual US kinetic strikes on Iran during Feb 8–25, 2026. All articles describe: (a) massive US military buildup and preparation; (b) diplomatic talks in Geneva (Feb 17–18); (c) Trump threatening 'bad things' if no deal in 10–15 days; (d) Pentagon saying 'everything is on the table' (Feb 24); (e) Iran and US heading to third round of Geneva talks on Feb 26. Multiple articles reference a prior strike (Operation Midnight Hammer, June 2025) — NOT within the resolution window. The only confirmed kinetic action referenced is the June 2025 operation, outside the question's window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article provides direct, explicit confirmation of US kinetic strikes on Iranian sovereign territory during Feb 8–25, 2026. [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/us-military-moves-into-place-for-possible-strikes-in-iran) confirms military positioning, not strikes. [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/pentagon-chief-says-everything-is-on-the-table-as-us-presses-iran-to-make-a-deal/3838305) reports Hegseth saying 'everything is on the table' (Feb 24), not a strike announcement. [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/98P849E) confirms Trump threatened action but no decision made. [Iran FM statements](https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2026/02/25/iran-s-negotiating-team-heads-to-geneva-for-a-fresh-round-of-nuclear-talks-with-us) confirm Iran heading to Geneva for talks on Feb 25–26, indicating no war had yet started. Criteria for Yes not met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp of a qualifying US kinetic strike on Iranian territory during the window could be extracted, because no such event was reported.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the window. The only referenced US strikes on Iran are from June 2025 (Operation Midnight Hammer), which is outside the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Strong contradictory evidence against Yes: (1) Geneva nuclear talks were scheduled for and proceeded on Feb 26, 2026, the day after the window closed — this is inconsistent with an ongoing military conflict; (2) Iran's FM Araghchi announced travel to Geneva on Feb 25 calling it a 'historic opportunity' — would not occur post-US strike; (3) Pentagon's Hegseth on Feb 24 said 'everything is on the table' in future conditional tense, not confirming past strikes; (4) Multiple third-party governments (India, Sweden, etc.) were advising citizens to leave Iran but no evacuation triggered by actual attack; (5) No DoD press release, no White House statement, no official confirmation found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence consistently shows that during Feb 8–25, 2026, the US was in a state of intense military preparation and diplomatic pressure regarding Iran, but did NOT conduct officially confirmed kinetic military strikes on Iranian sovereign territory. The window closed with diplomacy ongoing (Geneva talks Feb 26), no official US government confirmation of actual strikes, and no reporting of strikes having occurred. Resolution: No.

question: Will NewJeans perform again in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if NewJeans (뉴진스, NJZ) gives at least one live performance as a group at any point between June 3 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. A qualifying performance must involve at least three members of NewJeans performing together under the group name "NewJeans" in front of a live audience or as part of a livestreamed or televised event.

Prerecorded performances aired in 2025 that were filmed earlier will not count. Solo or sub-unit performances will not count. Dance practices or behind-the-scenes content do not qualify as performances for this market.

The resolution source will be official announcements from NewJeans (including verified social media) and ADOR, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will ADOR, HYBE, or NewJeans officially announce any new public group activities (such as a music release, fan event, or live performance) between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 30, 2025, the Seoul Central District Court ruled that NewJeans' exclusive contracts with ADOR remain valid until 2029, rejecting the members' attempts to terminate the agreements (https://www.nme.com). NewJeans previously rebranded as 'NJZ' for independent activities and performed in March 2025, but a court injunction halted those independent efforts (https://www.yahoo.com). Despite the recent ruling in ADOR's favor, NewJeans' legal representatives (Shin & Kim LLC) stated the members plan to appeal, citing a 'complete collapse of trust' and claiming it is 'impossible to continue activities under the current conditions' (https://www.soompi.com). 

For NewJeans to fulfill the ultimate question of performing live as a group in 2025, there must either be a reconciliation, a legal settlement, or forced compliance under ADOR's management. If ADOR or the group officially announces new public group activities by the end of November, it strongly indicates that a return to the stage in 2025 is plausible. Conversely, a lack of announcements likely signals ongoing legal gridlock, making a 2025 performance highly unlikely.

Sources:
NME: https://www.nme.com
Yahoo: https://www.yahoo.com
Soompi: https://www.soompi.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if ADOR, HYBE, or NewJeans (via their official social media channels, official press releases, or verified statements from their legal representatives) officially announce a new public group activity for NewJeans between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive).

A 'public group activity' is defined as any official schedule involving at least three members of NewJeans acting under the group name 'NewJeans' or any other name managed by ADOR/HYBE. Qualifying activities include, but are not limited to: the release of new music, an official fan meeting, a live concert or festival performance, or a scheduled television/livestream appearance.

The official announcement must occur between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, 11:59 PM ET. The activity itself does not need to take place within this window (e.g., an announcement in November for a 2026 tour still qualifies). 

Announcements of purely legal updates, court dates, internal company meetings, or solo/sub-unit activities do not qualify. Announcements regarding the re-airing of pre-recorded content or the release of behind-the-scenes footage from past events also do not qualify.

The primary resolution sources will be official channels from ADOR or HYBE (https://hybecorp.com), NewJeans' official social media (e.g., https://twitter.com/NewJeans_ADOR), or statements from their legal counsel, corroborated by a consensus of credible reporting from major South Korean news outlets or K-pop news sites like Soompi (https://www.soompi.com).
subquestions.rationale: Given the October 30 court ruling and NewJeans' declared intent to appeal, the group is currently at a legal standstill with their agency. If they are to perform again before the end of 2025, preparations and official announcements for such an event (or a general resumption of activities) would need to occur quickly. Monitoring whether any official group activities are announced by the end of November provides a critical early indicator of whether the group will remain on hiatus or resume active schedules.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official announcement (from ADOR/HYBE/NewJeans official channels or legal representatives) of a new public group activity involving at least 3 NewJeans members. Must be announced between Oct 31-Nov 30, 2025. Legal updates, pre-recorded re-airings, and solo activities do not qualify. The activity itself need not occur in the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'NewJeans ADOR HYBE official announcement group activity 2025' (Oct 31-Nov 30) - to find any qualifying announcements. 2) 'NewJeans music release concert fan event November 2025' - to find specific events. 3) 'NewJeans ADOR official comeback schedule concert album release announced' (Nov 1-30) - to find specific schedule announcements. 4) 'NewJeans ADOR official new music release concert announcement schedule late November 2025' - to find late-window events. 5) 'Min Hee-jin NewJeans world tour plan HYBE court November 2025' - to check world tour reference.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) ADOR's Nov 12 announcement that Haerin and Hyein will return to label activities - REJECTED: this is a legal/organizational update about contract compliance, not an announcement of a specific public group activity. (2) ADOR's statement that 'preparations for a full-length album are complete' - REJECTED: Not a specific announcement with dates/details, and multiple sources confirm ADOR had NOT announced an official comeback schedule. (3) All 5 members returning to ADOR (Nov 12-13) - REJECTED: Legal/organizational update, not a group activity announcement. (4) Min Hee-jin's court testimony mentioning a NewJeans world tour plan (Nov 27) - REJECTED: Historical context in legal proceedings, not an official announcement. (5) NewJeans winning 'Trend of the Year' at KGMA (Nov 15) - REJECTED: Award based on past activities, not a new announced group activity.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that exactly matches the resolution criteria. [Khan, Nov 14](https://www.khan.co.kr/article/202511141851197) explicitly states 'ADOR has not yet announced an official comeback schedule.' [Korea Herald, Nov 17](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10617857) confirms uncertainty persists with three members still in negotiations. [Korea Herald, Nov 27](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10624768) notes Minji, Danielle, and Hani 'remain in discussions with Ador.' ADOR's statements about album preparations being 'complete' and pledging to support activities constitute expressions of intent, not official announcements of specific scheduled group activities. The resolution criteria require an official announcement of a new public group activity; organizational/legal updates do not qualify.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with a reliable timestamp was found. ADOR's announcement on Nov 12 concerns member return status (legal/organizational). No specific concert, album release date, fan meeting announcement, or TV/livestream appearance announcement was identified within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable - no qualifying event was identified.
evidence.step7_verification: Counter-check: Could ADOR's repeated statements about album preparation count as an announcement of a music release? No - these statements lack specific release dates or scheduling details, and multiple credible sources (Khan, Korea Times, Korea Herald) explicitly note that ADOR had not announced an official comeback schedule as of mid-to-late November. The TimesNow article (Nov 27) about Min Hee-jin revealing a world tour plan was in the context of her court testimony about past plans, not an official announcement of a new activity. No contradictory evidence found showing a specific qualifying announcement was made.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence consistently shows that while ADOR announced album preparations were complete and all five members were returning to the label during the window, no official specific public group activity (with dates/details for a concert, album release, fan meeting, or scheduled appearance) was announced by ADOR, HYBE, or NewJeans between Oct 31-Nov 30, 2025. Multiple credible sources explicitly note the absence of an official comeback schedule announcement. The window closed without a qualifying event.
