question: Will the next government funding bill be a clean CR?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the next government funding bill that becomes law in the United States by December 31, 2025, is a clean continuing resolution. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

A clean continuing resolution is defined as a funding measure that temporarily extends current government spending at the previous fiscal year’s levels for a specified period, without incorporating any additional policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the US House of Representatives pass any Continuing Resolution (CR) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-10?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-October 2025, the U.S. federal government was in a partial shutdown, with lawmakers failing to agree on a federal funding measure. According to reports from October 17, 2025, the Senate had already held ten votes on a Republican-backed clean Continuing Resolution (CR) aimed at funding the government until mid-November, but no final agreement had materialized to end the shutdown. Since a clean CR has seen repeated Senate action but the shutdown persists, the House of Representatives is a critical bottleneck. Tracking whether the House can pass any CR by early November serves as a vital early indicator. If the House passes a CR laden with partisan riders, the final enacted law might not be 'clean' (or the shutdown may drag on). If they pass a clean CR, the ultimate question is highly likely to resolve Yes.

Sources:
Star Local Media: No progress on funding as Trump cuts programs amid shutdown. https://starlocalmedia.com/
Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives: https://clerk.house.gov/
Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the United States House of Representatives successfully passes any piece of legislation functioning as a Continuing Resolution (CR) to temporarily fund the federal government between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-10 (inclusive).

The CR passed by the House does not need to be a "clean" CR; it may contain policy riders, earmarks, spending cuts, or other modifications. The passage of any temporary CR measure by the House within the specified timeframe will trigger a "Yes" resolution. 

To resolve this question, the official roll call votes and legislative records from the Office of the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives (https://clerk.house.gov/Votes) and bill tracking on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/) will be used as the primary authoritative sources. The passage must be officially recorded on these sites with a date falling exactly within the resolution window.

If no such CR passes the House by the end of 2025-11-10, or if the House only passes full, permanent appropriations packages (such as an omnibus or minibus) rather than a temporary CR, the question resolves "No". If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the 2025-11-10 deadline, the question resolves "No".
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on whether the final enacted funding bill is a clean CR. Currently, there is an ongoing government shutdown, and the Senate has repeatedly attempted to advance a clean CR without success. The House's action is the immediate crux for legislative momentum. If the House passes a CR by November 10, 2025, it provides strong evidence regarding the shape of the final legislation. A House-passed CR with conservative policy riders would decrease the probability of a final 'clean' CR (indicating entrenched partisan demands), whereas a House-passed clean CR would drastically increase the probability of a clean CR ultimately becoming law. Thus, assessing House passage of *any* CR serves as a highly informative, distinct interim milestone.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The US House of Representatives must pass any legislation functioning as a Continuing Resolution (CR) to temporarily fund the federal government between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-10 (inclusive). Observable evidence: Official roll call vote recorded with date in the window. Key entities: US House of Representatives. Threshold: Majority vote passes. Timing: Must occur on or between Oct 31 and Nov 10, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'US House of Representatives Continuing Resolution CR passed November 2025' (to find any House CR passage in November 2025). Query 2: 'House vote continuing resolution government funding November 2025' (to identify specific House votes on CR). Query 3: 'House vote CR continuing resolution passed November 10 11 12 2025 government shutdown end' (to find the specific House vote date). Query 4: 'House passed CR 222-209 vote November 12 2025 government shutdown end' (to confirm the exact House vote date).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: House passed CR 222-209 on November 12-13, 2025. This is outside the Oct 31 - Nov 10 window. During the window, the House was entirely out of session — it had been absent since September 19, 2025, and Speaker Johnson only called members back after the Senate passed the CR on November 10. Senate passed the CR on November 10, 2025 — this is not a House passage. No House CR vote occurred within the window. The earlier House-passed CR referenced in many articles was passed on September 19, 2025, which is before the resolution window. All evidence indicates the House was out of session Oct 31 - Nov 10.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution requires the House to pass a CR within Oct 31 - Nov 10, 2025. Multiple sources confirm: (1) [JD Supra tracking article](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/tracking-the-2025-us-government-6534963/) states 'The House and Senate are both out of session, with no continuing resolution (CR) vote scheduled for the immediate future' as of Nov 4. (2) [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/senate-dems-emboldened-shutdown-strategy-after-election-sweep) confirms the House remained out of session through Nov 5. (3) [National Law Review](https://natlawreview.com/article/healthcare-preview-week-november-10-2025) published Nov 10 states 'House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA) stated he would provide a 36-hour notice for members to return after the Senate passes the CR, with House votes potentially occurring Wednesday or Thursday.' (4) [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-house-to-soon-vote-on-senate-bill-to-reopen-government-says-speaker-johnson/3740118) published Nov 10 reports Johnson announced House would vote 'as soon as possible' after the Senate passed the bill. (5) [News 9](https://www.news9.com/national-politics-oklahoma/house-votes-to-reopen-government-and-end-nearly-2-month-long-shutdown) and [Raw Story](https://www.rawstory.com/government-shutdown-2674286649/) confirm the House voted 222-209 on November 13, 2025 — outside the window. [JD Supra CR signed](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/cr-signed-sealed-and-delivered-7495298/) confirms House passed on November 12, 2025 and Trump signed on November 12. Multiple sources agree House voted on November 12-13, 2025, not within Oct 31-Nov 10 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: House vote on CR: November 12-13, 2025 (multiple sources confirm). This is outside the resolution window (Oct 31 - Nov 10, 2025). No House CR vote timestamp exists within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earlier House-passed CR referenced in sources was from September 19, 2025 (before the resolution window). No House CR passage occurred within the Oct 31 - Nov 10 window. The House was continuously out of session during the entire window period.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: Some sources say 'November 12' and others say 'November 13' for the House vote, but all agree it occurred after November 10. No source indicates the House passed any CR between Oct 31 and Nov 10. The House remained out of session throughout this entire period, with Speaker Johnson only issuing a 36-hour notice to return on November 10 after the Senate passed the CR. The House vote occurred on November 12-13, clearly outside the resolution window. The JD Supra article 'CR Signed, Sealed and Delivered' explicitly states 'On November 12, 2025, President Trump signed H.R. 5371' and 'The House passed the bill 222-209.' This is after the November 10 deadline.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The US House of Representatives did NOT pass any Continuing Resolution between October 31 and November 10, 2025 (inclusive). The House was entirely out of session during this period. The Senate passed a CR on November 10, 2025, but the House only voted on and passed the CR on November 12-13, 2025 — after the resolution window closed. Resolution: No.

question: Will Israeli troops enter Suwayda in 2025?
description:
This polymarket will resolve to "Yes" if Israeli military personnel physically enter Suwayda Governorate in Syria for military operations between July 17, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, aerial and maritime operations will not be considered. Only operations involving troops on the ground within Suwayda Governorate will count.

Undercover Israeli operatives and assets will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be photo and video evidence, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Israeli military aircraft or drones conduct at least one kinetic strike within Syria's Suwayda Governorate between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Since the fall of the Bashar al-Assad regime in December 2023, Israel has escalated military operations in southern Syria. Following severe sectarian clashes in July 2025 between Druze militias and Bedouin tribes in the Suwayda Governorate, Israel launched airstrikes targeting Syrian government forces in the region and positioned itself as a protector of the Druze minority (https://reliefweb.int/report/syrian-arab-republic/expert-comment-israels-campaign-syria-enters-new-phase-amid-al-suwayda-escalation). Throughout August and September 2025, Israeli ground troops made progressive incursions into the Quneitra and Daraa provinces, conducting surveys and raiding civilian homes (https://english.enabbaladi.net/archives/2025/09/quneitra-israel-conducts-survey-in-sida-golan). Reports in late September indicate that security negotiations between the Syrian transitional government and Israel have stalled due to Israel's demand to establish a 'humanitarian corridor' directly to Suwayda. Given that Israeli ground forces have not yet reached Suwayda, continued or renewed Israeli airstrikes in the governorate would serve as a strong indicator that Israel is maintaining an active military campaign in Suwayda, potentially shaping the environment for a future ground incursion.

Sources:
ReliefWeb: https://reliefweb.int/report/syrian-arab-republic/expert-comment-israels-campaign-syria-enters-new-phase-amid-al-suwayda-escalation
Enab Baladi: https://english.enabbaladi.net/archives/2025/09/quneitra-israel-conducts-survey-in-sida-golan
Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/27/israel-launches-new-operations-in-syria-after-strike-kills-soldiers
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves to 'Yes' if any credible international news organization, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/), BBC (https://www.bbc.com/), or AP (https://apnews.com/), or an official government/military source from Israel or Syria reports that the Israeli Air Force (IAF) or Israeli military drones conducted at least one kinetic strike (such as an airstrike, missile strike, or drone strike) within the geographic boundaries of the Suwayda Governorate, Syria, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

The strike must occur strictly within this timeframe. If a strike occurs within the window but is reported shortly after, it still counts toward a 'Yes' resolution. Airstrikes strictly outside Suwayda (e.g., in neighboring Daraa or Quneitra governorates) do not count. Non-kinetic operations (such as reconnaissance flights, sonic booms, dropping leaflets, or airdropping supplies) will not trigger a 'Yes' resolution.

If no qualifying strike is reported to have occurred between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 by November 7, 2025 (accounting for a 7-day reporting grace period), the question resolves to 'No'. In the event of conflicting reports about the origin or location of the strike, consensus from at least two major international news organizations or explicit confirmation by the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (SOHR, https://www.syriahr.com/en/) will be required to resolve the question as 'Yes'.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Israeli ground troops will physically enter Suwayda by the end of 2025. Israel is currently making ground incursions into provinces closer to the Golan Heights (Quneitra and Daraa) while demanding a 'humanitarian corridor' to Suwayda. Kinetic airstrikes in Suwayda would indicate that Israel is actively engaged in shaping the security environment in the province, either to support allied Druze factions, target hostile forces, or prepare for a ground corridor. An airstrike in October raises the probability that their military campaign will culminate in a ground deployment there. If no airstrikes occur, it suggests a pause or de-escalation in Israel's Suwayda-specific military operations, reducing the likelihood of a ground incursion before the end of the year.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Israeli Air Force (IAF) aircraft or Israeli military drones must conduct at least one kinetic strike (airstrike, missile strike, or drone strike) within the geographic boundaries of Syria's Suwayda Governorate, between 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z and 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z (inclusive). Observable evidence: credible report from Reuters, Al Jazeera, BBC, AP, SOHR, or official government/military source explicitly stating a kinetic Israeli strike in Suwayda between those dates. Key entities: IAF, Israeli military drones, Suwayda Governorate (not Daraa, not Quneitra). Timing: strictly October 1–31, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Israeli airstrike Suwayda Syria October 2025' — to find direct reports of a qualifying event; 2) 'Israel military strike Sweida governorate 2025' — alternative spelling; 3) 'Israeli airstrike Syria Suwayda October 2025 IAF drone strike' — more specific; 4) 'Israel Syria military operations strikes October 2025' — broader context; 5) 'Israel strike Suwayda Sweida October 2025 SOHR' — SOHR-specific; 6) 'Israel attack Syria southern governorates October November 2025' — broader geographic; 7) '"Suwayda" OR "Sweida" Israeli strike bombing October 2025' — direct; 8) 'Israel Syria Druze Suwayda military action ceasefire October 2025' — context.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Israeli strikes in Suwayda on July 16, 2025 — REJECTED: outside the October 1–31 window. (2) Israeli artillery strike in Al-Quneitra (Hursh Tel Ahmar) on October 12, 2025 (SOHR) — REJECTED: explicitly in Al-Quneitra, not Suwayda governorate. (3) Israeli military patrols in Al-Quneitra and Daraa on October 4, 2025 (SOHR) — REJECTED: non-kinetic patrol operations in Quneitra/Daraa, not Suwayda. (4) Israeli shelling of Daraa province (Koya village) on October 23, 2025 (Anadolu Agency) — REJECTED: explicitly in Daraa province, not Suwayda. (5) Israeli strike in Dmeir/Damascus region on October 3, 2025 (Spacewar) — REJECTED: near Damascus/Dmeir, not Suwayda. (6) October 8 article references 'possible airstrikes' near southern Damascus related to Suwayda clashes — REJECTED: vague, not confirmed Israeli strike, not explicitly in Suwayda. (7) Turkey's FM Fidan on October 12 condemning 'Israel's attacks on Syria, especially in Suwayda' — likely referring to July 2025 attacks, not new ones; no new strike confirmed. (8) ReliefWeb October 22 report mentions 'limited precision strikes' in Syria — REJECTED: no specific mention of Suwayda during October.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article explicitly reports an Israeli kinetic strike (airstrike, missile strike, or drone strike) within the geographic boundaries of Suwayda Governorate during October 1–31, 2025. All Israeli kinetic activity in Syria during October 2025 that was identified targeted Al-Quneitra or Daraa governorates, not Suwayda. Multiple articles about the Suwayda situation in October 2025 describe local clashes between Druze factions and Syrian government forces, a ceasefire framework, and humanitarian issues — without any mention of Israeli strikes during the month. The Israeli strikes referenced in context all trace back to July 16, 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp found within the October 1–31, 2025 window. The most recent Israeli strike in Suwayda referenced across all articles occurred on July 16, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (Israeli kinetic strike in Suwayda during October 2025) was identified in any of the searches. Therefore, there is no first occurrence to confirm.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove the 'No' conclusion by: (a) checking SOHR reports — SOHR's October 12 article only mentions Al-Quneitra strikes, not Suwayda; (b) checking Turkey's condemnation of Israeli attacks on Suwayda (October 12) — this refers to prior July events, not new October strikes; (c) checking ReliefWeb October 22 analysis — confirms Israel's Syria operations were 'limited precision strikes' for diplomatic leverage, with no specific Suwayda kinetic strike in October; (d) reviewing all articles mentioning Suwayda in October 2025 — none report Israeli strikes. The overall pattern is that a US-mediated ceasefire from July 19, 2025 governed Israeli-Syrian relations in this area, and no strike in Suwayda during October 2025 was reported. The absence is consistent across multiple sources covering the Suwayda situation extensively.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying Israeli kinetic strike in Suwayda Governorate during October 2025 was found across extensive searches. All Israeli military activity in southern Syria during October 2025 was located in Al-Quneitra and Daraa governorates. The Suwayda situation during October 2025 was characterized by: local Druze-government ceasefire tensions, humanitarian crises, prisoner exchanges, and diplomatic negotiations — but no Israeli strikes. The evidence consistently and coherently points to No resolution. The window closed on October 31, 2025 with no qualifying event reported.

question: Israel x Syria security agreement by January 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an official security agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the governments of Israel and Syria by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market refers only to agreements which directly address border security and demarcation, normalization, or diplomatic recognition or otherwise creates a formalized security framework between the two states.    

Ceasefire announcements or other announced de-escalations such as those relating to the July 16-18 skirmishes with the Druze, or any other future military engagements, which do not address the broader security relationship will not qualify.

Only deals which are officially announced will qualify. Informal announcements which do not constitute a formalized agreement will not count.

The primary resolution source will be official statements from the Israeli and Syrian governments. However, an agreement which is announced by only of the parties will qualify if an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirms that such a formal agreement has been reached.

subquestions.question: Will the Israeli government or the IDF officially announce a withdrawal of military forces from any territory in southern Syria occupied after December 8, 2024, between December 12, 2025 and January 11, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Following the fall of Bashar al-Assad's regime in December 2024, Israeli forces advanced into southern Syria, occupying strategic positions including Mount Hermon and parts of the 1974 buffer zone. According to reports from Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/20/after-israel-pms-trip-to-occupied-syria-is-a-deal-off-the-table), this expansion covered approximately 400 square kilometers to secure Israel's northern border. Syria's transitional president, Ahmed al-Sharaa, has explicitly conditioned any comprehensive peace or security deal on Israel withdrawing to the pre-December 8, 2024 borders, as confirmed by The Yeshiva World (https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/general/2356191/syrian-president-confirms-direct-negotiations-with-israel-for-first-time-since-assads-fall.html). The Israeli government, however, maintains that it will not withdraw its forces until a new formalized security deal is reached (https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5084931-netanyahu-denies-contacts-syria-have-led-final-agreement). Because troop withdrawal is the central point of contention, an announcement of withdrawal is a direct indicator of diplomatic breakthrough.

Sources:
Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/20/after-israel-pms-trip-to-occupied-syria-is-a-deal-off-the-table
The Yeshiva World: https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/general/2356191/syrian-president-confirms-direct-negotiations-with-israel-for-first-time-since-assads-fall.html
Asharq Al-Awsat English: https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5084931-netanyahu-denies-contacts-syria-have-led-final-agreement
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Israeli Prime Minister's Office, the Israeli Ministry of Defense, or the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) officially and publicly announces a planned, ongoing, or completed withdrawal of Israeli military personnel from at least one military post or territorial area in southern Syria that was occupied on or after December 8, 2024. The announcement must occur between the start date of 2025-12-12 and the end date of 2026-01-11 (inclusive).

The announcement must pertain to a territorial withdrawal or a relinquishment of positions, and not merely a routine rotation of troops where positions remain occupied. 

Resolution will rely on official statements published on the Israeli Prime Minister's Office website (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office), the IDF website (https://www.idf.il/en/), or their verified official social media accounts. Alternatively, an overwhelming consensus of major international news outlets, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) and the Associated Press (https://apnews.com), reporting an on-the-record statement by an Israeli official confirming the withdrawal will suffice for resolution. If no such announcement is made between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A primary obstacle to an Israel-Syria security agreement is the presence of Israeli troops in Syrian territory occupied after the fall of Bashar al-Assad. Syria demands a full withdrawal as a precondition for a deal, while Israel insists it will not withdraw until an agreement is finalized. An official announcement of an Israeli withdrawal would strongly signal that the core disputes have been resolved or that a finalized deal is practically guaranteed, making it a highly informative leading indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Official announcement by Israeli PM's Office, IDF, or MoD of a withdrawal (relinquishment of territorial positions, not rotation) from at least one military post in southern Syria occupied on/after December 8, 2024. Must occur between December 12, 2025 and January 11, 2026. Observable evidence: Official IDF/PMO/MoD statement indicating actual pullback from territory, not merely a troop swap. Key exclusion: 'routine rotation of troops where positions remain occupied' does NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searches performed: (1) 'Israel IDF withdrawal southern Syria 2025' Dec 12 - Jan 11; (2) 'Israel military Syria occupied territory withdrawal announcement' Dec 12 - Jan 11; (3) 'IDF 55th Reserve Brigade withdrawal southern Syria December 2025'; (4) 'Israel Syria troop rotation replacement brigade December 28 2025'; (5) 'IDF Israel territorial withdrawal Syria relinquish positions December 2025 January 2026'; (6) 'Israel Syria withdrawal official announcement IDF January 2026'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: December 28, 2025 IDF announcement that the 55th Reserve Brigade ('Spearhead' Brigade) completed its mission in southern Syria after ~100 days. REJECTED as qualifying event because: the announcement explicitly states the brigade 'will be replaced by another reserve brigade in the coming days to continue operations in southern Syria' — this is a troop rotation, not a territorial withdrawal. Candidate event 2: January 1, 2026 IDF announcement deploying the Hasmonean Brigade as a replacement in the same area, confirming positions remained occupied. REJECTED — confirms the rotation, not withdrawal. No other territorial withdrawal announcement found in the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The December 28, 2025 IDF announcement [Anadolu Ajansı](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/israel-withdraws-reserve-brigade-from-southern-syria-ahead-of-new-deployment/3783311) and [LatestLY](https://www.latestly.com/agency-news/world-news-spearhead-brigade-ends-more-than-100-days-on-combat-line-7254848.html) explicitly state the unit 'will be replaced by another reserve brigade in the coming days to continue operations in southern Syria and the Golan Heights.' The [Enab Baladi Jan 1, 2026](https://english.enabbaladi.net/archives/2026/01/israeli-army-deploys-ultra-orthodox-haredi-brigade-in-southern-syria/) confirms the Hasmonean Brigade was immediately deployed in the same area. This does NOT satisfy the resolution criteria, which explicitly excludes 'a routine rotation of troops where positions remain occupied.' Furthermore, Israeli Defense Minister Katz stated on December 23, 2025 [Anadolu Ajansı](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/israeli-defense-minister-vows-no-full-withdrawal-from-gaza-occupied-syrian-territories/3778947): 'We will not move an inch from Syria.' Syria continued to demand Israeli withdrawal throughout January 2026 talks, confirming no actual territorial relinquishment occurred.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The only possible qualifying announcement was December 28, 2025 (55th Brigade withdrawal), but this was a rotation not a territorial withdrawal. No territorial withdrawal announcement timestamp found within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying territorial withdrawal announcement was found at any point in the window. Israeli forces were actively expanding positions (constructing earthen berms, conducting daily incursions, deploying new brigades) throughout the entire December 12, 2025 – January 11, 2026 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) The December 23, 2025 statement by Defense Minister Katz explicitly ruling out withdrawal from Syria; (2) Ongoing Israeli incursions and arrests in Quneitra/Daraa throughout the window (Dec 12 to Jan 11); (3) Syria's January 5-7, 2026 negotiations demanding Israeli withdrawal, indicating Israel had not yet withdrawn; (4) Israeli forces still at 9 posts up to 15 km inside Syria as of late December 2025/early January 2026; (5) The Hasmonean Brigade deployment on Jan 1, 2026 confirming positions remained occupied. All evidence consistently confirms no territorial withdrawal announcement was made.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is NO. The only event that could superficially appear to be a withdrawal — the 55th Reserve Brigade completing its mission on December 28, 2025 — is explicitly described as a troop rotation, with positions handed over to the incoming Hasmonean Brigade. The resolution criteria explicitly excludes routine troop rotations where positions remain occupied. No official Israeli announcement of a territorial withdrawal or relinquishment of positions in southern Syria was made during the December 12, 2025 – January 11, 2026 window. In fact, the Israeli Defense Minister explicitly stated Israel would 'not move an inch from Syria' on December 23, 2025. The window closed on January 11, 2026 without a qualifying announcement.

question: Will Trump veto a bill in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump issues a presidential veto of any bill by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source will be official congressional records and a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Congress present a continuing resolution or appropriations bill to President Trump between October 31, 2025, and November 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The federal government has been in a shutdown since October 1, 2025, due to a deadlock between Republicans and Democrats over federal funding. As of late October, the Senate and House have been unable to agree on a continuing resolution (CR) or full-year appropriations bills, leaving many federal workers furloughed or unpaid. Prediction markets have suggested an 84% probability that a funding bill will not be passed until late November. If Congress can overcome the partisan gridlock and pass a funding bill, it will be presented to President Trump, providing him with a significant legislative decision: either sign it to reopen the government or veto it if he disagrees with the negotiated terms.

Sources:
Senate to reconvene on Monday amid funding stalemate as government shutdown drags on: https://abc13.com/senate-reconvene-monday-funding-stalemate-government-shutdown-drags
Congress Won't Pass A Funding Bill Until November, Majority of Polymarket Bettors Say: https://www.yahoo.com/news/congress-wont-pass-a-funding-bill-until-november
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Congress officially presents a continuing resolution (CR) or any full-year appropriations bill to President Donald Trump between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-25 (inclusive). The presentation of the bill must be officially recorded with the action 'Presented to President' on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov) during this time window. Only legislative vehicles that provide funding for the federal government (such as a continuing resolution, omnibus, minibus, or individual appropriations bill) qualify. If no such bill is presented to the President between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-25, this question resolves No. Delayed reporting on Congress.gov will be accepted as long as the official date of presentment falls within the specified window. If the website is unavailable, official White House statements (https://www.whitehouse.gov) or a consensus of credible reporting will be used as a fallback.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether President Trump will veto any bill in 2025. Given the ongoing government shutdown, a funding bill is the most consequential and contentious piece of legislation currently in play. For Trump to veto a funding bill, Congress must first successfully pass and present one to him. Tracking the presentment of a funding bill serves as an excellent crux: if Congress remains deadlocked and fails to present one by late November, the opportunity for a veto on this critical issue diminishes, thereby decreasing the likelihood of a veto occurring before December 31, 2025. Conversely, if a bill is presented, the risk of a veto increases significantly as he must choose to sign or reject it.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Congress must officially present a continuing resolution or appropriations bill to President Trump between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-25 inclusive. Observable evidence: Congress.gov 'Presented to President' action, White House signing statements, or consensus credible reporting. Key entities: H.R. 5371 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026), U.S. Congress, President Donald Trump. Timing: bill must be presented within the specified window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Congress continuing resolution appropriations bill presented President Trump November 2025' — to find any CR presented in the window; 2) 'government funding bill signed Trump November 2025' — to confirm signing within window; 3) 'H.R. 5371 presented to President Congress.gov November 2025' — to find specific bill details; 4) 'House passed continuing resolution November 13 2025 sent to president' — to confirm House action and presentment date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: H.R. 5371, the 'Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026'. Senate passed November 9/11, 2025 (60-40). House passed November 13, 2025 (222-209). Bill presented to President Trump and signed on November 13, 2025. No earlier qualifying event found within the window (prior to Oct 31, the government was in shutdown with no bill presented). This is the sole qualifying event within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: H.R. 5371 is explicitly a continuing resolution (CR) combined with three full-year appropriations bills — it qualifies under the resolution criteria as 'a continuing resolution, omnibus, minibus, or individual appropriations bill.' The House passed and sent it to Trump on November 13, 2025, and Trump signed it that same evening. This falls squarely within the Oct 31–Nov 25, 2025 window. Multiple high-quality sources confirm: [AP](https://apnews.com/4f04d5992fb5aecebfc892ed5599c468), [JD Supra](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/cr-signed-sealed-and-delivered-7495298/), [Newsmax](https://www.newsmax.com/newsfront/donald-trump-signs-funding-bill/2025/11/12/id/1234343/), [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-house-passes-funding-measure-to-end-longest-ever-government-shutdown/3742523).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: White House scheduled signing at 9:45 PM ET on November 13, 2025, per Hindustan Times and Cointelegraph. The House vote was on November 13, 2025 (bill sent to President the same day). The signing — which implies presentment — occurred November 13, 2025 at ~9:45 PM ET = 2025-11-14T02:45:00Z. The presentment itself occurred November 13, 2025 (within the window).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is the first and only qualifying event within the window. No other CR or appropriations bill was presented to the President between October 31 and November 25, 2025. The government was in shutdown from October 1, 2025 until H.R. 5371 was signed on November 13, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources consistently report the same event: H.R. 5371 passed House on November 13, 2025, was immediately sent to President Trump, and Trump signed it that same evening (November 13, 2025). Some sources mention November 12 date for the signing (JD Supra, McDermott+), possibly due to time zone differences or reporting error, but the majority of high-quality sources (AP, France 24, Euronews, India Today, The Sun) report November 13, 2025. Both dates fall within the October 31–November 25 window, so there is no material conflict on resolution. No contradictory evidence found that would suggest the bill was NOT presented within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: H.R. 5371, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act of 2026, was passed by both chambers of Congress and presented to (and signed by) President Trump on November 13, 2025. This is explicitly within the October 31–November 25, 2025 window. The bill qualifies as a continuing resolution combined with appropriations bills. Multiple high-quality, independent sources confirm the event with explicit timestamps. Resolution = Yes.

question: dogwifhat on the sphere in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if an advertisement for the cryptocurrency WIF (dogwifhat) is visibly displayed on the exterior of the Las Vegas Sphere by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will an official or credible media announcement confirm a scheduled date for the Dogwifhat (WIF) advertisement on the Las Vegas Sphere between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
In March 2024, the Dogwifhat (WIF) cryptocurrency community successfully crowdfunded over $650,000 to display their mascot—a Shiba Inu wearing a pink beanie—on the exterior of the Las Vegas Sphere. This initiative, known as 'Sphere Wif Hat', generated massive hype and was a significant catalyst for the token's early popularity. However, as of late October 2025, the advertisement has not yet materialized. A recent report highlights that this crowdfunded effort remains a key narrative for the token's community-driven momentum. Given the magnitude of the event and the public nature of the funding, it is highly probable that the organizers will announce the scheduled date of the advertisement ahead of time to maximize publicity. Monitoring for such an announcement provides a strong leading indicator of whether the advertisement will actually take place before the end of 2025.

Sources:
Brave New Coin - Best Crypto to Buy as XRP Amps Up for Rally: Ripple's Bank Integration Could Change Everything: https://bravenewcoin.com/
Decrypt - Ethereum and XRP Pump on Relief Rally, But These Coins Are Mooning Harder: Analysis: https://decrypt.co/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), an official announcement regarding the scheduled date or timeframe for the Dogwifhat (WIF) Las Vegas Sphere advertisement is published. The announcement must be made either on the official Dogwifhat X (formerly Twitter) account (https://x.com/dogwifcoin) OR reported by at least one credible cryptocurrency news outlet (such as CoinDesk at https://www.coindesk.com/, Decrypt at https://decrypt.co/, or Cointelegraph at https://cointelegraph.com/). To qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, the announcement or report must explicitly state a confirmed date or timeframe (e.g., a specific day, week, or month like 'December 2025') for the advertisement's display. Vague statements such as 'coming soon' or unconfirmed rumors without a designated timeframe will not suffice. The resolution window begins on 2025-10-31 and ends on 2025-11-30 at 11:59 PM UTC. If no qualifying announcement is made within this window, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: If the Dogwifhat community or the Las Vegas Sphere plans to display the advertisement by the end of 2025, it is highly likely they will announce the date several weeks in advance to build anticipation and capitalize on marketing momentum. An announcement by November 30 would strongly suggest the event will happen before the ultimate December 31 deadline, whereas the absence of one would significantly lower the probability of a 2025 display.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: An official announcement (from @dogwifcoin X account or credible crypto media such as CoinDesk, Decrypt, or Cointelegraph) confirming a specific scheduled date or timeframe for the Dogwifhat (WIF) advertisement on the Las Vegas Sphere, published between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive). Vague statements like 'coming soon' do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Dogwifhat WIF Las Vegas Sphere advertisement scheduled date 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30 window) — intended to find direct announcement. 2) 'dogwifcoin WIF Sphere Las Vegas announcement confirmed date' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find credible media reports. 3) 'dogwifhat WIF Sphere advertisement meme coin crypto Las Vegas display' (Oct 2025–Nov 2025) — broader search. 4) 'WIF dogwifhat Las Vegas Sphere billboard ad fundraising community' (2024–Nov 2025) — historical context and status updates. 5) 'dogwifhat Sphere Las Vegas exosphere display when update status 2025' — status of existing campaign. 6) 'dogwifhat OR dogwifcoin Sphere advertisement announcement confirmed' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — direct search for qualifying events. 7) 'WIF dogwifhat Las Vegas Sphere crowdfund community ad update news' (2024–Nov 2025) — crowdfunding updates. 8) 'dogwifhat Sphere Las Vegas crypto meme ad display scheduled confirmed 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30). 9) 'dogwifhat Sphere Las Vegas confirmed date announcement CoinDesk Decrypt Cointelegraph' (Oct 31–Nov 30).
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events were found. References to Dogwifhat's Sphere crowdfunding appeared only as historical background in articles (e.g., Brave New Coin Oct 14, 2025 mentioned 'a crowdfunded effort to place the dog-with-a-hat mascot on the Las Vegas Sphere' but provided no scheduled date). No news articles from CoinDesk, Decrypt, Cointelegraph, or any other outlet reported a confirmed scheduled date during the resolution window. No announcement from @dogwifcoin was referenced.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found that matches the resolution criteria. All Dogwifhat-related articles in the window (Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025) discuss only price action and market analysis — none mention a confirmed date or timeframe for the Las Vegas Sphere advertisement. The Las Vegas Sphere articles in the window discuss music events (Eagles, No Doubt, Zac Brown Band, Backstreet Boys) and holiday displays, with no mention of Dogwifhat.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found; no timestamp to extract.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple searches across different query formulations and date ranges consistently returned no evidence of a Dogwifhat Sphere advertisement announcement during the window. The only reference to the Sphere campaign was as historical background context (describing the fundraising effort as a past community action). No contradictory evidence exists that would suggest such an announcement was made.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying announcement confirming a scheduled date or timeframe for the Dogwifhat (WIF) Las Vegas Sphere advertisement was found within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 resolution window. The condition was never met within the window, and the window closed on November 30, 2025 without resolution as Yes.

question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the initial seasonally adjusted US unemployment rate for September 2025 be reported at 4.4% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
In September 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) lowered its benchmark federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 4.00% to 4.25%, marking the first rate cut of the year. The decision was driven largely by concerns over a cooling labor market, with the August 2025 unemployment rate having reached 4.3%—the highest level since October 2021. Fed Chair Jerome Powell described the move as a 'risk management cut' aimed at preventing further softening in employment. The FOMC's updated Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) suggested two more rate cuts could happen by the end of 2025.

Forecasting whether the Fed will follow a specific sequence of 'Cut-Pause-Pause' for the upcoming October, December, and January meetings depends heavily on labor market trajectory. If the unemployment rate continues to rise to 4.4% or higher in September, the Fed may be compelled to cut rates at both the October and December meetings, which would invalidate the 'Cut-Pause-Pause' sequence. Conversely, if the unemployment rate stabilizes or drops, the Fed might cut in October and pause in December and January as they observe the effects of previous cuts.

Sources:
BLS Employment Situation Summary: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
CNBC - Fed approves quarter-point interest rate cut and sees two more coming this year: https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/17/fed-approves-quarter-point-interest-rate-cut.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports an initial seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate (U-3) of 4.4% or higher for September 2025. The qualifying event must occur between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

The resolution will be based strictly on the headline "Unemployment rate" figure for September 2025 in the "Employment Situation" news release published by the BLS in October 2025 (typically on the first Friday of the month). The official data source for resolution is the BLS website (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm or the accompanying Table A-1 at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.t01.htm).

The headline rate reported to one decimal place will be used. If the reported figure is 4.4% or greater (e.g., 4.4%, 4.5%), the question resolves Yes. If the figure is 4.3% or lower (e.g., 4.3%, 4.2%), the question resolves No.

Only the initial release of the September 2025 data will be used; subsequent revisions to the data in later months will not affect the resolution. If the September 2025 Employment Situation report is delayed and not published by the BLS between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, this question will resolve as No.
subquestions.rationale: The Federal Reserve's recent rate cuts are highly sensitive to labor market weakness. For the Fed to execute a 'Cut-Pause-Pause' sequence, the labor market likely needs to stabilize so they feel comfortable pausing after a cut. A higher unemployment rate (4.4%+) would increase pressure for consecutive cuts in both October and December, serving as a strong early indicator that the 'Cut-Pause-Pause' sequence will fail.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: BLS must report initial seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate ≥ 4.4% for September 2025 in the Employment Situation report published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. Observable evidence: BLS 'Employment Situation' news release published at bls.gov showing ≥4.4% headline rate. Key constraint: If the report is not published within this window, the question resolves No per the stated resolution criteria.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'BLS unemployment rate September 2025 Employment Situation report' (Oct 1-31) — to find the report; 2) 'US unemployment rate October 2025 Bureau of Labor Statistics jobs report' (Oct 1-31) — alternative phrasing; 3) 'BLS Employment Situation report released September 2025 government shutdown ended' — to find if/when shutdown ended and report released; 4) 'government shutdown end October 2025 Congress spending bill passed' — to find shutdown end date; 5) 'BLS September 2025 unemployment rate released published October' (Oct 15-31) — late-window search; 6) 'employment situation September 2025 BLS released October 31' (Oct 25-31) — final window search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No qualifying event (BLS publication of September 2025 Employment Situation report) was found within the October 1-31, 2025 window. The government shutdown began October 1, 2025, causing the BLS to furlough staff and suspend all operations. The scheduled October 3/4 release was missed. The BLS did recall workers to release September CPI data (published October 24, 2025) for Social Security COLA purposes, but explicitly stated 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services.' Multiple sources through October 30, 2025 confirm the September employment report had not been released and the shutdown was still ongoing (day ~29).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires the BLS to publish the Employment Situation report between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. Multiple sources confirm this did NOT occur: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/03/shutdown-jobs-report-economy.html) — 'The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) did not release its monthly jobs report in October 2025 due to a federal government shutdown'; [altoonamirror.com](https://www.altoonamirror.com/news/local-news/2025/10/govt-shutdown-pa-jobless-data-limbo/) — 'The BLS website had not been updated since October 1, and the agency was not maintaining its operations during the shutdown' (as of Oct 21); [Investing.com UK](https://uk.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-to-release-september-inflation-data-despite-shutdown-93CH-4300183) — BLS explicitly stated 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services' besides the CPI; [bakercityherald.com](https://bakercityherald.com/2025/10/23/missing-federal-jobs-report-leaves-oregon-employment-department-businesses-in-the-dark/) — 'The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) failed to release the September 2025 jobs report due to the ongoing government shutdown'; [InsuranceNewsNet](https://insurancenewsnet.com/oarticle/federal-reserve-cuts-rates-for-second-time-as-shutdown-stalls-key-data) — as of October 30, the Federal Reserve was still acting 'without timely data' as 'The labor market [data] has slowed significantly' but 'BLS...has not released new employment data due to furloughed staff'.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for BLS September 2025 Employment Situation report publication can be extracted within the October 1-31 window, because the report was not published. The shutdown began 2025-10-01T04:01:00Z (12:01 AM Eastern). The report's scheduled release date of October 3, 2025 was missed. question: Will the Bank of Canada announce a 25 bps decrease at the March meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the target for the overnight rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Bank of Canada's March 2026 meeting.

The resolution source for this market is information released by the Bank of Canada after its March 18, 2026 policy meeting, as listed on the official Bank of Canada calendar: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/core-functions/monetary-policy/key-interest-rate/#target-dates

subquestions.question: Will Statistics Canada report a seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate of 7.2% or higher for December 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Bank of Canada's monetary policy is closely tied to the health of the labor market. In recent months, the BoC has shifted its focus from inflation to employment, with analysts noting that 'Inflation control is no longer the binding constraint; employment is' (Mortgage Professional America Magazine, https://www.mpamag.com). The Canadian economy experienced significant job losses in mid-2025, pushing the unemployment rate to 7.1% by September (CBC News, https://www.cbc.ca). A continued rise in the unemployment rate in December 2025 would provide strong evidence of ongoing labor market weakness, increasing the likelihood that the BoC will announce a 25 basis point decrease at its March 2026 meeting to support the economy.

Sources:
Mortgage Professional America Magazine - https://www.mpamag.com
CBC News - https://www.cbc.ca
Statistics Canada The Daily - https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/

The official resolution source is the Statistics Canada 'Labour Force Survey' publication for December 2025, published in The Daily (https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/). If the initially reported headline seasonally adjusted unemployment rate is 7.2% or greater, the market resolves Yes. If the reported rate is 7.1% or lower, it resolves No. 

If Statistics Canada does not release the December 2025 Labour Force Survey data between 2025-12-24 and 2026-01-23 (inclusive), this question will be considered unresolvable. Revisions to the data made in subsequent months' releases will not affect the resolution; only the initial reported figure for December 2025 applies.
subquestions.rationale: The Bank of Canada's recent deliberations highlight a shift from focusing strictly on inflation to managing economic weakness and a soft labor market. With the unemployment rate already hitting 7.1% in the latter half of 2025, further job market deterioration is a critical crux for forecasters. An unemployment rate of 7.2% or higher in December 2025 would provide concrete evidence of accelerating economic weakness, directly increasing the probability of a 25 bps rate cut at the BoC's March 2026 meeting.

Experts note that this discrepancy is driven by high immigration and adjustments to U.S. Census population estimates, which significantly increased the total population of women of childbearing age (the denominator in the fertility rate calculation). Therefore, the size of this demographic group is a critical crux. If the population of women of childbearing age continues to grow rapidly, it applies strong downward pressure on the fertility rate, making a rate increase mathematically less likely. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) tracks a closely related demographic, the civilian noninstitutional population of women aged 16 to 44 (Series ID: LNU00000026). The August 2025 estimate for this group will be released on September 5, 2025, in the monthly Employment Situation report. question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publish the September 2025 Employment Situation report between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?

As of October 1, 2025, the U.S. federal government faces a shutdown that threatens the release of key economic data, including the September 2025 Employment Situation report (jobs report) originally scheduled for October 3, 2025. The Department of Labor's contingency plan states that the BLS will suspend operations and data collection during a funding lapse. While the ultimate question explicitly states that temporary delays due to government shutdowns do not constitute 'cessation', a prolonged shutdown or structural defunding that extends through the entire month of October would push the BLS perilously close to the ultimate question's threshold of missing three consecutive scheduled releases by over 30 days. Whether the BLS manages to release this critical September report by the end of October serves as a highly informative early indicator of the severity of the agency's operational crisis.

Sources:
- BLS Release Schedule: https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm
- BLS Employment Situation News Releases: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
- DOL Budget & Contingency Plans: https://www.dol.gov/general/budget
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The official source for resolving this question is the Bureau of Labor Statistics website, specifically the Employment Situation releases page (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.toc.htm) or the BLS release calendar (https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm).

To qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, the publication must be the primary, full national employment report containing September 2025 nonfarm payrolls and the national unemployment rate. Publishing only preliminary data, partial estimates, or notices of delay does not qualify.

If the BLS website is offline due to a government shutdown, but the official September 2025 Employment Situation data is distributed by the BLS, the Department of Labor (https://www.dol.gov), or the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov) via alternative official channels within the resolution window, it will count as a 'Yes'.

If the September 2025 Employment Situation report is not published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 at 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks if the BLS will permanently cease regular publication of major reports, stipulating that missing three consecutive scheduled releases by more than 30 days counts as cessation. The September jobs report is scheduled for October 3, 2025. A failure to publish this report by October 31 (a 28-day delay) would be a severe early indicator of systemic dysfunction, an extended government shutdown, or drastic workforce cuts. A 'No' resolution on this subquestion strongly updates the probability of a 'Yes' on the ultimate question, as the agency would be on the brink of triggering the 30-day delay threshold for the first of three consecutive reports. Conversely, a 'Yes' resolution demonstrates agency resilience and its ability to resume operations, supporting a 'No' on the ultimate question.

evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. The government shutdown that began October 1, 2025 prevented the BLS from publishing the September 2025 Employment Situation report throughout the entire month. subquestions.question: Will the President of the Brazilian Federal Senate officially accept and read an impeachment request against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes in the plenary by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Recently, the U.S. government imposed sanctions on Moraes, further fueling the push for his removal [3]. Despite over 30 impeachment requests having been filed, the President of the Federal Senate has previously declined to advance them [1, 2]. However, mass protests are planned for September 7, 2025, to explicitly demand his impeachment, which could increase political pressure on the Senate leadership [2]. In Brazil, the impeachment of a Supreme Court Minister begins in the Federal Senate. The President of the Senate has the sole authority to accept an impeachment petition. Once accepted, it is formally read in the plenary, which initiates the process before it goes to a special committee. Tracking whether the Senate President accepts and reads a petition is a direct and necessary precursor to any floor vote on proceeding with an impeachment.

Sources:
[1] Breitbart: https://www.breitbart.com/
[2] NZ Herald: https://www.nzherald.co.nz/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The reading must be a formal step to initiate the impeachment procedure according to Senate rules (leitura do pedido de impeachment) and must be recorded in the official journal of the Senate (Diário do Senado Federal) or officially announced via the official Senate news portal (Agência Senado). 

If such a reading takes place within the specified timeframe, the question resolves Yes, regardless of whether a special committee is subsequently formed or if the ultimate impeachment vote succeeds or fails.

If no such reading takes place between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30, the question resolves No. If Alexandre de Moraes resigns or otherwise leaves his post before any request is read, this question will resolve No.

The primary data sources will be the official records of the Federal Senate of Brazil (https://www25.senado.leg.br/web/senado/diarios) and Agência Senado (https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias). A consensus of credible media reporting (e.g., Reuters, Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo) may also be used to confirm the event.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the Senate will vote to proceed with the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes by the end of 2025. With mass protests demanding his impeachment scheduled for September 7, 2025, observing whether the Senate leadership yields to this pressure and officially initiates the process in September will be a highly informative indicator for the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The President of the Brazilian Federal Senate (or acting President) must officially accept and formally read (or order reading of) an impeachment request against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes in the Senate plenary between September 1-30, 2025, as a formal step to initiate the impeachment procedure (leitura do pedido de impeachment), recorded in the Diário do Senado Federal or officially announced via Agência Senado. NO article from September 2025 reports a formal reading of an impeachment request against Moraes in the Senate plenary. question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States military initiate a drone, missile, or air strike that impacts the territory of Yemen between January 13, 2026, and February 12, 2026?

The primary resolution sources will be the US Central Command press releases (https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/) and credible major news reporting (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/, AP News: https://apnews.com/). Because the ultimate question resolves affirmatively if the US strikes three countries, a strike on Yemen (a highly probable target given ongoing Red Sea security operations) would serve as the decisive third country. Confirming a strike on Yemen within this one-month window would confidently update forecasters' probabilities on the ultimate question towards 100%.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: US military forces initiated a drone, missile, or air strike that impacted Yemeni ground territory between January 13, 2026 and February 12, 2026 (inclusive). Observable evidence: Official US government statements (DoD/CENTCOM) OR consensus of credible major news reporting confirming such a strike. evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'US military strike Yemen 2026' (Jan 13–Feb 12, 2026) — to find direct evidence of US strikes. However: (1) New America (Feb 13, 2026) explicitly states the US government has not officially confirmed any drone strikes against AQAP in Yemen since 2020, while acknowledging local Yemeni media and 'a few non-Yemeni news outlets' have reported multiple US airstrikes against AQAP throughout 2025 and into 2026. This meets the location (Yemen ground territory) and weapon type (drone) requirements. However: (1) No official CENTCOM confirmation found. The resolution criteria asks for 'a consensus of credible reporting' — a single outlet report may be insufficient.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Antiwar.com article published January 29, 2026. The article does not specify the exact date the strike occurred, only that it happened in eastern Yemen. The publication date suggests the strike likely occurred on or before January 29, 2026. No exact timestamp for the strike itself is available.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The January 29, 2026 Antiwar.com report is the only specific US strike on Yemen within the window found. CFR's guide mentions Operation Rough Rider ended in May 2025. No earlier qualifying event within the January 13–February 12, 2026 window was found with explicit evidence.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: New America (Feb 13, 2026) explicitly states the US government has NOT officially confirmed any AQAP drone strikes in Yemen since 2020, though it acknowledges reports exist in 2025-2026. This directly contradicts the possibility of official confirmation. However, New America does NOT deny that strikes occurred — it questions official transparency. Alternative interpretation: The strikes reported by Antiwar.com could be part of a covert campaign that is not officially acknowledged. The resolution criteria requires either official confirmation OR consensus of credible reporting — Antiwar.com alone may not constitute 'consensus.' Major outlets (Reuters, AP) did not confirm the specific strike within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is ambiguous. One credible outlet (Antiwar.com) reports a US drone strike in Yemen on approximately January 29, 2026, within the window. However: (1) No official CENTCOM confirmation exists. (2) New America explicitly states the US has not officially confirmed such strikes since 2020. (3) No 'consensus' of major credible news sources (Reuters, AP) confirms the specific strike. The resolution criteria requires 'official US government statements OR a consensus of credible reporting.' Neither threshold is clearly met. Given the instruction to prefer precision over recall and return resolvable=false if evidence is indirect or does not exactly match criteria, and given that the New America analysis explicitly flags the lack of official confirmation and the Antiwar.com report lacks corroboration from major outlets named in the criteria (Reuters, AP), this question cannot be definitively resolved as Yes. However, the Antiwar.com report is direct and explicit about a US drone strike occurring in Yemen within the window. This creates a genuine conflict: one credible source confirms the strike; the resolution's primary sources (CENTCOM, Reuters, AP) do not. Applying the strict rule — 'resolvable=false if evidence is indirect, inferred, or does not exactly match the criteria' — and noting that the resolution specifically names Reuters and AP as primary credible sources while neither confirmed this specific strike, I find this resolvable=false due to ambiguous evidence that does not clearly satisfy the stated resolution criteria.

Because Trump's core motivation for altering the Fed Board's composition is to force faster and deeper interest rate cuts, the Fed's actions at the September FOMC meeting serve as a crucial crux. If the Fed capitulates or independently agrees with the need for a deep cut (50 basis points or more), Trump may view his pressure campaign as successful and back off from attempting to fire another governor by his October 31 deadline. Conversely, if the Fed only cuts by 25 basis points or holds rates steady, Trump is highly likely to continue his aggressive overhaul and target another governor, such as Chair Jerome Powell.

Tracking whether the U.S. announces trade talks with Canada by November 30 provides a strong, early signal of whether a tariff reduction or pause is realistically on the table for December 31.

JD Vance recently lambasted a proposed annexation bill as an 'insult'. Netanyahu is caught between appeasing the Trump administration and satisfying his far-right coalition. If Netanyahu allows the Knesset to hold a plenum vote on the annexation bill, it would directly defy Trump. Given Trump's history of publicly attacking allies who defy him or undermine his deals, a Knesset vote on this issue is a strong crux that would highly increase the probability of Trump disparaging Netanyahu by December 31.

evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The only qualifying plenum vote on annexation/sovereignty bills was October 22, 2025 (outside the window). No timestamp could be extracted for a qualifying event within the October 25-November 24 window, because no such event appears to have occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The most recent qualifying event found was October 22, 2025 (outside the window). No qualifying event within the window was identified, so the first-occurrence check is moot for Yes resolution.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification attempts to disprove No conclusion: (1) Checked whether the November 16 article's reference to 'the first reading has already been completed' might imply a first reading occurred within the window — but the article context clearly refers to the October 22 preliminary reading as having completed the first stage, with the bills still stuck in committee. (2) Checked whether the death penalty bill votes (Nov 10-11) might qualify — but these bills concern criminal sentencing for terrorists, not application of Israeli sovereignty or civilian law to West Bank territory; they apply military court procedures, which is the opposite of applying Israeli civilian law to the West Bank. (3) Checked for any other sovereignty/annexation bills introduced — no evidence of new bills or votes found. (4) Netanyahu's office explicitly instructed coalition members to suspend bills' advancement (TASS/Zakharova, Oct 30). (5) As of Nov 23, ministers were still 'protesting outside cabinet meeting demanding annexation,' indicating no legislative action had occurred. (6) No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly establishes that: (1) The qualifying preliminary reading votes on West Bank sovereignty/annexation bills occurred on October 22, 2025 — three days BEFORE the window opens on October 25, 2025. (2) After those preliminary readings, the bills were referred to the Knesset Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, which was chaired by Boaz Bismuth (Likud). Netanyahu's office instructed coalition members to suspend the bills' advancement. (3) Throughout the October 25 - November 24, 2025 window, the bills remained stuck in committee, unscheduled for further debate, with MK Maoz explicitly accusing the government of blocking the bill from reaching its first (post-preliminary) reading in the Knesset plenum. (4) No evidence of any plenum vote on a West Bank sovereignty/annexation bill within the window was found from multiple credible sources. The question resolves No, with the window closing on November 24, 2025 without a qualifying event.
