question: Will Elon and DOGE cut 100-150k employees in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve based on the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) under the "All Employees, Federal" series (CES9091000001), displayed here (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001)

This market will resolve according to the decrease in the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees between the December 2024 report and the December 2025 report.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The difference will be calculated as the December 2024 value minus the December 2025 value.

The December 2024 figure will be based on the initial December 2024 BLS Employment Situation report scheduled for release on January 3, 2025, and the initial December 2025 figure will be based on the report scheduled for release on January 9, 2026. Revisions made to these figures will not be considered, only the values reported in the initial reports will be used.

The resolution source will be the BLS Employment Situation data, specifically the series CES9091000001, available at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 or the official BLS website.

subquestions.question: Will the BLS report a month-over-month decrease of at least 15,000 seasonally adjusted federal employees for November 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question seeks to determine if a total of 100,000 to 150,000 federal employee jobs will be cut in 2025 under the leadership of Elon Musk and the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). Achieving this annual target requires an average reduction of roughly 8,300 to 12,500 jobs per month. Recently, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) canceled the October 2025 jobs report due to incomplete data collection amidst a government shutdown, and the November 2025 report has been rescheduled to December 16, 2025. However, alternative employment data providers have already observed sharp public sector job losses; Revelio Labs reported a net reduction of 22,200 government employees in October 2025 alone. When the BLS releases its delayed November data, the month-over-month rate of job cuts will be a highly informative indicator. A reduction of 15,000 or more in a single month would demonstrate that DOGE is executing cuts at an aggressive pace that makes reaching the 100k-150k target highly probable. Sources: 
BLS Employment Situation: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm 
FRED Federal Employees Data: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 
TalkMarkets October Nonfarm Employment: https://talkmarkets.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports a month-over-month decrease of 15,000 or more in the seasonally adjusted 'All Employees, Federal' series (CES9091000001) for November 2025. 

The resolution window is between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30 (inclusive). Qualifying data must be published in a BLS Employment Situation report within this timeframe. 

The change will be calculated by subtracting the preliminary November 2025 figure from the October 2025 figure, exactly as reported in the same BLS release (expected December 16, 2025). If the difference (October value - November value) is 15,000 or greater, it resolves Yes. 

Fallback for missing October data: If the BLS does not publish an October 2025 figure due to the canceled October report, the average monthly decrease from the last reported month will be used to resolve the market. For example, ((September 2025 value - November 2025 value) / 2). If this average monthly decrease is 15,000 or greater, the question resolves Yes. 

If the decrease is less than 15,000, or if employment increases, it resolves No. 
If the BLS does not release a November 2025 figure for this series between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30, the question resolves as Unresolvable. 

The official resolution sources are the BLS Employment Situation release (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm) and the FRED database (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001).
subquestions.rationale: Rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, this subquestion focuses on the velocity of job cuts (month-over-month change). A decrease of 15,000 jobs in November signals that the ongoing workforce reductions are exceeding the average monthly pace needed to hit the 100k-150k annual target, providing a strong near-term signal of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: YES requires: BLS reports month-over-month decrease ≥15,000 in seasonally adjusted 'All Employees, Federal' (CES9091000001) for November 2025, published between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30. Calculation: October 2025 value − November 2025 value ≥ 15,000. Key fallback: if October not published, use (September − November)/2 ≥ 15,000.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'BLS Employment Situation November 2025 federal employees' — to find the December 2025 jobs report. Query 2: 'BLS jobs report December 2025 federal government employment decrease' — to find federal employment change figures. Query 3: 'CES9091000001 federal employees seasonally adjusted November 2025' — to find exact series data. Query 4: 'federal government employment October November 2025 BLS 6000 decrease payroll' — to verify specific figures.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: BLS released November 2025 Employment Situation on December 16, 2025, within the resolution window. Multiple sources (CalculatedRisk, The Center Square, PYMNTS, Daily Caller, Business Times, NBC News) all confirm federal government employment decreased by 6,000 in November 2025 (month-over-month from October). October data WAS published in the same report (federal payrolls fell 162,000 in October). No earlier qualifying occurrence found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The BLS report released December 16, 2025 showed: (1) October 2025 federal employment data was published (fell 162,000 from September), so the fallback formula does not apply. (2) November 2025 federal employment decreased by 6,000 from October. Thus: October value − November value = +6,000, which is less than the 15,000 threshold. Sources: [CalculatedRisk](http://www.calculatedriskblog.com/2025/12/november-employment-report-64-thousand.html) 'federal payrolls dropped by 6,000'; [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/personnel/2025/federal-government-employment-dropped-in-october-as-doge-cuts-took-effect/) 'Federal government employment dropped by 162,000 in October and 6,000 in November'; [Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2025/12/16/trump-federal-workforce-cuts-jobs/) 'federal government employment declined by 6,000 in November 2025, following a 162,000 drop in October.' ALL sources unanimously confirm a 6,000 November decrease.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: BLS Employment Situation report released on December 16, 2025. Exact timestamp: 2025-12-16T00:00:00Z (multiple sources confirm December 16, 2025 publication date). The No outcome became definitive at this point.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence. The November 2025 BLS data was only released once, on December 16, 2025, which is the first and only occurrence within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources consistently report the same figure: federal government employment decreased by 6,000 in November 2025 (month-over-month). No source reports a figure at or above 15,000 for November. The October figure of −162,000 refers to October vs. September, not October vs. November. The November month-over-month figure of 6,000 is far below the 15,000 threshold. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BLS released the November 2025 Employment Situation on December 16, 2025 (within the resolution window). The report showed federal government employment decreased by 6,000 in November 2025 (October value − November value = 6,000), which is less than the required 15,000 threshold. The question definitively resolves No as of December 16, 2025.

question: Pakistan strike on India by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will a militant or terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir result in the deaths of at least 5 Indian security personnel or civilians between October 15, 2025 and November 14, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

This conflict, marked by India's 'Operation Sindoor' and Pakistan's 'Operation Bunyan Ul Marsoos', was precipitated by the April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam, which killed 26 civilians. India's retaliatory kinetic actions against terror infrastructure and Pakistani military installations prompted Pakistan to launch its own guided rockets and drones at Indian cities and military sites. Because major militant attacks in Jammu and Kashmir have historically triggered escalatory cycles of cross-border military strikes between the two nuclear-armed neighbors, monitoring the region for mass-casualty terror events provides a critical early warning indicator for potential Pakistani strikes on India. A highly lethal attack would likely force Indian retaliation, significantly raising the probability of a subsequent Pakistani counter-strike.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The resolution will be based on official statements or press releases from the Jammu and Kashmir Police (https://jkpolice.gov.in/), the Indian Ministry of Home Affairs (https://mha.gov.in/), or a consensus of credible reporting from major Indian news outlets such as NDTV (https://www.ndtv.com/), India Today (https://www.indiatoday.in/), or The Hindu (https://www.thehindu.com/). subquestions.rationale: The recent May 2025 missile and drone exchanges between India and Pakistan were directly triggered by the deadly April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam. Because significant terrorist attacks in J&K are the primary catalyst for Indian cross-border retaliatory strikes (which then trigger Pakistani military responses), tracking mass-casualty terror events acts as a robust early indicator for whether the escalation ladder will be climbed again prior to December 31.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: A militant/terrorist attack (or coordinated series) in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir between Oct 15 and Nov 14, 2025, resulting in deaths of at least 5 Indian civilians and/or Indian security forces. Deaths of militants themselves do not count. The attack must physically occur in J&K. Evidence required: credible reporting of such an attack with 5+ qualifying deaths.

'Kashmir terror attack 5 dead killed November 2025' - to find any qualifying event. 7. 'Kishtwar Kupwara Udhampur encounter soldiers killed November 2025' - to check specific encounters. 8. 'Jammu Kashmir attack killed November 1-14 2025' - to find any qualifying events in Nov portion. 9. 'Kishtwar encounter outcome killed result November 2025' - to find outcomes of specific encounters.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events examined: (1) Oct 20, 2025 - IED found and neutralized in Shopian - NO deaths, not qualifying. (2) Oct 16 - Udhampur: terror suspects threatened/robbed a villager - no deaths, not qualifying. (3) Nov 5, 2025 - Kishtwar Chhatru encounter: one jawan injured, no deaths reported - not qualifying. (4) Nov 7-8, 2025 - Kupwara Operation Pimple: 2 terrorists killed (not qualifying), no Indian security force deaths. (5) Nov 10, 2025 - Delhi Red Fort blast: 8-13 civilians killed BUT in New Delhi, NOT in J&K - does not satisfy location criteria. All other events referenced were either before the window (Oct 13-14 Kupwara), outside J&K (Delhi blast), or resulted only in militant deaths.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that satisfies ALL criteria simultaneously: (a) occurred in J&K UT, (b) within Oct 15 - Nov 14, 2025, (c) killed 5+ Indian civilians or security personnel. The kashmirdotcom.in report [https://kashmirdotcom.in/2025/11/01/jk-sees-most-peaceful-october-in-25-years-says-report/] explicitly states 'no civilian or security force casualties reported during the month' of October. For November 1-14: the Kishtwar encounter (Nov 5) resulted in only one injury; the Kupwara encounter (Nov 7-8) killed only 2 militants; the Delhi blast (Nov 10) occurred outside J&K. No qualifying attack found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying event was found within the window in J&K.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found anywhere in the window. Multiple searches confirm absence of any attack in J&K killing 5+ Indian security forces or civilians between Oct 15 and Nov 14, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: The conclusion is strongly supported by: (1) Explicit report of 'no civilian or security force casualties in J&K in October 2025' from kashmirdotcom.in (Nov 1). subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs favorably report or advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633 or a Senate companion bill) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R. 3633) is a proposed comprehensive regulatory framework for digital assets. It successfully passed the U.S. House of Representatives on July 17, 2025, with a bipartisan 294-134 vote. For the bill to become law in 2025, it must navigate the U.S. Senate, which involves passing through the relevant committees before a floor vote. In August 2025, Senator Cynthia Lummis stated that the legislative goal is to move the bill through the Senate Banking Committee in September, followed by the Senate Agriculture Committee in October, aiming to reach the President's desk by the end of the year. Tracking the Senate Banking Committee's action during September provides a critical early indicator of the legislation's momentum and its real chances of meeting the year-end deadline.

Sources:
Congress.gov H.R.3633 - https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633
CryptoNews - https://cryptonews.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs officially advances, favorably reports, or 'orders to be reported' the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R. 3633) or a formally designated Senate companion bill. The primary resolution source will be the official legislative action tracker on Congress.gov for H.R. 3633 (https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633/all-actions) or its direct Senate equivalent. A qualifying event must be recorded in the official actions list indicating that the committee has approved or ordered the measure reported out of committee. If no such action occurs by 11:59 PM ET on 2025-10-01, the question resolves 'No'. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: For the CLARITY Act to be signed into law by the end of 2025, it must swiftly advance through the Senate. Proponents of the bill have explicitly outlined a timeline that requires the Senate Banking Committee to advance the legislation in September. If this specific milestone is missed or delayed, the likelihood of completing all remaining legislative steps—including the Senate Agriculture Committee, a full Senate vote, and reconciliation with the House—before year-end drops substantially, making this an ideal crux for forecasting the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs to officially advance, favorably report, or 'order to be reported' the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R. 3633) or a formally designated Senate companion bill between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). This requires an official committee markup/vote resulting in favorable reporting, not merely discussion drafts, hearings, or expressions of intent.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Digital Asset Market Clarity Act H.R. 3633 Senate Banking Committee 2025' - to find any committee actions on the House bill or its Senate companion; 2. 'Senate Banking Committee crypto digital asset legislation vote 2025' - to find any formal committee votes; 3. 'Senate Banking Committee vote markup crypto Responsible Financial Innovation Act September 30 October 2025' - to find if the markup occurred near the deadline; 4. 'Digital Asset Market Clarity Act H.R. 3633 Senate referred committee action September 2025' - to find referral/action status; 5. 'Senate Banking Committee markup postponed delayed October crypto bill 2025' - to find if the markup was postponed beyond the window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key findings: (1) H.R. 3633 was referred to the Senate Banking Committee on September 18, 2025. (2) The Senate Banking Committee released a 182-page discussion draft of the Responsible Financial Innovation Act of 2025 (a Senate alternative, not a formal companion to H.R. 3633) on September 5, 2025. (3) Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott initially set September 30 as a deadline for markup. (4) Multiple sources from September 22-29 explicitly state the markup was delayed/postponed to 'the week of October 20' or 'late October.' (5) CoinDesk (September 30) explicitly stated 'The Senate Banking Committee postponed a markup on market structure draft legislation to October.' (6) CoinTelegraph (September 29) stated the bill 'had been scheduled for committee consideration in late September but has already been pushed to October.' No source reports that the committee formally voted to advance any bill within the September 1–October 1 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence was found of the Senate Banking Committee officially advancing, favorably reporting, or 'ordering to be reported' H.R. 3633 or any formally designated Senate companion bill within the resolution window. The committee released a discussion draft (September 5) and held a roundtable (September 17), but these are not qualifying actions. The markup/vote that was planned for September 30 was explicitly postponed to late October per multiple sources including [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/09/30/bitcoin-steady-but-bitfinex-warns-of-downside-risks-as-government-shutdown-looms), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/owentedford/2025/09/22/passing-market-structure-legislation-is-no-sure-bet-for-congress-this-year), and [Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-government-shutdown-digital-asset-market-structure). The referral of H.R. 3633 to the Senate Banking Committee on September 18 is not a committee vote to report the bill.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp could be extracted for a qualifying event because no qualifying event (committee vote/markup ordering the bill reported) occurred within the window. The closest relevant action — the planned September 30 markup — was explicitly postponed to the week of October 20.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at any point within the September 1–October 1 window. The committee only released discussion drafts, held roundtables, and referred the House bill — none of these are qualifying actions under the resolution criteria.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: One article from The Bit Gazette (September 10) states 'Senate Republicans have advanced a major digital-asset bill in 2025' — but context makes clear this refers to the process of drafting/releasing an updated bill, not a formal committee vote to report. Multiple authoritative sources (CoinDesk, Forbes, Cointelegraph, cryptonews.com) uniformly confirm the committee markup was postponed beyond September 30. No source reports a successful committee vote ordering the bill reported during the window. The September 30 government shutdown concerns further confirm no markup occurred on that date.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is clear and consistent: the Senate Banking Committee did NOT hold a markup or formally advance/report the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633) or any formally designated Senate companion bill between September 1 and October 1, 2025. The planned September 30 markup was explicitly postponed to late October (week of October 20). The question resolves No, with the resolution datetime set to 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z (end of the window with no qualifying event).

subquestions.question: Will major news organizations report that federal prosecutors have presented evidence regarding John Bolton to a federal grand jury between October 1 and October 14, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Federal felony indictments require a grand jury to review evidence and vote to charge a defendant. In late September 2025, reports indicated that senior Justice Department leaders were pressuring prosecutors to bring swift charges against former National Security Adviser John Bolton over the alleged mishandling of classified information. According to a Reuters report syndicated on September 26, 2025, sources indicated that prosecutors were expected to present the case to a grand jury 'next week' (i.e., the first week of October 2025) despite some internal resistance from prosecutors who felt more investigation was necessary. The investigation centers around an August 2025 FBI raid of Bolton's home and office, which reportedly uncovered classified materials. Because an indictment requires grand jury approval, a report confirming that prosecutors are presenting evidence to a grand jury is a direct and necessary precursor to any formal charges being filed against Bolton before the end of October.

Sources:
KSL (Reuters syndication): https://www.ksl.com/
Devdiscourse: https://www.devdiscourse.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

- Reuters (https://www.reuters.com)
- The Associated Press (https://apnews.com)
- The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com)
- The Washington Post (https://www.washingtonpost.com)
- CNN (https://www.cnn.com)
- Fox News (https://www.foxnews.com)

The reporting must explicitly mention the active involvement of a federal grand jury in relation to the John Bolton classified documents probe, confirming that evidence or testimony has been or is being presented. Opinion pieces, editorials, and speculative commentary do not count; it must be presented as a factual news report citing sources or official statements. If no such qualifying report is published by the specified outlets within the resolution window (before 11:59 PM ET on 2025-10-14), the question will resolve 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: For the U.S. federal government to formally charge or indict Bolton by October 31, 2025, prosecutors must secure an indictment from a federal grand jury. Given the intense media scrutiny and leaks surrounding the DOJ's activities regarding Trump-era officials, grand jury activity is highly likely to be reported by major news outlets. If a grand jury receives evidence by October 14, a 'Yes' resolution would drastically increase the probability of an indictment by October 31. If no such action is reported by the end of the subquestion window, it suggests the internal DOJ resistance has delayed the process, lowering the likelihood of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: At least one of Reuters, AP, NYT, WaPo, CNN, or Fox News must publish a factual news report between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-14 stating that federal prosecutors have presented evidence, called witnesses, or convened a federal grand jury to review the criminal case against John Bolton. The reporting must explicitly mention active grand jury involvement (not speculation or opinion).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'John Bolton federal grand jury prosecutors evidence' [Oct 1-14] — found multiple articles about grand jury reviewing evidence; 2) 'John Bolton classified documents probe criminal investigation 2025' [Oct 1-14] — confirmed investigation details; 3) 'Bolton indictment CNN Fox News Washington Post October 2025' [Oct 1-14] — found Fox News article dated Oct 14 and CNN reporting via LocalNews8; 4) 'CNN Bolton prosecutors grand jury Maryland meeting October 11 2025' [Oct 10-14] — confirmed CNN reported on Oct 11 meeting; 5) 'Washington Post Bolton classified documents grand jury' [Oct 1-14] — found Gateway Pundit referencing WaPo

The CNN reporting via LocalNews8 (URL slug: cnn-us-politics) and UPI (citing CNN) explicitly confirms CNN reported on Oct 11 about the grand jury and prosecutors' meeting.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: CNN (qualifying outlet) reported on October 11, 2025 that: (1) federal prosecutors met that day to consider potential charges; (2) 'Federal prosecutors are now considering a federal grand jury indictment'; (3) the investigation involved a grand jury process. The LocalNews8 article (localnews8.com/politics/cnn-us-politics/2025/10/11/federal-prosecutors-meeting-this-weekend-to-finalize-potential-bolton-indictment/) with the CNN US Politics URL slug confirms CNN's own original reporting on Oct 11. subquestions.question: Will SpaceX fully stack the Starship Flight 12 vehicle (Ship on Super Heavy) at a launch pad between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-15?
subquestions.background_information:
SpaceX successfully launched Starship Flight 11 on October 13, 2025 (https://www.spacex.com/launches/). With a stated goal by CEO Elon Musk to increase the launch cadence to one flight every 3-4 weeks, Flight 12 is expected to follow shortly. Before any Starship test flight, the upper stage (Starship) must be lifted and placed on top of the Super Heavy booster at an orbital launch mount (a process known as "stacking"). This allows the company to perform fully integrated testing, such as a Wet Dress Rehearsal (WDR), which is required before a launch license can be utilized and the vehicle can be cleared for flight. Tracking when the vehicle is fully stacked is a crucial early indicator of the launch timeline. If the vehicle is stacked by mid-November, a launch by November 30 is highly plausible. If it is not, the timeline makes a November launch very difficult.

Sources:

question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $70 by end of June?

For CME Crude Oil (CL) futures contracts, the active month is the nearest of the contract months listed. The active month becomes a non-active month effective two business days prior to the spot month expiration. For example; if the spot month expires on a Friday the next listed contract will be considered the Active Month on the Wednesday prior to the spot month expiration.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Crude Oil (CL) futures.

question: David Baszucki out as Roblox CEO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if David Baszucki ceases to be CEO of Roblox for any length of time between August 14, and December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of David Baszucki's resignation/firing before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/firing goes into effect.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from Roblox and/or David Baszucki, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a major brand or publicly traded company publicly suspend or terminate its partnership or advertising with Roblox over safety concerns between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Roblox Corporation is currently embroiled in a significant public relations crisis regarding child safety on its platform. CEO David Baszucki is facing intense backlash, including a viral petition with over 250,000 signatures demanding his resignation and a lawsuit from the Louisiana Attorney General alleging the platform fails to protect minors. Historically, executive turnover during tech and social media scandals is often accelerated when controversies threaten core revenue streams—most notably through advertiser boycotts (as seen in past crises on platforms like YouTube and X/Twitter). Roblox partners with numerous major brands (e.g., Nike, Walmart, Gucci) to create in-game branded "experiences." If the ongoing scandal causes these corporate partners to withdraw, the financial and reputational damage would severely increase pressure on the Roblox Board of Directors to replace Baszucki.

Sources:
MediaPost: https://www.mediapost.com/
The Times of India: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/
Gameranx: https://gameranx.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), at least one publicly traded company or a company listed on the most recent Fortune 500 or Fortune Global 500 list publicly announces that it is pausing, suspending, or terminating its advertising spend, branded experiences, or formal partnership with Roblox Corporation.

To qualify for a Yes resolution:
1. The stated or widely reported reason for the suspension/termination must explicitly relate to child safety, content moderation, or the ongoing controversies surrounding Roblox's environment for minors.
2. The action must be confirmed via an official statement/press release from the brand OR verified reporting from at least two of the following credible news organizations: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com), CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com), The Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com), or The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com).

If the suspension or termination occurs but the company attributes it solely to routine business decisions (e.g., campaign end dates) without mentioning safety or platform controversies, it does not count.
If no qualifying event is confirmed to have occurred between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Brand safety is a paramount concern for major corporations. If the child safety scandal escalates to the point where Roblox loses high-profile corporate partners, the direct threat to the company's monetization and public image would serve as a strong catalyst for the Board of Directors to demand new leadership. Thus, an advertiser pullout is a highly informative early indicator of David Baszucki's potential ouster.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A publicly traded or Fortune 500/Global 500 company publicly announces pausing/suspending/terminating its advertising spend, branded experiences, or formal partnership with Roblox Corporation between Oct 1-31, 2025, where the stated reason explicitly relates to child safety, content moderation, or ongoing controversies surrounding Roblox's environment for minors. Must be confirmed via official press release OR by at least 2 of: Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, NYT.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'brand company suspend terminate Roblox advertising partnership safety concerns 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find direct qualifying events; 2. 'Roblox child safety controversy advertiser pullout October 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find advertiser responses to safety scandal; 3. 'Fortune 500 company pulls advertising Roblox safety October 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find specific Fortune 500 actions; 4. 'Roblox advertiser brand boycott withdraw partnership 2025' (Sept-Oct 2025) — to find any boycott activity; 5. 'Roblox pull/pause/suspend/terminate advertising partnership brand safety' (Oct 1-31) — direct search for qualifying actions; 6. 'Roblox Reuters Bloomberg WSJ NYT CNBC brand advertiser safety concerns' (Oct 1-31) — searching for tier-1 coverage of brand pullouts.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Extensive child safety controversy — Kentucky AG lawsuit (Oct 7), Florida AG criminal subpoenas (Oct 20-21), Iraq ban (Oct 20-22), 600+ family class-action lawsuits. (2) #BoycottRoblox trending on social media. (3) Mattel EXPANDED its Roblox partnership (Oct 15, Monster High launched Oct 24) — opposite of withdrawal. (4) Roblox Q3 2025 earnings showed strong 48% revenue growth and advertiser partnerships intact. (5) Attorney General Alliance named Roblox inaugural partner in child safety initiative (Oct 29-30). NO candidate events found showing any brand or publicly traded company suspending/terminating Roblox partnership over safety concerns.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No articles from Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, or NYT — or any other credible source — reported any Fortune 500 or publicly traded company suspending/terminating its Roblox partnership over safety concerns in October 2025. [Mattel expansion](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3144531) confirms the opposite trend. [Roblox Q3 2025 earnings call](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/25/10/48531317/roblox-q3-2025-earnings-call-transcript) showed advertising partnerships actively growing. [CNBC article](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/30/roblox-stock-earnings-safety.html) discussed Roblox earnings but no brand pullouts. No criteria match found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found, so no timestamp to extract.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event was found at any point within the October 1-31, 2025 window. Therefore, there is no first occurrence to verify.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence actively searched: Mattel (Fortune 500 company) EXPANDED its Roblox collaboration in October 2025 rather than withdrawing. Roblox's Q3 earnings showed strong advertising revenue growth. Attorney General Alliance endorsed Roblox as a child safety partner. Despite #BoycottRoblox trending and significant legal pressure, no major brand public withdrawal was found in any source. The absence of such reporting in tier-1 outlets (Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, NYT) despite extensive coverage of the Roblox safety controversy strongly suggests no qualifying event occurred.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Despite intense child safety controversy in October 2025 (AG lawsuits, criminal subpoenas, Iraq ban, class-action suits), no publicly traded or Fortune 500/Global 500 company was found to have publicly suspended or terminated its Roblox advertising or partnership over safety concerns during the October 1-31, 2025 window. The opposite trend was documented: Mattel expanded its partnership, Roblox's advertising business grew, and Roblox was named a child safety partner by the Attorney General Alliance. The question resolves No.

question: Will the U.S. national debt hit $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt reaches the listed value this year at any point by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) estimate the U.S. federal budget deficit for Fiscal Year 2025 to be $1.85 trillion or greater in its September 2025 Monthly Budget Review?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. national debt surpassed $37 trillion in August 2025 and has been growing at a rapid pace of about $1 trillion every five months (https://apnews.com/). A key driver of this continuous debt accumulation is the federal budget deficit. The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) regularly tracks government spending and revenues. In a report covering up to August 2025, the CBO estimated that the government had accumulated a $2 trillion deficit over the first 11 months of Fiscal Year 2025. However, because September typically sees an influx of quarterly corporate and individual tax receipts resulting in a monthly surplus, the CBO projected the final total deficit for the entirety of FY 2025 (which ended September 30, 2025) to settle at $1.8 trillion (https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/monthly-budget-review).

The CBO generally releases its 'Monthly Budget Review' for September—summarizing the completed fiscal year—by mid-October. This report provides an early, highly reliable estimate of the total fiscal year deficit before the Treasury Department publishes its final official year-end joint statement. If the September deficit estimate exceeds the previously projected $1.8 trillion and reaches $1.85 trillion or higher, it would signal that government spending outpaced late-year projections or revenues underperformed. This higher-than-expected borrowing requirement would be a direct indicator that the total national debt is accelerating even faster than anticipated.

Sources:
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- Congressional Budget Office Monthly Budget Review: https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/monthly-budget-review
- KPVI News: https://www.kpvi.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) officially publishes its 'Monthly Budget Review' for September 2025 between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19 (inclusive), and the report estimates the total U.S. federal budget deficit for Fiscal Year 2025 to be $1.85 trillion (equivalent to $1,850 billion) or greater. 

The primary resolution source will be the official CBO Monthly Budget Review published on the CBO website (https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/monthly-budget-review). Resolvers must use the total deficit figure reported for 'Fiscal Year 2025' or the 12-month 'Year-to-Date' total ending in September 2025.

If the stated deficit is exactly $1.85 trillion (or 1,850 billion) or higher, the question resolves Yes. If the figure is strictly less than $1.85 trillion, the question resolves No. 

Edge Cases and Clarifications:
- If the CBO provides a range for the estimated deficit rather than a point estimate, the arithmetic midpoint of the range will be used for resolution.
- If the September 2025 Monthly Budget Review is not published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19, the question will resolve as Unresolvable, as the event falls outside the resolution window.
- Any subsequent modifications, errata, or revisions to the deficit figure published by the CBO or the Treasury Department after 2025-10-19 will not be considered for the resolution of this market. Only the initial figure published in the report within the specified window will be evaluated.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the total U.S. national debt will hit $38 trillion by the end of 2025. The speed at which the gross debt grows is largely dictated by the size of the federal budget deficit. By measuring the CBO's preliminary year-end deficit estimate in mid-October, forecasters get a critical, early pulse on the government's borrowing velocity. A deficit of $1.85 trillion or more would mean the government overshot its $1.8 trillion baseline projection, implying the Treasury must issue more debt than planned, making the eventuality of reaching $38 trillion by December 31 much more likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: CBO's Monthly Budget Review for September 2025 must be published between Oct 1–19, 2025, AND the FY2025 total deficit must be $1.85 trillion ($1,850 billion) or greater. Condition for No: Report is published but the deficit figure is strictly less than $1.85 trillion.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'CBO Congressional Budget Office Monthly Budget Review September 2025' (Oct 1–19 window) — to find the report and its figures; 2) 'federal budget deficit fiscal year 2025 CBO estimate October 2025' — to find news coverage; 3) 'CBO Monthly Budget Review September 2025 exact deficit figure billion' — to find precise amounts; 4) 'CBO FY2025 deficit 1809 billion 1800 billion exact figure' — to confirm exact number; 5) 'CBO budget review October 2025 fiscal year 2025 deficit less than 1.85' — to verify the threshold comparison.
evidence.step3_event_detection: The CBO released its September 2025 Monthly Budget Review on October 8, 2025 (per Washington Examiner, Daily Caller, ArcaMax, Fox Business, Fortune, and AFP, all published Oct 8–10, 2025). The deficit figure is consistently reported as approximately $1.8 trillion. Fox Business specifically states '$1.809 trillion'. Washington Examiner confirms it is '$8 billion less than the $1.808 trillion deficit in FY2024', implying ~$1.800 trillion. Free Republic article states 'deficit exceeded $1.8 trillion' and was '$8 billion less than the $1.808 trillion deficit in fiscal 2024' = approximately $1.800 trillion. All sources are consistent: the figure is approximately $1.800–$1.809 trillion, well below the $1.85 trillion threshold.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: 1) Report published within window: YES — CBO Monthly Budget Review for September 2025 published October 8, 2025 [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/finance-and-economy/3842795/interest-payments-1-federal-deficit-hit-1-8-fiscal-2025-cbo/), [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/cbo-reports-1-8-trillion-federal-deficit-debt-costs-hit-record-1-trillion). 2) Deficit >= $1.85 trillion: NO — The reported FY2025 deficit is approximately $1.800–$1.809 trillion, which is strictly less than $1.85 trillion (the threshold). Fox Business states $1.809 trillion; multiple sources confirm it is '$8 billion less than the $1.808 trillion in FY2024'. The deficit is approximately $41–50 billion BELOW the $1.85 trillion threshold. Resolution criteria requires the figure to be $1.850 trillion or greater; the figure (~$1.800–$1.809T) does not meet this threshold.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: CBO report published October 8, 2025 (confirmed by Washington Examiner: 'The data was released by the CBO on Wednesday, October 8, 2025'). ISO 8601: 2025-10-08T00:00:00Z (exact time within the day not specified in sources, but date is confirmed as October 8, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: All sources consistently report the same deficit figure (~$1.800–$1.809 trillion) for the same CBO report released October 8, 2025. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists. This is the first and only Monthly Budget Review for September 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked multiple sources: Washington Examiner, Fox Business, Daily Caller, Conservative Daily News, Fortune, AFP, ArcaMax, Benzinga, Las Vegas Review-Journal, Winona Daily News, La Crosse Tribune, Dispatch Argus, Fibre2fashion. All consistently report the FY2025 deficit as approximately $1.8 trillion (with Fox Business giving the most precise figure of $1.809 trillion). No source reports a figure at or above $1.85 trillion. The comparison to FY2024 ($1.808–$1.817 trillion) and the consistent '$8 billion reduction' narrative confirms the FY2025 figure is ~$1.800–$1.809 trillion. There is no contradictory evidence suggesting the deficit was >= $1.85 trillion. The question therefore resolves No, as the CBO published the report within the window but the deficit figure ($1.800–$1.809T) is strictly less than the $1.85T threshold.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The CBO Monthly Budget Review for September 2025 was published on October 8, 2025 (within the Oct 1–19 window). The FY2025 deficit reported is approximately $1.800–$1.809 trillion, which is strictly less than $1.85 trillion ($1,850 billion). The resolution criteria requires the deficit to be $1.85 trillion or greater. Since the figure is approximately $41–50 billion below the threshold, the question resolves No. The condition became definitively met as impossible on October 8, 2025, when the CBO published its report with a deficit figure below the threshold.

question: Will CME self certify a sports contract in 2025?
description:
This market resolves to “Yes” if CME Group files a self-certification under CFTC Regulation 40.2 for at least one sport-based event contract by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it resolves to “No.”

For this market, “self-certify” means CME, acting as a DCM or self-listing exchange, submits a written certification per 17 C.F.R. § 40.2 that the contract complies with the Commodity Exchange Act and CFTC regulations. The contract must explicitly reference a sporting event (e.g. game result, player performance, etc.). Announcements alone do not qualify; the filing must be made and publicly verifiable.

The resolution source will be the CFTC’s public filings, CME’s disclosures, and a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will at least one U.S. state gaming regulator (other than Ohio) issue a formal public warning or regulatory directive to sportsbooks regarding sports-based event contracts between October 9, 2025, and November 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The intersection of prediction markets and sports betting has drawn increasing regulatory scrutiny as operators bridge the gap between commodity derivatives and gambling. In August 2025, the Ohio Casino Control Commission issued a stern warning to licensed sportsbooks that offering or associating with prediction-market contracts for sporting events could jeopardize their state gaming licenses (Covers, https://www.covers.com/). This warning directly impacts operators like FanDuel, which recently partnered with CME Group to offer event contracts on non-sporting events, while other operators pursue National Futures Association (NFA) licenses (Yahoo Sports, https://sports.yahoo.com/). At the federal level, the CFTC issued a non-interventionist advisory on September 30, 2025, leaving the legality of these contracts largely subject to ongoing court battles between state sovereignty and federal preemption (JD Supra, https://www.jdsupra.com/). Given that FanDuel and similar CME partners rely heavily on their state-licensed sports betting operations, the spread of state-level regulatory threats would likely deter them—and consequently CME—from pursuing sports event contracts.

Sources:
Covers - Ohio Warns Sportsbooks Contemplating Prediction Market Services: https://www.covers.com/
Yahoo Sports - States Rights Vs. Federalism: Can Prediction Markets Be Kept At Bay?: https://sports.yahoo.com/
JD Supra - CFTC's Advisory on Exchange-Listed Sports Event Contracts: https://www.jdsupra.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08 (inclusive), any U.S. state gaming regulatory agency or commission (excluding the Ohio Casino Control Commission) publishes a formal public warning, letter, advisory, or regulatory directive explicitly stating that offering, facilitating, or associating with sports-based event contracts (or sports prediction markets) may jeopardize a state sports wagering/gaming license or violates state gambling laws. The directive must be publicly verifiable via the official website of the respective state regulator (e.g., New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement at https://www.njoag.gov/about/divisions-and-offices/division-of-gaming-enforcement/, Nevada Gaming Control Board at https://gaming.nv.gov/, or Massachusetts Gaming Commission at https://massgaming.com/) or through consensus reporting by credible industry news sources such as Covers (https://www.covers.com) or Legal Sports Report (https://www.legalsportsreport.com). The event must occur and be made public strictly between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08. Internal, non-public communications do not count. If a state issued such a warning prior to 2025-10-09 and merely restates it without a new formal directive, it does not qualify. If no such warning is issued by a new state by 11:59 PM ET on 2025-11-08, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: CME Group's retail strategy for event contracts is heavily reliant on partnerships with major operators like FanDuel. These sportsbooks derive their primary revenue from state-licensed sports betting. If a wave of state regulators threatens to revoke these core licenses over the offering of federally-regulated sports event contracts, sportsbooks will refuse to clear or offer them. Consequently, CME would have no retail incentive or viable partner network to self-certify a sports contract. Tracking state regulatory pushback therefore serves as a highly informative leading indicator for CME's willingness to pursue sports event contracts in 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Any U.S. state gaming regulatory agency (excluding Ohio) must publish a formal public warning, letter, advisory, or regulatory directive explicitly stating that offering/facilitating/associating with sports-based event contracts (sports prediction markets) may jeopardize a state gaming license or violates state gambling laws. Must be publicly verifiable via official regulator website or credible industry sources (Covers, Legal Sports Report, etc.). Must occur strictly between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08 and must be NEW (not a restatement of a prior warning issued before 2025-10-09).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'state gaming regulator warning sports event contracts prediction markets sportsbooks 2025' (Oct 9 - Nov 8, 2025) — to find any state regulator actions; 2) 'sports prediction markets regulatory directive gaming commission warning license 2025' (same window) — to find formal directives; 3) 'New York State Gaming Commission cease and desist Kalshi sports prediction markets October 2025' — to verify NY action; 4) 'Nevada Gaming Control Board sports event contracts warning notice October 2025 formal directive' — to verify NV action and exact date; 5) 'Illinois Gaming Board warning prediction markets sportsbooks formal memorandum October 2025' — to verify IL action; 6) 'Nevada Gaming Control Board Notice to Licensees sports event contracts October 15 2025 first new warning' — to establish first occurrence and confirm newness; 7) 'Legal Sports Report Nevada New York Illinois state gaming regulator sports event contracts warning October 2025' — to check credible industry reporting.
evidence.step3_event_detection: THREE qualifying candidate events identified: (1) Nevada Gaming Control Board issued a formal two-page 'Notice to Licensees' titled 'Sports Event Contracts are Wagers' on October 15, 2025 (published/reported October 16-17, 2025). Confirmed by Covers.com, Las Vegas Review-Journal, iGaming Business, ArcaMax, ReadWrite, and JD Supra. This was a NEW notice to all licensees (distinct from cease-and-desist orders issued to Kalshi in March 2025). (2) New York State Gaming Commission issued a cease-and-desist order to Kalshi on October 24, 2025. Confirmed by multiple sources including Decrypt, ReadWrite, The Bit Gazette, Coinfomania. (3) Illinois Gaming Board issued a formal memorandum warning against participation in prediction markets (around October 28, 2025 based on reporting date). Confirmed by ReadWrite. All three events are within the window. No candidate events were rejected — all are explicitly stated and confirmed by multiple sources.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Nevada Gaming Control Board's October 15, 2025 'Notice to Licensees' fully satisfies all criteria: (a) it is a formal public notice from a state gaming regulatory agency; (b) it explicitly states that sports-based event contracts constitute wagering under Nevada law; (c) it explicitly warns that licensees who partner with prediction market companies like Kalshi, Crypto.com, and Robinhood could jeopardize their Nevada gaming licenses; (d) it was made public (published October 16-17, 2025) via reporting by Covers.com (one of the listed qualifying sources in the resolution criteria) [source](https://www.covers.com/industry/nevada-regulators-send-warning-to-operators-eyeing-prediction-markets-oct-16-2025) and the Las Vegas Review-Journal [source](https://www.reviewjournal.com/business/casinos-gaming/control-board-warns-gaming-companies-to-avoid-prediction-markets-3508661/); (e) it is NEW — the JD Supra analysis [source](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/nevada-gaming-control-board-issues-6067686/) confirms the NGCB issued the first 'Notice to Licensees' memorandum on October 15, 2025 (not prior to this date); Nevada is not Ohio. This is a new formal directive, not a mere restatement of a prior warning. Nevada is explicitly listed as a qualifying source in the resolution criteria (Nevada Gaming Control Board at https://gaming.nv.gov/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Nevada Gaming Control Board's formal Notice to Licensees was issued on October 15, 2025 (internal date of the memorandum), per JD Supra's legal analysis published November 4, 2025 which states 'The Nevada Gaming Control Board (NGCB) issued two 'Notice to Licensees' memoranda on October 15 and October 24, 2025.' Multiple news sources report the notice was made public on October 16-17, 2025. The Covers.com article (a listed qualifying source) is dated October 16, 2025. Exact timestamp: 2025-10-16T00:00:00Z (date of public reporting by Covers.com, a qualifying source under resolution criteria).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The JD Supra article confirms the Nevada NGCB issued the first Notice to Licensees on October 15, 2025 — this is the first such formal public notice from Nevada to its licensees about sports event contracts during the window. Prior Nevada actions (cease-and-desist orders to Kalshi in March 2025, and statements at the October 8, 2025 board meeting) are not the same type of formal advisory/directive to all licensees. Multiple sources confirm no similar Nevada notice to all licensees was issued before October 15, 2025. The Illinois and New York actions came later (October 24 and October 28, respectively), confirming Nevada's October 15-16 notice is the first qualifying occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove: (1) Was the Nevada notice a 'mere restatement' of a prior warning? No — prior Nevada actions (March 2025 C&D to Kalshi specifically, October 8 board meeting discussion) were different instruments and did not constitute a formal Notice to Licensees about license jeopardy. The October 15 notice is explicitly a NEW formal memorandum per JD Supra. (2) Did any qualifying action occur before October 9? ReadWrite states 'Nevada joins Arizona and Ohio' — Arizona's warning was in September 2025, Ohio's was in August 2025, but Nevada's was new in October 2025. (3) Are the reporting sources credible? Yes — Covers.com (explicitly named in resolution criteria), Las Vegas Review-Journal, iGaming Business, JD Supra, ReadWrite, ArcaMax all confirm consistently. (4) Is Nevada excluded? No — only Ohio is excluded. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves YES. The Nevada Gaming Control Board issued a formal 'Notice to Licensees' titled 'Sports Event Contracts are Wagers' on October 15, 2025 (publicly reported October 16-17, 2025), which explicitly warned that offering sports-based event contracts could jeopardize Nevada gaming licenses and that such contracts violate Nevada gambling law unless conducted under a nonrestricted gaming license with sports pool approval. This was reported by Covers.com (a listed qualifying source in the resolution criteria) on October 16, 2025. This is a new formal directive issued within the window, from a state gaming regulator (Nevada) other than Ohio. All resolution criteria are satisfied. The first qualifying event occurred on October 15-16, 2025.

question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 11 Superheavy explode?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the booster for the eleventh Starship-SuperHeavy test explodes at any point during the test from the start of fueling operations to 60 minutes after it makes contact with Earth upon landing. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An explosion is defined as a violent and catastrophic event resulting in the destruction of all or part of the vehicle, regardless of intent or context (e.g., a planned termination event would also count).

If the eleventh launch has not occurred by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: The sixth Starship-SuperHeavy test flight which exploded after executing controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico would qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official video provided by SpaceX (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX officially announce an attempt to catch the Super Heavy booster for Starship Flight 11 using the launch tower arms prior to October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
During SpaceX's Starship Flight 10 test in late August 2025, the Super Heavy booster executed a planned, controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico and eventually exploded in a fireball (https://earthsky.org/). While this marked a significant success, SpaceX's long-term operational goal is to fly the Super Heavy booster back to the Starbase launch site and catch it mid-air using the launch tower's mechanical arms, affectionately known as 'Mechazilla' or 'chopsticks'. Attempting a launch pad catch introduces immense operational risks: if a Raptor engine fails during the final descent or if the booster loses aerodynamic control, it could crash into the tower or the ground, likely resulting in a catastrophic explosion. Conversely, a planned water splashdown keeps the booster far away from launch infrastructure, meaning any impact-related explosion would happen over the ocean. Consequently, knowing whether SpaceX intends to perform this high-risk maneuver during Flight 11 is a key crux in forecasting the likelihood of a booster explosion.

Sources:
SpaceX Official Website: https://www.spacex.com/
SpaceX Official X Account: https://twitter.com/SpaceX
SpaceX Starship Page: https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/starship/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if an official SpaceX communication explicitly announces between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive) that the mission plan for Starship Flight 11 includes an attempt to catch the Super Heavy booster using the launch tower's arms.

Qualifying sources for resolution include:
1. Updates, press releases, or mission descriptions posted on SpaceX's official website (https://www.spacex.com/launches/ or https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/starship/).
2. Public posts from the official SpaceX X/Twitter account (https://twitter.com/SpaceX).
3. Public posts from SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's official X/Twitter account (https://twitter.com/elonmusk).
4. Statements made during official SpaceX livestreams or publicized company presentations.

The announcement must specify that the tower catch attempt is planned for Flight Test 11. If the announcement states that a catch attempt is conditional (e.g., 'we will attempt a tower catch if the boostback burn is nominal'), this will still count as a 'Yes' resolution, as the attempt is part of the mission profile. If SpaceX launches Flight 11 between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10 and attempts a catch without a prior written announcement, the question will also resolve 'Yes'.

If no such announcement is made by 2025-10-10 at 23:59:59 UTC, or if SpaceX explicitly announces that the catch attempt will be delayed to Flight 12 or a later mission, the question resolves 'No'. If an announcement is made within the window but later retracted before the end of the window, it will still resolve 'Yes' because the plan was officially announced.
subquestions.rationale: A launch tower catch is a completely unprecedented and highly dangerous maneuver. If SpaceX decides to attempt it on Flight 11, the Super Heavy booster will need to return to the launch site and hover over solid ground and infrastructure. Any slight error in navigation, engine relight, or structural integrity during this phase will likely result in a hard crash and a massive explosion. Therefore, the presence of a catch attempt drastically increases the baseline probability that the booster will explode compared to a safe, planned splashdown in the ocean.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: SpaceX officially announces between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10 that Flight 11's mission plan includes a tower arm catch of the Super Heavy booster. Observable evidence: official SpaceX X/Twitter post, website update, or livestream statement specifying a catch attempt for Flight 11. Key entities: SpaceX, Super Heavy booster, Flight 11, launch tower chopstick arms.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI release an iOS or Android version of the Atlas browser by November 22, 2025?

During the announcement, OpenAI explicitly stated that support for Windows, iOS, and Android is expected "soon" or in the "coming weeks". This subquestion evaluates whether OpenAI will launch either of the mobile versions (iOS or Android) within a month of the initial macOS rollout. A prompt release of mobile apps would signal strong momentum in their cross-platform rollout strategy, raising the likelihood that the Windows version will be deployed before the end of the year.

Fast Company: https://www.fastcompany.com/
OpenAI News: https://openai.com/news/

If no iOS or Android version of Atlas is made publicly available for download by November 22, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET, this question resolves No. Resolution will primarily be determined by official announcements from OpenAI (e.g., via https://openai.com/news or their official social media channels) and corroborated by verified public availability of the app on the respective platforms.
subquestions.rationale: OpenAI explicitly promised that Windows, iOS, and Android versions of their new Atlas browser are "forthcoming." If they successfully release mobile versions within a month of the macOS launch, it is highly likely that the Windows version is on track for a December 31 release. Conversely, if no additional platforms are launched by November 22, it suggests a slower-than-expected cross-platform development cycle, which would significantly lower the probability of the Windows app launching by the ultimate deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires OpenAI to publicly release an iOS or Android version of the Atlas browser between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive). The release must be: (1) officially by OpenAI, (2) a dedicated browser app branded as Atlas, (3) distinct from the existing ChatGPT app, and (4) available on Apple App Store, Google Play Store, official TestFlight, or a direct APK download link from OpenAI.

subquestions.question: Will Senator Bernie Sanders publicly withdraw his endorsement of Graham Platner for the U.S. Senate by November 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Graham Platner, a Democratic candidate for the U.S. Senate in Maine, is challenging incumbent Republican Susan Collins and prominent primary rival Governor Janet Mills. Platner secured a high-profile endorsement from Senator Bernie Sanders, who backed him over the establishment-supported Mills. However, in late October 2025, Platner's campaign faced severe controversies: on October 19, his political director resigned following the unearthing of old Reddit posts containing racist and xenophobic remarks by Platner. A few days later, on October 22, Platner publicly apologized for a tattoo resembling a Nazi SS symbol, which he promised to cover or remove. Despite these scandals and calls from fellow primary contender Jordan Wood to drop out, Platner has vowed to remain in the race, and Sanders had not immediately pulled his support. Because Sanders' endorsement is the cornerstone of Platner's progressive credibility and fundraising, the retraction of this endorsement would be a crucial indicator of Platner's campaign viability. If Sanders drops his support, Platner would likely face insurmountable pressure to withdraw before December 31.

Sources:
AP News: https://apnews.com
HuffPost: https://www.huffpost.com
The Maine Wire: https://www.themainewire.com
Bernie Sanders Official Site: https://berniesanders.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive), Senator Bernie Sanders or his official representatives publicly announce the withdrawal, retraction, or suspension of his endorsement of Graham Platner for the 2026 Maine U.S. Senate race. The question will also resolve Yes if Sanders officially endorses another candidate in the Maine Democratic Senate primary (such as Janet Mills or Jordan Wood) during this window, which would effectively revoke his exclusive support for Platner.

The announcement must be verifiable via official channels, such as Sanders' Senate website (https://www.sanders.senate.gov/), his campaign website (https://berniesanders.com/), his official social media accounts (e.g., https://x.com/SenSanders or https://x.com/BernieSanders), or via on-the-record statements reported by credible national news organizations (e.g., AP News: https://apnews.com or CNN: https://www.cnn.com).

If Sanders states he is 're-evaluating' his support but does not explicitly suspend or withdraw the endorsement, it does not qualify for a Yes resolution. If Platner withdraws from the race before Sanders explicitly retracts his endorsement, this question resolves No. If the resolution window ends on 2025-11-22 at 11:59 PM ET without a qualifying retraction or alternative endorsement by Sanders, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Bernie Sanders' endorsement is the primary pillar of Platner's national legitimacy and progressive fundraising. In light of the recent severe scandals regarding racist comments and a Nazi-style tattoo, immense pressure will be placed on Sanders to distance himself from Platner. If Sanders withdraws his endorsement, Platner's campaign will lose its main source of political capital and financial momentum, making his withdrawal from the race highly probable. Conversely, if Sanders holds firm, Platner is more likely to weather the storm and stay in the race.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: Bernie Sanders publicly withdraws/retracts/suspends his endorsement of Graham Platner for the Maine U.S. Senate race, OR Sanders endorses another Maine Democratic Senate primary candidate (Janet Mills or Jordan Wood), between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22. evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events reviewed: (1) On October 21-25, Sanders explicitly said 'absolutely' sticking by endorsement, calling Platner 'an excellent candidate' — this is a CONFIRMATION of endorsement, not withdrawal. (2) On November 6, Sanders predicted Platner's victory — CONFIRMATION, not withdrawal. (3) On November 15-17, multiple outlets describe Platner as 'endorsed by Bernie Sanders' with no withdrawal mentioned. (4) November 21 Medium article still identifies Platner as 'endorsed by Bernie Sanders.' (5) Jordan Wood dropped out of Maine Senate race on November 12 to run for House — Sanders never endorsed Wood in the Maine Senate race. (6) Sanders endorsed Peggy Flanagan (Minnesota Senate, November 10) — not related to Maine race. No candidate events found constituting a withdrawal, retraction, or suspension of Sanders' endorsement of Platner, nor an endorsement of Mills or Wood in the Maine Senate primary.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found matching the resolution criteria. evidence.step8_final_decision: Sanders did not withdraw, retract, or suspend his endorsement of Platner at any point between October 23 and November 22, 2025. The question resolves No. The window closed without any qualifying event, so the resolution_datetime is 2025-11-22T23:59:59Z.

question: Will Consensys IPO by December 31 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ConsenSys (the parent company of MetaMask) completes an Initial Public Offering (IPO) by the listed date ET, as confirmed by official company announcements and credible news sources. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The IPO refers to the first sale of stock by the listed company to the public on any recognized stock exchange.

If ConsenSys is acquired by another company that is already public, this market will immediately resolve to "No."

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will ConsenSys publicly file a Form S-1 or equivalent IPO registration statement with the SEC between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29?
subquestions.background_information: ConsenSys, the software developer and parent company of MetaMask, is reportedly planning an initial public offering (IPO) and has hired JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs to lead the process (Yahoo Finance, https://finance.yahoo.com). This follows favorable regulatory developments, such as the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) dropping its lawsuit against ConsenSys regarding MetaMask's staking features earlier in 2025. For a company to go public in the US, it must file a Form S-1 registration statement with the SEC. While companies can submit this confidentially at first, the SEC requires the S-1 to be filed publicly at least 15 days before the company begins its IPO roadshow. Tracking the public filing of ConsenSys's S-1 is a necessary leading indicator for whether it can execute an IPO by the end of 2025. Sources: Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com ; SEC EDGAR Company Search: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if ConsenSys (or its direct holding/parent company) publicly files a Form S-1, Form F-1, or equivalent initial public offering registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive). The resolution will be determined by searching the SEC's EDGAR database (https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch.html). A confidential submission that has not been made publicly accessible on EDGAR does not qualify. The public filing must be visible on the SEC database before 23:59 UTC on 2025-12-29. If no such filing occurs within the specified window, the question resolves No. In the event that the SEC EDGAR database is temporarily down or inaccessible at the time of resolution, the resolution window will be extended by up to 48 hours to check for filings made before the deadline. If EDGAR is permanently decommissioned, credible reporting from major financial news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, WSJ) confirming the public filing will be used as a fallback.
subquestions.rationale: To conduct an IPO by December 31, 2025, a company must first publicly file a registration statement with the SEC. The SEC requires this document to be public for at least 15 days before an IPO roadshow can commence. Therefore, if ConsenSys does not publicly file an S-1 by December 29, 2025, it is structurally impossible for them to complete the IPO by December 31. This subquestion acts as a decisive leading indicator for the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: ConsenSys (or its direct parent/holding company) must have publicly filed a Form S-1, Form F-1, or equivalent IPO registration statement with the SEC, visible on EDGAR, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29. A confidential submission does not qualify. Key entities: ConsenSys, SEC EDGAR database. Timing constraint: strictly within the Nov 30 – Dec 29 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'ConsenSys IPO S-1 SEC filing 2025' – to find any public filing news; 2) 'ConsenSys public offering registration statement SEC EDGAR' – to find EDGAR-specific filing confirmation; 3) 'ConsenSys S-1 F-1 registration statement' – to find news of a filed statement; 4) 'ConsenSys IPO JPMorgan Goldman Sachs underwriter 2025' – to find timeline/progress updates; 5) 'ConsenSys filed public offering registration statement Gemini BitGo' – to investigate claims about prior filings; 6) 'ConsenSys IPO update news December 2025' – to find any December filing; 7) 'ConsenSys IPO 2026 timeline delayed' – to check if no filing occurred in window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) Reports from late October/early November 2025 that ConsenSys hired JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs for an IPO – these describe preparation, not a filed registration statement. (b) Brave New Coin Nov 13, 2025 article stating 'Other firms including Gemini, BitGo, and Consensys have also filed for public offerings' – this appears to be inaccurate or refers to confidential DRS submissions, as no specific EDGAR filing was cited or corroborated. (c) Mid-December 2025 news that ConsenSys is 'preparing for a potential IPO' – future-oriented language, no confirmed public filing. All candidate events rejected due to lack of explicit, verifiable public S-1/F-1 filing on EDGAR within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No source explicitly confirms a publicly-accessible S-1 or F-1 filing by ConsenSys on SEC EDGAR within the Nov 30–Dec 29, 2025 window. All reporting as of December 2025 uses future-oriented language: 'preparing for a potential IPO' ([Brave New Coin Dec 16](https://bravenewcoin.com/insights/metamask-adds-bitcoin-support-after-10-month-wait)), 'preparing for an initial public offering (IPO) with JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs' ([Invezz Dec 16](https://invezz.com/news/2025/12/16/metamask-rolls-out-support-for-bitcoin-in-latest-update/)). The Axios report from October 2025 noted the IPO 'could occur as early as 2026' ([Yahoo Finance Oct 31](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/metamask-maker-consensys-plans-ipo-224845749.html)). A ConsenSys spokesperson stated 'nothing to announce at this time' in late October 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp of a qualifying public SEC filing by ConsenSys was found. No EDGAR filing confirmation exists in any news source for the Nov 30–Dec 29 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find any EDGAR filing announcement via multiple searches – none found. The Brave New Coin Nov 13 article's passing reference to ConsenSys having 'filed for public offerings' is contradicted by all other sources that consistently describe ConsenSys as still in preparation/planning stage through December 2025. No major financial outlet (Bloomberg, Reuters, WSJ) reported a ConsenSys S-1 public filing during this period. The US government shutdown (ended Nov 13) and SEC backlog further delayed IPO processes. All evidence points to ConsenSys remaining a pre-IPO company throughout the question window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No evidence exists of ConsenSys publicly filing an S-1, F-1, or equivalent IPO registration statement with the SEC between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29. All news sources through the end of the window describe ConsenSys as 'preparing' or 'planning' an IPO expected in 2026. The resolution window closed (2025-12-29) with no qualifying event.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or the U.S. Department of the Treasury publish an official document or press release mentioning a "housing emergency" between October 2 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In September 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated that the Trump administration is considering declaring a national housing emergency in the fall to address rising housing costs (Benzinga News). As of late August, the 30-year mortgage rate was at 6.58%, exacerbating affordability issues. Furthermore, Polymarket bettors assigned a 34% probability that President Trump would declare a housing emergency in 2025, following Bessent's comments (Benzinga News). An official press release, briefing, or statement from the White House or Treasury mentioning a "housing emergency" would serve as a strong leading indicator that the administration is preparing to formally declare one under the National Emergencies Act.

Sources:
Benzinga News, Trump Administration Weighs National Housing Emergency: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/09/trump-administration-weighs-national-housing-emergency
Benzinga News, Trump Could Declare Housing Emergency In 2025?: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/09/trump-could-declare-housing-emergency-in-2025-polymarket
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a press release, briefing transcript, official statement, or other official document containing the exact phrase "housing emergency" (case-insensitive) is published on the official White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov) or the U.S. Department of the Treasury website (https://home.treasury.gov) between 2025-10-02 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

The publication must occur during this specific window. To determine the resolution, the official websites will be searched using their native search functions or via site-specific searches on major search engines (e.g., Google `site:whitehouse.gov "housing emergency"`). The document must be officially published by the administration; user comments, third-party content, or archived historical documents from prior administrations republished in this window do not count. The phrase may be hyphenated (e.g., "housing-emergency") but must include both words consecutively.

If no such document is published between 2025-10-02 and 2025-10-31, the question resolves No. Documents published prior to 2025-10-02 or after 2025-10-31 do not count towards a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent explicitly stated that the administration 'may declare a national housing emergency in the fall.' The publication of an official document or press release using the phrase 'housing emergency' is a highly observable intermediate step that strongly signals the administration's active preparation for a formal emergency declaration under the National Emergencies Act. If they do not start using this terminology officially in October, the likelihood of a formal declaration by the end of the year decreases significantly.
