subquestions.question: Will the 10-Year U.S. Treasury yield fall below 3.60% at any point between September 3 and October 3, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage (FRM) is closely tied to the 10-Year U.S. Treasury yield. Lenders use the 10-year Treasury as a primary benchmark to price long-term fixed-rate mortgages, typically maintaining a spread of roughly 150 to 300 basis points over the Treasury yield. As of late August 2025, Freddie Mac reported the average 30-year FRM at a 10-month low of 6.56%. For the 30-year mortgage rate to eventually drop below the ultimate question's threshold of 6.00% by December 31, 2025, the 10-Year Treasury yield will likely need to compress further, approaching or breaking the 3.60% mark during the early fall. Monitoring whether the 10-Year yield falls below this threshold in September or early October provides a strong, distinct early indicator for the trajectory of mortgage rates through the rest of the year.

Sources:
Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) 10-Year Treasury Yield: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10
Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey: https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms
U.S. Department of the Treasury Yield Curve Data: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The primary resolution source for this market is the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) database, specifically the 'DGS10' series, available at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10. 

If FRED data is unavailable, the fallback resolution source will be the official Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates published directly by the U.S. Department of the Treasury at https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025. 

Resolution will be based on the first published data for the specified dates. Any subsequent ex-post revisions to the data made after October 10, 2025, will not affect the resolution of this market. If the yield never drops below 3.60% within the specified window, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Because the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage average is priced primarily at a premium over the 10-Year U.S. Treasury yield, analyzing the movement of the 10-Year Treasury is standard practice for forecasting mortgage rate trends. A drop in the Treasury yield below 3.60% in the near term would confirm significant downward momentum in long-term borrowing costs, serving as a critical crux for forecasters anticipating whether mortgage rates can clear the 6.00% hurdle by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: DGS10 (10-Year Treasury yield on investment basis) must be strictly less than 3.60% on at least one observation date between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03 (inclusive). evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require the daily yield to be strictly less than 3.60% (i.e., 3.59% or lower). Every reported yield during the window ranged from approximately 4.0% to 4.26%. The closest level to the threshold was ~4.0% (Sep 11 and Sep 17), which is still 40 basis points above the required threshold of 3.60%. subquestions.background_information:
Currently, the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) treats cryptocurrency as property, meaning that every transaction triggers a taxable event for capital gains, regardless of the transaction's size. There is currently no de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions in the U.S. (Decrypt, https://decrypt.co). Over 70 cryptocurrency organizations sent a letter to President Donald Trump on November 20, 2025, urging regulatory clarity, including a de minimis tax exemption for digital asset transactions up to $600 (CoinCentral, https://coincentral.com). Concurrently, crypto industry executives launched a coordinated campaign and held a private dinner with key members of the House Ways and Means Committee to build legislative support for this exemption (TechStory, https://techstory.in). U.S. Senator Cynthia Lummis has also previously proposed legislation to exempt crypto transactions under $300 from capital gains taxes (AMBCrypto, https://ambcrypto.com). Passing a bill in either chamber of Congress would be a major milestone toward enacting such a tax exemption into law.

Sources:
Decrypt: https://decrypt.co
CoinCentral: https://coincentral.com
TechStory: https://techstory.in
AMBCrypto: https://ambcrypto.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate passes a piece of legislation (e.g., a standalone bill or an amendment included in a broader passed bill) that contains a provision establishing a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions.

The legislation must stipulate that individual cryptocurrency transactions under a certain fiat value threshold (e.g., $200, $300, $600) are exempt from capital gains taxation for U.S. taxpayers. 

'Passes' means the bill must be approved by a successful floor vote in at least one full chamber of Congress (the House or the Senate). Approval by a congressional committee alone does not suffice unless the bill subsequently passes the full chamber. 

Resolution will be based on official legislative records from Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov) or the official websites of the U.S. House (https://www.house.gov) or U.S. Senate (https://www.senate.gov). A consensus of credible reporting from major news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters) may be used to confirm the contents of the passed bill.

If neither chamber passes such a bill between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29, the question resolves No. Delayed events extending past the resolution window will not be considered, and the question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: For Donald Trump to sign a bill into law before 2026 establishing a de minimis crypto tax exemption, the bill must first pass the House and the Senate. Tracking whether at least one chamber of Congress passes such a bill serves as an excellent early indicator of legislative momentum. If neither chamber passes such a bill by late December, the probability of the ultimate outcome occurring via legislation drops precipitously, leaving executive action as the only viable path.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29, either the U.S. House or Senate must pass (full floor vote) a bill containing a de minimis capital gains tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions under a specific dollar threshold (e.g., $200, $300, $600). Observable evidence would be a recorded floor vote result. Key entities: U.S. House, U.S. Senate, any cryptocurrency-related tax bill. Timing: strictly within the Nov 30 – Dec 29 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'cryptocurrency de minimis tax exemption bill Congress 2025' — to find any relevant bills in the window; 2) 'Virtual Currency Tax Fairness Act de minimis crypto exemption House Senate vote' — to find earlier versions; 3) 'PARITY Act crypto tax bill House floor vote passed December 2025' — to check for passage; 4) 'Congress crypto tax exemption bill passed floor vote 2025' — general passage check; 5) 'big beautiful bill reconciliation crypto tax exemption passed December 2025' — to check omnibus/reconciliation vehicles; 6) 'One Big Beautiful Bill OBBBA crypto de minimis exemption provision' — to check if OBBBA included such provision.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Digital Asset PARITY Act introduced as discussion draft on December 20, 2025 by Reps. Max Miller and Steven Horsford — includes $200 de minimis stablecoin exemption. REJECTED: explicitly described as a 'discussion draft' that had not been formally introduced or voted on, with a vote target of 'before August 2026'. (2) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) — passed July 4, 2025, outside window. Also, no evidence of crypto de minimis provision included. (3) Digital Asset Market Clarity Act — passed House in July 2025, outside window, and is a market structure bill not a tax exemption bill. (4) Senator Lummis's $300 de minimis proposal — a discussion draft only, not voted on. No other qualifying events found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Digital Asset PARITY Act contains a de minimis $200 exemption for stablecoin capital gains, matching the type of provision required. However, the bill is explicitly described as a 'discussion draft' not yet formally introduced, let alone passed by either chamber. [Analytics Insight](https://www.analyticsinsight.net/news/bipartisan-bill-seeks-crypto-tax-clarity-with-stablecoin-exemption-and-staking-deferral): 'The bill remains a discussion draft.' [TechStory](https://techstory.in/house-lawmakers-unveil-bipartisan-parity-act-to-overhaul-crypto-taxes/): 'The draft is currently under discussion and has not yet been introduced in the House.' [CoinDesk December 6](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2025/12/06/state-of-crypto-wrapping-up-the-month): market structure bill 'is unlikely to become law before 2026.' evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp of a floor vote passage could be extracted, because no floor vote occurred within the resolution window for any bill with a crypto de minimis tax exemption provision.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found within or before the window. The only relevant legislation (PARITY Act) was still a discussion draft as of late December 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked multiple angles: (1) OBBBA provisions — confirmed no crypto de minimis exemption included; (2) Broader crypto legislation — Digital Asset Market Clarity Act passed House in July but is market structure, not tax exemption; (3) Senate crypto bills — explicitly delayed to 2026; (4) Multiple independent sources consistently state the PARITY Act is a discussion draft with no floor vote scheduled before the window's end; (5) Rep. Miller explicitly targeted 'before August 2026' for a vote. No contradictory evidence suggesting a passage occurred.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No bill containing a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions passed a full floor vote in either the U.S. House or Senate between November 30 and December 29, 2025. The only relevant legislation (PARITY Act) was introduced as a discussion draft on December 20, 2025, and had not been formally introduced or voted on. All other crypto tax proposals remain in earlier stages. The question resolves No. The window closed on December 29, 2025 with the condition never met.

question: Russia x Ukraine buffer zone agreement by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an agreement on an official buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "buffer zone" is defined as a neutral or otherwise militarily restricted area that lies between the territories of Russia and Ukraine and is intended to reduce or manage conflict between them.

A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. It is sufficient that the agreement explicitly demonstrates mutual intent to suspend offensive military action within the designated zone, for example, by stipulating the withdrawal of heavy artillery, armored vehicles, etc.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the buffer zone is established formally by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, announcements of a partial implementation, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A mutual agreement on a buffer zone will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of potential subsequent violations of such an agreement.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a broad consensus of credible media reporting stating an official agreement regarding a buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

Negotiations exclusively limited to prisoner exchanges, the return of bodies, or isolated humanitarian corridors without broader ceasefire or settlement objectives do NOT qualify.

Otherwise, it resolves No. The primary resolution source will be the official U.S. Department of the Treasury website, specifically the data listed under 'Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates' for the column '2 Yr' (https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025). If the Treasury website is permanently unavailable or fails to publish data for the specified window by December 31, 2025, alternative reliable financial data providers such as FRED (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2) will be used to determine the official 2-year par yield for those dates. Delayed publication of the rates due to holidays or government shutdowns will not prevent a Yes resolution as long as the official rate assigned to a valid trading date within the window is below 3.50%.
subquestions.rationale: The 2-year Treasury yield is an effective gauge for the market's near-term monetary policy expectations, specifically regarding the Federal Reserve's path for rate cuts. If the 2-year yield breaks below 3.50% ahead of the December FOMC meeting, it demonstrates a strong shift toward pricing in lower interest rates. Because the 10-year yield and the 2-year yield are heavily correlated, tracking this shorter-duration instrument acts as an excellent early indicator for whether the broader rate environment is softening enough to push the 10-year yield below the 3.9% ultimate threshold.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rate '2 Yr' must be 3.49% or lower on any trading date between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-17 (inclusive). Observable evidence: official Treasury website closing yield data. Key threshold: <3.50% (i.e., 3.49% or lower). Timing: any trading day in the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for '2-year Treasury yield November December 2025', 'US Treasury 2yr yield rate 3.50% 3.49% 2025', '2-year Treasury yield daily close November 24 25 26 2025', 'Treasury yield December 16 17 2025 two-year 3.49', '2-year Treasury yield 3.48% 3.49% daily December 2025', '2-year Treasury par yield close November 25 26 2025', 'US 2-year Treasury yield settled closed December 16 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) November 24, 2025 - 2-year note AUCTION yield at 3.489% (ZeroHedge, InstaForex) - REJECTED as auction yield ≠ par yield curve rate; (2) December 16, 2025 - intraday 2-year yield at 3.48% (WAND-TV), 3.49% (Yahoo/AP), 3.492% (Barron's/Tradeweb) - these appear to be intraday/morning levels; AP explicitly states 'yields later fluctuated' suggesting possible rebound to above 3.50%; (3) December 15 - 2-year at ~3.509% (CNBC, early morning) - above threshold; (4) Various other dates show 2-year at 3.51%-3.60%+.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution requires the OFFICIAL Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rate (closing). The evidence shows intraday readings of 3.48%-3.492% on December 16, 2025 from [WAND-TV](https://www.wandtv.com/news/national/wall-street-loses-ground-following-mixed-data-on-the-economy/article_73ec2105-063b-5200-95e2-6cd53ab816e5.html), [AP/Yahoo Finance](https://apnews.com/article/stocks-markets-jobs-trump-ai-3af016aee68a46f9131db0450ed33048), and [Barron's](https://www.barrons.com/livecoverage/stock-market-news-today-121625/card/u-s-treasury-yields-fall-ahead-of-key-labor-market-data-CFmcMJvukn6gJZWZSEby). However, AP explicitly states 'yields later fluctuated' after the initial declines to 3.49%. The Barchart end-of-day settlement article does not report the 2-year closing yield. No source explicitly states the official daily par yield closed at or below 3.49% on any day in the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: December 16, 2025 is the strongest candidate date. Intraday yield of 3.48% was reported (WAND-TV), 3.49% (Yahoo/AP morning), 3.492% (Barron's Asian trade). However, AP notes yields 'later fluctuated' and Barchart end-of-day does not confirm sub-3.50% closing 2-year yield. No definitive closing par yield below 3.50% timestamp established.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: If any qualifying occurrence exists, December 16, 2025 would be the first candidate (or possibly November 24-25, 2025 if market rates reflected the auction result, but available evidence is insufficient). No earlier qualifying official par yield occurrence confirmed.
evidence.step7_verification: The AP article explicitly states yields 'initially' fell to 3.49% but 'later fluctuated' - this directly contradicts a clean Yes resolution for the closing official par yield. The Barchart end-of-day settle article (Dec 16) gives 10-year at 4.145% but omits 2-year closing yield. The Bond-Market Dec 14 article references 2-year 'currently at 3.5%'. Multiple end-of-day summaries for Dec 16 (Yahoo Finance analyst recap) report 10-year at 4.18% but don't report 2-year closing. The weight of evidence suggests intraday movement below 3.50% but uncertainty about official closing par yield.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence strongly suggests that the 2-year Treasury yield touched below 3.50% intraday on December 16, 2025 (as low as 3.48% per WAND-TV, 3.49% per AP/Yahoo Finance). However, the resolution criterion specifically requires the Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rate (official closing rate). The AP article explicitly states 'yields later fluctuated' after the initial decline to 3.49%, suggesting the close may have been above 3.50%. Without explicit confirmation of the official end-of-day par yield closing at or below 3.49%, I cannot definitively resolve Yes. However, Barchart's end-of-day report shows the 10-year settled at 4.145% (lower than intraday highs), and the pattern of data suggests the 2-year likely also closed lower. Given that multiple reliable sources (AP, Yahoo Finance, WAND-TV) report the 2-year at 3.48-3.49% on December 16, and these descriptions in WAND-TV appear in what reads as an end-of-day wrap (describing the full trading session), and the resolution criteria allows for alternative providers like FRED if Treasury data is unavailable - the balance of evidence tilts toward Yes but remains uncertain. Given the strict precision requirement and the AP statement about yields 'later fluctuating', I find this insufficient for a definitive Yes, but also insufficient for a definitive No. Marking as resolvable=false due to inability to confirm the official par yield closing rate.

question: Lisa Cook out as Fed Governor by February 28?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Lisa Cook announces her resignation or otherwise ceases to be a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors for any period of time between December 8, 2025, and February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only official announcements of Cook's resignation or removal before her term is scheduled to end, made by either Cook or the Board of Governors, will qualify. Announcements from Trump or his administration will not alone qualify.

Temporary absences or attempts at termination which do not actually remove Cook from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be information from the U.S. Government however a consensus of credible reporting will also suffice.

subquestions.question: Will Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook commence a formal leave of absence from her duties between December 9, 2025, and January 8, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
In August 2025, President Donald Trump announced his intention to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook from her position 'for cause' over allegations of mortgage fraud. Cook strongly denied the allegations, stating she would not resign and would continue to carry out her duties. Following the attempt to remove her, the administration explicitly pressured Cook to step aside temporarily; White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett stated that Cook should 'go on leave' until the legal and factual disputes over the accusations are resolved (https://finance.yahoo.com/). Cook, who was appointed in 2022 and whose term extends to 2038, has so far refused to step down or take leave, setting up a major legal and political standoff over the independence of the Federal Reserve.

Sources:
Yahoo! Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/
Federal Reserve Press Releases: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases.htm
CNN International: https://edition.cnn.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if an official statement from the Federal Reserve, the U.S. government, Lisa Cook, or a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg) confirms that Lisa Cook has officially commenced a leave of absence from her role as a Federal Reserve Governor between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 (inclusive).

The leave must be explicitly described as a 'leave of absence', 'administrative leave', or a complete temporary recusal from her official duties at the Federal Reserve. Routine vacations, sick leave, or exclusion from specific meetings that do not constitute a formal leave status will not qualify.

If Lisa Cook permanently resigns or is legally permanently removed during this window without first taking a leave of absence, this question resolves No, as that would trigger the ultimate question directly rather than this specific interim step. Delayed events announced to take effect after the resolution window will not qualify. The primary resolution source will be Federal Reserve press releases (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases.htm) alongside major financial news reporting (e.g., https://www.bloomberg.com/ or https://www.reuters.com/).
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question explicitly states that 'temporary absences... will not qualify' for its resolution. However, a formal leave of absence is exactly what the White House publicly pushed for as an interim step while the dispute over her attempted firing is litigated. If Cook goes on leave during this period, it would strongly indicate that she or the Fed is yielding to administration pressure or pending court proceedings, making her ultimate permanent departure by February 28 highly likely. Conversely, remaining actively on duty through early January signals a protracted stalemate, reducing the odds of a quick ouster by February.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Lisa Cook must explicitly commence a formal 'leave of absence,' 'administrative leave,' or complete temporary recusal from Fed duties between Dec 9, 2025 and Jan 8, 2026. Observable evidence would be: Fed press release, official statement, or consensus credible reporting (Reuters, Bloomberg) confirming one of these specific statuses. Key entity: Lisa Cook, Federal Reserve Governor. Timing: within the window Dec 9, 2025–Jan 8, 2026 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve leave of absence 2025' (Dec 9–Jan 8) — to find direct evidence of leave; 2) 'Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook resignation removal 2025' (Dec 1–Jan 8) — to find permanent removal or resignation; 3) 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve administrative leave recusal duties January 2026' (Dec 9–Jan 8) — to find administrative leave or recusal; 4) 'Lisa Cook Fed governor status Supreme Court January 2026 reinstatement' (Dec 9–Jan 8) — to confirm ongoing status and court proceedings.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events for a formal leave of absence were identified. All articles describe: (a) Trump fired Cook in August 2025 over alleged mortgage fraud; (b) a federal court reinstated her, allowing her to remain pending Supreme Court proceedings; (c) Supreme Court arguments on her case scheduled for January 21, 2026 — outside the resolution window; (d) As of January 6, 2026 (Reuters/Investing.com), Cook is classified as an active Fed policymaker (dove). No article mentions leave of absence, administrative leave, or formal recusal.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the articles confirm a formal leave of absence or administrative leave for Lisa Cook within the resolution window. [Market Screener Jan 5](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/new-president-powell-s-future-lisa-cook-s-dismissala-5-issues-for-the-fed-in-2026-ce7e59dedb81f524) states she was 'temporarily reinstated by a federal judge' with Supreme Court hearing Jan 21, 2026. [Reuters/Investing.com Jan 6](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/fed-hawks-and-doves-what-us-central-bankers-are-saying-4433288) lists Cook as an active 'dove' policymaker. [Cryptopolitan Jan 3](https://www.cryptopolitan.com/will-powell-stay-on-federal-reserve-board/) states she 'remains in office after a court suspended her removal.' No source describes a leave of absence.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a qualifying event exists, as no qualifying event (formal leave of absence) occurred within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence suggesting a leave of absence. All available evidence confirms Cook continued serving in her role throughout the resolution window, protected by a court order reinstating her. No contradictory evidence found. The situation is clearly that she was fighting to remain in her role (not voluntarily taking leave), and all reporting confirms she remained active on the Board of Governors through at least January 6, 2026.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout the Dec 9, 2025–Jan 8, 2026 window, Lisa Cook remained an active, reinstated Federal Reserve Governor pending the Supreme Court hearing scheduled for January 21, 2026. No credible source reports a formal leave of absence, administrative leave, or complete temporary recusal from duties. The window closed on January 8, 2026 with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between October 30 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will any NATO member state officially confirm a violation of its sovereign airspace by a Russian-launched drone or missile between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Recent Russian aerial bombardments of Ukraine have increasingly approached or crossed into NATO airspace, testing the alliance's air defense readiness. On September 20, 2025, Polish and other NATO jets scrambled to intercept a large Russian strike on Ukraine. Reports indicated that Russian drones had violated the airspace of Poland and Romania, prompting NATO to intercept and shoot down several drones over Poland. The Russian military has launched massive, frequent barrages, such as over 300 drones and 37 missiles on October 17, 2025, and 705 targets on October 30, 2025. These large-scale attacks increase the risk of stray drones or missiles crossing into neighboring countries. Monitoring whether airspace violations continue provides a critical early indicator of the likelihood that a projectile might ultimately impact NATO territory, accidentally or intentionally. Sources: Euronews: Russia batters Ukraine's energy grid with drone and missile strikes - https://www.euronews.com/ Ukrainian National News Agency: Ukraine’s air defenses down 623 drones and missiles out of 705 launched - https://www.ukrinform.net/ NATO Press Releases - https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/press_releases.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the government, defense ministry, or military command of any NATO member state officially confirms that a Russian-launched drone or missile entered its sovereign airspace between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive). The official statement must explicitly identify the object as an unmanned aerial vehicle (drone) or missile (including cruise or ballistic missiles, or loitering munitions) and attribute its launch to Russian forces. The airspace violation must have occurred within the specified time window (2025-10-31 to 2025-11-30). If the airspace violation occurs within this window but the official confirmation is delayed, it still counts toward a Yes resolution, provided the announcement is made before the end of the ultimate question's resolution date. If an event occurs but remains unconfirmed by official channels before the resolution window closes, it does not count. Events involving manned aircraft, helicopters, or naval vessels do not qualify. The projectile does not need to impact the ground; merely crossing into sovereign airspace (as confirmed by the state) is sufficient. If no such official confirmation is made regarding an incident occurring between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, this question resolves No. Resolution will be based on official government or military press releases, such as the Polish Armed Forces (https://www.wojsko-polskie.pl/), the Romanian Ministry of National Defence (https://english.mapn.ro/), or official NATO press releases (https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/press_releases.htm), and must be corroborated by major credible news outlets like Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) or AP News (https://apnews.com).
subquestions.rationale: Airspace violations by Russian drones or missiles are a direct precursor to potential strikes or impacts on NATO territory. The ultimate question asks whether a Russian projectile will 'impact' NATO ground. By tracking whether projectiles are crossing the border (even if intercepted or returning to Ukraine) in the preceding month, forecasters can better assess the frequency of border friction. A high rate of confirmed airspace violations suggests an elevated risk that a drone or missile will eventually crash or strike NATO territory, whereas a lack of violations indicates successful de-escalation or improved precision by Russian forces.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Any NATO member state government/defense ministry/military officially confirms a Russian-launched drone or missile entered its sovereign airspace between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30. Observable evidence: Official government statement explicitly identifying the object as drone/missile, attributing it to Russian forces, and confirming airspace entry within the window. Key entities: NATO member states (especially Romania, Poland), Russian-launched drones/missiles.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'NATO airspace violation Russian drone missile 2025 November' — to find general incidents; Query 2: 'Poland Romania airspace Russian missile drone violation November 2025' — to find specific country incidents; Query 3: 'Romania defense ministry official confirmation Russian drone airspace violation November 25 2025' — to verify official attribution for the Nov 25 incident; Query 4: 'Romania drone fragments Russian airspace November 10 11 2025 official statement' — to verify earlier qualifying incident.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) November 10-11, 2025: Romanian MoD confirms drone fragments from Russian military drones 5km inside Romanian territory during Russian strikes on Ukrainian Danube ports — qualifies as official confirmation of Russian drone crossing into NATO airspace. (2) November 19-20, 2025: Romania scrambles jets after a drone briefly entered Romanian airspace during massive Russian attack — qualifies. (3) November 25, 2025: Romania's defence ministry confirms two Russian drone incursions; Defence Minister calls it 'Russian provocation'; drone crashes on Romanian farm; jets scrambled — strongest qualification. Belgian drones (Nov 1-5) were not officially attributed to Russia — rejected. Earliest qualifying event is November 10-11.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: November 10-11, 2025: [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/83N44CQ) and [AP News](https://apnews.com/article/romania-drone-fragments-russia-ukraine-daa57cb972d1c6f7eb7b8cb7fb3fa93a) report Romania's MoD confirmed 'possible drone fragments' from drones 'similar to those used by the Russian military' were found 5km inside Romanian territory during Russian strikes. Foreign Minister Oana Toiu described it as part of 'Russia's war of aggression.' November 25, 2025: [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/russian-drones-breach-nato-airspace-in-long-range-strikes-ukraine-romania-11103426) reports Romania's defense ministry confirmed two drone incursions. [Firstpost](https://www.firstpost.com/world/romania-scrambles-nato-jets-after-deepest-ever-drone-incursion-calls-it-russian-provocation-13954019.html) reports Romanian Defence Minister Ionut Mosteanu described it as 'Russian provocation.' [DW](https://www.dw.com/en/russian-drones-fly-undeterred-over-moldova-and-romania/a-74944321) confirms 'Russian drone crashed on a farm in Puiesti, Romania.' [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/863F963) confirms 'Romania's defence ministry confirmed that a drone crossed from Vylkove, Ukraine, into the Chilia Veche area of Tulcea County in eastern Romania.' All criteria satisfied: NATO member (Romania), official confirmation (MoD + Defence Minister + Foreign Minister), drone (UAV), Russian attribution, within window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First qualifying event: November 10-11, 2025 overnight. AFP published 2025-11-11, AP News published 2025-11-11. The drone fragments were discovered after Romanian radars detected drone groups 'just after midnight' on November 11, 2025. Official confirmation by Romanian MoD published on November 11, 2025. More explicit qualifying event on November 25, 2025 at approximately 06:30 local time (Romania time), confirmed by defense ministry same day.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The November 10-11, 2025 event appears to be the first qualifying event within the window (October 31 - November 30, 2025). No earlier incidents within the window were found with official Romanian or other NATO government confirmation of Russian-launched drone/missile airspace entry. The DW article notes this was the '13th airspace breach since Russia's full-scale invasion' for Romania, with prior ones occurring before October 31, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Romanian President Nicusor Dan called the Nov 10-11 incident 'accidental,' but this does not contradict official MoD confirmation of Russian drone fragments inside Romanian territory — 'accidental' refers to unintentional straying, not denial of Russian origin. The DW article notes 'Romania has not formally accused Russia of deliberate targeting' for Nov 25, but the Defence Minister DID call it a 'Russian provocation.' AFP explicitly confirms Romania's MoD confirmed 'a drone crossed from Vylkove, Ukraine into' Romanian airspace on Nov 25. Multiple high-quality sources (AP, AFP, Reuters-cited, DW, Euronews) all corroborate. No source contradicts the Russian attribution of the drones.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: YES. Romania, a NATO member state, officially confirmed through its Ministry of National Defence and Defence Minister that Russian-launched drones entered Romanian sovereign airspace on at least two occasions within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window: (1) November 10-11, 2025 — drone fragments from Russian military drones found 5km inside Romania, confirmed by MoD and Foreign Minister (AP News, AFP, Euronews); (2) November 25, 2025 — two Russian drone incursions confirmed by MoD, described as 'Russian provocation' by Defence Minister, drone crashed on Romanian farm (AFP, Newsweek, DW, Firstpost). First occurrence within window: November 10-11, 2025.

question: Will Russia capture Drobysheve by February 28?
description:

If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. subquestions.question: Will the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) confirm a Russian advance within or the capture of Drobysheve, Yarova, or Sosnova between 2026-01-30 and 2026-02-18?
subquestions.background_information: On January 27, 2026, Russian General Staff Chief Valery Gerasimov claimed that the 20th Army was completing the capture of Drobysheve, Yarova, and Sosnova in the Donetsk region, with over 90% of residential areas under Russian control. However, the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) has recently disputed several of Gerasimov's claims (such as the capture of Kupyansk-Uzlovaya), noting a pattern of exaggerated Russian military achievements. The ultimate question asks whether Russia will capture a specific intersection in Drobysheve by February 28, 2026. Therefore, checking if ISW verifies any Russian advances in Drobysheve or the adjacent settlements of Yarova and Sosnova provides a strong early indicator. Sources: ISW Official Site (https://www.understandingwar.org/), DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-30 and 2026-02-18 (inclusive), the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) publishes a 'Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment' on its official website (https://www.understandingwar.org/) that explicitly confirms in its text that Russian forces have advanced within, entered, or gained control of any territory in the settlements of Drobysheve, Yarova, or Sosnova (Donetsk Oblast). To qualify: 1. The confirmation must appear in the text of a daily assessment published between 2026-01-30 and 2026-02-18. 2. The language must indicate an ISW assessment of actual Russian progress (e.g., 'Russian forces recently advanced in Drobysheve' or 'Geolocated footage indicates Russian forces captured Yarova'). 3. Statements that only report unverified Russian claims (e.g., 'The Russian MoD claimed that forces captured Drobysheve, but ISW has not observed visual confirmation') will NOT trigger a Yes resolution. 4. If the ISW confirms an advance but states it occurred prior to 2026-01-30, it still counts as long as the publication occurs within the resolution window. If no such explicit confirmation is published by ISW between 2026-01-30 and 2026-02-18, the question will resolve No. If the ISW website becomes permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting or DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) showing confirmed advances in these areas during the window may be used.
subquestions.rationale: If Russian forces are to capture the specified intersection in Drobysheve by February 28, their progress must be observable in the preceding weeks. Russian leadership has claimed near-total control of Drobysheve, Yarova, and Sosnova, but ISW has noted recent Russian exaggerations. Whether ISW independently confirms any advances in this specific sector by mid-February is a strong crux: an ISW confirmation validates the Russian claims to some degree, making the intersection's capture by February 28 highly plausible. A lack of confirmation strongly implies the claims are false and the intersection will not be reached in time.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: ISW publishes a 'Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment' between 2026-01-30 and 2026-02-18 explicitly confirming Russian forces have advanced within, entered, or gained control of territory in Drobysheve, Yarova, or Sosnova (Donetsk Oblast). Observable evidence: direct quotes from ISW assessments at understandingwar.org naming these settlements as areas of confirmed Russian progress. Key entities: ISW, Russian forces, Drobysheve, Yarova, Sosnova. Timing: publication between Jan 30-Feb 18, 2026.

'ISW Russian offensive assessment Lyman Drobysheve February 2026' - to find ISW daily assessments; 3. 'ISW Drobysheve Yarova Sosnova Russian capture 20th Army' - to find ISW response to Gerasimov claims; 4. 'ISW Gerasimov lying Drobysheve January 28 2026' - to find ISW debunking; 5. 'DeepState confirmed Russian capture Drobysheve Yarova Sosnova' - for alternative fallback evidence
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Gerasimov Jan 27 claim about 20th Army completing capture of Drobysheve, Yarova, Sosnova (Russian MoD claim - explicitly excluded by resolution criteria); (2) ISW Jan 28 article debunking Gerasimov claims - focused on Kupyansk-Uzlovaya, Kovsharovka, Glushkovka, NOT Drobysheve/Yarova/Sosnova; (3) Ukrainian General Staff reports throughout window mentioning Russian attacks 'near Drobysheve' - these indicate fighting, not confirmed captures; (4) Medium.com Feb 15 update noting 'no territorial movement in Lyman direction'; (5) No article found explicitly stating ISW confirmed Russian advances in these three settlements. question: Will Prince Andrew be named in newly released Epstein files by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump Administration (including any federal court) publicly releases previously unreleased files pertaining to the illegal activities of Jeffrey Epstein which contain any mention of the listed individual between market creation and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only previously unreleased files, as of market creation, which contain novel material not previously available to the public will qualify. Documents that are merely re-released, have had redactions removed, repackaged, or newly publicized versions of already available information do not qualify.

Any mention of the listed individual in connection with Jeffrey Epstein will qualify, regardless of if connected to nefarious or illegal activities.

Previously unreleased files is inclusive of any written, audio, photo or video documentation (e.g., qualifying photos which depict the listed individual will count).

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the DOJ Office of the Inspector General publicly confirm an investigation into the handling or delayed release of the Epstein files by January 25, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
On December 25, 2025, the U.S. Justice Department admitted it would miss the congressionally mandated deadline under the Epstein Files Transparency Act to release all Jeffrey Epstein-related records, citing the discovery of over one million previously unidentified documents that would take 'several more weeks' to review (https://face2faceafrica.com/article/justice-department-admits-newly-found-epstein-files-will-delay-disclosure-for-weeks). The delay sparked widespread criticism over potential cover-ups and unjustified redactions. In response, a bipartisan group of senators urged the DOJ's Office of the Inspector General (OIG) to investigate the delay and the department's history of resistance to disclosure. If the OIG formally investigates, the Justice Department will face heightened scrutiny, making it significantly harder to stall the release of the remaining documents beyond the ultimate March 2026 deadline. A timely release of the newly discovered files is essential for Prince Andrew's name to surface in newly unreleased documents.

Sources:
Face2Face Africa: https://face2faceafrica.com/article/justice-department-admits-newly-found-epstein-files-will-delay-disclosure-for-weeks
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General (DOJ OIG) publicly announces or confirms the initiation of an investigation, review, or audit into the DOJ's processing, redaction, or delayed release of the Jeffrey Epstein files between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-25 (inclusive). Qualifying events include an official press release or report on the DOJ OIG website (https://oig.justice.gov), a publicly released formal letter to Congress from the Inspector General, or confirmation from a DOJ OIG spokesperson reported by at least two credible news organizations (e.g., Reuters, AP News, or The New York Times). If no such investigation or review is publicly confirmed to have been initiated between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-25, the question resolves No. Delayed announcements beyond 2026-01-25 will not count toward a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate outcome depends heavily on whether the DOJ actually releases the remaining 1 million Epstein documents before March 31, 2026. Given the DOJ's recent announcement of a multi-week delay, an official OIG investigation would act as a strong forcing mechanism for transparency and timely compliance. Forecasting an OIG probe serves as a proxy for whether the DOJ will be pressured into releasing unredacted or comprehensive files (which would likely name prominent figures like Prince Andrew) rather than successfully stonewalling the release.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes: The DOJ OIG must PUBLICLY CONFIRM (not merely be asked to) an investigation/review/audit into the DOJ's processing, redaction, or delayed release of Epstein files between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-25. Qualifying events: (1) official press release/report on oig.justice.gov, (2) publicly released formal letter to Congress from IG, or (3) confirmation from DOJ OIG spokesperson reported by at least two credible news orgs. Key entities: Acting IG Don Berthiaume, DOJ OIG, Epstein Files Transparency Act. Threshold: Public confirmation of initiation of investigation/review/audit — not just requests made to the OIG.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'DOJ Office Inspector General investigation Epstein files delayed release' (2025-12-27 to 2026-01-25) — to find OIG confirmation; 2. 'DOJ OIG Epstein documents review audit 2025 2026' — to find OIG audit announcement; 3. 'DOJ Inspector General OIG confirm investigation Epstein files January 2026' — to find OIG confirmation specifically; 4. 'OIG Don Berthiaume Epstein investigation announcement press release' — to find specific IG announcement; 5. 'oig.justice.gov Epstein files investigation press release 2026' — to find official OIG website announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events identified: (1) Bipartisan group of 12 senators sent letter to Acting IG Berthiaume on Christmas Eve demanding audit [Zero Hedge, Dec 31]; (2) CBS News (Jan 8) reported calls for OIG review from survivors, Congress, and Democracy Defenders Fund — but explicitly stated 'The OIG has not confirmed or commented on the current requests'; (3) 19 Epstein survivors sent letter to Acting IG Berthiaume on Jan 14, 2026 requesting investigation [CNN, KTVZ, Raw Story, Anadolu Agency]; (4) Alternet (Jan 16) noted OIG's limited authority and 'questioned whether the OIG will even accept the request.' ALL candidate events represent REQUESTS TO the OIG — not confirmations BY the OIG. No event found where the OIG publicly confirmed, announced, or initiated an investigation. The CBS News article of Jan 8 explicitly states 'The OIG has not confirmed or commented on the current requests.'
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require the DOJ OIG to PUBLICLY ANNOUNCE OR CONFIRM the initiation of an investigation, review, or audit. The evidence shows: (a) Congress members requested OIG investigation [CBS News Jan 8](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/delayed-epstein-files-release-triggers-calls-for-internal-watchdog-review/); (b) Epstein survivors requested OIG investigation [CNN Jan 14](https://us.cnn.com/2026/01/14/politics/jeffrey-epstein-survivors-doj-inspector-general); (c) Democracy Defenders Fund requested OIG review [CBS News Jan 8]; (d) CBS News explicitly reported 'The OIG has not confirmed or commented on the current requests' as of Jan 8 [CBS News Jan 8]; (e) Alternet (Jan 16) noted OIG has not confirmed it will accept the request. NONE of these match the resolution criteria — they are requests to the OIG, not confirmations from the OIG.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp can be extracted because no confirming event was found. The most recent relevant reporting (Jan 16, 2026) still indicates no OIG confirmation had occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was found — the condition of OIG publicly confirming an investigation was never met within the window based on all available evidence.
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checked: (1) CBS News (Jan 8) explicitly confirms 'The OIG has not confirmed or commented on the current requests'; (2) Alternet (Jan 16) confirms OIG had not confirmed acceptance; (3) CNN (Jan 14) reports survivors 'urged' OIG — no response noted; (4) Multiple articles through Jan 16 consistently describe the situation as external parties calling for OIG action, with no OIG response. No contradictory evidence found suggesting OIG confirmed an investigation. The window closes Jan 25, and the most recent coverage up to Jan 16-17 shows no OIG confirmation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence consistently shows that while multiple parties (senators, survivors, watchdog groups) requested the DOJ OIG to open an investigation into the handling of Epstein files, the DOJ OIG never publicly confirmed, announced, or initiated such an investigation within the window (2025-12-27 to 2026-01-25). The resolution criteria specifically require the OIG to publicly confirm initiation — not merely be asked. Since the OIG explicitly declined to comment as of Jan 8 (per CBS News), and no subsequent OIG confirmation was reported through Jan 16-17, the question resolves No. The window closed on 2026-01-25 without the required confirming event.

subquestions.question: Will Maria Corina Machado make a confirmed in-person public appearance anywhere in the world between December 17, 2025, and January 13, 2026?
subquestions.background_information: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado was awarded the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize but did not attend the award ceremony in Oslo on December 10, 2025. According to reports, she has not appeared in public for 11 months due to safety concerns and hiding from the Maduro regime. Instead, she has engaged with international leaders remotely, such as delivering a live video address to the Council of the Americas business conference in Miami on December 16, 2025, an event attended by U.S. President Donald Trump. For Trump to meet Machado in person in 2026, she will likely need to come out of hiding and resume public appearances, or travel internationally to the United States. Assessing whether she emerges from hiding in early 2026 serves as a strong early indicator for the logistical feasibility of an in-person meeting with Trump later in the year. Sources: AP News: https://apnews.com/ | Council of the Americas: https://www.as-coa.org/ | The New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if credible media outlets, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) or the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), report that Maria Corina Machado made a confirmed, in-person public appearance anywhere in the world between 2025-12-17 and 2026-01-13 (inclusive). An 'in-person public appearance' is defined as her physical presence at an event, gathering, or location where members of the public or independent press are present and can visually confirm her presence. Remote video addresses, pre-recorded messages, or unverified claims of her whereabouts do not count toward a 'Yes' resolution. If no such public appearance is confirmed to have occurred between 2025-12-17 and 2026-01-13, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: A face-to-face meeting between Donald Trump and Maria Corina Machado in 2026 requires that Machado emerges from her 11-month period of deep hiding. If she begins making public appearances by early 2026, it would signal a significant change in her security posture or physical location (such as successfully leaving Venezuela), thereby dramatically increasing the logistical chances of an in-person meeting with Trump.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Maria Corina Machado physically present at an event/gathering where members of the public or independent press are present and can visually confirm her presence, between 2025-12-17T00:00:00Z and 2026-01-13T23:59:59Z. Observable evidence: credible media reports (Reuters, AP, or equivalent) explicitly describing an in-person appearance. Remote video/pre-recorded appearances do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Maria Corina Machado public appearance 2025 December' (to find any appearance in window), 2. 'Maria Corina Machado Venezuela opposition leader location sighting' (to find confirmed sightings), 3. 'Maria Corina Machado Nobel Prize ceremony Oslo December 10 2025 in person appearance' (to check pre-window appearances), 4. 'Maria Corina Machado Vatican Pope January 12 2026 meeting' (to verify Vatican appearance), 5. 'Maria Corina Machado Reuters AP confirmed appearance December 2025 January 2026' (to find authoritative sources), 6. 'Maria Corina Machado Fox News Hannity interview January 5 6 2026 location undisclosed video' (to verify whether Fox interview was remote or in-person), 7. 'Maria Corina Machado Vatican Pope Leo meeting January 12 2026 AP Reuters confirmed in person' (to verify with AP/Reuters).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) December 11, 2025 Oslo balcony appearance and press conference — REJECTED because it is BEFORE the resolution window start date of December 17, 2025. (B) December 17, 2025 departure from Oslo — sources confirm she left Oslo but location undisclosed; no confirmed in-person public appearance in the window from this date. (C) January 5-6, 2026 Fox News Hannity interview — REJECTED as qualifying event because multiple sources explicitly state she spoke 'from an undisclosed location,' making it a remote video interview, not an in-person public appearance. (D) January 12, 2026 Vatican meeting with Pope Leo XIV — ACCEPTED as qualifying event: confirmed in-person meeting at the Vatican Apostolic Palace, verified by Vatican daily bulletin, AFP, UPI/AP, USA Today, WCNC/Associated Press, Catholic World Report, Vatican News, Chicago Tribune, Linda Ikeji Blog. Vatican video clip showed Machado and the Pope shaking hands. The Vatican official confirmation counts as independent press verification of her physical presence.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The January 12, 2026 Vatican meeting fully satisfies the criteria: (1) In-person physical presence — confirmed by [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/92DY263), [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/01/12/vatican-machado-meets-pope-leo/6851768238910/), [USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2026/01/12/pope-leo-meets-venezuela-opposition-leader-machado/88140028007/), [WCNC/Associated Press](https://www.wcnc.com/article/syndication/associatedpress/pope-leo-xiv-meets-with-venezuelan-opposition-leader-maria-corina-machado-in-a-surprise-audience/616-44f613f0-8a75-49bb-9282-d98e247f9644), [Vatican News](https://www.vaticannews.va/en/pope/news/2026-01/pope-leo-xiv-maria-corina-machado-venezuela.html), and [Catholic World Report](https://www.catholicworldreport.com/2026/01/12/pope-leo-xiv-meets-venezuelan-opposition-leader-maria-corina-machado/). (2) Visually confirmed by Vatican video clip showing handshake at Pope's desk (per Linda Ikeji Blog). (3) Date January 12, 2026 is within the resolution window. (4) Vatican confirmed the meeting in its official daily bulletin, making it independently verified. (5) Press reported on her physical presence at the Vatican. The WCNC article is credited to the Associated Press, satisfying the resolution criteria for credible media sources.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: January 12, 2026, at approximately 12:00 noon (Vatican/Rome local time) per Catholic World Report which states the meeting was 'added to the pontiff's agenda at 12:00 p.m.' Multiple sources confirm the date as January 12, 2026. This corresponds to approximately 2026-01-12T11:00:00Z in UTC (Rome is UTC+1 in January).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The December 11, 2025 Oslo appearance (before the window) is excluded. The Fox News interview (Jan 5-6, 2026) was from an undisclosed remote location, not an in-person public appearance. No other in-person appearances within the window were found between December 17, 2025, and January 11, 2026. The Vatican meeting on January 12, 2026 appears to be the first qualifying in-person public appearance within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence: (1) Sources from early January consistently noted Machado's 'whereabouts unknown' and location 'undisclosed' — this is consistent with her not making in-person public appearances until January 12. (2) The Fox News interview was remote — confirmed by 'from an undisclosed location' language in NDTV, Daily Sabah, and other sources. (3) The Vatican meeting is confirmed by multiple independent, authoritative sources including AFP (wire agency), UPI, AP (via WCNC), USA Today, Vatican News, and ANSA — no conflicting reports found. (4) The 'surprise' nature of the Vatican meeting was later added to the Vatican's official daily bulletin, which is a formal confirmation of in-person presence. No contradictory evidence exists.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution = YES. Maria Corina Machado made a confirmed in-person public appearance at the Vatican on January 12, 2026, when she met with Pope Leo XIV in the Vatican Apostolic Palace. This is confirmed by multiple credible sources including AFP, UPI, the Associated Press (via WCNC), USA Today, Vatican News, and ANSA. The meeting was within the resolution window (December 17, 2025 – January 13, 2026). This constitutes a physically present appearance where the Vatican (as official body) and independent press visually confirmed her presence. The resolution criteria are satisfied.

question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring. 

The primary source of resolution for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. military or Coast Guard destroy at least one suspected drug-smuggling vessel in the Caribbean Sea between November 15, 2025, and December 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Tensions between the United States and Venezuela have risen dramatically amid a major U.S. military buildup in the Caribbean Sea. The U.S. has deployed naval assets, including the USS Gerald R. Ford carrier strike group, destroyers, and advanced aircraft, to conduct counter-narcotics operations (Newsweek https://www.newsweek.com; The Irish Times https://www.irishtimes.com). As part of this campaign, the U.S. has conducted multiple unprecedented kinetic strikes on suspected drug-smuggling vessels. Reports vary, but indicate that since September 2025, the U.S. has destroyed between 6 and 14 such vessels, resulting in dozens of casualties (ABC News https://abcnews.go.com; Raw Story https://www.rawstory.com). Venezuela has condemned these operations as a pretext for regime change and has mobilized its armed forces in response (Defense World https://www.defenseworld.net). Whether the U.S. continues these kinetic strikes is a critical indicator of its willingness to maintain or escalate military pressure in the region, which could precipitate a direct engagement with Venezuelan forces. Sources: Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com | The Irish Times: https://www.irishtimes.com | ABC News: https://abcnews.go.com | Raw Story: https://www.rawstory.com | Defense World: https://www.defenseworld.net
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. Southern Command, U.S. Coast Guard, or a consensus of credible media reporting confirms that U.S. military or Coast Guard forces have used kinetic force (e.g., missiles, gunfire) to destroy or sink at least one vessel suspected of drug smuggling or other illicit activity in the Caribbean Sea or waters near Venezuela. The qualifying incident must occur between the start date of 2025-11-15 and the end date of 2025-12-15 (inclusive). 'Destroy or sink' means the vessel is rendered completely inoperable and either sinks or is intentionally destroyed by U.S. forces. The strike must be carried out by U.S. military or Coast Guard forces. Vessels officially belonging to the Venezuelan military are excluded from this question (as a strike on a Venezuelan military vessel would trigger the ultimate question directly). If the vessel struck is a civilian, unidentified, or alleged cartel drug-smuggling vessel, it counts for this question. Information will be verified via official press releases from the U.S. Southern Command (https://www.southcom.mil/), the U.S. Department of Defense (https://www.defense.gov/), or major news outlets (e.g., Reuters https://www.reuters.com, AP News https://apnews.com). If the event is delayed or information remains unconfirmed by the end of the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The continuation of U.S. kinetic strikes on suspected drug vessels in the Caribbean is a key crux for whether a direct military engagement with Venezuela will occur. These strikes are the primary aggressive action currently being taken by U.S. forces in the theater. If the strikes continue, they maintain a high operational tempo and increase the risk of miscalculation, accidental targeting of Venezuelan assets, or a retaliatory response from Venezuela. If the strikes cease, it may indicate a U.S. policy shift toward de-escalation, significantly lowering the probability of a direct US-Venezuela military engagement.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: U.S. military or Coast Guard uses kinetic force to destroy/sink at least one vessel suspected of drug smuggling in the Caribbean Sea or waters near Venezuela between Nov 15 - Dec 15, 2025. Required observable evidence: Official SOUTHCOM/DoD press release or major news outlet confirming a kinetic strike destroying a drug-suspected vessel in the Caribbean (not Eastern Pacific) or waters near Venezuela within the window. Key threshold: vessel must be destroyed/sunk (not merely disabled). Key exclusion: Venezuelan military vessels don't count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'US military Coast Guard destroy sink drug smuggling vessel Caribbean 2025' - to find any confirmed Caribbean strikes; 2. 'SOUTHCOM drug interdiction vessel destroyed Caribbean November December 2025' - to find official SOUTHCOM confirmations; 3. 'US Coast Guard gunfire sunk boat drug trafficking Caribbean 2025' - to find Coast Guard-specific kinetic actions; 4. 'US military strike Caribbean drug boat November 2025 destroy sink' - targeted geographic search; 5. 'Operation Southern Spear strike vessel November 15-30 2025' - to find early window events; 6. 'SOUTHCOM lethal kinetic strike Caribbean November 15 2025 drug vessel' - specific date/location search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events identified: (1) Nov 10 strike in Caribbean (20th strike) - BEFORE window opens; confirmed by DVIDS, The Hindu, Boston Globe. (2) Nov 15 strike - confirmed by multiple sources as in EASTERN PACIFIC (21st strike), killing 3 people. Confirmed by Anadolu Agency, Daily Wire, BizPacReview, Chosun as Eastern Pacific. One lower-quality source (newsdirectory3.com) says 'Caribbean' but appears to conflate events. (3) Dec 4-5 strike in Eastern Pacific (22nd strike), killing 4 people, confirmed by The Hill, BNO News, Breitbart, Firstpost, US Southern Command. The Hill explicitly states this was 'the first U.S. strike against a suspected drug-smuggling vessel since mid-November 2025,' suggesting no Caribbean strikes occurred between the Nov 15 Eastern Pacific strike and the Dec 4-5 Eastern Pacific strike. The September 2 Caribbean strike + follow-on strikes account for all 11 Caribbean deaths in the total count. No confirmed Caribbean-specific strike identified within the Nov 15 - Dec 15 window based on authoritative sources.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires: (1) Caribbean Sea or waters near Venezuela - Most strikes within the window (Nov 15, Dec 4-5) are confirmed as EASTERN PACIFIC, not Caribbean Sea or waters near Venezuela; (2) Kinetic force used - Yes, confirmed; (3) Drug-suspected vessel - Yes, suspected narcotics vessels targeted; (4) Vessel destroyed - Yes, vessels destroyed in strikes. The geographic requirement is the key issue. The [BNO News article](https://bnonews.com/index.php/2025/12/u-s-launches-new-strike-on-alleged-drug-vessel-in-eastern-pacific-killing-4/) confirms the Dec 5 strike was Eastern Pacific. The [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-strike-on-boat-in-eastern-pacific-involved-in-illicit-narcotics-smuggling-kills-3/3745530) confirms Nov 15 strike was Eastern Pacific. The [DVIDS source](https://www.dvidshub.net/video/987855/lethal-kinetic-strike-nov-10-2025) for the Nov 10 Caribbean strike places it before the window. However, [The Intercept tracker](https://theintercept.com/2025/11/17/trump-boat-strikes-death-toll-caribbean-pacific/) documents strikes in the Caribbean theater throughout, and [WCIV/ABC News 4](https://abcnews4.com/news/nation-world/us-military-strikes-vessel-carrying-alleged-narcoterrorists-department-of-war-confirms-pete-hegseth-marco-rubio-donald-trump-venezuela) confirms the Nov 15 strike was part of an ongoing campaign 'in the Caribbean,' though the specific strike was in the Eastern Pacific. The resolution criteria is broad enough to potentially include the Eastern Pacific if 'waters near Venezuela' is interpreted broadly, but geographically Venezuela is not on the Eastern Pacific coast — Venezuela borders the Caribbean Sea/Atlantic. Critically, the criteria says 'Caribbean Sea or waters near Venezuela' and the Eastern Pacific is neither.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The most reliable timestamps for strikes within the window: Nov 15, 2025 (Eastern Pacific) - confirmed by multiple sources; Dec 4-5, 2025 (Eastern Pacific) - confirmed by multiple sources. For Caribbean-specific strikes: Nov 10, 2025 (before window); Sept 2, 2025 (well before window). No confirmed timestamp of a Caribbean-specific strike within the Nov 15 - Dec 15 window found in authoritative sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: If any Caribbean/near-Venezuela strike within window exists, the first would need to be identified. question: Will 7-9 SpaceX Starship launches successfully reach Space in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if between 7 (inclusive) and 9 (inclusive) SpaceX Starship launches successfully reach an altitude of 62 miles above sea level between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A successful launch is defined as the Starship taking off from its launchpad and reaching a minimum altitude of 62 miles above sea level. Any subsequent anomaly (e.g. an explosion) after the vehicle reaches 62 miles will have no bearing on the outcome.

The primary resolution source for this market will be SpaceX’s official video feed of the launches (e.g. via SpaceX YouTube Channel), as well as secondary video feeds or written reports if necessary. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX fully stack a Starship vehicle on the Orbital Launch Mount at Starbase between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, SpaceX successfully completed Starship's 10th flight, which marked the 4th test flight of 2025. To achieve the ultimate question's threshold of 7 to 9 successful space-reaching flights in 2025, SpaceX needs to execute at least 3 more successful flights in the final four months of the year (September through December). Elon Musk recently outlined an accelerated timeline, aiming for a flight cadence of once every 3 to 4 weeks. Achieving such a high cadence requires extremely rapid turnaround of the launch infrastructure. 

Before any Starship can fly or complete final pre-launch testing like a Wet Dress Rehearsal (WDR), SpaceX must "fully stack" the vehicle—mating the Starship upper stage atop the Super Heavy booster on the Orbital Launch Mount (OLM). Because Flight 10 occupied the OLM until late August, preparing the pad and stacking the next vehicle (Flight 11) is the immediate operational bottleneck. If SpaceX fails to stack a vehicle by October 1, it provides strong evidence that the 3-4 week launch cadence is slipping, making it highly unlikely they will reach the 7-flight threshold by December 31.

Sources:
Yahoo News - SpaceX Starship flight 10 coverage: https://www.yahoo.com/news
SpaceX Official Website: https://www.spacex.com
NASASpaceflight: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if SpaceX fully stacks a Starship vehicle on the Orbital Launch Mount (OLM) at Starbase, Texas, at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). 

"Fully stacks" is specifically defined as the physical placement and mating of a Starship upper stage atop a Super Heavy booster while resting on the OLM. The vehicle does not need to launch, undergo a static fire, or complete a Wet Dress Rehearsal (WDR) during this window; visual confirmation of a complete stack is sufficient. If the vehicle is fully stacked and subsequently unstacked within the time window, the condition is still met and the question resolves Yes. 

If no full stacking event occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question resolves No. Delayed events extending past 2025-10-01 will not count toward a Yes resolution.

Resolution will primarily rely on visual confirmation and reporting from NASASpaceflight's continuous Starbase coverage (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com) or official communications, videos, and images released by SpaceX (https://www.spacex.com or https://x.com/SpaceX). In the event of minor timeline discrepancies, the earliest publicly verifiable timestamp of the completed stacking operation will be used.
subquestions.rationale: SpaceX must maintain a launch cadence of roughly one flight per month to achieve 7-9 total successful flights in 2025. Stacking the vehicle on the launch mount is a strictly necessary precursor to any launch or final testing. If they cannot reach this milestone within one month of the previous launch, it is an early, highly informative indicator that their turnaround time is too slow to meet the end-of-year target.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Physical placement and mating of Starship upper stage atop Super Heavy booster on the OLM at Starbase, Texas, between 2025-09-01T00:00:00Z and 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z inclusive. Observable evidence: visual confirmation/reporting of the complete stack on the OLM. Key entities: Ship (upper stage), Super Heavy booster, OLM at Starbase. The stages must be physically mated on the OLM.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'SpaceX Starship full stack OLM Starbase September 2025' — to find stacking events in window. 2) 'Starship Super Heavy stacking Orbital Launch Mount 2025' — for any stacking news. 3) 'Starship Flight 11 full stack mating upper stage booster OLM September 2025' — specific mating event. 4) 'Starship Ship 37 Booster 15 stacked launch mount September 2025' — specific vehicle stacking. 5) 'SpaceX Starship wet dress rehearsal WDR stacked Flight 11 preparation October 2025' — pre-launch activities. 6) 'Starship full stack mated booster upper stage launch pad September October 2025' — general stacking search. 7) 'SpaceX Starship booster rolled out pad October 9 10 11 stacked 2025' — exact date of booster arrival and stacking.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Sept 17, 2025: Ship (upper stage) moved to pad, held by chopsticks. (2) Sept 23, 2025: Ship static fire conducted (upper stage only, on OLM). (3) ~Oct 7, 2025: Chopsticks practicing stacking maneuver (not yet stacked). (4) ~Oct 9, 2025: Super Heavy booster rolled out to pad. (5) ~Oct 10-12, 2025: Full stacking occurred (booster + ship mated on OLM). (6) Oct 13, 2025: Flight 11 launched. Rejected: No evidence of full stacking (both stages mated) within the Sept 1–Oct 1 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Per [Yahoo/USA TODAY, Sept 19-20](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/next-starship-launch-date-spacex-090455831.html): 'The vehicle has not yet been mated with the 232-foot Super Heavy booster' as of Sept 17. Per [Digital Trends, Oct 7](https://www.digitaltrends.com/space/spacex-preps-starbase-tower-11-starship-launch/): Chopsticks were 'practicing the maneuver to stack the upper-stage Ship onto the first-stage Super Heavy booster' — implying stacking had not yet occurred. Per [Space.com, Oct 9](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-moves-giant-super-heavy-booster-to-pad-ahead-of-starship-flight-11-launch-photos): Super Heavy booster moved to pad on/around Oct 9. Per [NewsBytes, Oct 13](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/science/spacex-starship-11th-flight-test-today-timings-live-streaming-details/story): 'images have been released showing the upper-stage Ship being stacked atop the first-stage Super Heavy booster.' Full stacking occurred between Oct 9–12, 2025 — after the Oct 1 deadline.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The full stacking (mating of Ship atop Super Heavy on OLM) occurred approximately October 9-12, 2025. The Super Heavy booster was not at the pad until ~Oct 9, and images of the full stack appeared around Oct 12-13. No evidence places stacking within Sept 1–Oct 1 window. Exact timestamp within window: none found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying stacking event occurred within the Sept 1–Oct 1 window. The first (and only) full stacking for Flight 11 occurred in early-to-mid October 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources confirm: (1) As of Sept 17-20, Ship was at pad but NOT mated to booster. No contradictory evidence suggests stacking occurred before Oct 1. The static fire of the upper stage on ~Sept 23 was conducted with only the Ship on the OLM (no booster mated), which does not meet the 'fully stacked' criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The full stacking (physical mating of Ship atop Super Heavy on OLM) did not occur within the Sept 1–Oct 1 window. The booster didn't even arrive at the pad until ~Oct 9, and stacking occurred approximately Oct 10-12, 2025. The question resolves No, with the window closing at 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z with no qualifying event.
