subquestions.question: Will OpenAI officially announce or release a standalone web browser between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
OpenAI has been developing its own AI-based web browser to expand its ecosystem of consumer applications. In August 2025, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman expressed interest in acquiring Google's Chrome browser, but noted this would likely only happen if a U.S. court ordered Alphabet to divest it due to antitrust violations. On September 3, 2025, a federal judge ruled that Google does not have to sell Chrome to resolve its monopoly case, instead ordering data sharing with rivals. Given this ruling, Alphabet is highly unlikely to voluntarily sell its dominant browser to a major AI competitor. Consequently, OpenAI may accelerate the launch of its own proprietary browser. Tracking whether OpenAI announces its own browser provides a strong early indicator: launching an independent browser would signal a pivot away from acquiring Chrome, directly informing the ultimate question's outcome.

Sources:
Mint: https://www.livemint.com/
AP News: https://apnews.com/
Computerworld: https://www.computerworld.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if OpenAI officially announces, releases a public beta, or fully launches a standalone web browser product between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025, inclusive. 

To qualify as a "standalone web browser," the product must be a distinct browser software application (for desktop or mobile operating systems) intended for general web browsing. Browser extensions, standalone search engine websites, or new browsing features integrated into the existing ChatGPT application do not qualify.

The announcement or release must be confirmed via official OpenAI channels (e.g., a blog post on https://openai.com/news, an official press release, or a public statement/presentation by CEO Sam Altman or another authorized executive). The qualifying event must occur strictly within the resolution window: starting on October 1, 2025, and ending on October 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET. If no such announcement or release occurs within this timeframe, the question resolves "No". In cases of ambiguity regarding whether a product constitutes a "standalone web browser," a consensus of credible tech journalism (e.g., https://www.bloomberg.com/, https://www.theverge.com/, https://techcrunch.com/) will be used to determine the industry's classification of the product.
subquestions.rationale: If OpenAI commits to its own standalone AI browser by officially announcing or releasing it in October 2025, it strongly indicates a strategic decision to build rather than buy. This would severely decrease the probability of OpenAI acquiring Chrome by the end of the year, serving as a highly informative crux for forecasters.

Browser extensions, search engine websites, or ChatGPT-integrated features do not qualify.

question: U.S. x Russia Nuclear deal by December 31?

Only agreements that are publicly announced and acknowledged by both the U.S. and Russia will qualify. The agreement must pertain to nuclear arms control or limitation—such as a treaty, framework, or memorandum—addressing matters including (but not limited to) nuclear warheads, delivery systems, verification mechanisms, or strategic stability.

An extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty will qualify, provided it is publicly announced as a concluded agreement by both parties within the time frame. Exploratory discussions or stated intent to extend without a finalized agreement will not qualify.

Agreements that include both the United States and Russia as named parties—whether bilateral or as part of a broader multilateral framework—will qualify, provided the agreement directly addresses nuclear arms control.

The agreement does not need to be ratified or implemented for this market to resolve "Yes"; a formal announcement of a concluded agreement is sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the U.S. government (e.g., the White House, State Department) and/or the Russian Federation (e.g., the Kremlin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs). However, a clear and overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming that such an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the United States and the Russian Federation hold formal bilateral talks on nuclear arms control between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?

Following this, U.S. President Donald Trump indicated that the proposal sounded like a good idea. However, formalizing any such agreement or a broader arms control framework requires official bilateral negotiations. Security experts like Daryl G. Kimball of the Arms Control Association have emphasized that to finalize an extension, the Kremlin and the White House must formalize the arrangement and begin immediate negotiations. Because the ultimate question seeks a finalized agreement by December 31, 2025, tracking whether direct, formal talks actually commence in November is a critical early indicator. Sources: 1. TASS (https://tass.com) 2. Firstpost (https://www.firstpost.com) 3. Arms Control Association (https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/NewSTART)

subquestions.rationale: Reaching a finalized nuclear arms agreement by December 31, 2025, practically necessitates formal diplomatic talks beforehand. If the U.S. and Russia do not engage in dedicated bilateral arms control talks by November 30, it becomes highly improbable that a finalized agreement will be signed and announced before the end of the year, making this a strong early indicator.

question: Will Russia enter Borova by December 31?
description:

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the ISW map indicate Russian control or advance at coordinate 49.380, 37.695 (approximately 5km east of Borova) between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-20?

Throughout late 2024 and 2025, Russian forces have sustained localized offensive operations along the Kupiansk-Svatove-Kreminna line, aiming to push toward the Oskil river to establish a natural defensive barrier and disrupt Ukrainian logistics. Russian tactics in this sector have heavily relied on "a thousand cuts," deploying small infantry groups of four to six soldiers to infiltrate Ukrainian lines rather than executing massive mechanized breakthroughs. The coordinate 49.380, 37.695 corresponds to a location in the settlement of Shyikivka, approximately 5.3 kilometers almost directly east of Borova's center (49.374, 37.622). To enter Borova from the main eastern axis of advance, Russian forces would necessarily have to push through or immediately bypass this area. Establishing control over this 5km marker would place Russian forces on the immediate outskirts of Borova.

Institute for the Study of War (ISW) Interactive Map - https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
CNN (Reporting on Russian incremental tactics) - https://edition.cnn.com/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any time between the start_date of 2025-11-28 and the end_date of 2025-12-20 (inclusive), the specific coordinate 49.380, 37.695 is shaded under any of the following layers on the official ISW Ukraine map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375): "Assessed Russian Control", "Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine", "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", or "Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours". 

For a change on the ISW map to qualify, the relevant shading indicating Russian control or advance over the exact coordinate must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle to rule out temporary mapping errors or glitches. Once this qualifying condition is met within the specified time window (2025-11-28 to 2025-12-20), any subsequent loss of control of the coordinate will not affect the "Yes" resolution.

If the ISW map is rendered permanently unavailable during the resolution window, DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) will be used as the fallback source. In this fallback scenario, the question resolves Yes if the coordinate 49.380, 37.695 falls under Russian control (shaded red) or the "gray zone" (contested territory) on DeepStateMap between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-20. If neither map is available, the question will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting confirming Russian presence at the coordinate during the timeframe.
subquestions.rationale: Capturing or entering Borova by December 31, 2025, requires Russian forces to cross the remaining kilometers east of the settlement. The selected coordinate is exactly ~5 km east of Borova, serving as a direct gatekeeper. If Russian forces cannot reach this 5-kilometer threshold by December 20, their momentum and the tactical timeline strongly suggest they will lack the capacity to conquer the remaining fortified distance and enter Borova by December 31. Conversely, if they hit this milestone, an attack on Borova itself becomes highly probable, making this a perfect early-warning crux.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition: ISW map shades coordinate 49.380, 37.695 (5km east of Borova, Kharkiv Oblast) under Russian control/advance/infiltration/gains layers between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-20. Observable evidence would be direct ISW map screenshots or credible reports confirming the exact coordinate under Russian control. Key entities: Borova, Novoplatonivka, Kharkiv Oblast, ISW map.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: 'Russian advance Borova Kharkiv Oblast December 2025'; 'ISW map Russian control Borova Ukraine November December 2025'; 'Borova Ukraine Russian advance east Kharkiv November December 2025'; 'Borovsk Borova Kharkiv ISW Russian control 2025'; 'Russian advance east of Borova Kharkiv frontline December 2025 ISW'; 'Novoplatonivka Borova Russian advance Kharkiv December 2025'; 'ISW daily update Borova direction advance December 2025'; 'Kucherivka Borova direction Kharkiv Russian advance December 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: 1) ReliefWeb (22-28 Nov 2025): 'Russian forces advanced...in Kharkiv toward Kupiansk and Borova' — within window start (Nov 28 falls in this period). 2) Ukrainska Pravda (Nov 20): Russian advance 'near Borova' and near 'Borivska Andriivka' — just before window. 3) TASS/AA/Devdiscourse (Dec 16): Russia captured Novoplatonivka in Kharkiv region (confirmed as in Borova community). 4) Times of India (Dec 17): 'Russian forces are advancing toward Borovaya.' 5) Ukrinform (Dec 10-11): Attack 'in Kupiansk direction near Novoplatonivka' — suggesting area near Borova was contested before Dec 16. Rejected: Direct ISW map confirmation of specific coordinate was not found in any article.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Novoplatonivka is confirmed to be in the Borova community (Izium district, Kharkiv Oblast) per Ukrinform articles. Russia captured Novoplatonivka on Dec 16, 2025 per [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2059419) and [AA](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/russia-claims-capturing-another-village-in-ukraine/3772585). Russian forces were advancing 'toward Borova' per [Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/international/russia-wins-novoplatonovka-zelensky-digs-his-own-grave-as-ukrainian-frontlines-crumbles/videoshow/126033865.cms). However, the exact coordinate 49.380, 37.695 cannot be confirmed as Novoplatonivka without geographic cross-referencing. Novoplatonivka appears to be east/southeast of Borova but the exact distance/bearing is uncertain. The ISW map shading at this coordinate cannot be directly confirmed from news sources alone.

evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The coordinate is described as '5km east of Borova.' Novoplatonivka is described in a November article as a location 'near Borova' and is in the Borova community. The geographic fit is plausible but not confirmed. The ISW map was not directly accessed. Russian advance toward Borova is documented but ISW's specific shading at 49.380, 37.695 is not directly confirmed by any article. No definitive ISW map data available in news sources.
evidence.step8_final_decision: While there is substantial evidence that Russian forces advanced toward Borova and captured Novoplatonivka (which appears to be near or at the coordinate in question) during the window, the resolution criteria specifically require ISW map shading at the exact coordinate. No news article directly confirms ISW map shading at 49.380, 37.695. The evidence is indirect and requires geographic inference. Therefore, this cannot be resolved definitively.

question: Will Ukraine agree to cede territory to Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede any territory under its control at the time of the agreement is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. 

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will a formal ceasefire or cessation of hostilities agreement between Ukraine and the Russian Federation be publicly announced between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late 2025, the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine has seen shifting frontlines and renewed diplomatic pressure for a resolution. Reports indicate that Ukraine's Western allies have been discussing peace plans that might involve freezing the conflict along current battle lines, effectively leaving Russia with de facto control of occupied territories like Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia (https://www.dw.com). However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has consistently maintained that Ukraine will not formally cede territory it currently holds, though international mediators have suggested negotiations could lead to de facto recognition of Russian control over certain areas (https://www.firstpost.com). Any comprehensive peace agreement in 2025 that includes formal or de facto territorial concessions by Ukraine would likely necessitate an immediate cessation of hostilities to allow for final diplomatic negotiations and border demarcations. A formal ceasefire is a standard precursor to such treaties. If a ceasefire is not reached by the end of October 2025, the timeline to negotiate and finalize a complex territorial agreement by the end of the year becomes exceedingly tight.

Sources:
Deutsche Welle: https://www.dw.com
Firstpost: https://www.firstpost.com
Daily Sabah: https://www.dailysabah.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a mutual agreement for a ceasefire, armistice, or generalized cessation of hostilities between the armed forces of Ukraine and the Russian Federation is officially and publicly announced between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

The agreement must apply to the majority of the active frontline between the two nations. Localized truces (e.g., temporary humanitarian corridors, localized pauses for prisoner swaps, or holiday truces lasting less than 7 days) do not count.

The public announcement must occur within the resolution window (between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31), regardless of when the ceasefire is actually scheduled to take effect on the battlefield.

A unilateral ceasefire declaration by one party that is not explicitly accepted or adhered to by the other does not qualify.

Resolution will be based on official announcements from the Office of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en) or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation (https://mid.ru/en/). In the absence of direct official statements, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting from major international news agencies (e.g., Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com)) confirming that a mutual ceasefire agreement has been reached will suffice for a Yes resolution. If no such agreement is announced by 23:59 UTC on 2025-10-31, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A deal involving the cession of currently held territory requires significant diplomatic negotiation, which historically occurs after or alongside a formal ceasefire. If a ceasefire is established by late October, it strongly indicates that serious, substantive negotiations (which could include territorial concessions) are underway, significantly raising the probability of a final agreement by December 31, 2025. Conversely, if fighting continues uninterrupted through October, the remaining two months of the year are highly unlikely to be sufficient to negotiate and conclude a major territorial concession agreement.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: A MUTUAL agreement for a ceasefire, armistice, or generalized cessation of hostilities between Ukraine and Russia officially and publicly announced between Oct 1–31, 2025. Must apply to the majority of the frontline. Must be accepted by BOTH parties. Localized/short truces do not qualify. Observable evidence: Official statements from Ukrainian or Russian governments, or overwhelming consensus from major international news agencies confirming a mutual agreement.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Ukraine Russia ceasefire agreement October 2025' — to find any formal ceasefire announcement; 2) 'Ukraine Russia peace deal armistice cessation hostilities 2025' — to find any armistice or formal cessation; 3) 'Russia Ukraine ceasefire signed agreement announced October 2025' — to find a signed, formal deal; 4) 'Russia rejects ceasefire Ukraine October 2025' — to find evidence of non-agreement; 5) 'Ukraine Russia ceasefire deal announced end of October 2025' — to check late October; 6) 'Ukraine war fighting frontline combat October 31 2025' — to verify fighting continued.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Joint statement by Ukraine and European leaders on Oct 21, 2025 calling for ceasefire along current lines — but Russia explicitly rejected this. (2) Russia offered a localized 5-6 hour ceasefire near Pokrovsk, Dymytrov, and Kupiansk on Oct 30 for journalist access — this is a localized truce of less than 7 days and not accepted by Ukraine as a mutual agreement. (3) Ukraine and allies agreed to DEVELOP a ceasefire plan within 7-10 days (announced Oct 27) — this is a plan to be developed, not an actual ceasefire agreement. (4) Meeting of advisers scheduled for Oct 31/Nov 1 to DISCUSS plan details — still in planning stage. (5) Trump-Putin Budapest summit was put on hold after Russia rejected ceasefire proposals. All candidate events were rejected because: none constitute a mutual ceasefire agreement accepted by both Ukraine and Russia.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that matches the resolution criteria. Russia explicitly rejected all ceasefire proposals throughout October 2025: [Russia Rejects Europe's Frontlines Proposal](https://www.worthynews.com/109555-russia-rejects-europes-frontlines-proposal-for-ukraine-as-trump-putin-summit-in-doubt); [Lavrov: Russia's conditions unchanged](https://en.protothema.gr/2025/10/21/lavrov-russias-conditions-for-peace-in-ukraine-unchanged-since-alaska-summit/); [ISW: Kremlin signals unwillingness](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/4049711-kremlin-signals-unwillingness-to-accept-anything-less-than-ukrainian-capitulation-isw.html); [Moscow: no illusions about EU ceasefire plan](https://tass.com/politics/2035675). Active combat continued through Oct 30-31: [Russia strikes Ukraine Oct 22](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/russia-strikes-ukraine-as-latest-trump-peace-efforts-falter); [Pokrovsk fighting Oct 28-30](https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-russia-pokrovsk-war-battlefield-troops-/33577230.html); [Russian casualties Oct 29](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/4052624-russias-war-casualty-toll-in-ukraine-up-by-1150-over-past-day.html). The Russian limited ceasefire offer of Oct 30 was localized (3 areas, 5-6 hours) and unilateral — explicitly excluded by resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp found. The window closed on 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z with no mutual ceasefire agreement announced.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found anywhere in the October 1–31, 2025 window. The evidence is consistent across multiple searches — throughout the entire month, diplomacy was still in planning stages and Russia consistently rejected ceasefire proposals.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No credible source (Reuters, AP, official Ukrainian/Russian government) reported a mutual ceasefire agreement. Instead, all evidence confirms: (a) Russia rejected ceasefire proposals from Ukraine and European allies; (b) Active fighting continued throughout October 2025 with Russian strikes on Oct 22, Oct 28-30; (c) Trump-Putin Budapest summit was postponed after Russia rejected ceasefire; (d) Ukraine was still only developing a ceasefire PLAN as of Oct 27-28; (e) Russia's limited Oct 30 offer was localized and unilateral. The evidence is consistent: no mutual ceasefire was agreed.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout October 2025, despite intensive diplomatic activity (Ukraine-EU joint statement Oct 21, Trump's calls for ceasefire, ongoing negotiations), Russia repeatedly and explicitly rejected ceasefire proposals. Active combat continued across the frontline through the end of October. Ukraine was still in the early stages of developing a ceasefire plan (announced Oct 27) that would only be discussed by advisers on Oct 31/Nov 1. No mutual agreement for ceasefire, armistice, or generalized cessation of hostilities was publicly announced between Oct 1-31, 2025. The window closed with no qualifying event occurring.

question: Will 2025 be the second hottest year on record?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the data for the Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index for 2025 shows the second greatest increase of any previously recorded year when it is released. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An anomaly which is the second greatest of any previously recorded year for 2025 is necessary and sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes" immediately once the data becomes available, regardless of whether the figure for 2024 and/or 2025 is later revised.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the figure found in the table titled "Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)" under the column "No_Smoothing" in the row "2025" (https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt). If NASA's "Global Temperature Index" is rendered permanently unavailable, other information from NASA may be used. If no information for 2025 is provided by NASA by March 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) officially report that 2025 was the second-warmest year on record globally by January 11, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) tracks global surface air temperatures using the ERA5 dataset. According to news reports in December 2025, C3S indicated that the global average temperature anomaly for January to November 2025 tied with 2023 as the second-warmest on record, making 2025 virtually certain to finish as either the second- or third-hottest year globally, behind 2024. C3S typically releases its annual Global Climate Highlights report detailing the full year's rankings in the first or second week of January (often around January 8-10). Because NASA's GISTEMP dataset (the resolution source for the ultimate question) and the C3S dataset usually closely agree on global temperature rankings, the C3S announcement serves as a highly informative early indicator for the NASA record.

Sources:
Copernicus Press Releases: https://climate.copernicus.eu/news-and-media/press-releases
Copernicus Climate Bulletins: https://climate.copernicus.eu/climate-bulletins
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) officially publishes its annual global climate summary for 2025 (such as the "Global Climate Highlights 2025" or an equivalent press release) between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-11 (inclusive), and the publication explicitly states that the entire year 2025 was the second-warmest (or second-hottest) year on record globally, or tied for second-warmest.

This question resolves "No" if C3S publishes the aforementioned summary between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-11 and explicitly ranks 2025 as the third-warmest year on record globally, or any other rank (e.g., first, fourth) other than second (or tied for second). It also resolves "No" if C3S does not publish its annual summary for 2025 by 2026-01-11 at 23:59 UTC.

The primary resolution source will be the official announcements, press releases, and reports published on the Copernicus Climate Change Service website (https://climate.copernicus.eu/news-and-media/press-releases).
subquestions.rationale: C3S typically publishes its annual global temperature report a few days before NASA releases the GISTEMP dataset. Since both datasets track the same global climate phenomena closely, knowing whether C3S ranks 2025 as the second-warmest year serves as a highly accurate and timely crux to forecast the outcome of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Resolution requires: (1) C3S officially publishes its annual global climate summary for 2025 between Dec 30, 2025 and Jan 11, 2026 (inclusive); AND (2) The publication explicitly states 2025 was the second-warmest (or tied for second-warmest) year on record globally. Key entities: Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S), climate.copernicus.eu. Observable evidence: official press release or 'Global Climate Highlights 2025' published on C3S website within the window, with explicit second-warmest ranking.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Copernicus Climate Change Service C3S 2025 annual climate summary warmest year record' (to find official annual report); Query 2: 'C3S Copernicus 2025 global temperature ranking second warmest hottest year' (to find ranking); Query 3: 'Copernicus Climate Change Service Global Climate Highlights 2025 press release January 2026' (to find specific press release); Query 4: 'C3S Copernicus ERA5 2025 annual temperature confirmed second warmest third warmest global' (to find confirmed official ranking); Query 5: 'Copernicus climate.copernicus.eu annual report 2025 press release second warmest' (to find official source).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Yale E360 (Dec 30, 2025): reports 2025 as 'second hottest on record' citing C3S, but this is a third-party article, not an official C3S publication. (2) Multiple sources (Jan 1-10, 2026): cite C3S as 'forecasting' 2025 as 'second OR third warmest' — ambiguous ranking, not an official definitive report. (3) AFP analysis (Jan 1, 2026): projects 2025 as third hottest following 2024 and 2023, expecting confirmation from Copernicus in early January. (4) WMO announcement (Jan 8-9, 2026): consolidated official temperature data scheduled for January 14, 2026 — outside the resolution window. No official C3S 'Global Climate Highlights 2025' press release or equivalent annual summary was found published within the Dec 30–Jan 11 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No explicit, official C3S annual climate summary for 2025 published within the window was identified in the search results. Most sources citing C3S during this period describe it as 'projecting' or 'forecasting' 2025 as 'second or third warmest,' which is ambiguous and pre-final. The AFP analysis [Prothomalo, Jan 1](https://en.prothomalo.com/environment/climate-change/rrwsvtigj6) explicitly stated 'final confirmation expected from Copernicus in its annual report in early January 2026,' suggesting the report had NOT yet been published as of Jan 1. The WMO's [announcement](https://www.miragenews.com/wmo-to-reveal-2025-global-temperature-data-1599230/) indicates consolidated global temperature data (using ERA5/C3S) was not scheduled until January 14, 2026. The [Vancouver Sun (Jan 10, 2026)](https://vancouversun.com/news/climate-change-news-to-jan-11-26) still describes C3S as projecting 2025 as 'the second or third warmest year on record,' suggesting no definitive official ranking had been released by that date.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp of an official C3S annual 2025 summary publication within the window could be extracted. The WMO's consolidated data release is confirmed for January 14, 2026, outside the window. Multiple sources as late as January 10, 2026, still describe the ranking as uncertain (second or third).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Some sources (Yale E360, Dec 30) say 2025 was definitively second warmest; others (AFP, Vancouver Sun, Straits Times, Euronews, Scientific American) say C3S forecast it as 'second or third warmest' without commitment. Sea surface temperature rankings from Copernicus Marine data show 2025 as third warmest by SST metric. The WMO announcement scheduled for Jan 14 confirms that the official consolidated temperature ranking had not yet been released within the window. The absence of any news article reporting on an official C3S press release titled 'Global Climate Highlights 2025' or equivalent published before Jan 11, despite extensive searching, strongly suggests no such publication occurred within the window. Even if the report was published, available evidence up to Jan 10 still describes C3S's position as 'second or third warmest,' not definitively second-warmest.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Two separate grounds exist: (1) No official C3S annual climate summary for 2025 was found to have been published within the window (Dec 30, 2025 – Jan 11, 2026); multiple sources as of Jan 10, 2026 still describe C3S as 'projecting' or 'forecasting' rather than officially confirming a ranking, and the WMO consolidated data (using C3S data) was scheduled for January 14, outside the window. (2) Even if some C3S data was published within the window, available evidence does not show C3S explicitly stated 2025 was 'second-warmest' — instead it used 'second or third warmest' language throughout the window period. The window closed January 11, 2026 with neither condition for a Yes resolution confirmed.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. or Venezuelan government officially confirm direct diplomatic talks between the two nations between 2025-11-15 and 2025-12-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Tensions between the United States and Venezuela have escalated, with the U.S. launching military strikes in the Caribbean against alleged drug-smuggling vessels linked to Venezuelan criminal networks. During an October 17, 2025, press conference, U.S. President Donald Trump claimed that Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro 'has offered everything' to avoid conflict, hinting at possible backchannel communications and significant economic concessions (https://www.thedailybeast.com/). subquestions.question: Will Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump hold an in-person meeting between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-20?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent reports from late November 2025 indicate that Ukraine, the United States, and Russia are in the process of finalizing a peace plan to end the ongoing war. A pivotal component of this 28-point framework, backed by the Trump administration, requires Ukraine to formally abandon its bid for NATO membership in exchange for US security guarantees that mirror NATO's Article 5. According to reports covering the negotiations in Geneva, "The final agreement is expected to be finalized in a meeting between Zelenskiy and Trump" (https://www.bne.eu). Ukrainian officials also expressed optimism that Zelenskyy would travel to the US (possibly Mar-a-Lago) to cement the deal (https://www.cbsnews.com). Since finalizing the agreement hinges heavily on this highly anticipated leader-to-leader interaction, tracking whether this meeting occurs is a vital early indicator of whether Ukraine will ultimately agree to the NATO concessions embedded in the peace plan.

CBS News - Ukraine agrees to peace proposal, with only "minor details" to settle: https://www.cbsnews.com

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump hold an in-person meeting between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-20 at 23:59:59 UTC. 

An "in-person meeting" is defined as both leaders being physically present in the same room or immediate geographic vicinity for the purpose of a discussion. Video conferences, phone calls, or exchanges through intermediaries do not qualify. 

The primary sources for resolution will be official press releases, schedules, or statements published by the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov) or the Office of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en). In the absence of direct government press releases, a clear consensus of credible reporting from major news agencies—such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), or Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com)—confirming that the meeting took place within the specified time window will be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution.

subquestions.rationale: The broader peace framework—which mandates Ukraine not joining NATO—is reportedly awaiting finalization at an upcoming meeting between Zelenskyy and Trump. If this in-person meeting happens, it strongly signals that the terms of the peace deal are agreeable to both sides and nearing formal adoption. If the meeting is delayed or canceled, it indicates a breakdown or stall in negotiations, significantly lowering the likelihood that Ukraine publicly pledges not to join NATO by the end of 2025.

question: Will a new country join the Abraham Accords in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any country not already a part of the Abraham Accords formally signs a normalization agreement with Israel under the framework of the Abraham Accords by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A formal signing refers to an official agreement between Israel and another country that is publicly acknowledged by both governments and clearly attributed to the Abraham Accords or their continuation.

Countries already part of the Abraham Accords as of June 26, 2025—including the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan—will not count.

The resolution source will be official government statements, however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the United States, Israel, or any prospective member country publicly announce active negotiations for a new country to join the Abraham Accords between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The Abraham Accords, initially signed in 2020, established formal diplomatic relations between Israel and several Arab states, including the UAE, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/). On October 17, 2025, former U.S. President Donald Trump indicated he expects an expansion of the accords soon, hoping Saudi Arabia will join, while other reports have mentioned potential expansion to Azerbaijan or Central Asian nations (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/). However, expansion efforts currently face significant hurdles due to the ongoing conflicts in the region, along with widespread negative public sentiment in Arab nations. Saudi Arabia has continually maintained that the establishment of a Palestinian state is a strict precondition for normalization. If a new country is to formally join the Accords by December 31, 2025, it is highly likely that formal negotiations will be publicly acknowledged or a framework agreement announced in the preceding months. Sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), an official representative (head of state, head of government, foreign minister, or their official spokespersons) of the United States, Israel, or any country not currently in the Abraham Accords publicly confirms that active negotiations are taking place or have concluded for a new country to join the Abraham Accords or establish formal diplomatic relations with Israel. The confirmation must be published in an official government press release (e.g., US State Department at https://www.state.gov or Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs at https://www.gov.il) or quoted directly by major, credible international news organizations (e.g., Reuters at https://www.reuters.com or AP News at https://apnews.com). Statements expressing mere 'hope' or 'desire' for a country to join do not qualify; the statement must explicitly acknowledge active, formal bilateral or mediated negotiations, or a completed agreement framework. If no such announcement occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: To formally sign a normalization agreement and join the Abraham Accords by the end of 2025, significant diplomatic groundwork must be laid, which typically involves a period of publicly acknowledged negotiation or an imminent pre-signing announcement. Given the current geopolitical climate and the lack of confirmed imminent candidates as of late October 2025, an official announcement of negotiations by late November serves as a crucial leading indicator. If this subquestion resolves No, the probability of a sudden signing by December 31 drops dramatically, making it an excellent crux for forecasting the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: An official representative (head of state, head of government, foreign minister, or spokesperson) of the US, Israel, or any prospective member country must publicly confirm — between Oct 31 and Nov 30, 2025 — that active, formal negotiations are taking place or have concluded for a new country to join the Abraham Accords. The statement must be from an official government press release or quoted by major credible news organizations. Mere 'hope' or 'desire' statements do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Abraham Accords new country join negotiations 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find any qualifying announcement; 2) 'Israel normalization agreement diplomatic relations negotiations November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find normalization-related news; 3) 'Steve Witkoff Abraham Accords announcement November 6 2025' (Nov 6–8) — to pinpoint Witkoff's announcement; 4) 'Kazakhstan Abraham Accords signing ceremony formal announcement' (Nov 6–10) — to confirm Kazakhstan's accession details.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: On November 6, 2025, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff publicly stated at the America Business Forum in Miami that 'a new country will join the Abraham Accords tonight,' explicitly confirming active negotiations had concluded. Quoted by AFP, CBS News, Times of Israel, Al Arabiya, and others. Candidate event 2: On November 7, 2025, President Trump announced on Truth Social that 'Kazakhstan is the first country of my second term to join the Abraham Accords,' after a joint call with Netanyahu and Kazakh President Tokayev. Kazakhstan's government confirmed this was in the 'final stage of negotiations.' No earlier qualifying events found within the window. Both events are clearly within the Oct 31–Nov 30 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Steve Witkoff is the U.S. Special Envoy (official representative of the U.S.). His statement on November 6, 2025 explicitly confirmed that concluded negotiations would result in a new country joining the Abraham Accords — not merely expressing 'hope' or 'desire.' Quoted by [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/83B6363), [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/kazakhstan-abraham-accords-israel-trump/), [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/witkoff-us-to-announce-additional-country-joining-abraham-accords-tonight/), [Al Arabiya](https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2025/11/06/new-country-to-join-abraham-accords-us-envoy-teases-ahead-of-announcement), and [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/new-country-to-join-abraham-accords-normalization-deals-with-israel-us-special-envoy/3737075) — all major credible international news organizations. Kazakhstan's government itself confirmed the matter was in the 'final stage of negotiations.' All resolution criteria are met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: November 6, 2025 — multiple sources published on this date reporting Witkoff's statement. The AFP article (http://doc.afp.com/83B6363) was published November 6, 2025. U.S. News & World Report reported a publication timestamp of November 6, 2025, 12:34 PM. This is within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent, high-quality sources (AFP, CBS News, Times of Israel, Al Arabiya, Anadolu Agency, Newsweek, Fox News) uniformly report Witkoff's explicit announcement on November 6, 2025. Kazakhstan's own government (Akorda press service) confirmed the negotiations and the Kazakh president's intention to join. No contradictory evidence was found denying these negotiations occurred. The event is unambiguously within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves Yes. On November 6, 2025, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff — an official U.S. government representative — publicly confirmed that active negotiations had concluded for Kazakhstan to join the Abraham Accords, explicitly acknowledging a completed agreement framework. This was quoted by multiple major credible international news organizations including AFP and CBS News. The announcement is within the resolution window (Oct 31 – Nov 30, 2025), and the statement clearly goes beyond mere 'hope' or 'desire' — it confirms a completed agreement pending formal signing.

question: Another France debt downgrade by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if France's long-term sovereign credit letter rating is downgraded by any of the three major credit rating agencies (S&P, Moody's, Fitch) at any point between September 12, 6:15 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Standard & Poor's, Moody's, or Fitch; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the daily closing yield of the France 10-Year Government Bond be 3.60% or higher on any trading day between September 13, 2025, and October 13, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 12, 2025, Fitch downgraded France's sovereign credit rating from 'AA-' to 'A+', citing political instability and strained public finances following the resignation of former Prime Minister Francois Bayrou. The downgrade and associated political turbulence pushed the French 10-year bond yield to 3.47%, a level close to Italy's, reflecting increased market anxiety over France's debt trajectory and governance (https://www.barrons.com/news/fitch-downgrades-france-s-credit-rating-in-new-debt-blow-01682718000). With both Moody's and S&P Global scheduled to update their ratings later in the fall, market pricing on sovereign bonds will act as a real-time gauge of downgrade risk. If investors anticipate that the new Prime Minister, Sebastien Lecornu, will fail to enact a credible deficit consolidation plan, sovereign bond yields will likely face continued upward pressure. A crossing of the 3.60% threshold would signal severe distress and align with expectations of a further downgrade by the remaining major rating agencies.

Sources:
- Barron's: https://www.barrons.com/news/fitch-downgrades-france-s-credit-rating-in-new-debt-blow-01682718000
- Investing.com France 10-Year Bond Yield: https://www.investing.com/rates-bonds/france-10-year
- MarketWatch France 10-Year Yield: https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/bond/tmbmkfr-10y?countrycode=bx
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the daily closing yield of the France 10-Year Government Bond reaches or exceeds 3.60% on any trading day between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13 (inclusive). Resolution will be determined using the 'Price' column (which denotes the closing yield percentage) for the relevant dates on the historical data page for the France 10-Year Bond Yield on Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/rates-bonds/france-10-year-bond-yield-historical-data). If Investing.com is unavailable or its data is demonstrably erroneous, equivalent daily closing yield data from MarketWatch (https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/bond/tmbmkfr-10y?countrycode=bx) or Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/markets/rates-bonds/government-bonds/france) will be used as a fallback. Intraday yields that spike at or above 3.60% but close below 3.60% do not count toward a Yes resolution. If the yield does not close at or above 3.60% during the specified window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Sovereign bond yields are a direct market proxy for a nation's creditworthiness. Because credit rating agencies (Moody's and S&P) use similar macroeconomic indicators and market realities as bond investors, a significant spike in the 10-year yield (rising from the recent 3.47% up to 3.60% or higher) serves as a strong, market-driven early indicator that conditions are worsening. This makes an official agency downgrade highly probable by the end of the year without just asking the ultimate question with an earlier date.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: France 10-Year Government Bond daily closing yield >= 3.60% on any trading day between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13 inclusive. Observable evidence: Daily closing yield data from Investing.com or equivalent sources. Key threshold: 3.60%. Key entity: France 10-Year Government Bond (OAT).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'France 10-Year Government Bond yield September October 2025' - general data; 2) 'French OAT 10-year bond yield 3.60% 2025' - specific threshold; 3) 'France OAT 10-year yield 3.60 September 25 26 27 2025' - late September period; 4) 'French bond yield 14-year high 3.60 percent late September 2025' - historical high; 5) 'France 10-year OAT yield closing price September 26 2025 exact percentage' - precise close; 6) 'French 10-year bond yield October 6 2025 closing 3.57 3.58 3.59 3.60' - October 6 data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) September 26, 2025 - InstaForex reports yield 'remained steady at about 3.60%'; (2) Late September (unspecified exact date) - October 2 InstaForex article references '14-year high of 3.6% in late September'; (3) October 6, 2025 - AFP/Macau Business report intraday spike to 3.61% before settling at 3.57% (closing below 3.60%). Rejected: October 6 event - intraday spike does not count per resolution criteria; the closing was 3.57-3.587%.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: September 26 InstaForex [https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2756374] states yield 'remained steady at about 3.60%' — the phrasing 'about 3.60%' is consistent with a closing AT 3.60%. The October 2 InstaForex article [https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2764227] confirms '14-year high of 3.6% in late September' as the peak before declining to 3.52%. On October 6, AFP and Macau Business confirm the 10-year yield 'spiked to 3.61% before easing to 3.57%', explicitly noting the closing was below 3.60%. The September 26 daily close of 'about 3.60%' within the resolution window (Sept 13–Oct 13) appears to satisfy the criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 26, 2025 — InstaForex daily market report published on 2025-09-26 explicitly states the yield was 'about 3.60%' for that trading day. The October 2 article confirms a '14-year high of 3.6% in late September', corroborating this date.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The window starts September 13. Data shows: Sept 15 ~3.51%, Sept 16 ~3.51-3.55%, Sept 19 ~3.55%, Sept 22 ~3.55%, Sept 23 ~3.55%, Sept 24 ~3.56%, Sept 25 ~3.58%, Sept 26 ~3.60%. No earlier occurrence at or above 3.60% within the window has been found. September 26 appears to be the first qualifying occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The October 2 article says yields 'fell to 3.47% by month-end' after reaching 3.6% — consistent with September 26 being the high. The Tradeweb September summary states a '3.61% on September 2' high (before the window), then the monthly close was 3.47%. The September 26 'about 3.60%' is described as 'near March high'. October 6 explicitly shows intraday 3.61% spike but closing at ~3.57%. The phrase 'about 3.60%' on September 26 could technically be 3.595% rounded up, but the October 2 reference to '14-year high of 3.6% in late September' uses 3.6% as the exact peak, suggesting it was at or reached 3.60%. There is some ambiguity in 'about 3.60%' but the weight of evidence (multiple sources confirming a 3.6% late-September high) supports resolution as Yes.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The France 10-year bond yield reached 'about 3.60%' on September 26, 2025, within the resolution window. Multiple sources confirm a '14-year high of 3.6% in late September.' The InstaForex September 26 daily market article explicitly reports the yield at 'about 3.60%', consistent with a closing at exactly 3.60% (the threshold). The October 6 intraday spike to 3.61% did not result in a closing at or above 3.60%. The best supported first qualifying occurrence is September 26, 2025.

Furthermore, Trump expressed a desire to meet with Kim Jong Un again in 2025, noting his "very good relationship" with the North Korean leader (https://www.latestly.com/). Because traveling to the Korean Peninsula would serve as a major logistical and diplomatic stepping stone for any visit to North Korea, tracking whether Trump enters South Korea during the APEC window is a strong leading indicator for a potential visit to North Korea.

LatestLY: https://www.latestly.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Therefore, whether Trump actually makes the trip to South Korea by the end of October serves as a highly informative crux for whether he will subsequently or concurrently visit North Korea.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires Trump to physically enter South Korean territory (terrestrial, territorial waters, or airspace) between Oct 1–31, 2025. KST = UTC+9, so these correspond to approximately 02:32–02:40 UTC on October 29, 2025. The first qualifying entry into South Korean airspace/territory occurred on October 29, 2025, well within the Oct 1–31 window.

question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by June 30?

question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. officially announce an agreed framework or draft for a bilateral military security guarantee with Ukraine between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?

Furthermore, a coalition of Western leaders met in Paris on September 4, 2025, to discuss military-support frameworks, emphasizing that any European military role would require U.S. security guarantees as a 'back-stop.' Because negotiating a formal, binding treaty or executive agreement takes considerable time, a formal commitment by the U.S. before the end of 2025 would highly likely be preceded by the announcement of an agreed framework, draft text, or agreement-in-principle. Tracking whether the U.S. government officially confirms a draft framework in November acts as a strong leading indicator for a finalized, binding security guarantee in December.

To qualify, the announced framework or draft must explicitly include a proposed U.S. commitment to a military defense obligation, a military 'backstop,' or a direct military response mechanism in the event of an attack on Ukraine (similar in character to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment). Announcements of purely financial aid, weapons transfers without a defense guarantee, or cooperative/consultative mechanisms that do not obligate military defense will not qualify.

subquestions.rationale: A formalized, legally binding mutual defense commitment takes time to draft, finalize, and sign. By asking whether an official framework or draft agreement is announced in November, we are measuring a necessary precursor event. A 'Yes' resolution would strongly indicate that the parties have aligned on the core military commitments, making the finalization of the ultimate binding agreement by December 31, 2025, highly probable.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: (1) Within Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025 window; (2) Official publication on whitehouse.gov or state.gov; (3) Explicit announcement that U.S. and Ukraine have 'reached' an agreed framework/draft/agreed-in-principle text; (4) Specifically for a bilateral security guarantee; (5) That explicitly includes a U.S. military defense obligation, backstop, or direct military response mechanism (Article 5-style). evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence actively confirms the No resolution: (1) Nov 27 reports explicitly state 'the nature of US security guarantees' is among the two remaining unresolved 'delicate issues.' evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. While there was significant diplomatic activity during the window (Geneva talks, a leaked 28-point draft plan with Article 5-style elements, White House statements of 'significant progress'), no official announcement from the White House or State Department explicitly announced an agreed/agreed-in-principle bilateral security guarantee with a U.S. military defense obligation for Ukraine during Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025. Although the rocket crashed shortly after takeoff, the company considered the test a "great success" for data-gathering purposes, noting that Spectrum launch vehicles 2 and 3 were already in production. 

To conduct a second orbital launch attempt by the end of 2025, Isar Aerospace would typically need to confirm a launch window several weeks in advance. This lead time is necessary to coordinate range safety, secure final regulatory approvals, and finalize logistics with payload customers—such as those confirmed under the European Space Agency's Flight Ticket Initiative. If a 2025 launch date is not publicly targeted or reaffirmed by late November, it strongly indicates that the launch will slip into 2026.

subquestions.question: Will the initial US Employment Situation report show an increase of 100,000 or more nonfarm payroll jobs for December 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
According to recent economic data, the US economy expanded at a robust 4.3% annualized rate in Q3 2025, driven largely by consumer spending. However, intermediate indicators showed labor market conditions cooling toward the end of the year. In November 2025, the economy added only 64,000 jobs, and the unemployment rate unexpectedly rose to 4.6% (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm). Since consumer spending is a primary driver of US GDP—accounting for more than two-thirds of economic activity—labor market health is deeply intertwined with GDP growth. The December 2025 nonfarm payrolls report will be the final major employment data point for Q4. A rebound in job creation to 100,000 or more would suggest sustained economic momentum, whereas another weak print would indicate softening conditions that could drag Q4 GDP growth down closer to the 2.0% - 2.5% range.

Sources:
US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) GDP Data: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Employment Situation: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Any subsequent revisions to the December 2025 figure made in later months will not be considered. If the reported figure is exactly 100,000, the question resolves Yes.

If the BLS report for December 2025 is delayed and not published between 2025-12-29 and 2026-01-28, this question will be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: December's nonfarm payroll data acts as a crucial proxy for household income and consumer spending in the final month of the quarter. Given the reported slowdown to 64k jobs in November, knowing whether job growth recovered to >= 100k or remained weak in December will significantly update forecasters on whether Q4 GDP has lost enough momentum to decelerate from 4.3% down to the narrower 2.0%–2.5% bracket.

question: Foreign intervention in Gaza in 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will the United Nations Security Council adopt a resolution authorizing the deployment of a multinational military, security, or peacekeeping force to the Gaza Strip before November 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas went into effect on October 10, 2025, initiating the first phase of a peace plan mediated by U.S. President Donald Trump. While the U.S. has deployed 200 Central Command troops to Israel to coordinate aid and monitor the truce, these forces are prohibited from physically entering Gaza (Fortune, https://fortune.com/). To manage security and govern Gaza post-conflict, discussions are underway to deploy an International Stabilization Force (ISF) or a joint Arab-international force. However, international and regional stakeholders, including Egypt, have emphasized that any foreign force deployment requires a legal framework, specifically a United Nations Security Council (UNSC) resolution with a clear mandate (Middle East Monitor, https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/). On October 14, 2025, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul announced that talks had begun with permanent UNSC members, including Russia and China, to secure a resolution authorizing the ISF's deployment (Anadolu Ajansı, https://www.aa.com.tr/en/). 

Sources:
Fortune: https://fortune.com/
Middle East Monitor: https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/
Anadolu Ajansı: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/
UN Security Council: https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) officially adopts a resolution between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15 (inclusive) that explicitly mandates, authorizes, or establishes the deployment of a multinational military, security, police, or peacekeeping force to the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip. 

The resolution must be officially adopted by the UNSC within this timeframe; proposed drafts or resolutions vetoed by permanent members will not count. The authorization must clearly permit the force to physically enter the terrestrial territory of Gaza for an operational role (e.g., stabilization, peacekeeping, border security inside Gaza, or enforcement). Resolutions that strictly limit the force to operating exclusively on the Egyptian side of the border or solely in maritime territory do not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be the official text published on the UN Security Council Resolutions page (https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/content/resolutions-0) or official UN press releases (https://press.un.org/en/content/security-council). If the UN site is unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting from major international news organizations (e.g., Reuters, AP News, BBC) confirming the resolution's adoption and mandate will be used.
subquestions.rationale: For a foreign military or peacekeeping force to legitimately deploy to Gaza, establishing international legal backing via a UN Security Council resolution is widely considered a prerequisite. Current diplomatic efforts are actively pursuing this authorization. If a UNSC resolution is adopted within this one-month window, it indicates that major geopolitical roadblocks have been cleared, significantly raising the probability of troops physically entering Gaza by the end of 2025. Conversely, if no resolution is reached due to vetoes or diplomatic stalling, a formal foreign deployment becomes much less likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: The exact condition for Yes: UNSC officially adopts a resolution between Oct 16-Nov 15, 2025 that explicitly mandates/authorizes/establishes deployment of a multinational military/security/peacekeeping force to the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip. Observable evidence: an official UNSC adopted resolution text or credible reporting of its adoption within the window. Key entities: UNSC (15 members), veto-holding P5, Gaza Strip. Threshold: must be adopted (not just proposed/drafted/vetoed). Timing: Oct 16 - Nov 15, 2025 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'UN Security Council resolution Gaza multinational force 2025' (Oct 16-Nov 15) — to find qualifying resolutions within the window. Query 2: 'UNSC Gaza peacekeeping deployment authorization vote' (Oct 16-Nov 15) — to find voting events. Query 3: 'UN Security Council Resolution 2803 Gaza adopted November 2025' — to find the specific resolution. Query 4: 'UNSC vote Gaza resolution adopted passed November 15 2025' — to check if vote happened on or before Nov 15. Query 5: 'November 17 OR November 18 UNSC Gaza resolution vote 2025 date' — to confirm exact date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: UNSC Resolution 2803 (also referred to as 2802 in some sources) authorizing the International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza. Sources consistently indicate the vote was held on November 17, 2025. During the Oct 16-Nov 15 window, only draft resolutions and negotiations were reported — no adopted resolution. The Nov 15 articles (Dawn, The Hindu, CNA) specifically stated the vote was 'scheduled for Monday, November 17, 2025.' No evidence of any UNSC resolution authorizing a Gaza force being adopted within the Oct 16-Nov 15 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Resolution 2803 fully meets the substantive criteria — it authorizes an International Stabilization Force (ISF) to deploy in the terrestrial territory of Gaza with a mandate to use 'all necessary measures.' However, the adoption date of November 17, 2025 is outside the resolution window (Oct 16-Nov 15, 2025). Sources: [Dawn](https://www.dawn.com/news/1955234), [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/un-security-council-to-vote-on-november-17-on-trumps-gaza-plan/article70282905.ece), [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/trump-gaza-plan-un-security-council-vote-nov-17-5469426), [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/84BQ7G4), [UN News](https://news.un.org/en/story/2025/11/1166391). The resolution was not adopted on or before November 15, 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The vote took place on November 17, 2025 (UTC). This is confirmed by: (1) Dawn article published Nov 15 stating 'set to vote on November 17, 2025'; (2) The Hindu Nov 15 article: 'scheduled to vote on Monday, November 17, 2025'; (3) CNA Nov 15 article: 'set to vote on Monday, November 17, 2025'; (4) Express Tribune: 'adopted a US-drafted resolution on November 17, 2025'; (5) Truthout: 'On November 17, 2025, the United Nations Security Council adopted Resolution 2803'; (6) AFP report confirms November 17. Some sources say November 18, likely due to timezone differences between New York (EST) and publication locations. The actual UN vote occurred November 17, 2025 EST.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence within the Oct 16-Nov 15 window. All evidence confirms the vote was scheduled for and occurred on November 17, 2025. As of November 14-15, 2025, the resolution had not been voted on — only a joint statement urging 'swift adoption' was issued. No other qualifying UNSC resolution on Gaza peacekeeping was found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Some sources date the vote November 18, but this is due to timezone offsets (the UN vote in New York on Nov 17 evening ET would be Nov 18 in many Asian/European timezones). The UN News article itself refers to the resolution as adopted, citing November 17 in the URL slug. No evidence of any UNSC adoption of a qualifying resolution on or before November 15, 2025. The November 14 joint statement explicitly calls for 'swift adoption' of the resolution 'currently under consideration' — meaning it had NOT been adopted as of November 14. The window definitively closed on November 15 with no qualifying resolution adopted.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The UNSC adopted Resolution 2803 authorizing the International Stabilization Force in Gaza on November 17, 2025 — two days after the resolution window closed. The question resolves No. The window closed on November 15, 2025 with no qualifying UNSC resolution having been adopted. Resolution_datetime is set to 2025-11-15T23:59:59Z (window close) as the condition became definitively impossible once the window expired without adoption.

If no such meeting is announced, the likelihood of resolving the complex legal and diplomatic hurdles necessary to recognize Crimea by year-end drops significantly.

evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: No. Throughout the entire resolution window (Oct 31 - Nov 30, 2025), the White House did not officially announce or confirm an in-person bilateral meeting between Trump and Putin. question: TikTok sale announced in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if ByteDance announces their intention to sell TikTok by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to “No”.

A public announcement of the intention to sell TikTok will qualify even if a sale has not been finalized. This includes any formal declaration made by ByteDance or its authorized representatives regarding their plans to sell or transfer ownership of TikTok.

subquestions.question: Will TikTok be removed from the U.S. Apple App Store or Google Play Store between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Under U.S. law, ByteDance has been ordered to divest its U.S. operations of TikTok to address national security concerns. The deadline for this divestiture has been extended multiple times by President Donald Trump, with the current deadline set for September 17, 2025 (https://invezz.com/news/trump-grants-bytedance-another-90-day-extension-to-sell-tiktok). President Trump has stated that a group of 'very wealthy people' is prepared to buy the platform, but the transaction still requires explicit approval from the Chinese government (https://gizmodo.com/trump-says-very-wealthy-people-are-ready-to-buy-tiktok). If ByteDance does not divest TikTok by the deadline and no further extension is granted by the U.S. administration, the app is expected to face a nationwide ban, which includes being removed from U.S. app stores. The outcome of the September 17 deadline is a critical indicator for any potential sale: a ban would strongly signal that a sale will not occur (likely due to Beijing's refusal to approve it), while an extension or avoidance of a ban keeps the possibility of a sale announcement alive for the remainder of 2025.

Sources:
Trump grants ByteDance another 90-day extension to sell TikTok - https://invezz.com/news/trump-grants-bytedance-another-90-day-extension-to-sell-tiktok
Trump Says 'Very Wealthy People' Are Ready to Buy TikTok - https://gizmodo.com/trump-says-very-wealthy-people-are-ready-to-buy-tiktok
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if, at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the TikTok application is removed and becomes unavailable for download by new users on either the iOS Apple App Store (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tiktok/id835599320) or the Google Play Store (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.zhiliaoapp.musically) in the United States for a continuous period of at least 24 hours. 

To qualify for a "Yes" resolution, the removal must be explicitly attributed to U.S. government action, enforcement of the U.S. divestment law, or compliance with a U.S. federal ban. 

Removal due to routine technical glitches, voluntary temporary removal by ByteDance for maintenance, or standard developer policy violations (e.g., an app store guideline violation unrelated to the divestment mandate) will not trigger a "Yes" resolution. If the September 17, 2025 deadline passes and the app remains available continuously through the end date, or if it is removed but restored within 24 hours, the question resolves "No".

Primary sources for resolution will be credible media reporting from major technology and news outlets (e.g., https://www.reuters.com, https://www.bloomberg.com, https://techcrunch.com) explicitly confirming the app's removal from the U.S. storefronts in compliance with the U.S. government mandate.
subquestions.rationale: The current divestment deadline is September 17, 2025. Tracking whether TikTok is actually removed from U.S. app stores shortly after this deadline provides an unambiguous, observable crux. If a ban is enacted, it likely means negotiations failed or the Chinese government blocked the sale, drastically reducing the odds of a sale announcement by the end of 2025. Conversely, if no ban occurs, it implies either a sale is imminent or another extension was secured, making a later sale announcement much more probable.

evidence.step1_decompose: YES requires: TikTok removed from U.S. Apple App Store OR Google Play Store between Sept 1–Oct 1, 2025; removal lasting ≥24 continuous hours; removal explicitly due to U.S. government action/divestment law enforcement. Observable evidence: credible media reporting TikTok unavailable for download in U.S. app stores for ≥24h due to government enforcement.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'TikTok removed Apple App Store Google Play Store United States September 2025' — to find any removal events. Query 2: 'TikTok ban US September 2025 deadline divestment ByteDance' — to find enforcement actions. Query 3: 'TikTok available download app store September 17 2025 deadline extension' — to confirm availability after key deadline. Query 4: 'TikTok US ban enforcement Apple Google remove app October 2025' — to check for any removal in late September.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate removal events identified. All articles confirm TikTok remained available. Key events found: (1) Trump signed executive order on Sept 16, 2025 extending deadline to Dec 16, 2025 — preventing any removal. (2) Sept 17 deadline passed with TikTok still available. (3) Trump-Xi call Sept 19 confirmed deal framework. (4) Sept 21 Trump announced deal with U.S. investors. (5) TikTok still listed in App Store revenue data as of Sept 30. All events confirm continuous availability.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No match for YES criteria. Multiple sources confirm TikTok was NOT removed: [Hindustan Times](https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/donald-trump-extends-tiktok-deal-deadline-until-december-16-101758053306881.html) reports Trump signed executive order Sept 16 extending deadline to Dec 16 'allowing TikTok to continue operating in the U.S. and for partners such as Apple and Google to keep the app in their stores.' [Yahoo Finance/UPI](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/trump-extends-tiktok-ban-deadline-131854675.html) confirms extension 'to avoid the app's removal from U.S. app stores.' [KTVH](https://www.ktvh.com/science-and-tech/social-media/trump-extends-deadline-for-tiktok-ban-keeping-the-app-available-in-the-us-for-now) states 'TikTok to remain available in the United States through at least December 16, 2025.' [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/report/786748/tiktok-deal-trump-administration-legal-uncertainty) confirms continued availability as of Sept 26.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp of removal found. The definitive No moment: Trump signed executive order on September 16, 2025 (exact date confirmed by multiple sources), extending enforcement deadline to December 16, 2025, thereby preventing any app store removal within the question window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying removal event found at any point within the window. The app remained continuously available from Sept 1 through Oct 1, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for any contradictory evidence suggesting removal: none found. The January 2025 brief outage (~12-14 hours) was outside the window and pre-dated the question start date. All September 2025 coverage consistently reports TikTok remained available. The extension to December 16 was signed before the September 17 deadline, making removal within this window definitively impossible by government enforcement.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is NO. Trump signed an executive order on September 16, 2025 extending the TikTok enforcement deadline to December 16, 2025. This prevented any government-mandated removal from app stores within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window. The September 17, 2025 deadline — the only potential trigger for removal within this window — passed without any enforcement action. TikTok remained continuously available in U.S. app stores throughout the entire question period. The 'Yes' condition became definitively impossible on September 16, 2025, when Trump signed the fourth extension executive order.
