subquestions.question: Will North Korean leader Kim Jong Un physically attend the APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea between October 25, 2025 and November 5, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
US President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit South Korea for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Gyeongju, which will run from October 31 to November 1, 2025. During his Asia trip, Trump is expected to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Speculation is also high regarding a potential meeting between Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has suggested the APEC summit as a platform for a possible Trump-Kim meeting, and South Korea's reunification minister noted a 'considerable' chance of such a meeting occurring during the regional summit. However, it remains uncertain whether Kim Jong Un will travel to Gyeongju to attend the APEC summit. If Kim makes the trip to attend the summit, it would act as a highly informative indicator that an in-person meeting with Trump is imminent.

Sources:
The Indian Express: https://indianexpress.com/
AFP: https://www.afp.com/
India TV News: https://www.indiatvnews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a consensus of credible reporting confirms that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un physically attended any official event, session, or sidelines gathering associated with the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-05 (inclusive).

'Attending' is defined as Kim Jong Un being physically present in Gyeongju and participating in the summit or holding official bilateral or multilateral meetings at or directly adjacent to the summit venue. If Kim Jong Un travels to South Korea but does not attend any APEC-associated events (for example, if he only meets leaders at the DMZ or in Seoul), this question resolves No. If the APEC summit is cancelled or postponed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No.

The resolution will be based on major global news agencies. Resolvers should check the following sources to determine the outcome:
Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
AP News: https://apnews.com/
Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com/
subquestions.rationale: For the ultimate question to resolve Yes, Trump must meet Xi, Putin, and Kim by December 31, 2025. With Trump already visiting South Korea for the APEC summit to meet Xi, a meeting with Kim Jong Un is a critical missing piece. Kim's physical attendance at the APEC summit in Gyeongju is a distinct observable event that serves as a massive crux: if Kim attends, the probability of him meeting Trump jumps significantly, pointing to a higher likelihood for the ultimate question. If he skips the summit, the timeframe and venues for a potential meeting become much more constrained.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Kim Jong Un must physically attend at least one APEC-associated event in Gyeongju, South Korea, between October 25–November 5, 2025. Observable evidence would be credible reporting from Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, or consensus of major global news agencies confirming his physical presence at an official APEC event, session, or sidelines meeting in Gyeongju.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Kim Jong Un APEC summit Gyeongju South Korea 2025' — to find direct reports of Kim attending APEC; 2) 'APEC summit Gyeongju South Korea November 2025' — to find summit details and attendee list; 3) 'Kim Jong Un South Korea visit attend APEC November 2025' — to find any reports of Kim visiting South Korea; 4) 'Trump Kim Jong Un meeting Gyeongju APEC 2025' — to find Trump-Kim meeting reports; 5) 'Kim Jong Un location whereabouts North Korea October November 2025' — to establish Kim's actual location during the window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Multiple reports speculated about a possible Trump-Kim meeting at or near APEC (Oct 25–29), but these were all speculative. (B) Trump himself stated on Oct 29 they 'couldn't work out timing' — explicitly ruling out a meeting. (C) Kim Jong Un was confirmed by KCNA to be in North Korea on Oct 31 inspecting a military unit (11th Corps at its headquarters). (D) The APEC summit ran Oct 31–Nov 1 with Xi, Trump, Takaichi, Lee, etc. — no Kim Jong Un mentioned as attendee. (E) South Korea NIS confirmed Nov 4 that no summit occurred during APEC. All candidate events for a 'Yes' outcome were rejected: they were either speculative pre-summit hopes or explicitly contradicted by confirmed reports.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence matches the resolution criteria. Kim Jong Un did NOT physically attend any APEC-associated events in Gyeongju. [Yonhap (Oct 29)](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20251029009700315): Trump says meeting with Kim 'won't happen' — Kim not coming to APEC. [JoongAng Daily (Nov 2)](https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2025-11-02/national/northKorea/North-Koreas-Kim-inspects-special-operations-units-war-readiness/2434569): Kim was in North Korea inspecting military unit on Oct 31 (same day APEC Leaders' Meeting began). [Yonhap (Nov 4)](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20251104012152320): NIS confirmed no meeting occurred during APEC. [Nikkei Asia (Nov 1)](https://asia.nikkei.com/politics/international-relations/south-korea-s-apec-two-days-of-heavy-diplomacy-end): APEC concluded with no mention of Kim Jong Un attending.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The definitive 'No' moment can be established at October 29, 2025, when Trump explicitly confirmed no Kim meeting would occur ('We really weren't able to work out timing'), and further confirmed by Kim's presence in North Korea on October 31 per KCNA reports. The APEC summit ended November 1, 2025, with no Kim attendance. The window closed November 5, 2025, with no subsequent Kim APEC appearance.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence (Kim attending APEC in Gyeongju) was found at any point in the resolution window. Kim Jong Un never traveled to South Korea during this period.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No report from any major news source (Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, Yonhap, JoongAng, Nikkei Asia, etc.) suggests Kim Jong Un traveled to South Korea or attended APEC. On the contrary, Kim was confirmed to be in North Korea conducting domestic activities. North Korea is not an APEC member economy, making Kim's attendance structurally unprecedented. Multiple reports confirm Trump-Kim meeting did not happen. The APEC concluded November 1 with the Gyeongju Declaration adopted by 21 member economies — North Korea is not one of them.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is definitively No. Kim Jong Un did not physically attend the APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, during the resolution window (Oct 25–Nov 5, 2025). He was confirmed to be in North Korea during the summit period. The earliest definitive 'No' moment was October 29, 2025, when Trump explicitly stated the timing for a meeting could not be worked out. This became fully confirmed when Kim was reported to be in North Korea on October 31 during the APEC Leaders' Meeting.

question: EU sanctions on Israel by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the European Union officially imposes new sanctions of any form against Israel between September 2 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Sanctions could include measures like tariffs, trade restrictions, financial penalties, diplomatic expulsions, travel bans, restrictions on specific individuals, or any other actions that are commonly recognized as sanctions.

Sanctions against Israeli citizens or entities which do not directly target the Israeli state or members of the Israeli government will not qualify.

The passage of an official act authorizing sanctions on Israel within this market's timeframe will count toward a "Yes" resolution, regardless of if/when the sanctions come into effect.

Only the imposition of sanctions on Israel by the EU as an entity will qualify; if individual member states of the EU apply sanctions against Israel (e.g., France imposes novel trade restrictions on Israel unilaterally), it will not be sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes".

The primary resolution source will be official information from the European Union; however, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the European Commission or the EU High Representative formally propose new sanctions, tariffs, or trade restrictions against the Israeli state or its government by October 3, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The European Union has faced mounting internal and external pressure to impose punitive measures on Israel in response to the humanitarian situation in Gaza. In July 2025, the European External Action Service (EEAS) prepared a list of potential options, including suspending the EU-Israel Association Agreement, imposing an arms embargo, and enacting targeted sanctions on Israeli government ministers. However, EU sanctions typically require the unanimous agreement of all 27 member states, a threshold that has proven difficult to reach due to strong opposition from countries like Germany and Hungary (https://www.rt.com/).

During an informal meeting of EU foreign ministers in Copenhagen on August 30, 2025, divisions remained apparent. Nonetheless, EU High Representative Kaja Kallas stated that concrete measures would be proposed "next week." Additionally, Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen noted that while an import ban might be politically impossible, the EU could potentially impose heavy tariffs on imports from Israel, an action that might only require a qualified majority rather than unanimity (https://www.euronews.com/). Before the Council of the EU can vote on adopting any such sanctions or tariffs, a formal proposal must first be drafted and submitted by the European Commission or the High Representative. Tracking whether this official proposal is submitted is a critical leading indicator for whether actual sanctions will materialize later in the year.

Sources:
RT: EU to propose sanctions on Israel - media - https://www.rt.com/
Euronews: EU Member States divided over Gaza at their Copenhagen meeting - https://www.euronews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the European Commission or the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy officially submits or presents a formal proposal for new sanctions, tariffs, or trade restrictions directly targeting the State of Israel, its government ministers, or its military to the Council of the European Union between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03 (inclusive).

To qualify, the proposed measures must target the Israeli state, its government, or its military apparatus. Proposals that exclusively target non-governmental Israeli citizens or private entities (such as individual settlers) without directly targeting the Israeli state or government will not trigger a Yes resolution.

The proposal does not need to be adopted, voted on, or enacted by the Council within this timeframe; the formal submission or official presentation of the proposal is sufficient for a Yes resolution. If the proposal is submitted confidentially, it will count toward resolution if its submission is subsequently confirmed by official EU statements or a strong consensus of credible reporting by major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AFP).

If no such qualifying proposal is submitted between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03, this question resolves No. Any proposals submitted after October 3, 2025, will not be considered, and the question will be resolved as No.

Primary resolution sources will be official press releases, session minutes, or statements from the EU:
- Council of the EU Press Releases (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/)
- European Commission Press Corner (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en)
- European External Action Service (EEAS) (https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/press-material_en)
subquestions.rationale: Before the EU can enact new sanctions or tariffs against Israel, an official proposal must be submitted by the European Commission or the High Representative. Given the EU's highly bureaucratic and often slow legislative process, if no formal proposal is even tabled by early October, it becomes highly improbable that the EU will achieve the necessary political consensus to actually impose sanctions by the end of December. Monitoring this procedural milestone provides a strong, early signal for the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes condition: European Commission or EU High Representative officially submits/presents a formal proposal for new sanctions, tariffs, or trade restrictions directly targeting the State of Israel, its government ministers, or military, to the Council of the EU between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03. Observable evidence: official EU press releases, credible news reports of formal submission to Council. Key entities: European Commission (von der Leyen), High Representative (Kaja Kallas), Council of the EU.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'European Commission EU sanctions Israel proposal 2025' (Sep 3 - Oct 3, 2025) — to find any formal proposal; 2) 'EU High Representative Kaja Kallas Israel sanctions tariffs trade restrictions' (Sep 3 - Oct 3, 2025) — to find Kallas-specific proposals; 3) 'European Commission formal proposal Council EU Israel sanctions September 17 2025' — to confirm exact date; 4) 'EU Israel Association Agreement suspension proposal von der Leyen State of Union' — to find earlier announcements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events found: (1) September 10, 2025 — Von der Leyen's State of the Union speech announced intention to propose sanctions; (2) September 17, 2025 — European Commission formally presented proposals to the Council, with Kaja Kallas leading a press conference. The September 17 event is the formal submission. Both are within the window. The September 17 event is the formal proposal submission to the Council.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The European Commission formally presented to the EU Council on September 17, 2025: (1) A proposal to suspend trade-related provisions of the EU-Israel Association Agreement — directly targeting the Israeli state's trade access; (2) Sanctions including asset freezes and travel bans on Israeli government ministers Ben Gvir and Smotrich — directly targeting Israeli government ministers; (3) Suspension of bilateral financial support. Sources confirming this include [Politico](https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-unveils-plans-hit-israel-with-tariffs-sanctions-amid-gaza-war-outcry/), [Haaretz](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2025-09-17/ty-article/eu-proposes-sanctions-on-israel-suspending-trade-benefits-targeting-far-right-ministers/00000199-577e-d907-a5db-77fef5210000), [Euronews](http://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/09/17/eu-moves-to-sanction-israel-over-gaza-west-bank-humanitarian-crisis), [AgenSIR](https://www.agensir.it/quotidiano/2025/9/17/eu-commission-sanctions-against-israel-tel-aviv-breached-terms-of-the-association-agreement-regarding-human-rights-and-democracy/), [EUbusiness](https://www.eubusiness.com/trade/eu-to-suspend-trade-concessions-with-israel/), [Interfax-Ukraine](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1105455.html). The proposals target the Israeli state (trade suspension) AND Israeli government ministers (Ben Gvir, Smotrich). This satisfies the resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple sources explicitly report September 17, 2025 as the date of the formal proposal presentation to the Council. The AgenSIR article states: 'today the EU Commission is presenting to the EU Council its proposal.' This is a reliable timestamp consistent across numerous major international news sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: September 10, 2025 (State of Union speech) was an announcement of intent/plans, not a formal submission. The formal submission to the Council occurred on September 17, 2025. No earlier formal submission (between Sep 3 and Sep 17) has been identified. September 17 is confirmed as the first formal proposal.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence. No sources dispute that September 17, 2025 was the date of formal presentation. The proposal clearly targets the Israeli state (trade suspension of Association Agreement provisions) and Israeli government ministers (Ben Gvir and Smotrich). The criteria explicitly require proposals targeting 'the Israeli state, its government ministers, or its military apparatus' — both the trade suspension (targeting the state) and individual minister sanctions satisfy this. The proposals were presented to the Council by both Commission President von der Leyen and High Representative Kallas. No conflicting evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: On September 17, 2025, the European Commission formally presented to the EU Council a package of proposals including: (1) suspension of trade-related provisions of the EU-Israel Association Agreement (targeting the Israeli state's trade preferences), and (2) sanctions on Israeli government ministers Ben Gvir and Smotrich. This constitutes a formal proposal for new sanctions AND trade restrictions directly targeting the State of Israel and its government ministers, submitted within the September 3 – October 3, 2025 window. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by December 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla be publicly confirmed to have applied for a driverless autonomous vehicle permit in Texas between September 1 and September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In June 2025, Tesla launched a limited 'Robotaxi' trial in Austin, Texas, using a fleet of Model Y vehicles. Contrary to CEO Elon Musk's previous claims of fully unsupervised rides, the trial vehicles operate with a human 'safety monitor' in the passenger seat. This cautious rollout occurred as Texas lawmakers requested Tesla to delay fully driverless operations until a new autonomous vehicle law took effect. Signed by Governor Greg Abbott, the law requires firms to obtain a permit from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) before operating self-driving vehicles on public streets without a human driver, and this law officially comes into effect on September 1, 2025. Since Texas is currently Tesla's primary testing ground for its Robotaxi pilot, securing this driverless permit is a critical regulatory milestone. Whether Tesla files for this permit immediately after the application window opens will serve as a strong indicator of its readiness and timeline to remove human safety monitors and launch a fully driverless service by the end of 2025.

Sources:
Popular Mechanics: https://www.popularmechanics.com/
The Express Tribune: https://tribune.com.pk/
CNA: https://www.channelnewsasia.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 (inclusive), credible reporting from major media outlets (such as https://www.reuters.com/ or https://techcrunch.com/) or an official statement/record from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (https://www.txdmv.gov/) publicly confirms that Tesla has formally submitted an application—or has an active application pending—for a permit to operate autonomous vehicles without a human driver on public roads in Texas. The application must explicitly be for fully driverless operation, without any onboard safety driver or monitor, to comply with the Texas law that became effective on September 1, 2025. If no such application is publicly confirmed by 11:59 PM ET on 2025-09-08, the question resolves No. If an application is submitted but kept completely secret and not publicly reported during the resolution window, it will not count towards a Yes resolution. Announcements of mere intent to apply without actual confirmed submission will not qualify.
subquestions.rationale: For Tesla to launch a fully driverless Robotaxi service in 2025, it must secure regulatory approval in the states where it intends to operate. Texas is currently Tesla's primary testbed for its robotaxi fleet. With a new Texas law requiring driverless autonomous vehicle permits going into effect on September 1, 2025, Tesla must secure this permit to transition its monitor-supervised trial to a fully driverless service. If Tesla immediately applies for this permit upon the law's enactment (between September 1 and September 8), it strongly signals readiness to launch a public, fully driverless service before the 2025 year-end deadline of the ultimate question. A failure to apply during this initial window suggests technical or regulatory delays that make a 2025 driverless launch highly unlikely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: Tesla must be publicly confirmed (via credible reporting or official TxDMV record) to have formally submitted/have pending an application for a permit to operate AVs without any human driver on Texas public roads, confirmed between Sept 1-8, 2025. The permit must be explicitly for fully driverless (Level 4+) operation. Observable evidence: credible media report or TxDMV record specifically stating Tesla applied/has active application for driverless AV permit under SB 2807.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Tesla driverless autonomous vehicle permit Texas 2025' (Sept 1-8) - sought confirmation of permit application; 2) 'Texas autonomous vehicle law driverless permit September 2025' - sought SB2807 context; 3) 'Tesla apply driverless permit Texas DMV SB 2807 application September 2025' - sought specific application confirmation; 4) 'Tesla Level 4 autonomous Texas permit application TxDMV' (Aug-Sept) - sought any prior application; 5) 'Tesla secured Texas DMV permit driverless operations earlier this month' - sought confirmation of Statesman claim; 6) 'Tesla robotaxi Texas permit driverless no safety driver secured granted' - sought confirmation of fully driverless permit.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate 1: Austin American-Statesman (Sept 4) states 'New Texas regulations now require a permit from the Department of Motor Vehicles for driverless operations, a permit Tesla secured earlier this month.' — REJECTED as qualifying event because: (a) 'earlier this month' from a Sept 4 article likely refers to August, outside the window; (b) the Statesman's characterization conflicts with multiple other sources saying Tesla's FSD remains Level 2 requiring safety monitors; (c) Business Insider (Aug 9) confirms Tesla's August Texas permit was a ride-hailing license from TDLR, not a TxDMV driverless AV permit. Candidate 2: Multiple sources confirm Tesla operating with safety monitors (Level 2) as of Sept 1-8, specifically to avoid the driverless permit requirement — these contradict any claim Tesla applied for a driverless permit during the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Austin American-Statesman [statesman.com, Sept 4, 2025] claim about Tesla having 'secured' a 'permit for driverless operations' is directly contradicted by: (1) The US Sun [Sept 1] and The US Sun [Sept 2]: 'Tesla's robotaxi service exempt because it includes a human safety monitor'; (2) Mashable [Sept 5]: 'the state classifies Tesla's Full Self-Driving system as Level 2, so oversight is mandatory'; (3) Gizmodo [Sept 5]: Tesla 'remains a Level 2 system that needs constant driver supervision'; (4) Investor's Business Daily [Sept 3]: 'Tesla's Full Self-Driving remains a Level 2 system'; (5) Business Insider [Aug 9]: Tesla's Texas permit did not classify Tesla as autonomous and 'the company must seek authorization from the state Department of Motor Vehicles' for autonomous classification — implying Tesla had NOT yet sought that TxDMV authorization as of Aug 9. No source explicitly states Tesla submitted a Level 4/5 fully driverless (no onboard human) permit application to TxDMV during Sept 1-8.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No reliable exact timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event. The Statesman's 'earlier this month' (from Sept 4) is vague and likely refers to August. No other source within Sept 1-8 window explicitly confirms Tesla applied for a fully driverless AV permit from TxDMV.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence confirmed in the window. The permit Tesla obtained in August was a ride-hailing (transportation network company) permit from TDLR, not a TxDMV driverless AV permit under SB 2807.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Multiple high-quality sources (Mashable, Gizmodo, IBD, CNET, Benzinga, US Sun) consistently characterize Tesla's Austin operation as Level 2 with required safety monitors, explicitly exempt from the driverless permit requirement precisely because it has safety monitors. The Cryptopolitan article (Sept 5) vaguely claims Tesla 'won a permit to run a robotaxi service without a human driver' but this appears to reference the August ride-hailing permit, not a TxDMV driverless AV permit. SFist (Sept 4) notes Tesla 'has not applied for the required permits' in California — suggesting a pattern of not seeking formal driverless permits. The weight of evidence indicates Tesla did NOT apply for a fully driverless TxDMV permit during the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence does not meet the resolution criteria. No credible source within the Sept 1-8 window explicitly confirms Tesla formally applied for or has an active application pending for a fully driverless (Level 4+, no onboard human) AV permit from TxDMV under SB 2807. All sources consistently indicate Tesla operates with safety monitors (Level 2) and is exempt from the driverless permit requirement because of those monitors. The Statesman's ambiguous reference to a 'driverless operations' permit likely refers to the August ride-hailing permit, which was not a TxDMV autonomous vehicle permit. Resolution: No.

question: Will there be no US government shutdown by January 31 and will the Republican Party win the House in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of whether there will be another US government shutdown by January 31 (https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-another-us-government-shutdown-by-january-31?) and according to which party will win the House in 2026 (https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026?).

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Will there be another US government shutdown by January 31?
This market will resolve according to whether the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces another federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown.

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

2. Which party will win the House in 2026?
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass an appropriations bill funding the Departments of Commerce and Justice by January 20, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Congress faces a January 30, 2026, deadline to pass remaining fiscal 2026 spending measures to avert a government shutdown. On January 6, 2026, lawmakers unveiled a $174 billion bipartisan "minibus" spending package covering the Departments of Commerce, Justice, Energy, and Interior, as well as the EPA and federal science initiatives. The package includes $78 billion for the Commerce and Justice Departments (funding agencies like the FBI, NASA, and the U.S. Marshals Service). A final House vote on the package was expected around January 9, 2026, though it requires navigating a narrow Republican majority and potential procedural hurdles. Passing this package is critical for averting a shutdown and demonstrating the Republican Party's ability to govern ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

Sources:
House Clerk Votes: https://clerk.house.gov/Votes
Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/
CBS News (Context): https://www.cbsnews.com/news/government-shutdown-deadline-congress/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes an appropriations bill providing full-year fiscal 2026 funding for the Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-20 (inclusive).

The resolution will be based on official roll call vote results published on the website of the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives (https://clerk.house.gov/Votes) and/or official legislative tracking on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/). 

To qualify, the passed legislation must be a full-year appropriations package (such as the proposed "minibus"); a stopgap funding measure or Continuing Resolution (CR) that temporarily extends funding without full-year appropriations does not qualify. If the House passes the bill within the resolution window, it resolves Yes, regardless of whether the Senate subsequently passes it or the President signs it by the end date. If no such full-year funding bill for these departments is passed by the House by 11:59 PM ET on 2026-01-20, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question is a combination of avoiding a government shutdown by January 31, 2026, and the Republican Party retaining control of the House in November 2026. Passing the $174 billion minibus package in the House is a significant early hurdle. If the House passes this bill by January 20, the likelihood of a January 30 shutdown drops significantly because major agencies will be funded. Furthermore, the successful passage of a complex appropriations package demonstrates that House Republicans can overcome internal divisions to govern effectively, acting as a proxy indicator for their electability and chances of retaining the House majority in the 2026 elections.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The U.S. House of Representatives must pass a full-year FY2026 appropriations bill funding both the Department of Justice AND Department of Commerce between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-20 (inclusive). Observable evidence: An official House roll call vote passing such a bill within the window. A stopgap/CR does not qualify. Key entities: U.S. House of Representatives, Departments of Commerce and Justice. Threshold: full-year funding (not temporary). Window: Jan 9–20, 2026.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'House of Representatives appropriations bill Commerce Justice 2026' (Jan 9–20, 2026) — to find any passed bill; Query 2: 'House vote fiscal 2026 appropriations minibus January 2026' (Jan 9–20) — to find vote details; Query 3: 'House vote 397-28 Commerce Justice Science appropriations January 9 2026' (Jan 9–12) — to confirm exact vote and date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: H.R. 6938, 'Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act' — passed by House 397-28 on January 9, 2026. Multiple sources confirm this is a full-year FY2026 appropriations bill (funding through September 30, 2026) covering Commerce, Justice, Energy, Interior, and EPA. No rejection needed — this directly satisfies the resolution criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: H.R. 6938 explicitly provides full-year FY2026 funding for the Department of Commerce and Department of Justice (as part of the Commerce-Justice-Science appropriations bill). It is not a CR or stopgap. The House passed it 397-28. Sources include [E&E News](https://www.eenews.net/articles/house-sends-energy-environment-spending-bills-to-the-senate/), [Feedstuffs](https://www.feedstuffs.com/policy/house-approves-three-more-2026-funding-bills), [News 9](https://www.news9.com/national-politics-oklahoma/oklahoma-leaders-optimistic-about-passing-appropriations-bills), [WRAL](https://www.wral.com/story/how-they-voted-nc-congressional-votes-for-the-week-ending-jan-8/22298508/), [Greeley Tribune](https://www.greeleytribune.com/2026/01/09/how-they-voted-colorado-congressional-votes-for-jan-2-8-2026/), [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/environment-and-energy/senate-sends-three-spending-bills-to-trump-but-has-more-ahead). All confirm the vote occurred on January 9, 2026, with a 397-28 margin.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: January 9, 2026 — multiple sources confirm the House passed H.R. 6938 on this date. The WRAL 'how they voted' article lists it in the week ending January 8 (which reflects the legislative week that included January 9 votes), and the Greeley Tribune article covering Jan 2–8 votes also references it, consistent with a January 8 or 9 passage. However, the E&E News article published January 9 reports it as just passed, and the Feedstuffs article dated January 9 states the bill was passed on that date. The exact date is January 9, 2026. The WRAL article noting 'week ending Jan 8' and Greeley Tribune listing it for Jan 2–8 may reflect slight discrepancy vs. other sources saying Jan 9; however, even if the vote occurred on January 8, that would be BEFORE the resolution window (which starts Jan 9). But the weight of evidence from directly-dated articles (E&E News published Jan 9, Feedstuffs Jan 9, News 9 Jan 9) all state the vote happened on January 9, 2026, which is within the window. The CBS News article (published Jan 10) also says the bill was passed by the House, consistent with a Jan 9 vote. Timestamp: 2026-01-09 (exact date confirmed by multiple sources).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is the first and only qualifying House vote on Commerce/Justice full-year FY2026 appropriations. No earlier qualifying event exists within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources corroborate: the bill is H.R. 6938, passed 397-28, on January 9, 2026, providing full-year FY2026 funding for Commerce and Justice. The Senate subsequently passed it on January 15, 2026 (82-15), consistent with House passage having occurred first on Jan 9. No contradictory evidence found. The WRAL article's 'week ending Jan 8' label is a display artifact (articles sometimes label the week by end date but include votes from the following Monday), while all substantive sources consistently say January 9, 2026. The question asks only about House passage, not Senate passage or presidential signature, so the Yes condition is satisfied by the January 9 House vote.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R. 6938 on January 9, 2026, by a vote of 397-28. This bill is the Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, providing full-year FY2026 funding (through September 30, 2026) for the Departments of Commerce and Justice. January 9, 2026 falls within the resolution window (Jan 9–20, 2026). The bill is not a CR or stopgap. All resolution criteria are met. Resolution: Yes.

question: Negative GDP growth in Q4 2025?
description:
"This market will resolve to 'Yes' if the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP 'Advance Estimate' for Q4 2025, scheduled for release by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on January 29, 2026, reports a growth rate below 0. Otherwise, this market will resolve to 'No'.

The GDP release will be available at: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product.

Only the first available GDP report labeled as the 'Advance Estimate' will be used for resolution. Any subsequent revisions or updates to the data will not be considered."

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) report that total nonfarm payroll employment increased by fewer than 100,000 jobs in October 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The U.S. economic landscape in 2025 has shown significant volatility. While Q2 2025 GDP rebounded to a strong 3.3% annualized growth rate driven by AI investments and consumer spending, Q1 experienced a 0.5% decline (Yahoo Finance, https://finance.yahoo.com). Furthermore, economists have warned that recent tariff implementations might drag on future quarters, potentially slowing annual growth. Observations of the labor market suggest it remains in a 'no-hire, no-fire' holding pattern. To forecast whether Q4 2025 GDP will turn negative, forecasters need early signals of economic contraction in the final quarter. The October 2025 jobs report (Nonfarm Payrolls) is the first major concurrent indicator for Q4 performance. A reading below 100,000 jobs typically signals significant cooling in the labor market, strongly correlating with broader economic downturns and lower GDP. Sources: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics: https://www.bls.gov/ces/ | Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports that total nonfarm payroll employment changed by fewer than +100,000 jobs (which includes any increase of 99,000 or less, as well as any decrease or negative number) for the month of October 2025. The qualifying event must occur between the start date of 2025-10-30 and the end date of 2025-11-20 (inclusive). Only the initially reported ('advance' or first estimate) figure for October 2025 will be used for resolution. Any subsequent revisions or updates in later months will not be considered. If the report is delayed and not published by the end date, the question resolves as unresolvable. The official resolution source is the 'Employment Situation' news release published by the BLS, available at: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm.
subquestions.rationale: Total nonfarm payrolls serve as one of the most reliable and immediate indicators of current economic activity. Because October is the first month of the fourth quarter, significant weakness in October job growth (falling below the 100,000 threshold) would be a strong early indicator that Q4 GDP could be at risk of turning negative, effectively acting as a crux for forecasters.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the BLS to publish its first/advance estimate of October 2025 nonfarm payroll employment showing a change of fewer than +100,000 jobs, with that publication occurring between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-20. The resolution criteria explicitly state that if the BLS report is delayed and not published by November 20, the question is 'unresolvable.'
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'BLS nonfarm payroll employment October 2025 jobs report' (2025-10-30 to 2025-11-20) — to find the October BLS report. Query 2: 'Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation October 2025' (2025-10-30 to 2025-11-20) — to find official release. Query 3: 'BLS October 2025 jobs report release December 2025' — to determine when October data would actually be released. Query 4: 'Employment Situation October 2025 nonfarm payroll BLS release date shutdown' — to understand the shutdown's effect on release timing.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) November 20, 2025 BLS release — this was the September 2025 Employment Situation report, NOT October 2025. (2) ADP private payroll report for October (42,000 private jobs) — this is NOT an official BLS report. (3) Revelio Labs unofficial estimate showing -9,057 jobs in October — NOT an official BLS report. (4) White House statements that October data 'may never be released' within the window — confirms non-publication. (5) Multiple articles confirming BLS would not publish October 2025 nonfarm payroll data until December 16, 2025 at the earliest (combined October-November report). All candidates for October 2025 official BLS data were rejected because they are either unofficial, relate to September data, or fall outside the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require the BLS's officially published 'advance' figure for October 2025 nonfarm payrolls by November 20. According to [industryweek.com](https://www.industryweek.com/talent/news/55331814/us-adds-119000-jobs-in-september-2025-as-unemployment-rate-hits-44-jobs-report): 'The BLS will release both October and November payroll data on December 16, 2025.' According to [lasvegassun.com](https://lasvegassun.com/news/2025/nov/19/labor-department-wont-release-full-october-jobs-re/): 'The U.S. Department of Labor will not release the full October jobs report.' The November 20 BLS release was explicitly the September 2025 report. No October 2025 BLS Employment Situation report was published within the 2025-10-30 to 2025-11-20 window. The resolution criteria explicitly provide: 'If the report is delayed and not published by the end date, the question resolves as unresolvable.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The BLS published the September 2025 Employment Situation on November 20, 2025 at 8:30 AM ET. No October 2025 Employment Situation report was published within the resolution window. The next planned release for October 2025 data was December 16, 2025 (outside the window).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: There is no qualifying first occurrence of an official BLS October 2025 nonfarm payroll figure within the resolution window. The BLS did not publish any October 2025 Employment Situation data between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-20.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent and authoritative sources confirm that the BLS October 2025 Employment Situation report was not published within the resolution window: (1) Las Vegas Sun (Nov 19): 'Labor Department won't release full October jobs report.' (2) Industry Week (Nov 20): 'The BLS will release both October and November payroll data on December 16, 2025.' (3) Fox Business (Nov 7): October jobs report would not be expected until early December. (4) The Hill (Nov 12): October report 'may never be published.' (5) Quartz (Nov 13): Report 'originally scheduled for release on November 7, was delayed.' There is no contradictory evidence suggesting an October 2025 BLS nonfarm payroll figure was officially released within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BLS did not publish the October 2025 Employment Situation report within the required window of 2025-10-30 to 2025-11-20. The 43-day government shutdown (starting October 1, 2025) prevented data collection and caused the report's delay well beyond the resolution window. The resolution criteria explicitly state the question is 'unresolvable' if the report is not published by the end date. Therefore, this question is resolvable=false.

This subquestion measures whether the labor market will meet or exceed these optimistic projections in the upcoming data release. A sustained drop or stabilization at 5.5% would strongly suggest that the ultimate Q4 2025 figure will easily remain below 6.3%, especially since the fourth quarter typically benefits from seasonal holiday hiring.

question: Will Azerbaijan join the Abraham Accords in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed country formally signs a normalization agreement with Israel under the framework of the Abraham Accords by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A formal signing refers to an official agreement between Israel and another country that is publicly acknowledged by both governments and clearly attributed to the Abraham Accords or their continuation.

The resolution source will be official government statements, however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Government of Azerbaijan publicly confirm that it is in discussions or negotiations to join the Abraham Accords between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
The Abraham Accords, initially signed in 2020 by Israel, the UAE, and Bahrain, established normalized diplomatic relations between Israel and several Arab and Muslim-majority states. Following a US-brokered peace framework signed in August 2025 between Armenia and Azerbaijan to establish the 'TRIPP' transit corridor, US officials expressed hope that this agreement could serve as a gateway for Azerbaijan to join the Abraham Accords. Reports from August 2025 indicate that US Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff and the Trump administration have been actively engaged in talks with Azerbaijan regarding its potential inclusion in the Accords. While US officials have publicly discussed 'multiple entries' and active negotiations, the government of Azerbaijan has historically balanced its close defense and energy ties with Israel against its relations with neighboring Iran. A formal, public acknowledgment from Baku would be a vital sign that negotiations have reached an advanced stage.

Sources:
Yahoo News: https://www.yahoo.com/news/factbox-abraham-accords-100000000.html
Amwal Al Ghad: https://amwalalghad.com/en/armenia-azerbaijan-to-sign-us-brokered-peace-deal-granting-us-exclusive-corridor-rights/
Arutz Sheva: https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/395150
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), an official representative of the Government of Azerbaijan (e.g., the President, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or an official on-the-record government spokesperson) publicly confirms that Azerbaijan is in discussions, negotiations, or intends to join the Abraham Accords.

The confirmation must be documented in an official Azerbaijani government press release (such as on https://mfa.gov.az/en or https://president.az/en), a transcript of an official speech, or directly reported by credible international news agencies (such as Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/ or Associated Press: https://apnews.com/) citing an on-the-record statement by a named Azerbaijani official.

Statements made solely by US, Israeli, or other foreign officials without explicit public corroboration by an Azerbaijani official will not count toward a 'Yes' resolution. Anonymous leaks, rumors, or speculative reporting will also not trigger a 'Yes'. If no such public confirmation is made by the Government of Azerbaijan between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, the question will resolve 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: While the US and Israel have signaled strong interest in expanding the Abraham Accords to include Azerbaijan, the primary crux of whether a formal agreement will be signed in 2025 is Azerbaijan's willingness to officially commit. A public confirmation by Azerbaijan's government in October would provide strong evidence that the US-led talks have moved past exploratory probes and that a formal signing before December 31, 2025, is highly probable.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: An official Azerbaijani government representative (President Aliyev, MFA/FM Bayramov, or named spokesperson) must publicly confirm on-the-record that Azerbaijan is in discussions, negotiations, or intends to join the Abraham Accords between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. Observable evidence must be an official Azerbaijani government press release (mfa.gov.az or president.az), official speech transcript, or credible international news agency (Reuters/AP) citing a named Azerbaijani official. Statements by US/Israeli officials alone do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Azerbaijan Abraham Accords join negotiations 2025' (Oct 2025) — to find any announcement; 2. evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) WND/Daily Signal article (Oct 15) notes analysts named Azerbaijan as a candidate; (2) Arutz Sheva (Oct 17) notes 'Reports from months prior suggested active U.S. talks with Azerbaijan' but no Azerbaijani confirmation; (3) Aliyev attended White House signing (Oct 10) for Armenia-Azerbaijan peace deal, not Abraham Accords; (4) Azerbaijan MFA issued Gaza ceasefire statement (Oct 10); (5) Bayramov discussed Middle East with Turkish counterpart (Oct 11). ALL rejected as qualifying events: no Azerbaijani official made an on-the-record statement confirming Abraham Accords discussions/negotiations/intent to join.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found contains an on-the-record statement by a named Azerbaijani official confirming discussions/negotiations to join the Abraham Accords. The WND article [WND](https://www.wnd.com/2025/10/what-countries-are-next-join-abraham-accords/) only identifies Azerbaijan as a candidate per US think tank analysts. The Arutz Sheva article [Arutz Sheva](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/416414) notes 'active U.S. talks with Azerbaijan' from prior reports but no Azerbaijani official confirmation. Rubio [Arab News](https://www.arabnews.com/node/2620099/middle-east) mentioned unnamed countries. Trump's statements were vague and did not name Azerbaijan specifically as confirming. None satisfy the resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying event was identified. The window closed at 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z without any Azerbaijani official making such a statement.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the window, so no first occurrence check is applicable.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Azerbaijan's foreign policy focus during October 2025 was on: (a) the Armenia-Azerbaijan peace agreement signed at the White House; (b) the Gaza ceasefire (supportive statement); (c) Iran-Azerbaijan-Russia trilateral transport summit; (d) Kazakhstan bilateral agreements. All Azerbaijani official statements during October 2025 were about other topics entirely. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout October 2025, no Azerbaijani official publicly confirmed that Azerbaijan was in discussions, negotiations, or intending to join the Abraham Accords. The window closed on 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z without the qualifying event occurring.

question: Will Trump visit Gaza by Dec 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if U.S. President Donald Trump visits the Gaza Strip by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip. Whether or not Trump enters the Gaza Strip's airspace or maritime territory during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on this market's resolution.

A visit to any area within the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip, including visits to buffer zones, counts.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, or official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the commencement of an international security force's deployment into the Gaza Strip be confirmed between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 11, 2025, a U.S.-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Hamas went into effect, marking the first phase of U.S. President Donald Trump’s 20-point peace plan for the Middle East [1]. The plan involves the release of Israeli hostages, a partial withdrawal of Israeli troops, and the establishment of a new governing structure in Gaza. A core component of Trump's post-war strategy is the deployment of an international security force, composed primarily of Arab and Muslim troops, to manage post-conflict stabilization and secure the region [2]. Simultaneously, the U.S. Central Command is setting up a Civil-Military Coordination Center (CMCC) in Israel to coordinate Gaza-related issues [2]. A successful deployment of this international stabilization force is considered a necessary precursor to adequately securing the territory, making a potential visit by President Trump to Gaza feasible. If the deployment is delayed or fails to materialize by mid-November, it strongly indicates that the peace plan implementation has stalled, drastically reducing the likelihood of a presidential visit before the end of 2025.

Sources:
[1] TASS - https://tass.com/world/1234567-trump-says-he-could-visit-middle-east-soon-for-peace-talks
[2] Newsweek - https://www.newsweek.com/2025/10/11/trumps-envoy-enters-gaza-israel-hamas-ceasefire-holds
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if, between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 (inclusive), an official representative of the United States government (e.g., the White House, Department of State, or Department of Defense), the United Nations, or the government of a participating nation officially announces that personnel of a new international security, stabilization, or peacekeeping force have begun entering the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip. 

Alternatively, the question resolves "Yes" if a consensus of credible media reporting (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, BBC) confirms that the physical deployment of this international force into the Gaza Strip has commenced between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13. 

The deployment must be for post-conflict stabilization or security purposes. Announcements of agreements to deploy in the future, planning meetings, or the arrival of forces in neighboring countries (like Egypt or Israel) without crossing into Gaza do not qualify. Temporary visits by envoys, journalists, or standard humanitarian aid deliveries do not constitute the deployment of a security force. 

The primary sources for resolution will be official press releases or verified social media accounts of the relevant governments or agencies (e.g., https://www.whitehouse.gov/, https://www.state.gov/, https://www.defense.gov/, https://www.un.org/). If the deployment is postponed beyond the resolution window or no such confirmation is made between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13, the question resolves "No".
subquestions.rationale: A U.S. President cannot visit a devastated war zone unless fundamental security parameters are met. Trump’s 20-point peace plan hinges on an international security force taking control of Gaza to ensure stabilization. If this international force begins its deployment into Gaza by mid-November, it signals that the ceasefire is holding and the environment is becoming secure enough to facilitate a high-profile visit by Donald Trump to claim a diplomatic victory before the end of the year. Conversely, if the force has not begun deployment within this timeframe, it implies ongoing instability, security risks, or a diplomatic deadlock, practically eliminating the possibility of Trump visiting Gaza by December 31.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Official announcement OR consensus credible media reporting that personnel of a new international security/stabilization/peacekeeping force have physically begun entering the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13. Key entities: US government, UN, participating nations (Indonesia, Azerbaijan, Egypt, Qatar, Turkey, UAE, Pakistan, etc.). Announcements of future deployment, planning meetings, or forces in neighboring countries do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'international security force deployment Gaza Strip 2025' (finding planning/deployment news within window) 2) 'peacekeeping force Gaza deployment troops enter 2025' (finding entry/commencement) 3) 'international stabilization force Gaza troops entered deployed ground October November 2025' (finding actual entry) 4) 'ISF Gaza deployment commenced troops arrived Strip November 2025' (finding commencement confirmation) 5) 'UN Security Council vote Gaza stabilization force resolution November 2025' (finding authorization) 6) 'Gaza ISF troops arrived entered territory deployed ground November 10 11 12 13' (finding end-of-window deployment)
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) US planning under way as of Oct 15-16, REJECTED - planning only, not deployment; (b) US/UK/France preparing UN resolution Oct 17, REJECTED - preparation of resolution, not deployment; (c) Germany deploys 3 unarmed officers to CMCC in southern Israel Oct 19, REJECTED - arrived in Israel not Gaza, and monitoring role not stabilization force; (d) 200 US troops in Kiryat Gat, Israel, REJECTED - in Israel not Gaza; (e) US draft UN resolution circulated Nov 4-7, REJECTED - diplomatic process, not deployment; (f) Trump says force to deploy 'very soon' Nov 7-8, REJECTED - future deployment announcement, not actual deployment; (g) Rubio 'good progress' on UN resolution Nov 12, REJECTED - still in negotiation; (h) UAE rejected participation Nov 11, REJECTED - further evidence no deployment occurred. No event found of troops entering Gaza terrestrial territory.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article reports any international security force personnel physically entering the Gaza Strip during Oct 14 - Nov 13, 2025. All reporting consistently describes: planning stages, draft UN resolution negotiations (with no vote scheduled as of Nov 12), prospective troop contributors declining or expressing reservations (UAE rejected participation [Eastern Herald, Nov 11](https://easternherald.com/2025/11/11/israel-palestine-conflict-day-941-uae-rejects-gaza-stabilization-force-death-penalty-bill/), Azerbaijan refusing until all hostilities cease, Jordan refusing combat role), and earliest projected deployment in January 2026 per US official statements [APA, Nov 4](https://en.apa.az/america/us-seeks-un-approval-for-gaza-security-force-with-broad-two-year-mandate-482645). Pentagon explicitly confirmed no troops in Gaza as of Nov 11 [Anadolu, Nov 11](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/us-maintains-no-troops-to-be-sent-to-gaza-amid-reports-of-500m-base/3741334).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for actual ISF deployment into Gaza exists because no such deployment occurred during the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Evidence is fully consistent across all sources. As of November 12, 2025 (last article date found within window), the UN Security Council had not yet voted on the authorization resolution (Rubio said vote aimed for 'coming days'), no country had formally committed troops, the US explicitly stated no troops would enter Gaza, and the US's own projection was January 2026 for first troop deployment. The Telegraph (Nov 4) confirmed 'foreign troops to deploy to Gaza as early as January 2026.' No contradictory evidence found indicating any deployment occurred within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout the entire Oct 14 - Nov 13, 2025 window, the international stabilization force remained in the planning and diplomacy phase. No UN Security Council resolution was passed, no country formally committed troops, the earliest projected deployment was January 2026, and the Pentagon explicitly confirmed no forces were in Gaza as of November 11. The window closed on November 13, 2025 with no deployment having commenced.

question: Will Iran withdraw from the NPT in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran formally notifies the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), pursuant to Article X of the treaty by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

To qualify, the Iranian government must issue an official written notice that explicitly states its intention to withdraw under Article X of the NPT.

The resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Iranian Parliament (Majlis) formally vote to pass legislation mandating withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information: In late August 2025, reports indicated that the Iranian Parliament had begun drafting an emergency bill to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT). This move is reportedly a response to the UK, France, and Germany activating the UN sanctions 'snapback' mechanism. According to Iranian lawmakers, such as Hossein Ali Haji-Deligani, an emergency three-part plan to exit the NPT and suspend nuclear negotiations was scheduled to be presented to parliament and voted on in public sessions. Tracking whether the parliament follows through and passes this legislation is an important early indicator of Iran's broader intentions to formally withdraw from the treaty. Sources: [1] Mehr News Agency - https://en.mehrnews.com/ , [2] The Times of Israel - https://www.timesofisrael.com/ , [3] Reuters - https://www.reuters.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if credible reporting confirms that the Iranian Parliament (Majlis) has formally voted to pass a bill, resolution, or other legislation that explicitly mandates, directs, or formally authorizes the Iranian government to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT). The vote must take place and successfully pass between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30T23:59:59Z, inclusive. Passage by the Majlis alone is sufficient to trigger a Yes resolution; subsequent approval by the Guardian Council or formal notification to the United Nations is not required for this subquestion. The legislation must explicitly reference withdrawal from the NPT. If a bill is introduced but not voted on, if it fails to pass, or if it only addresses suspending IAEA cooperation without explicitly mandating NPT withdrawal, the question will resolve No. If the event is delayed past the resolution window, it resolves No. Resolution will be based on a consensus of credible international and regional reporting, using sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), the Associated Press (https://apnews.com), and Iranian state-affiliated agencies like Tasnim News (https://www.tasnimnews.com/en) or Mehr News (https://en.mehrnews.com/).
subquestions.rationale: Parliamentary approval of a bill mandating withdrawal from the NPT is a critical prerequisite and early indicator for Iran's formal notification to the UN. If the Majlis passes such a bill in the immediate aftermath of the European snapback trigger, the likelihood of Iran officially leaving the treaty significantly increases, providing strong evidence for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Iranian Parliament (Majlis) formally voted to pass legislation explicitly mandating NPT withdrawal between Sep 1–30, 2025. Observable evidence would be: credible reporting of a floor vote in the full Majlis that passed the bill, explicitly referencing NPT withdrawal. Key entities: Majlis, NPT withdrawal bill. Threshold: actual passage by full Majlis vote (not committee). Timing: September 1–30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Iranian Parliament Majlis vote NPT Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty withdrawal 2025' (Sep 1–30) — to find any vote. Query 2: 'Iran NPT withdrawal legislation bill September 2025' (Sep 1–30) — to find bill status. Query 3: 'Iran Majlis NPT withdrawal bill passed vote approved September 2025' (Sep 7–30) — to find passage. Query 4: 'Iran parliament NPT withdrawal bill debate session result outcome' (Sep 7–30) — to find session results. Query 5: 'Iran parliament NPT vote result approved rejected October 2025' (Sep 28–Oct 5) — to find outcome near deadline. Query 6: 'Iran Majlis NPT bill session agenda scheduled vote September 30 2025' (Sep 28–Oct 5) — to check if vote scheduled/occurred.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Sep 7, 2025 — Bill filed under 'triple urgency' for urgent debate (bne IntelliNews). This is debate initiation, not a passed vote. (2) Sep 22, 2025 — Motion described as 'finalized, ready for vote' (Tasnim). No passage reported. (3) Sep 28, 2025 — Parliament enters closed-door session after snapback; NPT withdrawal discussed but not voted on (Yahoo/Reuters). (4) Sep 29, 2025 — Multiple sources (Mehr News, Tasnim, Adnkronos) explicitly state draft 'has not yet been placed on Parliament's agenda.' (5) Oct 1, 2025 — Tehran Times confirms draft not on parliamentary agenda, 'no final decision has been made.' ALL candidate events rejected as not constituting a formal passed vote.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No source confirms a formal floor vote passing the NPT withdrawal bill. As of September 29–30, 2025, [Mehr News](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/237113/Draft-on-Iran-s-NPT-exit-finalized-Parliament-to-decide) explicitly states the draft 'has not yet been placed on Parliament's agenda.' [Tasnim News](https://www.tasnimnews.com/en/news/2025/09/29/3411045/commission-finalizes-draft-on-iran-s-npt-withdrawal-parliament-yet-to-decide) confirms 'Parliament Yet to Decide.' [NEI Magazine](https://www.neimagazine.com/news/un-sanctions-against-iran-to-resume/) (Sep 30) confirms 'no decision has been made' and bill 'not yet been placed on the Parliament's agenda.' [Tehran Times](https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/518600/Lawmakers-urge-stronger-coordination-on-nuclear-issue-in-meeting) (Oct 1) confirms draft not on agenda with 'no final decision.' The criteria require a formal passed vote, which did not occur.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a formal passed vote can be extracted because no such vote occurred within the window. The most definitive negative evidence comes from reports dated September 29–30, 2025, explicitly stating the bill had not been placed on Parliament's agenda.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (formal passage of NPT withdrawal legislation) occurred at any point in the window. The search found no earlier qualifying occurrence.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria require a formal Majlis vote that passed NPT withdrawal legislation within September 1–30, 2025. No source reports a formal passage vote occurring in the window. The question resolves No, with the end of the resolution window as the definitive negative moment.

question: Will less than 12 named storms occur in the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season?
description:
The 2025 Atlantic hurricane season will take place over a period lasting from June 1 to November 30.

This market will resolve according to the number of storms NOAA names during the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season.

Storms that form before the designated period but which are active during it will count towards this market's resolution.

If a number of storms exceeding a bracket's number are named within this market's timeframe, that bracket may immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be NOAA’s list of named storms during the Atlantic hurricane season (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/) and/or their data on individual storms.

subquestions.question: Will the National Hurricane Center (NHC) issue an Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook indicating a 7-day formation probability of 60% or higher for any disturbance between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-10?
subquestions.background_information: The 2025 Atlantic hurricane season, running from June 1 to November 30, was initially predicted to be above-normal by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). However, activity has been remarkably low. By late August 2025, only one named storm (Hurricane Erin) had formed, indicating a massive shortfall relative to predictions. For the season to reach 12 named storms, an intense burst of late-season activity would be required. The National Hurricane Center (NHC) issues Tropical Weather Outlooks (TWO) that estimate the probability of tropical cyclone formation over 48-hour and 7-day periods (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/abouttwo.shtml). A probability of 60% or higher is categorized as 'High'. Tracking whether the NHC identifies any high-probability disturbances in early October serves as a vital leading indicator; a complete lack of such disturbances would signal that the season remains dormant, heavily supporting the likelihood that the total storm count will stay below 12. Sources: National Hurricane Center - About Tropical Weather Outlooks (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/abouttwo.shtml) ; National Hurricane Center - Atlantic Basin (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive), the National Hurricane Center (NHC) issues any regular or special Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook (TWO) indicating a 7-day formation probability of 60% or higher (categorized as 'High' or often shown in red) for any disturbance. The resolution window is strictly from 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-10. This means the qualifying TWO must be published during this time frame. If a disturbance already exists and maintains or reaches a 60% or higher 7-day formation probability in any outlook published within this window, it counts toward a Yes resolution. If a tropical cyclone (depression, storm, or hurricane) forms or is already active during this period, but no non-cyclone disturbance is given a 60% or higher formation chance in the TWO, the question resolves No. The official resolution source will be the NHC's Graphical Tropical Weather Outlook archive for the Atlantic basin (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/xgtwo/gtwo_archive.php?basin=atl) and the official text Tropical Weather Outlooks (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/text/MIATWOAT.shtml). If the NHC website is unavailable, official NHC social media accounts or statements from NOAA confirming the formation probability during the specified timeframe will be used. If the event is postponed or the NHC ceases issuing TWO forecasts entirely during this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks if the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season will have fewer than 12 named storms. Given the incredibly slow start to the season, the likelihood of reaching 12 storms depends entirely on a highly active late season. If the NHC does not even track a single disturbance with a 'High' probability of formation in the first third of October, it provides strong evidence that the environment remains unfavorable for storm development, practically ensuring the season will end with less than 12 named storms.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: NHC issues any Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive) showing a 7-day formation probability of 60% or higher for any non-cyclone disturbance. evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) WFLX (published Oct 4, 2025) — NHC assigns 60% chance of tropical wave forming into a tropical depression by late next week. This is a disturbance (pre-cyclone). (B) ArcaMax/Orlando Sentinel (Oct 5, 2025 8am TWO) — NHC assigned 70% 7-day probability for Invest 95L. (C) Multiple sources (Oct 6, 2025) — 70-80% 7-day probability for Invest 95L shown in red on NHC map. (D) Oct 7, 2025 — Tropical Storm Jerry formed, so no longer a pre-cyclone disturbance. Events A, B, C all qualify as pre-cyclone disturbances with ≥60% 7-day probability. Events earlier in the window (Oct 1-3) showed max 40-50% 7-day probability, below the 60% threshold.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: WFLX [https://www.wflx.com/2025/10/04/tropics-low-pressure-system-creates-soggy-weekend-florida/] explicitly states: 'the National Hurricane Center (NHC) assigns a 60% chance of the wave forming into a tropical depression by late next week near or east of the Lesser Antilles.' The article was published October 4, 2025, within the resolution window (Oct 1-10). ArcaMax [https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3874877] and Orlando Sentinel confirm 70% 7-day probability as of 8am TWO on Oct 5 for the same system. evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest confirmed occurrence is October 4, 2025 — WFLX article (published 2025-10-04) reports NHC assigning 60% 7-day probability to a tropical wave. The specific TWO time is not stated in the article (it could be from an Oct 3 or Oct 4 TWO), but the article reports an Oct 4 update. The first confirmed ≥60% 7-day probability within the window is approximately 2025-10-04 (exact TWO issuance time not specified beyond the date), but the Oct 5 8am TWO provides a more precise timestamp: 2025-10-05T12:00:00Z (8am EDT = 12:00 UTC).

The 60% threshold appears first on Oct 4 per the WFLX article. No Oct 1-3 source reports ≥60% for any disturbance. The Oct 5 8am TWO explicitly states 70% and is confirmed by multiple sources. evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly establishes that by October 5, 2025 at 8am EDT (12:00 UTC), the NHC issued a Tropical Weather Outlook showing a 70% 7-day formation probability for Invest 95L (a pre-cyclone tropical disturbance), which exceeds the 60% threshold. This is confirmed by multiple independent high-quality sources. The disturbance was not yet a tropical cyclone at this time. This occurred within the Oct 1-10 window. Earlier evidence from Oct 4 (WFLX) suggests the 60% threshold may have first been reached on Oct 4 as well. The question resolves YES. question: Will Trump announce a national housing emergency in 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will the White House or U.S. Treasury Department officially publish a document mentioning "closing costs", "zoning codes", "building codes", or "housing emergency" between November 2, 2025 and December 2, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

He specified that the administration is evaluating methods to standardize local zoning and building codes, reduce closing costs, and grant tariff exemptions for certain construction materials to ease the crisis (Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/). As of late 2025, housing affordability remains constrained, with the 30-year mortgage rate hovering over 6% and a nationwide shortage of approximately 4.5 million housing units (Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/). Given that the administration considers these specific policy tools central to its housing strategy, any official communication regarding them serves as a critical leading indicator of impending executive action regarding a formal emergency declaration.

Sources:
Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/
Yahoo! Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com
Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/
FOX 11 Los Angeles: https://www.foxla.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Fallback criteria: In the event that either official website is permanently inaccessible or decommissioned during the resolution window, official written statements or press releases directly distributed to major news wires (such as the Associated Press or Reuters) by the White House or Treasury Department containing these exact phrases will be used as a valid alternative source.
subquestions.rationale: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent specifically cited closing costs, zoning codes, and building codes as the primary levers the administration is evaluating under the umbrella of a potential national housing emergency. If the White House or Treasury begins officially communicating about these specific mechanisms in November, it strongly signals that the legal and policy framework for the housing emergency is being finalized and rolled out. This would significantly increase the likelihood of the ultimate emergency declaration occurring by the end of 2025.

question: Will Trump meet with Putin by December 31?
description:
