subquestions.question: Will U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio or U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff hold an in-person meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov or Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 15, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin met at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson in Anchorage, Alaska, to discuss potential resolutions to the war in Ukraine. The summit concluded without a concrete agreement, though both leaders indicated a willingness to continue the dialogue (https://www.salon.com/2025/08/16/no-deal-in-alaska-trump-putin-talk-peace/). The U.S. delegation included Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, while the Russian delegation was represented by Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov (https://tass.com/politics/1834925). 

Historically, negotiations of this magnitude rely heavily on continuous engagement between high-level diplomats to hammer out details before subsequent leader-level summits are held. The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) High-Level Week typically takes place in late September, offering a highly probable venue for these officials to hold bilateral sideline meetings. 

Sources:
Salon - No deal in Alaska: Trump, Putin talk peace, with no resolution: https://www.salon.com/2025/08/16/no-deal-in-alaska-trump-putin-talk-peace/
TASS - Kremlin says it keeps details of Putin-Trump summit under wraps to protect peace process: https://tass.com/politics/1834925
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if any of the specified U.S. officials (Secretary of State Marco Rubio or Special Envoy Steve Witkoff) meets in person with any of the specified Russian officials (Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov or Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

A "meeting" is defined as a deliberate, direct in-person interaction, such as a formal bilateral meeting or a substantive "pull-aside" discussion. Merely attending the same multilateral event (such as a UN General Assembly session), being in the same room, or exchanging brief pleasantries without a substantive discussion does not qualify.

The meeting must be publicly acknowledged or reported by official government sources, such as the U.S. Department of State (https://www.state.gov/), the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://mid.ru/en/), or the Kremlin (https://en.kremlin.ru/), or it must be reported by a consensus of credible, independent media outlets (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, Bloomberg). 

If the meeting is scheduled to occur after 2025-10-01, or if a meeting is postponed beyond the resolution window, it does not count toward a Yes resolution. If no such meeting occurs and is reported by the end of 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: High-level diplomatic summits between heads of state usually require extensive preparation and intermediate negotiations by top diplomats. A meeting between the principal aides and foreign ministers who attended the Alaska summit would serve as a powerful indicator that substantive talks are advancing, significantly increasing the likelihood of a subsequent Trump-Putin summit by the end of 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: A deliberate, direct in-person meeting between (Rubio OR Witkoff) AND (Lavrov OR Ushakov) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Meeting must be a formal bilateral or substantive pull-aside, not merely co-attendance at a multilateral event. Must be reported by official government sources or consensus of credible media.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Rubio Lavrov meeting September 2025' - to find direct bilateral meetings; 2) 'Witkoff Ushakov meeting September 2025' - to find Witkoff-Ushakov meetings; 3) 'Rubio Lavrov bilateral meeting September 24 2025 UNGA New York State Department' - to confirm the UNGA meeting; 4) 'Witkoff Ushakov Lavrov meeting bilateral September 2025' - to check for other meetings before Sept 24.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Rubio-Lavrov bilateral meeting on September 24, 2025, on sidelines of UNGA 80th session in New York - 50 minutes, behind closed doors, substantive discussion about Ukraine. Reported by TASS, RT, State Department, multiple credible outlets. (2) Alaska summit (Aug 15, 2025) where Rubio, Witkoff, Lavrov, and Ushakov all participated - REJECTED as outside the window (before Sep 1, 2025). No qualifying Witkoff-Ushakov or Witkoff-Lavrov bilateral meetings found in September 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Rubio-Lavrov meeting on September 24, 2025, at UNGA sidelines satisfies all criteria: (a) It was a deliberate, direct in-person interaction — a formal bilateral meeting lasting approximately 50 minutes held behind closed doors, NOT merely co-attendance at a multilateral session. [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2020907), [TASS State Dept statement](https://tass.com/world/2020945), [RT](https://www.rt.com/news/625219-lavrov-rubio-unga-talks/), [Interfax-Ukraine](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1107258.html); (b) It was publicly acknowledged by official sources: the U.S. State Department released a written statement via Deputy Spokesperson Tommy Piggott: 'Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. The Secretary reiterated President Trump's call for the killing to stop and the need for Moscow to take meaningful steps toward a durable resolution of the Russia-Ukraine war'; (c) Russian MFA also confirmed the meeting; (d) Multiple credible independent media (Reuters, TASS, RT, etc.) reported it; (e) The meeting occurred within the resolution window (September 24, 2025).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The meeting occurred on September 24, 2025. The Russian Foreign Ministry confirmed it was scheduled for 7 p.m. Moscow time (4 p.m. GMT / 16:00 UTC) on September 24, 2025. Multiple sources confirm the September 24, 2025 date. evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying meeting within the September 1–October 1 window was found. evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) The meeting was described as on the 'sidelines' of UNGA — however, the resolution criteria explicitly distinguish between 'merely attending the same multilateral event' and a 'formal bilateral meeting or substantive pull-aside discussion.' (2) Multiple high-quality sources (TASS, RT, Interfax-Ukraine, Mehr News, State Department official statement) all confirm the same event on the same date with consistent details. (3) No conflicting evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Rubio-Lavrov bilateral meeting on September 24, 2025, on the sidelines of the 80th UN General Assembly in New York clearly satisfies all resolution criteria. It was a deliberate, in-person, substantive 50-minute bilateral meeting between U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, publicly acknowledged by both the U.S. State Department and Russian Foreign Ministry, reported by multiple credible media outlets, and occurring within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window. question: TrumpRX launched by January 31, 2026?

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve's primary credit outstanding (Discount Window borrowing) exceed $10 billion in any H.4.1 release between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve's discount window, specifically the primary credit facility, serves as a vital backup source of liquidity for depository institutions. Under normal market conditions, banks prefer to borrow from the federal funds market or use other private funding sources rather than the discount window to avoid any associated stigma. Consequently, primary credit usage typically remains quite low (often under $3 billion). However, a sudden spike in discount window borrowing is a strong indicator of acute liquidity stress in the banking sector. During the regional banking crisis in March 2023, which saw the failures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, primary credit borrowing surged from roughly $4.5 billion to over $152 billion in a single week. Given recent concerns highlighted by a Federal Reserve analysis indicating that large U.S. banks face higher failure risks than before the 2008 Great Financial Crisis due to increased reliance on uninsured deposits and weaker economic capital, monitoring discount window usage is crucial. Tracking whether primary credit outstanding exceeds a $10 billion threshold provides an observable, early warning signal of banking sector distress that could culminate in an FDIC-administered bank failure by March 31, 2026.

Sources:
Federal Reserve H.4.1 Release: https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/
Federal Reserve Discount Window: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/discountwindow.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the 'Wednesday level' for 'Primary credit' (listed under 'Factors Affecting Reserve Balances of Depository Institutions') reported in any official Federal Reserve H.4.1 statistical release published between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 (inclusive) exceeds 10,000 (which corresponds to $10 billion, as the figures in the release are reported in millions of dollars). The official H.4.1 release can be found at https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/.

If no H.4.1 release published within this exact timeframe (between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12) reports a Wednesday level for primary credit strictly greater than 10,000, the question resolves No. If the Federal Reserve ceases to publish the H.4.1 release, delays publication beyond the resolution window, or changes its format such that 'Primary credit' is no longer reported, the question will be resolved using any official Federal Reserve statement or data release that provides the equivalent discount window primary credit outstanding for dates within the specified window.
subquestions.rationale: A significant increase in primary credit borrowing indicates that banks are facing severe liquidity shortages and are unable to secure funding through normal interbank channels. Historically, such spikes (e.g., in March 2023) have immediately preceded or accompanied major bank failures. Therefore, if primary credit exceeds $10 billion, it strongly signals that at least one institution is in distress, directly updating the probability of an ultimate bank failure by March 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Any H.4.1 release published 2025-12-13 to 2026-01-12 must report Wednesday level for 'Primary credit' > 10,000 (i.e., > $10 billion). Key entities: Federal Reserve H.4.1, Primary credit line item, threshold of $10,000 million, window 2025-12-13 to 2026-01-12.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Federal Reserve H.4.1 primary credit discount window borrowing 2025 December' - to find direct H.4.1 data reports. 2. 'Federal Reserve discount window primary credit outstanding billion 2025' - to find specific dollar levels. 3. 'Federal Reserve H.4.1 factors affecting reserve balances primary credit December 2025 January 2026' - for H.4.1-specific coverage. 4. 'Federal Reserve discount window banks avoidance stigma primary credit low level 2025' - to establish baseline behavior. 5. 'Federal Reserve balance sheet primary credit borrowing banks weekly release January 2026' - for January 2026 releases.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Standing Repo Facility recorded $74.6B on Dec 31, 2025 — REJECTED: this is a different facility from the Discount Window/primary credit. (2) Banks reported to be avoiding the discount window due to stigma per multiple sources — SUPPORTS a No resolution. (3) No news article explicitly reported primary credit exceeding $10B in any H.4.1 release in the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article directly reported a primary credit Wednesday level > 10,000 in any H.4.1 release from 2025-12-13 to 2026-01-12. The Burning Platform (Jan 2, 2026) explicitly stated 'banks are avoiding the emergency window due to stigma' [https://www.theburningplatform.com/2026/01/01/anyone-knows-a-good-plumber/]. FXStreet (Nov 5, 2025) confirmed stigma discourages discount window use. Historical norms show primary credit typically near zero in non-crisis periods. All evidence points to very low discount window usage, far below $10 billion.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp of a qualifying event (primary credit > $10B) could be extracted — no such event was reported.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at all, so first-occurrence check is moot. All evidence indicates primary credit remained very low throughout the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The $74.6B Standing Repo Facility usage on Dec 31, 2025 might suggest banks were borrowing heavily from the Fed, but this is explicitly NOT the Discount Window/primary credit — it is a different facility. Multiple sources confirmed banks specifically avoided the discount window due to stigma while using the SRF. No source reported elevated discount window primary credit near $10B. The question resolves No.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence consistently indicates that primary credit (Discount Window borrowing) remained far below $10 billion during the window. Banks avoided the discount window due to stigma, instead using the Standing Repo Facility. No H.4.1 release in the window reported primary credit > 10,000 million. Resolution: No.

question: Will ChatGPT reach 1b monthly active users in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will Similarweb report that chatgpt.com received 6.2 billion or more total visits in August 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
To determine if ChatGPT is on track to reach 1 billion monthly active users (MAUs) by the end of 2025, tracking its near-term web traffic growth is a crucial indicator. According to Decrypt, in May 2025 Similarweb reported that ChatGPT commanded 80% of the generative AI market traffic with 5.5 billion visits (https://decrypt.co/). By early August 2025, OpenAI announced that the platform was on track to hit 700 million weekly active users, representing a massive fourfold increase year-over-year and surging engagement following the release of new models (https://techcrunch.com/). 

Since Weekly Active Users (WAU) have already reached 700 million, the total MAU figure is likely higher. However, to confidently project reaching the 1 billion MAU mark by December 2025, engagement and traffic must maintain a strong upward trajectory through the latter half of the year. Reaching 6.2 billion visits on Similarweb in August 2025 would represent a steady ~12.7% growth compared to May 2025, confirming the sustained momentum required to hit the ultimate 1 billion MAU milestone.

Sources:
Decrypt: https://decrypt.co/
TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/
Similarweb: https://www.similarweb.com/website/chatgpt.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Similarweb publicly reports that the 'Total Visits' to chatgpt.com for the month of August 2025 was 6.2 billion (6.2B) or higher, and this data is published or accessed between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01.

The primary resolution source will be the publicly available data on the Similarweb platform (https://www.similarweb.com/website/chatgpt.com/). If the exact figure is reported with decimals (e.g., 6.2B, 6.3B), it will count as a 'Yes' if it is exactly 6.2B or greater. If the reported total visits are 6.1B or lower, this question resolves to 'No'.

Fallback criteria: If Similarweb does not update its platform with August 2025 data between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, or if the data becomes paywalled and inaccessible to the public, resolution will be based on a consensus of reputable media reports (e.g., TechCrunch, Bloomberg, Reuters) covering Similarweb's August 2025 traffic data for chatgpt.com published within the same timeframe. 

If neither the Similarweb platform nor reputable media report this specific August 2025 data by 2025-10-01, the question will resolve as 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Similarweb's monthly visit metrics are highly correlated with OpenAI's active user counts. Tracking whether August 2025 traffic breached 6.2 billion visits provides an objective, early-indicator benchmark. If traffic reaches this level, it demonstrates that ChatGPT is successfully sustaining the high growth needed to achieve 1 billion MAUs by the end of 2025. If it falls short, it may indicate user base saturation, significantly lowering the probability of reaching the ultimate milestone.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question resolves Yes if Similarweb publicly reports that chatgpt.com received 6.2 billion (6.2B) or more total visits in August 2025, with this data published or accessed between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. The threshold is 6.2B; any figure of 6.1B or lower resolves No.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Similarweb chatgpt.com total visits August 2025' (to find direct Similarweb data on August traffic). Query 2: 'chatgpt.com traffic August 2025 billion visits' (to find media reports on ChatGPT's August traffic figures). evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple sources from within the resolution window (September 2025) explicitly report ChatGPT received 5.8 billion visits in August 2025, citing Similarweb data: (1) Search Engine Land (2025-09-09) citing Similarweb/Brodie Clark: '5.8 billion visits'; (2) TechRadar (2025-09-25) citing Hostinger referencing Similarweb: '5.8 billion visits'; (3) Search Engine Roundtable (2025-09-09) citing Similarweb. No source reports 6.2 billion or more visits for August 2025. The AI Big Bang Study (I Programmer, 2025-09-03) notes ChatGPT 'averaged 5 billion visits per month in the latest quarter', further consistent with the sub-6.2B figure.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criterion requires ≥6.2 billion visits. The explicitly reported figure from Similarweb data for August 2025 is 5.8 billion visits, as reported by [Search Engine Land](https://searchengineland.com/nearly-all-chatgpt-users-visit-google-461830) (2025-09-09) and [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/website-building/you-can-now-get-your-website-ai-ready-with-just-one-click-thanks-to-hostinger) (2025-09-25). 5.8B is explicitly below the 6.2B threshold. The criteria are not met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest publication reporting the 5.8 billion visits figure for August 2025 is Search Engine Land on 2025-09-09. This is within the resolution window (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01). The figure is explicitly stated as 5.8 billion visits, attributed to Similarweb data.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence (a report of ≥6.2B visits) exists. The first occurrence of August 2025 data reporting was 5.8B visits (Search Engine Land, 2025-09-09), which definitively does not meet the 6.2B threshold.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for any source reporting ≥6.2B visits for chatgpt.com in August 2025 — none found. The 5.8B figure is consistent across multiple independent sources citing Similarweb. evidence.step8_final_decision: Similarweb data, as reported by multiple reputable media outlets (Search Engine Land, TechRadar) within the resolution window, clearly places chatgpt.com's August 2025 total visits at 5.8 billion — well below the 6.2 billion threshold required for a Yes resolution. subquestions.question: Will Israel and Turkey publicly announce a formalized military deconfliction agreement regarding Syria between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information: Following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, both Israel and Turkey have increased their military involvement in Syria. Israel has conducted strikes to protect Druze civilians and counter Iranian influence, while Turkey has expanded its footprint by backing the transitional government led by Ahmad al-Sharaa (https://waovam.com/regional-powers-clash-after-israel-targets-syrian-territory-in-defense-of-vulnerable-druze-civilians). The overlapping operations have led to near-misses, including an incident where Turkish jets allegedly used electronic signals to warn Israeli aircraft near Palmyra (https://www.turkishminute.com/israeli-defense-minister-katz-thanks-azerbaijan-for-mediating-with-turkey-over-syria). In May 2025, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz confirmed that Azerbaijan was mediating talks between Israel and Turkey to establish a deconfliction mechanism to prevent unwanted direct military clashes in Syria. Whether these talks succeed and result in a formalized agreement is a critical indicator of the likelihood of a kinetic military clash between the two nations later in the year. Sources: waovam.com (https://waovam.com/regional-powers-clash-after-israel-targets-syrian-territory-in-defense-of-vulnerable-druze-civilians); Turkish Minute (https://www.turkishminute.com/israeli-defense-minister-katz-thanks-azerbaijan-for-mediating-with-turkey-over-syria).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if official government representatives from either Israel or Turkey, or an official mediating party (such as Azerbaijan), publicly announce the establishment or finalization of a military deconfliction mechanism or agreement specifically concerning their respective military operations in or around Syria, and this announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The agreement does not need to be a formal peace treaty, but must explicitly address military coordination, deconfliction, or the prevention of accidental clashes between Israeli and Turkish armed forces. Resolution will be based on consensus reporting from credible international news agencies such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) or the Associated Press (https://apnews.com), or official government press releases. If no such announcement is made within the specified window (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01), the question resolves No. Rumors or unofficial leaks without on-the-record confirmation from government officials will not suffice for a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The successful establishment of a deconfliction mechanism would significantly reduce the probability of an accidental or intentional military clash between Israel and Turkey in Syria. If the talks stall and no agreement is reached by October 2025, the risk of their ongoing operations intersecting and escalating into a direct clash remains elevated, thereby acting as a crucial indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Official government representatives from Israel or Turkey (or Azerbaijan as mediator) must publicly announce the establishment or finalization of a military deconfliction mechanism or agreement specifically about Israeli and Turkish military operations in/around Syria, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive. Required: on-the-record confirmation from government officials, reported by credible international news agencies. Observable evidence: Press release, news conference, or credible news agency reporting of such an announcement.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Israel Turkey military deconfliction agreement Syria 2025' (Sept-Oct window) — to find direct evidence; 2) 'Israel Turkey Syria military coordination announcement' (Sept-Oct window) — broader coordination search; 3) 'Israel Turkey deconfliction hotline Syria military agreement September 2025' — specific mechanism search; 4) 'Azerbaijan mediation Israel Turkey Syria military deal 2025' — mediator search; 5) 'Israel Turkey military coordination pact signed September 2025' — signed agreement search; 6) 'Israel Turkey relations collision course military confrontation Syria 2025' — to find contradictory evidence showing no agreement
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (a) Israel-Turkey tensions escalating throughout September 2025, with Israeli strikes on Turkish-supplied equipment in Syria on Sept 8-9, 2025; (b) Turkey-Syria military cooperation agreement signed in August 2025 (pre-window); (c) Israel-Syria security negotiations ongoing but not finalized by end of September; (d) Turkey attempting to block Israel-Syria security agreement (reported Sept 29); (e) U.S. envoy confirmed Israel-Syria close to 'de-escalation' pact (Sept 24). None of these constitute an Israel-Turkey bilateral deconfliction agreement. All rejected as not meeting criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of any bilateral Israel-Turkey military deconfliction agreement or mechanism. Instead, evidence shows the opposite: [The National Interest](https://nationalinterest.org/blog/middle-east-watch/are-israel-and-turkiye-on-a-collision-course) describes both sides 'openly acknowledging the possibility of military confrontation'; [bne IntelliNews](https://www.intellinews.com/israeli-airstrikes-in-syria-target-turkish-weapons-stockpiles-400235/) reports Israel striking Turkish-supplied weapons stockpiles in Syria on Sept 9; [indyturk.com](https://www.indyturk.com/node/765590) reports Turkey attempting to block Israel-Syria security agreement as of Sept 29; [AOL/Reuters](https://www.aol.com/articles/turkey-wary-israeli-threat-following-050154246.html) reports Turkey 'wary' of Israeli threat. No official announcement of any Israel-Turkey deconfliction mechanism was found anywhere in the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no qualifying event occurred.
